<!-- https://walletfeed.app/ -->
# WalletFeed

Spending for Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings

Ask about your spending in your own words, and Apple Intelligence on your iPhone answers with a chart and a summary. WalletFeed needs no account and has no servers of its own. Your transactions go only where you send them.

Coming soon to the App Store

## Apple Intelligence

- Ask Spending: Ask “dining this month vs last” to see a chart, the categories, the matching transactions and a summary.
- Monthly Summary: A short summary of your month, written from figures WalletFeed calculates.
- Search: Type “dining over $50 last month” to see those transactions and their total.
- Recurring charge names: “NETFLIX.COM 866-579” appears as Netflix, with the kind of service.

WalletFeed calculates every chart, total and list. Apple Intelligence runs on your iPhone and sees only what each feature needs. Requires an iPhone that supports Apple Intelligence, with Apple Intelligence turned on.

## Privacy

- No account: There’s nothing to sign up for, and WalletFeed doesn’t know who you are.
- No tracking: WalletFeed has no analytics, advertising or third-party code.
- No WalletFeed servers: WalletFeed reads transactions from Wallet on your iPhone when it needs them and doesn’t keep a copy.
- On your iPhone: Apple Intelligence features run on the device, and nothing is sent to a server.
- Destinations you add: With Pro, transactions go straight from your iPhone to the services you choose. Keys and sign-ins stay in the Keychain on your iPhone.

Read the [privacy policy](https://walletfeed.app/privacy/).

## Spending

- Spending: This month by day, category and merchant, compared with the same point last month.
- Transactions: Transactions from the Wallet accounts you share, grouped by month.
- Recurring Charges: Subscriptions and other charges that repeat, found in your history.
- Recurring Charge Alerts: A notification when a charge starts repeating or its price changes.
- Monthly Installments: Apple Card Monthly Installments charges, in their own section of Spending.
- Spending widget: This month’s spending and the same point last month, on your Home Screen or Lock Screen.
- Search and export: Search all your transactions, and export a CSV file when you need one.
- Siri and Shortcuts: Ask Siri to show your spending or search your transactions.

## WalletFeed Pro

WalletFeed Pro is optional. It sends new and changed transactions from your iPhone to the destinations you add.

- Budgeting apps: BankSync, Lunch Money, PocketSmith, Firefly III, Sure and Toshl Finance. BankSync also offers Sign In with BankSync.
- Sheets and databases: Google Sheets, Airtable, Notion, Coda, Supabase and Linear
- Automations: Zapier, Make and signed [webhooks](https://walletfeed.app/docs/webhooks/)
- Files: One CSV file, or a CSV, OFX or QIF file a month, in iCloud Drive or another folder
- AWS: Amazon S3, SQS, Kinesis Data Streams, DynamoDB and EventBridge

- Background Sync: Your destinations update within the hour, even when WalletFeed is closed.
- Send History: By default, a new destination also receives your earlier transactions, at a pace the service accepts. Zapier, Make and Linear start 30 days back.
- Shortcuts: Sync after each card tap, or get recent transactions in a shortcut.

## Pricing

- Yearly: $4.99/year, 1 week free
- Monthly: $0.99/month, 1 week free
- Lifetime: $19.99, One payment

The spending features are free, including the Apple Intelligence ones. WalletFeed Pro adds destinations, Background Sync, Send History and the Shortcuts actions that send or get transactions. It works with Family Sharing. WalletFeed runs on iPhone with iOS 26 or later, in the US.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/privacy/ -->
# Privacy policy

Last updated October 29, 2026

WalletFeed needs no account and has no servers of its own. It reads your transactions from Wallet on your iPhone, holds them in memory only while it uses them, and doesn't keep a copy.

## Developer

WalletFeed is made by Phillip Harrison, an independent developer. Send questions about this policy to [support@walletfeed.app](mailto:support@walletfeed.app).

WalletFeed has no servers, so the developer holds no data about you to access, export or delete. If you email support, your message is used only to reply to you and is deleted once your question is resolved.

## Wallet data

WalletFeed reads transactions and account names from the Wallet accounts you choose to share through Apple's FinanceKit: Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings. iOS asks for your permission first.

You can change what you share at any time in the Settings app.

## Data on your iPhone

WalletFeed keeps only this on your iPhone:

- Sync positions (FinanceKit history tokens), so each destination receives only new changes.
- Your settings and each destination's settings, such as its name and filter.
- Destination credentials, such as API keys, webhook URLs and secrets, and folder access, in the Keychain. They stay on this iPhone and don't sync to iCloud Keychain.
- Sync status without transaction details: when each destination last synced, how many changes were sent, how far back its history has been sent, and a short error description if it failed. WalletFeed's widget can show this status.
- When WalletFeed's Shortcuts actions last ran, so Settings can show whether your automations work.
- For the Spending widget, two totals: your spending this month and at the same point last month, with their currency and the time they were updated. iOS keeps a copy of what the widget shows.
- If you turn on Recurring Charge Alerts, the IDs of transactions WalletFeed has already alerted on, so no alert comes twice. No amounts or merchants are kept for alerts.

WalletFeed doesn't keep a copy of your transactions. A Files destination saves them in the folder you choose.

## Destinations and exports

WalletFeed sends transactions only where you tell it to:

- A Files destination saves transactions in a folder you choose, such as one in iCloud Drive or On My iPhone, as one CSV file or as one CSV, OFX or QIF file per month.
- Services you connect, such as Lunch Money, Notion or AWS, receive transactions over HTTPS directly from your iPhone. WalletFeed connects with the key you paste, which stays in the Keychain on this iPhone.
- Google Sheets uses Google sign-in instead of a key, and the sign-in stays in the Keychain on this iPhone. WalletFeed asks Google only for access to files it creates, so it can open only its own spreadsheet in your Google Drive, where it adds and updates your transactions. It doesn't read, keep or share anything else from your Google Account. WalletFeed's use of information received from Google APIs adheres to the [Google API Services User Data Policy](https://developers.google.com/terms/api-services-user-data-policy), including the Limited Use requirements.
- BankSync can use Sign In with BankSync instead of a key. The sign-in stays in the Keychain on this iPhone, and WalletFeed can open only its own Apple Card table in your workspace.
- Webhooks, Zapier and Make receive each change at the address you paste. Webhook requests are signed with a secret made on your iPhone, which you share with your server.
- When you export a CSV, the file goes only where you send it from the share sheet.
- If you use WalletFeed's actions in Shortcuts, your shortcut receives the transactions they return.

Before a new destination receives anything, WalletFeed shows what it will get: which details of each transaction, from which accounts and from what date. Nothing is sent unless you agree.

Once data reaches a destination, that service's own terms and privacy policy apply. Removing a destination stops new data from going there, but WalletFeed can't delete what it already sent.

## Apple Intelligence and Siri

When Apple Intelligence is available, WalletFeed uses Apple's on-device model to write your monthly summary and a summary of each request on Spending, interpret searches and requests, name recurring charges and turn a rule you describe into a filter. It all runs on your iPhone, and nothing is sent to a server.

WalletFeed calculates every chart, total and list itself. The model writes the summaries in its own words from figures WalletFeed works out, such as your totals, the change from last month, categories, merchants and largest purchases, and for a request, the words you typed. It can get a figure wrong, so rely on the page's figures. To read a search, request or rule, the model gets only the words you type or say, and to name recurring charges, only their merchant names. Examples you tap on Spending are read by WalletFeed without the model. Nothing the model writes is saved, except the filter a rule creates.

Summarize Spending in Settings turns off both summaries. A request you send on Spending still goes to the model to be read.

When you ask Siri to show your spending or search WalletFeed, Siri opens the app and receives none of your transactions or spending. The Get Recent Card Transactions action is different: it returns transactions to the shortcut or Siri request that runs it.

## Analytics and tracking

WalletFeed has no analytics, advertising or third-party SDKs, and doesn't track you across apps or websites. If you share analytics with app developers in iOS Settings, Apple may share crash reports with the developer.

Sign In with BankSync goes through WalletFeed's referral link, so WalletFeed may earn a commission if you then pay for a BankSync plan.

## Purchases and notifications

Apple handles purchases and payments. WalletFeed checks on your iPhone which plan you have and whether it's active, and never sees your payment details.

If you turn on Remind If Sync Stops, WalletFeed schedules a local notification on your iPhone. It contains no transaction details.

If you turn on Recurring Charge Alerts, WalletFeed works out on your iPhone when a charge starts repeating or changes price, and posts a local notification with the charge's name and amounts. Notification Center keeps it until you clear it.

## Security

- WalletFeed covers its screen when you leave the app, so transactions don't appear in the app switcher.
- Transactions and spending are hidden while your screen is recorded or mirrored.
- The Spending widget's amounts are marked as private, so iOS can hide them while your iPhone is locked.
- You can require Face ID, Touch ID or your passcode to open WalletFeed.
- WalletFeed doesn't cache network responses on disk.

## Your choices

- Delete a destination in Destinations, or remove all of them in Settings. WalletFeed then deletes their credentials, sync positions and sync status from your iPhone.
- Stop sharing Wallet accounts in the Settings app. WalletFeed then clears the Spending widget's totals the next time it runs.
- Turn off Recurring Charge Alerts in Settings, or remove the Spending widget from your Home Screen or Lock Screen.
- Deleting WalletFeed removes its settings and sync status. Keychain items can remain after an app is deleted; if you install WalletFeed again, it erases them when it first opens.

## Children

WalletFeed is a personal finance app for adults and isn't directed at children under 13.

## This website

This site has no cookies, analytics or trackers. It's hosted on GitHub Pages, which may log visits under [GitHub's privacy statement](https://docs.github.com/site-policy/privacy-policies/github-general-privacy-statement).

## Changes

When this policy changes, this page and the app's privacy statement change together, with a new date.

# Terms of use

Last updated October 30, 2026

WalletFeed is made by Phillip Harrison, an independent developer. Apple’s [Licensed Application End User License Agreement](https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/dev/stdeula/) (the Standard EULA) is the license for the app. These terms add the points below.

## WalletFeed Pro

Apple sells WalletFeed Pro and processes every payment under the App Store’s terms. A subscription renews automatically unless you cancel it at least 24 hours before the end of the current period. To cancel or change your plan, open Settings on your iPhone, tap your name, then tap Subscriptions.

## Services you connect

When you add a destination, WalletFeed sends transactions from your iPhone directly to the service you choose. That service’s terms and privacy policy apply to the data it receives. You are responsible for the accounts, keys and sign-ins you connect, and for what you do with the data in those services. Removing a destination stops new data from going there, but WalletFeed can’t delete data that it already sent.

## Information, not advice

WalletFeed shows information from the Wallet accounts you share. It doesn’t give financial, tax or legal advice. Summaries from Apple Intelligence can contain errors, so use the figures that WalletFeed calculates.

## Trademarks

WalletFeed isn’t affiliated with Apple. Apple, Apple Card, Apple Cash, Apple Intelligence and Wallet are trademarks of Apple Inc. Other product names are trademarks of their owners.

## Contact and changes

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/support/ -->
# Support

Send an email to [support@walletfeed.app](mailto:support@walletfeed.app?subject=WalletFeed). In the email, include the model of your iPhone and the version of iOS on it. For a problem with a destination, also include the type of destination. Do not send API keys, tokens or data about your transactions.

To correct a problem, find it on this page or in [Troubleshooting](https://walletfeed.app/docs/troubleshooting/).

## If WalletFeed does not show your cards

WalletFeed is available only in the US. It reads only the Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings accounts that you share with it.

To share accounts for the first time, tap **Settings** (the gear button) › **Choose Accounts** in WalletFeed. WalletFeed shows **Choose Accounts** until you tap **Share** or **Don’t Share** on the iOS screen **Share Wallet Data**.

After that, **Settings** › **Wallet** shows **Open Settings**, and you change the accounts in the Settings app:

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select the accounts and the start date of each account.

Refer to [Select the Wallet accounts that WalletFeed reads](https://walletfeed.app/docs/wallet-accounts/).

## If WalletFeed does not show Ask Spending

These functions operate only on an iPhone that can use Apple Intelligence, with Apple Intelligence on:

- Ask Spending
- The Monthly Summary
- Search with Apple Intelligence
- Names in Recurring Charges

If your iPhone can use Apple Intelligence, set Apple Intelligence to on in the Settings app. Without Apple Intelligence, **Spending** and **Search** continue to operate, and **Search** finds the words that you type.

Use **Summarize Spending** in WalletFeed **Settings** to start or stop the summaries. Refer to [Ask Spending with Apple Intelligence](https://walletfeed.app/docs/ask-spending/).

## If a destination shows “Authentication failed”

The service did not accept the key, the token or the sign-in of the destination. A change to the access of the destination in the service can also cause this message.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Replace Key**, **Replace Token** or **Sign In Again**.
4. Paste a new key or token, or sign in again.

WalletFeed keeps the sync position and the history of the destination. Thus, the destination continues where it stopped. Refer to [Troubleshooting](https://walletfeed.app/docs/troubleshooting/#if-a-destination-shows-authentication-failed).

## If a destination receives changes only while WalletFeed is open

While WalletFeed is open, a destination receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. WalletFeed then updates the Spending widget and Recurring Charge Alerts. With WalletFeed Pro and **Background Sync** on, it also sends the change to your destinations.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Sync** section, set **Background Sync** to on.

**Settings** shows the **Sync** section only with WalletFeed Pro. After your iPhone starts again, destinations do not receive changes until you type your passcode one time.

To send each purchase seconds after you tap your iPhone to make the purchase, do the steps for **After Each Card Tap** in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Automations**. Refer to [Background Sync](https://walletfeed.app/docs/background-sync/).

## If a file changes only when you open WalletFeed

If WalletFeed cannot open the folder of a CSV, OFX or QIF file in the background, it does not update the file. WalletFeed updates the file the next time that you open WalletFeed, or while your iPhone charges. Refer to [Troubleshooting](https://walletfeed.app/docs/troubleshooting/#if-a-file-changes-only-when-you-open-walletfeed).

## If a destination does not have your previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it.

If **Send** is **Each Transaction**, a new Zapier, Make or Linear destination receives a maximum of 30 days of previous transactions. In these services, each transaction runs a Zap, uses a Make credit or becomes an issue.

WalletFeed sends the newest transactions first, at the speed that each service accepts. The screen of the destination shows **Sending History** and the number of transactions that WalletFeed sent. The history continues in the background. A long history to a slow service can continue for some days.

To send more previous transactions to a destination, do these steps:

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Send History**.
4. Select a period, for example **90 Days**.

To stop the history, tap **Send History** › **Stop Sending**. The destination keeps the transactions that it received before you stopped the history. Refer to [Send previous transactions](https://walletfeed.app/docs/send-history/).

## If you want to sign in with BankSync

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.
3. Tap **BankSync**.
4. Tap **Sign In with BankSync**.
5. Give your approval as the owner or an admin of the workspace.
6. Tap **Add**.

After your approval, BankSync makes an Apple Card table, and WalletFeed can see only that table. WalletFeed waits for the table for approximately 30 seconds.

If BankSync does not make the table, WalletFeed shows “You’re signed in, but BankSync hasn’t created or shared the Apple Card table.”

The BankSync Free plan has a limit of one table. If your plan is at its limit, delete a table in BankSync or change to a plan that has more tables. Then, in WalletFeed, tap **Try Again**.

To use an API key, tap **Use an API Key Instead**. API keys are available only on the Standard plan of BankSync or higher. Refer to [Send Apple Card transactions to BankSync](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/).

**Note:** Sign In with BankSync uses the referral link of WalletFeed. Thus, the BankSync screen in WalletFeed shows “WalletFeed may earn a commission if you pay for BankSync.”

## If a destination shows a pending charge

Most destinations receive a charge while it is pending. When the charge posts, WalletFeed updates it. WalletFeed removes declined and expired charges from the destination.

OFX and QIF files include a charge only after it posts.

A webhook, Zapier, Make and the AWS queues and streams receive a message for each change. Your server or automation must then update its data. Refer to [Destinations](https://walletfeed.app/docs/destinations/#new-and-changed-transactions).

## If you want a destination to receive only some transactions

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Set the **Filter** switch to on.
4. Use **Accounts**, **Categories** or **Minimum** to select the transactions.

With Apple Intelligence, you can also type the filter as a sentence, for example “Travel over $50, not Uber”. Refer to [Choose what a destination receives](https://walletfeed.app/docs/choose-what-to-send/).

## If you want to change or cancel your plan

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Subscription** section, tap **Change Plan** or **Manage Subscription**.

You can also change or cancel the subscription in the Settings app:

1. Open the Settings app.
2. Tap your name.
3. Tap **Subscriptions**.

**Restore Purchases** is on the **WalletFeed Pro** screen. Refer to [WalletFeed Pro](https://walletfeed.app/docs/walletfeed-pro/).

## If you want to delete your data

WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. Thus, there is no account data or server data to delete.

When you delete a destination, WalletFeed removes its credentials, its sync position and its sync status from your iPhone. The transactions that WalletFeed sent stay in that service.

Refer to [Privacy and security](https://walletfeed.app/docs/privacy-and-security/) and the [privacy policy](https://walletfeed.app/privacy/).

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/webhooks/ -->
# Webhook format

A Webhook destination posts JSON to your HTTPS URL whenever transactions change. Requests come straight from your iPhone and are signed with [Standard Webhooks](https://www.standardwebhooks.com), so any Standard Webhooks library can verify them.

## Request

- `POST` to the URL you entered, with `Content-Type: application/json` and `User-Agent: WalletFeed-Webhooks/1`.
- `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp` and `webhook-signature` headers (see [Verify](https://walletfeed.app/docs/webhooks/#verify)).
- Your `Authorization` value, if you set one in WalletFeed.
- Up to 100 transactions per request. Any 2xx response counts as delivered; anything else is retried on the next sync.

## Body

```
{
  "type": "transactions.changed",
  "timestamp": "2026-10-27T17:41:21Z",
  "data": {
    "upserted": [
      {
        "id": "8B3F0C2E-6D7A-4E8F-9C1B-2A4D5E6F7A8B",
        "accountID": "4F1E2D3C-…",
        "accountName": "Apple Card",
        "accountType": "liability",
        "date": "2026-10-27T15:02:11Z",
        "amount": 6.75,
        "currencyCode": "USD",
        "direction": "debit",
        "description": "Blue Bottle Coffee",
        "originalDescription": "BLUE BOTTLE COFFEE OAKLAND CA",
        "merchantName": "Blue Bottle Coffee",
        "merchantCategoryCode": 5814,
        "category": "dining",
        "status": "pending",
        "type": "purchase"
      }
    ],
    "deletedIDs": []
  }
}
```

Send Test in WalletFeed posts the same shape with `"type": "walletfeed.test"` and one sample transaction.

## Handling changes

- Upsert on `id`. A pending charge (`status` `pending` or `authorized`) arrives again under the same `id` when it posts (`booked`), with its final amount.
- Delete the transactions listed in `deletedIDs`: declined and expired charges, and transactions removed from Wallet.
- Earlier transactions, sent as the destination's history, arrive the same way in `transactions.changed` requests, newest first, so upserting on `id` covers them too.
- To drop repeated deliveries, deduplicate on `webhook-id`. It's derived from the request's contents, so a retried request carries the same ID.

## Fields

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Wallet's transaction ID. Stable across updates. |
| `accountID`, `accountName` | The Wallet account, such as Apple Card. |
| `accountType` | `liability` (Apple Card) or `asset` (Apple Cash, Savings). |
| `date`, `postedDate` | ISO 8601. `postedDate` appears once the charge posts, when Wallet provides it. |
| `amount` | A positive number; `direction` gives the sign. |
| `direction` | `debit` (purchases, fees) or `credit` (refunds, payments, deposits). |
| `currencyCode` | ISO 4217, such as `USD`. `foreignAmount` and `foreignCurrencyCode` appear for purchases in another currency. |
| `description`, `originalDescription` | Wallet's cleaned-up description, and the raw one from the network. |
| `merchantName`, `merchantCategoryCode` | When Wallet knows them. The category code is the card network's MCC. |
| `category` | WalletFeed's category from the MCC: `groceries`, `dining`, `transport`, `fuel`, `travel`, `shopping`, `entertainment`, `subscriptions`, `utilities`, `health`, `services`, `cash` or `other`. |
| `status` | Wallet's status: `authorized`, `pending`, `booked` or `memo`. |
| `type` | Wallet's transaction type, such as `purchase`, `refund`, `payment` or `transfer`. |

Fields without a value are left out.

## Verify

Get the signing secret from Share Signing Secret in WalletFeed, on the setup screen or the destination's screen. It's `whsec_` followed by base64. With a Standard Webhooks library:

```
// Node: npm install standardwebhooks
import { Webhook } from "standardwebhooks";
const payload = new Webhook(process.env.WALLETFEED_SECRET).verify(rawBody, request.headers);
```

```
# Python: pip install standardwebhooks
from standardwebhooks.webhooks import Webhook
payload = Webhook(os.environ["WALLETFEED_SECRET"]).verify(raw_body, request.headers)
```

Or by hand:

1. Base64-decode the secret after `whsec_`.
2. Compute HMAC-SHA256 of `{webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{raw body}` with it, and base64-encode the result.
3. Compare it, in constant time, with the value after `v1,` in `webhook-signature`.
4. Reject timestamps more than five minutes from now.

Verify the raw body exactly as received, before parsing it.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/ask-spending/ -->
# Ask Spending with Apple Intelligence

Ask Spending lets you type a question about your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions, for example `Dining this month vs last`. Apple Intelligence on your iPhone reads the question. WalletFeed calculates the result and shows it as a chart and a list. Apple Intelligence writes a summary of the result.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone that can use Apple Intelligence, with iOS 26 or a newer version. Apple Intelligence must be on.
- WalletFeed, with [access to your Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/). WalletFeed is available only in the US.

[WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/) is not necessary for Ask Spending. If Apple Intelligence is not available, [**Spending**](/docs/spending/) shows this month without the question field.

## Type a question

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Spending** at the bottom of the screen.
3. Tap the **Ask about your spending** field at the top of the screen.
4. Type a question, for example `Groceries over $50`.

   The question can have a maximum of 200 characters.

5. Tap **Go** on the keyboard.

   While WalletFeed gets the result, a progress indicator shows in the field. Then WalletFeed shows the result below the field.

   ![The result for Dining this month vs last, with 9 transactions, a total of $188.70 and a line chart of this month and last month.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/ask-spending/walletfeed-ask-spending.webp)

6. Optional: To see one day, week or month, move your finger along the chart.

   The top of the result then shows the date and the amount at that point on the chart.

## Use an example

When no result is on the screen, WalletFeed shows an example question below the field. The example starts with "Try". At intervals of 4 seconds, the next example shows. WalletFeed shows only the examples that give a result for your transactions from this month and the two months before this month.

1. Tap the example below the field.

   ![The Spending screen with the empty Ask about your spending field and the example Dining this month vs last below it.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/ask-spending/walletfeed-spending.webp)

   The example then shows in the field.

2. Optional: Change the question.
3. Tap **Go** on the keyboard.

If you do not change the example, WalletFeed reads it without Apple Intelligence.

> **Note:** The example stays the same while you type and while VoiceOver is on. With VoiceOver, the example button has the other examples as actions. With Reduce Motion, the next example shows at intervals of 8 seconds.

## Write a question that WalletFeed can read

A question can contain the items in this table. It can also start with `how much did I spend`.

| Item | Examples |
|---|---|
| A period | `today`, `this week`, `last 30 days`, `September`, `last year` |
| A period to compare with | `vs last month`, `vs last year` |
| A category | `dining`, `groceries`, `travel` |
| A merchant name, or a part of it | `coffee` |
| An amount limit for each transaction | `over $50`, `under $20`, `at least $50` |
| Refunds, money in or recurring charges | `refunds`, `money in`, `subscriptions` |
| A chart type | `by day`, `by week`, `by category`, `by merchant`, `trend` |
| The largest transactions first | `biggest purchases`, `largest purchases` |

WalletFeed uses these rules for periods:

- If the question has no period, WalletFeed uses this month.
- `last month` is the calendar month before this one, and `past month` is the last 30 days. Weeks and years have the same rule. For example, `past year` is the last 12 months.
- For a month name, for example `September`, WalletFeed uses the last September. If this month is September, WalletFeed uses this month.
- WalletFeed compares a period only with the previous period, or with the same period of the previous year.
- If the period has not ended, WalletFeed uses the other period only up to the same day and time. For example, on October 20, `Dining this month vs last` compares October 1 to 20 with September 1 to 20.

If a question contains one of these items, WalletFeed shows "Couldn't read this." below the field:

- A part that removes transactions, for example `except`, `not` or `without`.
- Two amount limits, for example `between $10 and $50`.
- Two types of transactions, for example `refunds and deposits`.
- Two categories or two merchants to compare, for example `dining vs groceries`.
- A period that WalletFeed cannot use, for example `yesterday`, `since March`, `this quarter` or `on Fridays`.
- A question about balances or budgets.

## Read the result

The result shows these items, from top to bottom:

- How WalletFeed read the question, with the Apple Intelligence icon, for example "Dining · This month · vs last month".
- The number of transactions and their total. If you compare two periods, the change also shows, for example "↑ 38% VS SEP". If the other period has a total of zero or less, the change does not show.
- A chart, by day, week, month, category or merchant. If you compare two periods by day, week or month, the chart usually shows the total from the start of each period.
- A summary. If the summary has the Apple Intelligence icon, Apple Intelligence wrote it. This summary can contain an incorrect number. A light bulb icon shows that WalletFeed wrote the summary from the facts that it calculates.
- The **Categories** section, with the five largest categories, and **Other** for the remaining categories. The category totals include refunds, and their sum is the total. If the refunds in a category are more than its purchases, the category total has a plus sign (+).
- The **Merchants** section, with the five merchants that have the largest totals. This section shows only if the result has two or more merchants and the chart does not show merchants. It does not show for recurring charges.
- The transactions, in a section for each month, with the last transaction first. If the question asks for the largest transactions, the **Largest** section shows them, largest first.

If the question is about recurring charges, the [**Recurring Charges**](/docs/recurring-charges/) section shows above **Categories**. If the question also has no period and does not compare two periods, the total is the sum of the charges for one month. The top of the result then shows the number of recurring charges, and the total has "a month" after it.

If no transactions agree with the question, the result shows "0 TRANSACTIONS" and $0.00.

## Change the question

When you change the question, WalletFeed removes the result and shows this month again.

1. Tap **Clear** (the x button) in the field.
2. Type a different question.
3. Tap **Go** on the keyboard.

## Update the result

WalletFeed reads Wallet each time you go back to WalletFeed, and when you pull down on **Spending**. Then WalletFeed calculates the result again from the transactions that it reads. Apple Intelligence does not read the question again.

To update the result now, pull down on **Spending**.

## Set Summarize Spending to off

If you set **Summarize Spending** to off, Apple Intelligence does not write the summary of each result or the Monthly Summary. WalletFeed then shows a light bulb icon and two facts that it calculates. Apple Intelligence continues to read each question that you type.

1. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In **Privacy & Security**, set **Summarize Spending** to off.

   ![Settings with the Privacy & Security section, where Summarize Spending is on.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/ask-spending/walletfeed-settings-2.webp)

3. Tap **Done**.

**Settings** shows **Summarize Spending** only when Apple Intelligence is available on your iPhone.

## Privacy

Apple Intelligence operates on your iPhone. Ask Spending does not send data to a server. To read a question, Apple Intelligence gets only the question. To write a summary, it gets the question and the data that WalletFeed calculates. This data includes your totals, the change between two periods, the categories, the merchants and the largest purchases.

WalletFeed does not keep your questions, results or summaries. For more information, refer to the [WalletFeed privacy policy](/privacy/).

## If there is a problem

### If WalletFeed shows "Couldn't read this."

WalletFeed cannot get a result from the question. The question stays in the field, and an example shows below it.

1. Change the question to use the items in [Write a question that WalletFeed can read](#write-a-question-that-walletfeed-can-read).
2. Tap **Go** on the keyboard.

You can also tap the example below the field.

### If WalletFeed shows "Couldn't read Wallet. Pull down to try again."

WalletFeed did not get the transactions for the result from Wallet. To try again, pull down on **Spending**. WalletFeed then reads Wallet and the question again.

### If Spending does not show "Ask about your spending"

The field shows only if Apple Intelligence is available on your iPhone.

1. Make sure that your iPhone can use Apple Intelligence.

   Apple gives the list of iPhone models in [How to get Apple Intelligence](https://support.apple.com/en-us/121115).

2. In the Settings app, tap **Apple Intelligence & Siri**.
3. Set **Apple Intelligence** to on.

When Apple Intelligence becomes available, **Spending** shows the field.

### If the result shows "0 TRANSACTIONS"

WalletFeed read the question, but no transactions agree with it.

1. Make sure that the text above the result shows the correct period and category.
2. If this text is not correct, change the question.
3. Tap **Go** on the keyboard.

### If the summary has an incorrect number

Apple Intelligence writes the summary from the numbers that WalletFeed calculates. WalletFeed does not examine the summary.

1. Use the total, the chart and the list, because WalletFeed calculates them.
2. To get the summary from WalletFeed, [set Summarize Spending to off](#set-summarize-spending-to-off).

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/background-sync/ -->
# Background Sync

**Background Sync** sends your new and changed Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions to your destinations while WalletFeed is closed. To send transactions to [destinations](/docs/destinations/), you must have [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/). WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.

## Times that destinations receive changes

A destination receives a new or changed transaction at these times:

| Condition | A destination receives the change |
| --- | --- |
| WalletFeed is open. | In seconds. |
| WalletFeed is closed, and **Background Sync** is on. | In approximately 1 hour or less after the change in Wallet. |
| You tap your iPhone to make a purchase, and you have an **After Each Card Tap** automation. | Seconds after you tap your iPhone. |
| Your **Every Day** automation starts. | At the time that you set in Shortcuts. |
| You tap **Sync Now** in **Settings** › **Sync**. | In seconds. |
| Your iPhone charges. | At a time that iOS selects. |

While WalletFeed is closed, iOS also starts WalletFeed after a change in Wallet to update the Spending widget and Recurring Charge Alerts. WalletFeed does this without WalletFeed Pro, and also while **Background Sync** is off.

After your iPhone starts again, WalletFeed does not send changes to your destinations until you type your passcode one time.

If **Background Sync** cannot open the folder of a CSV, OFX or QIF file, it does not update the file. WalletFeed updates the file when you open WalletFeed, when an automation starts, or while your iPhone charges.

A new destination also receives previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. If **Send** is **Each Transaction** for Zapier, Make or Linear, the destination receives a maximum of 30 days of previous transactions. Refer to [Send History](/docs/send-history/).

## Make sure that Background Sync is on

**Background Sync** is on until you set it to off. **Settings** shows the **Sync** section only with WalletFeed Pro.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Sync** section, make sure that **Background Sync** is on.

   ![The Sync section of WalletFeed Settings, with the Background Sync switch on.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/background-sync/walletfeed-settings.webp)

3. If **Background Sync** is off, set it to on.
4. Tap **Done**.

## Add an After Each Card Tap automation

An **After Each Card Tap** automation sends each purchase seconds after you tap your iPhone to make the purchase. While **Background Sync** is on, this automation is not necessary. Without the automation, a destination receives the purchase in approximately 1 hour or less while WalletFeed is closed.

iOS does not let apps make automations. Thus, you add the automation in the Shortcuts app, and WalletFeed gives you the steps.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Sync** section, tap **Automations**.

   ![The Automations screen, with the steps for After Each Card Tap and Every Day.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/background-sync/walletfeed-automations.webp)

3. In the **After Each Card Tap** section, do the steps for your iPhone.

   The sections that follow give these steps. The steps are different on iOS 26 and on iOS 27. On iOS 27, they are also different with Apple Intelligence.

### Paste the text in Shortcuts

If step 1 in the **After Each Card Tap** section is **Copy Description**, do these steps. WalletFeed shows them on iOS 27 with Apple Intelligence, and after you tap **Describe It Instead**.

1. Tap **Copy Description**.

   **Copy Description** changes to **Copied**. WalletFeed copies the text `When I tap my Apple Card or Apple Cash card, run Sync New Purchase from WalletFeed without asking.`

2. Tap **Open Shortcuts**.
3. In Shortcuts, tap **+**.
4. Paste the text.
5. Make sure that the automation uses your cards.
6. Make sure that the automation does not wait for your approval.
7. Tap **Done**.

> **Note:** If Shortcuts does not make the automation from the text, **Set It Up Yourself** in WalletFeed gives a different procedure. This procedure is also in [Make the automation on iOS 27](#make-the-automation-on-ios-27).

### Make the automation on iOS 26

If step 2 in the **After Each Card Tap** section tells you to tap **Automation**, do these steps. WalletFeed shows them on iOS 26.

1. Tap **Open Shortcuts**.
2. In Shortcuts, tap **Automation**.
3. Tap **+** or **New Automation**.
4. Tap **Transaction**.
5. Select your cards.
6. Select **Run Immediately**.
7. Tap **Next**.
8. Tap **New Blank Automation** › **Add Action**.
9. Type WalletFeed in the search field.
10. Tap **Sync New Purchase**.
11. Tap **Done**.

### Make the automation on iOS 27

If step 2 in the **After Each Card Tap** section tells you to tap **Add Action**, do these steps. WalletFeed shows them on iOS 27 when Apple Intelligence is not available, and after you tap **Set It Up Yourself**.

1. Tap **Open Shortcuts**.
2. In Shortcuts, tap **Add Action**.
3. Type WalletFeed in the search field.
4. Tap **Sync New Purchase**.
5. In the action list, tap **Automation** › **Transaction**.
6. Select your cards.
7. Tap the arrow adjacent to the trigger.
8. Set **Confirm Before Run** to off.
9. Tap the information button **ⓘ** › **Privacy**.
10. Set **Allow Running When Locked** to on.
11. Tap **Done**.

### Automations and Last Run

iOS does not tell apps about the automations that you have. Thus, WalletFeed records the last time that **Sync New Purchase** and **Sync Transactions** started. **Last Run** shows this time. If Siri or a shortcut starts **Sync Transactions**, the **Last Run** of **Every Day** also changes. Until an action starts for the first time, its **Last Run** shows **Never**.

In **Settings** › **Sync**, **Automations** shows one of these values:

| Value | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| **On** | Each automation on the **Automations** screen started in its time limit. |
| **1 of 2** | One of the two automations started in its time limit. |
| **Off** | **Background Sync** is on, **Sample Data** is off, and **After Each Card Tap** did not start in its time limit. |
| **Set Up** | **Background Sync** is off or **Sample Data** is on, and no automation started in its time limit. |

The time limit is 14 days for **After Each Card Tap**, and 3 days for **Every Day**.

For the messages that the automations show, refer to [Siri and Shortcuts](/docs/siri-and-shortcuts/).

## Add an Every Day automation

An **Every Day** automation sends changes one time each day, at a time that you select. It sends the changes that an **After Each Card Tap** automation does not send, for example purchases on the internet and changes to pending transactions.

**Automations** shows **Every Day** only when **Background Sync** is off or **Sample Data** is on. While **Background Sync** is on, an **Every Day** automation is not necessary. If you have an **Every Day** automation, it stays in Shortcuts and continues to send changes.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Sync** section, tap **Automations**.
3. In the **Every Day** section, do the steps for your iPhone.

   These steps are the same as the steps in [Add an After Each Card Tap automation](#add-an-after-each-card-tap-automation), but the parts in the table that follows are different.

| Part | **After Each Card Tap** | **Every Day** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The text that you copy | `When I tap my Apple Card or Apple Cash card, run Sync New Purchase from WalletFeed without asking.` | `Every day at 9 PM, run Sync Transactions from WalletFeed without asking.` |
| The trigger in Shortcuts | **Transaction**, then your cards | **Time of Day**, then a time |
| The WalletFeed action | **Sync New Purchase** | **Sync Transactions** |
| The last check before you tap **Done** | Your cards | The time |

## Get the Sync Stopped notification

If **Remind If Sync Stops** is on and WalletFeed does not send to all your destinations correctly for 3 days, you get the **Sync Stopped** notification. The notification does not show information about your transactions.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Sync** section, set **Remind If Sync Stops** to on.
3. If iOS shows a message about notifications, let WalletFeed send notifications.

   If you do not let WalletFeed send notifications, **Remind If Sync Stops** stays off.

4. Tap **Done**.

Each time that WalletFeed sends to all your destinations correctly, the 3-day period starts again. The text of the notification is "WalletFeed hasn't synced in 3 days. Open it to catch up."

## Send changes with Sync Now

**Sync Now** sends the changes to your destinations when you tap it.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Sync** section, tap **Sync Now**.

   ![WalletFeed Settings, with Initial History set to All and Sync Now with the time 1 minute ago.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/background-sync/walletfeed-settings-2.webp)

   While WalletFeed sends the changes, **Sync Now** shows a progress indicator. Then it shows a time, for example "1 minute ago".

3. Tap **Done**.

## Stop Background Sync

If you set **Background Sync** to off, iOS continues to start WalletFeed after a change in Wallet. But WalletFeed then updates only the Spending widget and Recurring Charge Alerts.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Sync** section, set **Background Sync** to off.
3. Tap **Done**.

While **Background Sync** is off, your destinations receive changes at these times:

- When you open WalletFeed
- When you tap **Sync Now**
- When an automation from **Automations** starts
- While your iPhone charges
- At other times that iOS selects

**Automations** then also shows **Every Day**. Refer to [Add an Every Day automation](#add-an-every-day-automation).

## If something goes wrong

### If a destination does not receive a change after 1 hour

**Background Sync** is off, your iPhone started again, or the destination has a problem.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.

   While WalletFeed is open, it sends changes in seconds.

2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In the **Sync** section, if **Background Sync** is off, set it to on.
4. Tap **Sync Now**.
5. Tap **Done**.
6. Tap **Destinations** at the bottom of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen, where the n8n destination shows Authentication failed.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/background-sync/walletfeed-destinations-failure.webp)

7. If a destination shows a problem, for example "Authentication failed", refer to [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting/).

### If Settings does not show the Sync section

**Settings** shows the **Sync** section only with WalletFeed Pro.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Subscription** section, tap **WalletFeed Pro**.
3. Select a plan.
4. Tap **Start Free Trial**, **Subscribe** or **Buy Lifetime**.

For the plans, refer to [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/).

### If you get the Sync Stopped notification

In the last 3 days, WalletFeed did not send to all your destinations correctly.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations** at the bottom of the screen.
3. If a destination shows a problem, refer to [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting/).
4. If no destination shows a problem, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
5. In the **Sync** section, tap **Sync Now**.

### If Last Run shows Never

**Last Run** changes only after **Sync New Purchase** starts. An **After Each Card Tap** automation starts it only when you tap your iPhone to make a purchase.

1. After you make a purchase with your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In the **Sync** section, tap **Automations**.
4. In the **After Each Card Tap** section, if **Last Run** shows **Never**, do the steps in [Add an After Each Card Tap automation](#add-an-after-each-card-tap-automation) again.

> **Note:** On iOS 27, **Set It Up Yourself** and **Describe It Instead** give a different procedure to make the same automation.

### If Remind If Sync Stops does not stay on

iOS does not let WalletFeed send notifications.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Notifications** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Set **Allow Notifications** to on.
4. Open WalletFeed.
5. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
6. In the **Sync** section, set **Remind If Sync Stops** to on.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/choose-what-to-send/ -->
# Choose what a destination receives

A filter selects which of your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions a destination receives from WalletFeed. Without a filter, a destination receives all the transactions from the Wallet accounts that you share with WalletFeed.

Each destination has its own filter. For example, you can send your Apple Card transactions to one file and your Apple Cash transactions to a different file.

You set the filter on the screen of the destination, after you add the destination. To add a destination, you must have [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/). WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase. Refer to [Destinations](/docs/destinations/).

## Set a filter for a destination

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations** at the bottom of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with four destinations: Lunch Money, Budget 2026, Monthly CSV and n8n.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/choose-what-to-send/walletfeed-destinations.webp)

3. Tap the destination.

   ![The Lunch Money destination screen, with the Filter switch set to off.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/choose-what-to-send/walletfeed-destination-detail.webp)

4. Set the **Filter** switch to on.

   The filter controls show below the switch: **Include**, **Minimum**, **Include Pending**, **Accounts**, **Categories** and **Exclude**.

Until you change a control, the filter includes all transactions. WalletFeed saves each change when you make it.

A destination receives a transaction only if all the filter controls include it. When you change the filter, WalletFeed does not remove the transactions that it sent before.

## Send only purchases or only credits

1. On the screen of the destination, tap **Include**.
2. Tap **Purchases** or **Credits**.

   With **Purchases**, the destination receives purchases and fees. With **Credits**, it receives credits, such as refunds and payments.

To send all transactions again, select **All** in **Include**.

## Set a minimum amount

1. On the screen of the destination, tap **None** in the **Minimum** row.
2. Type the amount, for example 50.

   The destination receives only transactions of $50 or more.

The minimum is also for credits. Thus, a destination with a minimum of 50 does not receive a refund of $20. To remove the minimum, delete the number.

## Send charges only after they post

A pending charge can change before it posts. To send each charge only after it posts, set the **Include Pending** switch to off on the screen of the destination.

OFX and QIF files include a charge only after it posts, also when **Include Pending** is on.

## Select the accounts

1. On the screen of the destination, tap **Accounts**.

   **Accounts** opens with the Wallet accounts that you share with WalletFeed.

2. Tap each account that the destination receives.

   **Accounts** shows a check mark on the row of each account that you select.

3. Tap the back button at the top of the screen.

   The **Accounts** row shows the number of accounts that you selected.

To send all the accounts again, tap **All** at the top of the **Accounts** screen.

## Select the categories

WalletFeed sets the category of each transaction from its merchant category code (MCC). The categories are **Groceries**, **Dining**, **Transport**, **Fuel**, **Travel**, **Shopping**, **Entertainment**, **Subscriptions**, **Utilities**, **Health**, **Services**, **Cash & Transfers** and **Other**.

1. On the screen of the destination, tap **Categories**.
2. Tap each category that the destination receives.

   **Categories** shows a check mark on the row of each category that you select.

3. Tap the back button at the top of the screen.

   The **Categories** row shows the number of categories that you selected.

To send all the categories again, tap **All** at the top of the **Categories** screen.

## Send no transactions from some merchants

1. On the screen of the destination, tap **Merchants** in the **Exclude** row.
2. Type the merchants, with a comma between them, for example `Uber, Starbucks`.

   The destination does not receive transactions from these merchants.

The destination does not receive a transaction if its merchant name or description contains one of the names. Part of a name is sufficient. For example, with `uber`, the destination receives no transactions from Uber or Uber Eats. Uppercase and lowercase letters give the same result.

## Make a filter with Apple Intelligence

With Apple Intelligence, you can type the filter as a sentence. WalletFeed shows the text field for Apple Intelligence only on an iPhone that can use Apple Intelligence, with Apple Intelligence on.

1. On the screen of the destination, tap the text field below **Filter**.

   Until you type, the field shows the example "Travel over $50, not Uber".

2. Type a sentence about the transactions to send, for example `Dining over $20, not Starbucks`.
3. Tap the Apple Intelligence symbol at the end of the field.

   Apple Intelligence sets the filter controls from your sentence.

4. Examine the controls below the field.
5. If the value of a control is not correct, change it.

Your sentence replaces the values of all the controls, but not **Accounts**. Apple Intelligence uses an amount or a merchant only if your sentence contains it.

Apple Intelligence operates on your iPhone. It gets only your sentence, and not your transactions.

## Send previous transactions with the filter

To send previous transactions with the filter, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/).

1. On the screen of the destination, tap **Send History**.
2. Select **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.
3. If WalletFeed shows a message, tap **Send**.

   The destination receives the transactions from that period that agree with the filter.

## Filter the history of a new destination

A new destination has no filter. Before it receives transactions, WalletFeed shows a message. The message tells what the destination receives, from which accounts and from when. Because the destination has no filter, the message names all the Wallet accounts that you share.

When you tap **Send**, the destination starts to receive transactions from the date in **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. If **Send** is **Each Transaction** for Zapier, Make or Linear, the date is a maximum of 30 days before today.

To send only the transactions from today before you set the filter, do these steps:

1. In **Destinations**, tap **Settings** at the top of the screen.
2. In **Sync**, tap **Initial History**.

   ![WalletFeed Settings with Initial History set to All in the Sync section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/choose-what-to-send/walletfeed-settings.webp)

3. Tap **Today**.
4. Tap **Done**.
5. Add the destination. Refer to [Destinations](/docs/destinations/).
6. In the message from WalletFeed, tap **Send** (**Save** for Files).
7. Set the filter. Refer to [Set a filter for a destination](#set-a-filter-for-a-destination).
8. Tap **Send History**.
9. Select **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.
10. If WalletFeed shows a message, tap **Send**.

    The destination receives the previous transactions that agree with the filter.

**Initial History** stays at **Today** for the destinations that you add after this.

## Remove the filter

To remove the filter, set the **Filter** switch to off on the screen of the destination. WalletFeed removes the values of all the filter controls, and the destination receives all transactions again. If you set **Filter** to on again, you must set each control again.

## If something goes wrong

### If WalletFeed shows "Couldn't create a rule. Try describing it another way."

Apple Intelligence cannot make a filter from your sentence.

1. Write the sentence in a different way.
2. Tap the Apple Intelligence symbol again.
3. If the message shows again, change the controls below the field.

### If the text field for Apple Intelligence does not show

Your iPhone cannot use Apple Intelligence, or Apple Intelligence is off. You can set the filter without Apple Intelligence.

1. Make sure that your iPhone can use Apple Intelligence, and that Apple Intelligence is on.
2. Open the screen of the destination again.

### If a destination does not receive a transaction

One or more filter controls do not include the transaction. If the charge is pending and **Include Pending** is off, the destination receives the charge after it posts.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Examine the filter controls, for example **Minimum** and **Accounts**.
3. Change the control that does not include the transaction.
4. Tap **Send History**.
5. Select a period that includes the date of the transaction.
6. If WalletFeed shows a message, tap **Send**.

If the filter includes the transaction, find the cause in the guide for the destination. Refer to [Guides](/guides/).

### If a destination has transactions that the filter does not include

WalletFeed sent these transactions before you set the filter. A filter change does not remove them.

1. Open the service or the file that receives the transactions, for example your spreadsheet or budget app.
2. Remove the transactions that the filter does not include.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/destinations/ -->
# Destinations

A destination is an app, a spreadsheet, a file or a server that receives your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from WalletFeed. After you add a destination, WalletFeed sends your new and changed transactions to it from your iPhone.

To send transactions to a destination, you must have [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/). WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase. You can see the list of destination types without WalletFeed Pro.

## Destination types

**Add Destination** shows the destination types in these sections. Each type has a guide with all the steps:

| Section | Destinations |
|---|---|
| **Budgeting** | [BankSync](/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/), [Lunch Money](/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/), [PocketSmith](/guides/apple-card-to-pocketsmith/), [Firefly III](/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/), [Sure](/guides/apple-card-to-sure/), [Toshl Finance](/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/) |
| **Sheets & Databases** | [Google Sheets](/guides/apple-card-to-google-sheets/), [Airtable](/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/), [Notion](/guides/apple-card-to-notion/), [Coda](/guides/apple-card-to-coda/), [Supabase](/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/), [Linear](/guides/apple-card-to-linear/) |
| **Automations** | [Zapier](/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/), [Make](/guides/apple-card-to-make/) |
| **Files** | [CSV File](/guides/apple-card-to-csv/), [OFX File](/guides/apple-card-to-ofx/), [QIF File](/guides/apple-card-to-qif/) |
| **Developers** | [AWS](/guides/apple-card-to-aws/) (Amazon S3, Amazon SQS, Kinesis Data Streams, DynamoDB and EventBridge), [Webhook](/guides/apple-card-to-webhook/) |

**Files** and **AWS** show as one row each. In the setup form, you select the file format in **Format**, or the AWS service in **Service**. OFX and QIF files include a charge only after it posts.

Firefly III and Sure show **Self-hosted**. You install them on a server.

You can add more than one destination of the same type. For example, you can send each Wallet account to a different CSV file.

To find a destination, type its name in the search field at the top of **Add Destination**. The search also finds a file format from the name of an app that uses it. For example, "GnuCash" finds **OFX File** and **QIF File**.

![The Add Destination search with PocketSmith in the search field and PocketSmith as the result.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/destinations/walletfeed-add-destination-search.webp)

## Add a destination

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations** at the bottom of the screen.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The empty Destinations screen with the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/destinations/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. Tap the destination type, for example **Lunch Money**.

   ![The Add Destination screen with the search field, and the Budgeting and Sheets & Databases sections.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/destinations/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, the **WalletFeed Pro** screen opens. After you get WalletFeed Pro or tap **Restore Purchases**, the setup form opens.

5. Do the steps in the setup form.

   ![The Lunch Money setup form with the Access Token field, three numbered steps and the Open Developers link.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/destinations/walletfeed-setup-lunch-money.webp)

   The form shows numbered steps below its fields. For all the steps, refer to the guide for the destination type.

6. Tap **Add**.

   WalletFeed shows a message, for example **Send Transactions to Lunch Money?**

   The message tells you which data the destination receives, from which Wallet accounts and from which date.

7. Tap **Send**. For a Files destination, tap **Save**.

   WalletFeed closes **Add Destination** and starts to send transactions to the destination.

If you tap **Cancel** in the message, WalletFeed sends nothing and removes the destination. The setup form stays open, so you can change it. If you close **Add Destination** before you tap **Send**, WalletFeed also removes the destination.

A new destination also receives previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. If **Send** is **Each Transaction** for Zapier, Make or Linear, the destination receives a maximum of 30 days of previous transactions. To send more previous transactions after you add the destination, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/).

> **Note:** WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. WalletFeed sends your transactions from your iPhone directly to the service that you select. The key or sign-in for each destination stays in the Keychain on your iPhone.

The service keeps the data that it receives. To know how the service uses your data, refer to the terms of that service.

## Destination status

**Destinations** shows each destination with its status below its name.

![The Destinations screen with three destinations. The n8n webhook shows Authentication failed and an orange exclamation mark.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/destinations/walletfeed-destinations-failure.webp)

The status can be one of these:

| Status | Description |
|---|---|
| A time, for example "2 minutes ago" | The time of the last sync. |
| "Sending history · 46%" | WalletFeed sends previous transactions to the destination. |
| "History paused · 46%" | WalletFeed does not send previous transactions now. Refer to [Send History](/docs/send-history/). |
| "Off" | **Enabled** is off. WalletFeed does not send transactions to the destination. |
| A failure, for example "Authentication failed" | The last sync had a failure. Some failures also tell you what to do. An orange exclamation mark shows on the row. |

## New and changed transactions

While WalletFeed is open, a destination receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet.

For changes while WalletFeed is closed, **Background Sync** in **Settings** › **Sync** must be on. Refer to [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/).

To sync all destinations now, pull down the list in **Destinations**. You can also tap **Settings** › **Sync** › **Sync Now**.

## Change a destination

To open a destination, tap it in **Destinations**.

![The Lunch Money destination with Name, Enabled, Last Sync, Replace Token, Filter, Send History, Send Test and Delete.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/destinations/walletfeed-destination-detail.webp)

The screen of the destination has these rows, from top to bottom:

| Rows | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **Name**, **Enabled** and **Last Sync** | Change the name, stop or start the destination, and see the time and result of the last sync. |
| **Replace Key**, **Replace Token**, **Sign In Again** or **Change Folder** | Repair the connection. The rows are different for each destination type. |
| **Filter** | Send only some transactions. Refer to [Choose what a destination receives](/docs/choose-what-to-send/). |
| **Send History** | Send previous transactions. Refer to [Send History](/docs/send-history/). |
| **Send Test** | Send a sample transaction to the destination. |
| **Delete** | Remove the destination. |

**Last Sync** shows the time of the last sync. If WalletFeed sent transactions in that sync, it also shows the number, for example "1 minute ago · 2 sent". If the last sync had a failure, the failure shows below **Last Sync**.

## Change the name of a destination

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap **Name**.
3. Type the new name.

   **Destinations** shows the new name.

## Stop and start a destination

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Set **Enabled** to off.

   In **Destinations**, the destination shows "Off". WalletFeed does not send transactions to it while **Enabled** is off.

To send transactions to the destination again, set **Enabled** to on.

## Send a test

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap **Send Test**.

   WalletFeed sends one sample transaction to the destination. If the destination receives it, a green check mark shows next to **Send Test**. If not, the failure shows below **Send Test**.

The sample transaction has the merchant name WalletFeed and the amount 4.20 USD. For a Files destination, WalletFeed writes a test file in the folder, for example `WalletFeed Test.csv`. You can delete the sample from the destination.

## Replace a key or sign in again

If you make a new key in the service, replace the key in WalletFeed. You do not have to remove the destination and add it again.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap the row for the key, for example **Replace Key** or **Replace Token**.
3. Paste the new key.
4. Tap **Replace**.

   WalletFeed examines the new key with the service. If the key is correct, WalletFeed keeps it and shows a check mark.

For other destination types, use these rows at step 2:

- For Google Sheets and BankSync, tap **Sign In Again**.
- For Zapier and Make, tap **Replace URL**, then paste the new webhook URL.
- For a Files destination, tap **Change Folder**, then select the folder again.
- For a Webhook destination, tap **URL** or **Authorization**, type the new value, then tap **Save**.

## Remove a destination

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap **Delete**.

   WalletFeed shows a message with the name of the destination, for example **Delete Lunch Money?**

3. Tap **Delete**.

WalletFeed removes the destination and its key from your iPhone. The transactions that WalletFeed sent stay in the service. If you made a key in the service for WalletFeed, you can also delete the key in the service.

In **Destinations**, you can also swipe left on a destination, then tap **Delete**. WalletFeed then removes the destination without a message.

## Remove all destinations

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Data** section, tap **Remove All Destinations**.

   ![The Settings screen with Export CSV and Remove All Destinations in the Data section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/destinations/walletfeed-settings-4.webp)

3. Tap **Remove All**.

   WalletFeed removes all your destinations. The transactions that WalletFeed sent stay at each destination.

## If something goes wrong

### If a destination shows "Authentication failed"

The service does not let WalletFeed use the key, token or sign-in of the destination. For example, you deleted the key in the service.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.

   ![The n8n destination with Authentication failed below Last Sync, and the URL and Authorization rows.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/destinations/walletfeed-destination-failure.webp)

2. If the destination uses a key, make a new key in the service. For the steps, refer to the guide for the destination type.
3. In WalletFeed, replace the key or sign in again. Refer to [Replace a key or sign in again](#replace-a-key-or-sign-in-again).

### If a destination shows "Can't connect"

WalletFeed cannot connect to the service.

1. Make sure that your iPhone has an internet connection.
2. If the destination is on your server, make sure that the server operates.
3. In **Destinations**, pull down the list.

   WalletFeed syncs the destinations again.

### If a destination shows "Server error"

The service has a problem. WalletFeed does not lose the changes, and sends them at the next sync. To sync again, pull down the list in **Destinations** after some minutes.

### If a destination shows "Off"

The **Enabled** switch is off for the destination.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Set **Enabled** to on.

### If Destinations shows "Sync Requires Pro"

You do not have WalletFeed Pro now, so WalletFeed does not send transactions to your destinations. Your destinations stay in the list.

1. In **Destinations**, tap **Upgrade**.

   The **WalletFeed Pro** screen opens.

2. Select a plan, or tap **Restore Purchases**.

### If a destination receives changes only while WalletFeed is open

The **Background Sync** switch is off.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Sync** section, set **Background Sync** to on.

For more information, refer to [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/).

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/export-csv/ -->
# Export a CSV file

**Export CSV** in WalletFeed makes a CSV file with your Apple Card transactions from a period that you select. You can save the file in Files or send it to a different app. [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/) is not necessary for **Export CSV**.

## Export your transactions

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.

   ![The Transactions screen with the gear button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/export-csv/walletfeed-transactions.webp)

3. In the **Data** section, tap **Export CSV**.

   ![The Settings screen with Export CSV in the Data section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/export-csv/walletfeed-settings-3.webp)

4. Tap **Range**.
5. Select a period.

   ![The Export CSV screen shows This Month in Range, 29 in Transactions and the Export button.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/export-csv/walletfeed-export-csv.webp)

   **Transactions** shows the number of transactions in the period.

6. Tap **Export**.

   The share sheet opens with the name of the file, for example `Apple Card This Month.csv`.

7. Tap **Save to Files**.
8. Select a folder.
9. Tap **Save**.

At step 7, you can also select AirDrop, Mail or a different app in the share sheet. The file goes only to the app or person that you select.

## Periods in Range

When you open **Export CSV**, **Range** shows **This Month**. You can select one of these periods:

| Period | Transactions in the file |
| --- | --- |
| **This Month** | The transactions from the first day of this month. |
| **Last Month** | All the transactions of the month before this month. |
| **Last 90 Days** | The transactions from the last 90 days. |
| **This Year** | The transactions from January 1 of this year. |
| **All** | All the transactions that WalletFeed can read in Wallet. |

## The file

The name of the file has the period in it, for example `Apple Card Last Month.csv` or `Apple Card All.csv`. The first part of the name is always `Apple Card`, although the file can also have Apple Cash or Savings transactions.

The file has the transactions from each Wallet account that WalletFeed can read. The **Account** column shows the account of each transaction. To change the accounts that WalletFeed can read, refer to [Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/).

The first row has the names of the columns. Each row after it has one transaction. The rows are in date sequence, and the transaction with the last date is first. The file also has pending transactions.

The file does not change after you export it. To get new transactions, or a pending charge after it posts, export a new file.

WalletFeed makes the file on your iPhone and does not keep it. You can open the file in [Numbers](/guides/apple-card-to-numbers/) or [Excel](/guides/apple-card-to-excel/).

## Columns in the file

The file has these columns, from left to right:

| Column | Data |
| --- | --- |
| **Date** | The date of the transaction in the time zone of your iPhone, for example 2026-10-28. |
| **Posted Date** | The date when the transaction posted. This cell is empty until the transaction posts. |
| **Merchant** | The name of the merchant. If Wallet has no merchant name, this cell has the text from **Description**. |
| **Description** | The text of the transaction in Wallet. |
| **Original Description** | The initial text of the transaction in Wallet. |
| **Amount** | The value, for example -23.40. The value of a `debit` is less than zero, and the value of a `credit` is more than zero. |
| **Currency** | The currency code, for example USD. |
| **Direction** | `debit` or `credit`. For example, purchases and fees are `debit`, and payments and refunds are `credit`. |
| **Status** | The status in Wallet, for example `pending` or `authorized` before the charge posts, `booked` after it posts, or `rejected` for a declined charge. |
| **Type** | The type of transaction in Wallet, for example `pointOfSale` for a purchase, `refund`, `transfer` or `fee`. |
| **Category** | The WalletFeed category, for example Groceries, Travel or Cash & Transfers. |
| **MCC** | The merchant category code, for example 5411. If Wallet has no code, this cell is empty. |
| **Account** | The name of the Wallet account, for example Apple Card. |
| **Foreign Amount** | For a transaction in a different currency, the value in that currency. |
| **Foreign Currency** | The code of the currency in **Foreign Amount**. |
| **WalletFeed ID** | The ID of the transaction. A transaction has the same ID in each file that you export. |

Each value in **Amount** and **Foreign Amount** has two digits after the decimal point and no commas, for example 1250.00. The file is UTF-8 text in the RFC 4180 CSV format.

If the first character in **Merchant**, **Description**, **Original Description** or **Account** is `=`, `+`, `-` or `@`, WalletFeed puts an apostrophe (`'`) before it. With the apostrophe, a spreadsheet does not use the text as a formula.

## Get a file that WalletFeed updates

With [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), WalletFeed can write your transactions to a [CSV file in a folder](/guides/apple-card-to-csv/). This file has the same columns. WalletFeed then updates the file when your transactions change. For the times when WalletFeed updates the file, refer to [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/). WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.

## If there is a problem

### If you cannot tap Export

You cannot tap **Export** while WalletFeed reads your transactions, or when the period has no transactions.

1. Wait until **Transactions** shows a number.
2. If the number is 0, select a different period in **Range**.

### If each period has 0 transactions

WalletFeed cannot read the transactions of your Wallet accounts.

If **Settings** › **Wallet** in WalletFeed shows **Choose Accounts**, do these steps:

1. Tap **Choose Accounts**.

   The Wallet access screen opens.

2. Select the accounts that WalletFeed can read.
3. Tap **Share**.

If **Settings** › **Wallet** shows **Open Settings**, do these steps:

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select the accounts that WalletFeed can read.
4. Open WalletFeed.

For all the steps, refer to [Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/).

### If the file has sample transactions

When **Sample Data** is on, WalletFeed shows two months of sample transactions, and the file has only sample transactions. It does not have your Wallet transactions.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings**.
2. In the **Data** section, set **Sample Data** to off.
3. Export the file again.

### If the file does not have a new transaction

The file does not change after you export it.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings**.
2. Tap **Export CSV**.
3. Select the period in **Range**.
4. Tap **Export**.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/get-started/ -->
# First steps with WalletFeed

WalletFeed shows the transactions from your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings accounts on your iPhone. To start, you open WalletFeed and select the Wallet accounts that it can read.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- An Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account in Wallet on the iPhone.
- WalletFeed on the iPhone. You can get WalletFeed from the App Store.

If you do not have one of these accounts, refer to [Use WalletFeed with sample transactions](#use-walletfeed-with-sample-transactions).

## Open WalletFeed for the first time

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.

   The **Welcome to WalletFeed** screen opens. It tells you about **Ask Spending**, **Destinations**, **On-Device Privacy** and **Background Sync**.

   ![The Welcome to WalletFeed screen with the Continue button at the bottom.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/get-started/walletfeed-welcome.webp)

   If Apple Intelligence is not available on your iPhone, the first item is **Spending and Search**.

2. Tap **Continue**.

   **Transactions** opens, and iOS shows a message with the buttons **Don't Allow** and **Select Accounts**.

## Select the Wallet accounts for WalletFeed

After you share accounts or tap **Don't Allow**, iOS does not show this message again. Then you can change the accounts that you share only in the Settings app.

1. Tap **Select Accounts**.

   The list of Wallet accounts opens.

2. Select each account for WalletFeed, for example your Apple Card.

   You can also select a start date for each account. WalletFeed can read only the transactions that occur on or after that date.

3. Tap the **Share with** button.

   **Transactions** shows the transactions from the accounts that you selected.

If you tap **Don't Allow**, **Transactions** shows **Wallet Access Off**. To let WalletFeed read Wallet after that, refer to [If Transactions shows "Wallet Access Off"](#if-transactions-shows-wallet-access-off).

If you tap **Cancel** in the list of Wallet accounts, **Transactions** shows **No Cards**. To select the accounts again, refer to [If Transactions shows "No Cards"](#if-transactions-shows-no-cards).

> **Note:** WalletFeed reads your transactions from Wallet on your iPhone. It does not keep the transactions. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers.

## See your transactions

**Transactions** shows your transactions below the name of each month. The newest transactions are at the top.
