![The Transactions screen with the October transactions and the tabs at the bottom of the screen.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/get-started/walletfeed-transactions.webp)

Each row shows the merchant and the amount. The day is below the amount. Below the merchant, a row can also show "Pending". If a transaction is not from the account that has the most transactions, its row also shows the account name, for example Apple Cash.

At the end of the list, WalletFeed shows the date of the first transaction that it can read. To see transactions from before that date, refer to [Change the accounts that you share](/docs/wallet-accounts/#change-the-accounts-that-you-share).

## Use the other tabs

The tabs and the search button at the bottom of the screen open the other parts of WalletFeed:

- The **Spending** tab shows the total of your purchases this month, for each day, category and merchant. Refer to [Spending](/docs/spending/).
- The **Destinations** tab shows where WalletFeed sends your transactions, for example to a budget app or a spreadsheet. Refer to [Destinations](/docs/destinations/).
- The search button opens **Search**, which finds the transactions that have the merchant or the amount that you type. Refer to [Search](/docs/search/).

You can use Spending, [Ask Spending](/docs/ask-spending/), Search, [Recurring Charges](/docs/recurring-charges/), the [Spending widget](/docs/spending-widget/) and [CSV export](/docs/export-csv/) without [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/). To send transactions to a destination, you must have WalletFeed Pro. WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.

## Use WalletFeed with sample transactions

If you do not have an Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account, you can use WalletFeed with sample transactions. WalletFeed shows the **Sample Data** switch only if you have no destinations or if the switch is on.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Data** section, set the **Sample Data** switch to on.
3. Tap **Done**.

   **Transactions** shows two months of sample transactions. It does not show the transactions from your Wallet.

When you set the **Sample Data** switch to off, WalletFeed shows the transactions from your Wallet again.

## Correct problems with Wallet accounts

### If Transactions shows "Wallet Access Off"

WalletFeed cannot read your Wallet accounts. This problem occurs after you tap **Don't Allow**, or after you remove the Wallet access for WalletFeed in the Settings app.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select the accounts that WalletFeed can read.
4. Open WalletFeed again.

   **Transactions** shows your transactions.

### If Transactions shows "No Cards"

You did not share Wallet accounts with WalletFeed, and you did not tap **Don't Allow**. This problem occurs after you tap **Cancel** in the list of Wallet accounts.

1. In **Transactions**, tap **Choose Accounts**.
2. Do the steps in [Select the Wallet accounts for WalletFeed](#select-the-wallet-accounts-for-walletfeed).

### If Transactions shows "No Transactions"

WalletFeed can read Wallet, but it finds no transactions in the accounts that you selected.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select more Wallet accounts for WalletFeed.
4. Open WalletFeed again.

### If Transactions shows "Wallet Unavailable"

On this iPhone, WalletFeed cannot read transactions from Wallet. Below **Wallet Unavailable**, WalletFeed shows "This iPhone can't share Wallet data." To use WalletFeed without Wallet data, refer to [Use WalletFeed with sample transactions](#use-walletfeed-with-sample-transactions).

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/ -->
# WalletFeed User Guide

How to use each part of WalletFeed on your iPhone.

- [First steps with WalletFeed](https://walletfeed.app/docs/get-started/index.md): Open WalletFeed on your iPhone for the first time and select the Wallet accounts that it can read. Then see your Apple Card transactions.
- [Select the Wallet accounts that WalletFeed reads](https://walletfeed.app/docs/wallet-accounts/index.md): Share your Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account with WalletFeed on your iPhone. Change the accounts and their start dates in the Settings app.
- [Transactions](https://walletfeed.app/docs/transactions/index.md): See your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions by month in WalletFeed on your iPhone, with pending transactions and refunds.
- [Spending](https://walletfeed.app/docs/spending/index.md): Spending in WalletFeed shows the total of your Apple Card and Apple Cash purchases this month on your iPhone, by day, category and merchant.
- [Ask Spending with Apple Intelligence](https://walletfeed.app/docs/ask-spending/index.md): Type a question about your Apple Card spending on iPhone, for example "Dining this month vs last". WalletFeed shows a chart, a list and a summary.
- [Search](https://walletfeed.app/docs/search/index.md): Find your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions with Search in WalletFeed. Type a merchant, a category or an amount, or use Apple Intelligence.
- [Recurring Charges and alerts](https://walletfeed.app/docs/recurring-charges/index.md): WalletFeed finds the recurring charges on your Apple Card, such as subscriptions, and can send a notification when a new one starts or a price changes.
- [Spending widget](https://walletfeed.app/docs/spending-widget/index.md): Put the WalletFeed Spending widget on your iPhone Home Screen or Lock Screen. It shows this month's total and last month's total to the same day and time.
- [Export a CSV file](https://walletfeed.app/docs/export-csv/index.md): Export your Apple Card transactions to a CSV file on your iPhone with Export CSV in WalletFeed. You select a period, then save or send the file.
- [Siri and Shortcuts](https://walletfeed.app/docs/siri-and-shortcuts/index.md): Use Siri and the Shortcuts app with WalletFeed on your iPhone to open Spending, find transactions and send Apple Card transactions to destinations.
- [WalletFeed Pro](https://walletfeed.app/docs/walletfeed-pro/index.md): WalletFeed Pro lets WalletFeed send your Apple Card transactions to destinations. This page gives the prices and tells you how to change or cancel a plan.
- [Destinations](https://walletfeed.app/docs/destinations/index.md): Send your Apple Card transactions from your iPhone to an app, a spreadsheet or a file with WalletFeed. Add, test, change or remove a destination.
- [Choose what a destination receives](https://walletfeed.app/docs/choose-what-to-send/index.md): Select which of your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions a WalletFeed destination receives, by account, category, merchant or amount.
- [Background Sync](https://walletfeed.app/docs/background-sync/index.md): Send your Apple Card transactions to your destinations while WalletFeed is closed, with Background Sync and automations in Shortcuts on your iPhone.
- [Send previous transactions](https://walletfeed.app/docs/send-history/index.md): Send your previous Apple Card transactions to a WalletFeed destination with Send History, and set the start date of new destinations with Initial History.
- [Privacy and security](https://walletfeed.app/docs/privacy-and-security/index.md): WalletFeed privacy and security on iPhone: the data that WalletFeed keeps, the data that it sends, and how to lock the app with Face ID.
- [Troubleshooting](https://walletfeed.app/docs/troubleshooting/index.md): Correct problems with WalletFeed: missing cards, Ask Spending, Authentication failed, a sync that stops, and copies of transactions.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/privacy-and-security/ -->
# Privacy and security

WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. It reads your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from Wallet on your iPhone. It sends them directly from your iPhone to the [destinations](/docs/destinations/) that you add. For the full text, refer to the [WalletFeed privacy policy](/privacy/).

## Data that WalletFeed keeps

WalletFeed keeps your transactions in memory only while it uses them. It does not save a copy of them.

WalletFeed keeps some settings and status data on your iPhone. For example, it keeps these items:

- Your settings, and the settings of each destination, such as its name and [filter](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).
- The keys, webhook addresses and sign-ins of your destinations. They stay in the Keychain on your iPhone, and they do not go to iCloud Keychain.
- The sync status of each destination, without transaction data. For example, the time of the last sync and the number of changes that WalletFeed sent.
- Two totals for the [Spending widget](/docs/spending-widget/): this month, and the same days of last month. iOS also keeps the data that the widget shows.

## Data that WalletFeed sends

WalletFeed sends your transactions only to the services, folders and apps that you select:

- A service that you connect, such as Lunch Money or Notion, receives the transactions over HTTPS directly from your iPhone.
- A Files destination saves the transactions in a folder that you select, for example a folder in iCloud Drive.
- When you [export a CSV file](/docs/export-csv/), the file goes only to the app that you select in the share sheet.
- When a [shortcut](/docs/siri-and-shortcuts/) or Siri runs the **Get Recent Card Transactions** action, that shortcut or Siri receives your transactions.

If you tell Siri to show Spending or to search WalletFeed, Siri opens WalletFeed. Siri receives none of your transactions.

Before a new destination receives transactions, WalletFeed shows a message, for example "Send Transactions to Lunch Money?". The message tells you which data the destination receives, from which accounts and from which date. For a service, it also tells you "It keeps what it receives." WalletFeed sends nothing until you tap **Send**, or **Save** for a Files destination. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes the destination.

After a service receives your data, the terms and privacy policy of that service are applicable to it. If you delete a destination, WalletFeed does not send more data to it. But WalletFeed cannot delete the data that it sent before.

## Apple Intelligence

If Apple Intelligence is available on your iPhone, WalletFeed uses it for these features:

- The [Monthly Summary](/docs/spending/), and the summary of each answer in [Ask Spending](/docs/ask-spending/).
- Your searches, your questions in Ask Spending, and the rules that you write for a destination filter.
- The names of your [recurring charges](/docs/recurring-charges/).

Apple Intelligence operates on your iPhone, and WalletFeed sends nothing to a server for these features. To read a search, a question or a rule, Apple Intelligence gets only the words that you type or speak. To give names to recurring charges, it gets only the merchant names.

WalletFeed calculates all the charts, totals and lists. Apple Intelligence can write an incorrect number in a summary. If a summary and the numbers on the screen are different, use the numbers on the screen.

WalletFeed does not keep the text that Apple Intelligence writes. It keeps only the filter that a rule makes.

## Stop the Apple Intelligence summaries

**Summarize Spending** shows in **Settings** only if Apple Intelligence is available on your iPhone.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In **Privacy & Security**, set the **Summarize Spending** switch to off.

   ![WalletFeed Settings, with Require Face ID, Summarize Spending and Privacy in the Privacy & Security section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/privacy-and-security/walletfeed-settings-2.webp)

4. Tap **Done**.

Apple Intelligence then does not write the Monthly Summary or the summary of each answer. It continues to read the questions that you send in Ask Spending.

## Lock WalletFeed with Face ID

You can lock WalletFeed with Face ID, Touch ID or your passcode. The name of the switch changes with the type of iPhone:

- **Require Face ID**, on an iPhone with Face ID.
- **Require Touch ID**, on an iPhone with Touch ID.
- **Require Passcode**, on an iPhone without Face ID or Touch ID.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In **Privacy & Security**, set the **Require Face ID** switch to on.

   ![WalletFeed Settings, with the Require Face ID switch in the Privacy & Security section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/privacy-and-security/walletfeed-settings-2.webp)

4. Use Face ID, Touch ID or your passcode.

   If Face ID does not identify you, the switch stays off.

5. Tap **Done**.

WalletFeed locks each time that you go away from it. When you open WalletFeed again, it starts Face ID one time. If Face ID does not identify you, tap **Unlock** to try again.

To open WalletFeed without Face ID again, set the **Require Face ID** switch to off.

## Screen protection

WalletFeed also keeps your transactions out of view in these conditions:

- When you go away from WalletFeed, it puts a cover on its screen. Thus the app switcher does not show your transactions.
- While you record the screen of your iPhone, or show it on a different screen, WalletFeed does not show your transactions or amounts.
- While your iPhone is locked, iOS can show the Spending widget without its amounts.

## Notifications

If you set the **Recurring Charge Alerts** switch to on, WalletFeed finds new and changed recurring charges on your iPhone. Each notification shows the name and the amounts of the charge. Notification Center keeps the notification until you clear it.

A **Remind If Sync Stops** notification contains no transaction data.

## Analytics and purchases

WalletFeed has no analytics, no advertisements and no third-party SDKs. It does not monitor what you do in other apps or on websites.

If you share analytics with app developers in the Settings app, Apple can share crash reports with the developer.

Purchases of [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/) go through Apple. WalletFeed does not see your payment information.

## Delete a destination

When you delete a destination, WalletFeed erases its settings, its key and its sync status from your iPhone.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Delete**.

   ![The screen of a Lunch Money destination, with Delete at the bottom.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/privacy-and-security/walletfeed-destination-detail.webp)

4. In the message, tap **Delete** again.

The message tells you "Transactions already sent stay at the destination." WalletFeed cannot delete the data that the destination received.

## Remove all destinations

**Remove All Destinations** shows in **Settings** only if you have a destination.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In **Data**, tap **Remove All Destinations**.

   ![WalletFeed Settings, with Export CSV and Remove All Destinations in the Data section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/privacy-and-security/walletfeed-settings-3.webp)

4. Tap **Remove All**.

WalletFeed erases the keys and the sync status of all your destinations from your iPhone. The transactions that WalletFeed sent stay at each destination.

## Change the Wallet accounts that WalletFeed reads

To remove an account from WalletFeed, deselect it in the Settings app. Refer to [Change the accounts that you share](/docs/wallet-accounts/#change-the-accounts-that-you-share).

If WalletFeed cannot read a Wallet account, it erases the totals of the Spending widget the next time that it runs.

## Data after you delete WalletFeed

When you delete WalletFeed, iOS removes its settings and its sync status. Keychain items can stay on your iPhone after you delete the app. If you install WalletFeed again, it erases them when it opens for the first time.

## Read the privacy statement in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In **Privacy & Security**, tap **Privacy**.

   ![The Privacy screen in WalletFeed, with the Wallet data and Data on your iPhone sections.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/privacy-and-security/walletfeed-privacy.webp)

In the **About** section of **Settings**, **Privacy Policy** opens the [privacy policy](/privacy/) on this website.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/recurring-charges/ -->
# Recurring Charges and alerts

WalletFeed finds the recurring charges on your Apple Card, such as subscriptions and monthly bills, and shows them on the [Spending](/docs/spending/) screen. Recurring Charge Alerts can send you a notification when a new recurring charge starts or a price changes.

[WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/) is not necessary for Recurring Charges or for Recurring Charge Alerts.

## Find your recurring charges

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Spending**.
3. Scroll down to **Recurring Charges**.

   ![The Recurring Charges section of the Spending screen, with PG&E, Netflix and Spotify and the price of each charge.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/recurring-charges/walletfeed-recurring.webp)

Each row shows these items:

- An icon for the category of the charge.
- The name of the charge.
- The word **Monthly** or **Weekly**. With Apple Intelligence, the type of service comes first, for example **Streaming · Monthly**.
- The price of the last charge.

The first charge in the list has the largest total for one month. For a weekly charge, this total is approximately 4.3 times the weekly price.

If WalletFeed finds no recurring charges, the **Recurring Charges** section does not show.

## Rules for a recurring charge

WalletFeed reads your purchases from this month and from the two months before it. It puts the charges from one merchant in **Recurring Charges** when they agree with these rules:

- All the charges have the same merchant name. For example, “Netflix.com” and “NETFLIX.COM” are the same merchant.
- The difference between the price of each charge and the price of the last charge is 15% or less.
- For **Monthly**, there is a minimum of two charges. Each charge is 26 to 35 days after the charge before it.
- For **Weekly**, there is a minimum of three charges. Each charge is 6 to 8 days after the charge before it.

For example, if a month between two charges has no charge from the merchant, the merchant does not show in the list.

These transactions are not in **Recurring Charges**:

- Refunds, transfers, bill payments and rejected transactions.
- Apple Card Monthly Installments. **Spending** shows them in the **Monthly Installments** section.
- Charges that occur each year. WalletFeed finds only monthly and weekly charges.

## Names from Apple Intelligence

Wallet can show a merchant name such as “NETFLIX.COM 866-579”. With Apple Intelligence, WalletFeed shows a short name, such as Netflix. It can also show a type of service, such as Streaming. Below the list, WalletFeed then shows **Apple Intelligence suggested these names.**

WalletFeed uses a name only if the first word of the name is in the merchant name from Wallet. It gets names for the first 12 charges in the list only. If a charge has no name from Apple Intelligence, the row shows the merchant name from Wallet.

For these names, you must have an iPhone that is compatible with Apple Intelligence, and Apple Intelligence must be on.

## Start Recurring Charge Alerts

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In **Notifications**, set the **Recurring Charge Alerts** switch to on.

   ![WalletFeed Settings with the Recurring Charge Alerts switch in the Notifications section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/recurring-charges/walletfeed-settings.webp)

4. If iOS shows a message about notifications, let WalletFeed send them.

   If you do not let WalletFeed send notifications, the switch stays off.

5. Tap **Done**.

When you set the switch to on, WalletFeed sends no notifications for the charges that are in Wallet at that time. You get notifications only for new charges.

## Notifications for recurring charges

WalletFeed sends a notification for these changes:

| Change | Title of the notification | Text of the notification |
|---|---|---|
| A charge becomes a recurring charge | “Netflix repeats monthly” or “Netflix repeats weekly” | “$15.49 each month” or “$15.49 each week” |
| The price of a recurring charge increases | “Netflix costs more” | “$17.99, up from $15.49” |
| The price of a recurring charge decreases | “Netflix costs less” | “$15.49, down from $17.99” |

WalletFeed sends a notification about a price change only in these conditions:

- The charges from the merchant were in **Recurring Charges** before the new charge.
- The new charge comes at the usual time. This is 26 to 35 days after the charge before it, or 6 to 8 days for a weekly charge.
- The new price is more than 2% different from the price before it.

After a price change of more than 15%, the charge can go out of **Recurring Charges**. It comes back when all the charges in the three months have the new price.

WalletFeed sends a notification only for a charge from the last 7 days, and only one notification for each charge. The notification uses the name from Apple Intelligence if it is available. If not, it uses the merchant name from Wallet.

WalletFeed examines your transactions when you open it. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. WalletFeed Pro and **Background Sync** are not necessary for this.

## Stop Recurring Charge Alerts

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In **Notifications**, set the **Recurring Charge Alerts** switch to off.
3. Tap **Done**.

## Privacy

WalletFeed finds your recurring charges on your iPhone. It reads your transactions from Wallet each time, and it does not keep a copy.

To give names to the charges, Apple Intelligence gets only the merchant names. It runs on your iPhone, and WalletFeed sends nothing to a server.

For Recurring Charge Alerts, WalletFeed keeps only the IDs of the transactions that it sent a notification for. It keeps no prices and no merchant names.

A notification shows the name of the charge and its prices. Notification Center keeps the notification until you remove it. When notification previews are off, iOS does not show the text on the Lock Screen.

For more information, refer to the [WalletFeed privacy policy](/privacy/).

## If something goes wrong

### If a new subscription is not in Recurring Charges

WalletFeed shows a monthly charge only after its second charge, and a weekly charge only after its third charge.

After the next charge from the merchant, open **Spending** again. If the list does not show the charge after that, refer to [Rules for a recurring charge](#rules-for-a-recurring-charge).

### If the switch does not stay on

iOS does not let WalletFeed send notifications.

1. In the Settings app on your iPhone, let WalletFeed send notifications.
2. In WalletFeed, set the **Recurring Charge Alerts** switch to on again.

### If no notification comes

WalletFeed sends a notification only for a new recurring charge or a price change from the last 7 days.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. Make sure that the **Recurring Charge Alerts** switch is on.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/search/ -->
# Search

Search in WalletFeed finds your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions. You type a part of a merchant name, a description, a category or an amount. Search then shows each transaction that has this text. With Apple Intelligence, Search can also read your text, for example `Dining over $50 last month`, and change it into filters. You can use Search without [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/).

Search uses the transactions of the [Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/) that you share with WalletFeed. When you open Search, WalletFeed reads these transactions on your iPhone. It does not keep a copy of them.

## Find a transaction

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap the search button at the bottom of the screen.

   ![The Transactions screen, with the tab bar and the search button at the bottom of the screen.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/search/walletfeed-transactions.webp)

   Search shows the search field and the keyboard.

3. Type a part of a merchant name, a category or an amount, for example `Uber`, `Dining` or `23.40`.

   Search shows the results while you type.

Search finds the same transactions for `uber`, `Uber` and `UBER`. The results show in a section for each month, as in [Transactions](/docs/transactions/).

To type different text, tap the clear button in the search field. To close Search, tap the close button (X). WalletFeed then shows the last tab that you used.

## Find transactions in a category

When the search field is empty, Search shows **Categories**. This list has the categories of your transactions.

1. Tap the search button.
2. In **Categories**, tap a category, for example **Groceries**.

   Search puts the name of the category in the search field and shows the results.

## Find transactions with Apple Intelligence

Search with Apple Intelligence reads your text and changes it into filters. For example, it changes `Dining over $50 last month` into **Dining · Over $50.00 · Last month**. Search with Apple Intelligence is available only if your iPhone can use Apple Intelligence and Apple Intelligence is on. On these iPhones, the empty search field shows **Dining over $50 last month** as an example.

1. Tap the search button.
2. Type the category, merchant, amount or period to find, for example `Dining over $50 last month`.

   While you type, Search shows the transactions that have the text. If no transaction has the text, Search shows **Tap Search to use Apple Intelligence.**

3. Tap **Search** on the keyboard.

   While Apple Intelligence reads the text, the Apple Intelligence icon and a progress indicator show at the top of the list.

   ![The Search screen with the filters Groceries, Over $50.00 and Last 30 days, and a row with 4 transactions and a total of $277.57.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/search/walletfeed-search.webp)

At the top of the results, Search shows the filters that Apple Intelligence found in your text, for example **Groceries · Over $50.00 · Last 30 days**. Below the filters, a row shows the number of transactions and their total. If no transaction agrees with the filters, the row shows **0 transactions** and $0.00.

Apple Intelligence can find these filters in your text:

- One or more categories, for example **Dining** or **Groceries**. Other text can also give a category. For example, `restaurants` gives **Dining**, and `gas` gives **Fuel**.
- A merchant, for example `Uber`. WalletFeed uses the merchant only if it is in your text.
- Only purchases (**Purchases**), or only money that you received (**Money in**).
- An amount, with `over` or `under`, for example `over $50`. WalletFeed uses the amount only if it is in your text.
- One period: **Last 7 days**, **Last 30 days**, **This month** or **Last month**.

WalletFeed also finds a merchant when your text is not the same as the name. For example, `Ubers` finds Uber, and `trader joes` finds Trader Joe's.

WalletFeed calculates the number of transactions and the total. Apple Intelligence does not calculate them.

For **Money in**, the total is the money that you received. For all other filters, WalletFeed adds the amounts of your purchases. Refunds decrease the total. Payments and transfers do not change it.

If Apple Intelligence cannot read your text, Search shows **Couldn't read this search. Showing text matches.** The list then shows the transactions that have your text.

When you change the text, WalletFeed removes the filters. To use Apple Intelligence again, tap **Search** on the keyboard.

> **Note:** Apple Intelligence reads your text on your iPhone. It receives only the text that you type. It does not receive your transactions.

## Open Search with Siri

1. Tell Siri "Search WalletFeed" or "Find a transaction in WalletFeed".
2. When Siri shows **What are you looking for?**, tell Siri the transactions to find, for example "dining over $50 last month".

   Search opens with your text in the search field. If Search with Apple Intelligence is available, Apple Intelligence then reads the text.

Siri does not receive your transactions or the total. They show only in WalletFeed.

In the Shortcuts app, the same action has the name **Search Transactions**. For more information, refer to [Siri and Shortcuts](/docs/siri-and-shortcuts/).

## If there is a problem

### If Search shows **No Cards**

You did not tap **Share** or **Don't Share** on the Wallet access screen.

1. Tap **Choose Accounts**.

   The Wallet access screen opens.

2. Make sure that the switch for each account to share is on.

   ![The Share Wallet Data screen, with the switches for Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings on.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/search/walletfeed-wallet-access.webp)

3. Tap **Share**.

### If Search shows **Wallet Access Off**

You tapped **Don't Share**, or you stopped Wallet access for WalletFeed in the Settings app. iOS shows the Wallet access screen only one time.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select the accounts to share with WalletFeed.
4. Open WalletFeed.

### If Search shows **No Results for “…”**

No transaction has your text in its merchant name, description, category or amount.

1. Make sure that the text is correct.
2. Type shorter text, for example only the first part of the merchant name.
3. If Search shows **Tap Search to use Apple Intelligence.**, tap **Search** on the keyboard.

### If Apple Intelligence does not read your text

Apple Intelligence reads text that has 2 to 200 characters. If the empty search field shows **Transactions**, Search with Apple Intelligence is not available on this iPhone.

1. Make sure that your iPhone can use Apple Intelligence.
2. Make sure that Apple Intelligence is on.
3. Make sure that the text has 2 to 200 characters.
4. Tap **Search** on the keyboard.

### If Search shows **Couldn't read this search. Showing text matches.**

Apple Intelligence did not find filters in your text that WalletFeed can use. Search then shows the transactions that have your text.

1. Type shorter text that has a category, a merchant, an amount or a period, for example `groceries this month`.
2. Tap **Search** on the keyboard.

### If a transaction is not in the results

Search finds only the transactions of the Wallet accounts that you share with WalletFeed. Wallet shares the transactions of each account from a start date that you selected.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Change the accounts or the start dates that you share.
4. Open WalletFeed.
5. Type your text in the search field again.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/send-history/ -->
# Send previous transactions

A WalletFeed [destination](/docs/destinations/) can also receive your previous Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions. In WalletFeed, **Initial History** sets the start date of each new destination, and **Send History** sends previous transactions to one of your destinations.

Destinations and **Send History** are part of [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/). WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase. If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, **Send History** opens the **WalletFeed Pro** screen.

## Set the start date for new destinations

When you add a destination, it receives your transactions from the date that **Initial History** sets. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. If you change **Initial History**, only the destinations that you add after the change use the new period. WalletFeed shows the **Sync** section only if you have WalletFeed Pro.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Sync** section, tap **Initial History**.

   ![The WalletFeed Settings screen, where Initial History shows All in the Sync section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/send-history/walletfeed-settings.webp)

3. Select a period.
4. Tap **Done**.

These are the periods of **Initial History**:

| Period | A new destination receives |
| --- | --- |
| **Today** | The transactions from the day that you add the destination. |
| **30 Days** | The transactions from the last 30 days. |
| **90 Days** | The transactions from the last 90 days. |
| **1 Year** | The transactions from the last 12 months. |
| **All** | All the transactions that WalletFeed can read. |

If **Send** is **Each Transaction** for Zapier, Make or Linear, each transaction starts a Zap, uses a Make credit or becomes an issue. Thus, the start date is a maximum of 30 days before you add the destination. To send previous transactions to it, use **Send History**. If **Send** is **Monthly**, there is no 30-day limit, and the start date is the first day of a month.

WalletFeed can read only the Wallet accounts and the period that you select in iOS. You can change them in the Settings app, in **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.

## Send to a new destination

Before a new destination receives transactions, WalletFeed shows a message. The message tells you the data that the destination receives, the accounts and the start date.

1. To add the destination, do the steps in [Add a destination](/docs/destinations/#add-a-destination).
2. Read the message, for example **Send Transactions to Lunch Money?**

   If **Initial History** is **All**, the message shows "including earlier ones" and no date. If **Send** is **Each Transaction** for Zapier, Make or Linear, the message shows the start date.

   For a CSV, OFX or QIF file, the title of the message is **Save Transactions to Files?**, and the button is **Save**.

3. Tap **Send** or **Save**.

WalletFeed then sends your transactions to the destination. It sends the newest transactions first.

If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes the new destination and does not send transactions to it.

## Send previous transactions to a destination

You can send the transactions of a period to a destination at any time, for example after you change its [filter](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations** at the bottom of the screen.
2. Tap the destination.

   ![The Destinations tab with Lunch Money, Budget 2026, Monthly CSV and n8n.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/send-history/walletfeed-destinations.webp)

3. Tap **Send History**.

   ![The Lunch Money destination screen, with Send History below Filter.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/send-history/walletfeed-destination-detail.webp)

4. Select **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.
5. If WalletFeed shows a message, for example **Send History to Zapier?**, tap **Send**.

   This message shows only for Zapier, Make and Linear. It tells you the result in the service, for example:

   - "Each month runs your Zap once."
   - "Each transaction runs your scenario."
   - "Each month becomes one issue."

WalletFeed then starts to send the history. Above **Send History**, the destination screen shows **Sending History** and a progress bar.

WalletFeed sends all the transactions of the period, and it starts with the newest transactions. It uses the filter of the destination and does not send declined transactions.

The first day of the period also becomes the start date of the destination. After that, WalletFeed sends changes only for transactions from that date. If **Send** is **Monthly** for Zapier, Make or Linear, the period starts on the first day of a month.

If a new transaction occurs while WalletFeed sends the history, WalletFeed sends the new transaction first.

Webhook, Zapier, Make, Amazon SQS, Kinesis Data Streams and EventBridge destinations receive each transaction again. If **Send** is **Monthly**, Zapier and Make receive each month again. Other destinations keep one copy of each transaction.

> **Note:** On the Linear Free plan, a workspace can have a maximum of 250 issues.

## Monitor the history

While WalletFeed sends the history, the destination screen shows **Sending History** above **Send History**. It also shows numbers and a month, for example "2,340 of 5,120 · back to March 2023":

- The first number is the number of transactions that WalletFeed sent. This number also includes the transactions that the destination had and the transactions that the filter does not include.
- The second number is the number of transactions in the period.
- The month tells you that WalletFeed sent all the transactions after a date in that month.

The progress bar shows less than 100% until WalletFeed completes the history. In **Destinations**, the row of the destination shows "Sending history · 46%". When WalletFeed waits or cannot continue the history, the row shows "History paused · 46%".

The destination screen shows one of these items above **Send History**:

| Item | Information |
| --- | --- |
| **Sending History** and numbers | WalletFeed sends the history. |
| "Paused" | WalletFeed does not send the history at this time. For example, **Enabled** is off, or you do not have WalletFeed Pro. |
| "Too many requests.", "Can't connect." or "Server error (502).", then "Trying again in 10 min." | The service has a problem or a limit, or WalletFeed cannot connect to it. WalletFeed tries again at the time that the message shows. |
| An orange symbol, a message and **Try Again** | WalletFeed cannot continue until you correct a problem. For the steps, refer to [Correct a problem with the history](#correct-a-problem-with-the-history). |
| **History** with "All sent" | WalletFeed sent all the transactions. |
| **History** with "Sent from March 3, 2023" | WalletFeed sent all the transactions from that date. |
| **History** with "Stopped" | You tapped **Stop Sending**. |

## History while WalletFeed is closed

While WalletFeed is open, it sends the history. When you go to a different app, iOS can let WalletFeed continue. This can occur after you select a period in **Send History**, or after you tap **Send** for a new destination.

iOS then shows a Live Activity, for example "Sending history to Lunch Money" with "2,340 of 5,120". In the Live Activity, **Cancel** does not stop the history. **Cancel** stops WalletFeed only until the next time that WalletFeed can send. If you close WalletFeed in the app switcher, the result is the same. To stop the history, do the steps in [Stop the history](#stop-the-history).

iOS can also let WalletFeed send the history while your iPhone charges and you do not use it. For short periods, iOS can start WalletFeed to send the history.

WalletFeed sends the history to each service at a speed that the service accepts. Thus, if a slow service receives a large history, the history can continue for some days.

## Stop the history

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap **Send History**.
3. Tap **Stop Sending**.

   **History** shows "Stopped".

WalletFeed shows **Stop Sending** only until it completes the history. The destination keeps the transactions that it received. WalletFeed continues to send new transactions to the destination.

To send the history again, select a period in **Send History**.

## Send previous transactions after a filter change

A change to the filter of a destination changes only the transactions that WalletFeed sends after the change.

If the new filter includes more transactions, WalletFeed does not send the previous transactions that the new filter adds. If the new filter does not include some transactions, the destination keeps the transactions that it received before the change.

To send the previous transactions with the new filter, do the steps in [Send previous transactions to a destination](#send-previous-transactions-to-a-destination).

## Correct a problem with the history

### If the history shows "Authentication failed"

The service did not accept the key, token or sign-in of the destination, or the permissions of the key changed.

1. If the message includes "Replace the key.", make a new key in the service. For the steps, refer to the [guide for the destination type](/guides/).
2. In WalletFeed, replace the key, sign in again or correct the connection. For the steps, refer to [Replace a key or sign in again](/docs/destinations/#replace-a-key-or-sign-in-again).
3. On the destination screen, tap **Try Again**.

WalletFeed also tries again after approximately 1 hour, and then after longer periods, to a maximum of 24 hours. When a new transaction goes to the destination correctly, the history also continues.

### If the history shows "Can't open the folder. Choose it again."

WalletFeed cannot open the folder of the CSV, OFX or QIF file.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap **Change Folder**.
3. Select the folder.

   The history starts again, and WalletFeed writes the transactions to that folder.

### If the history shows "Check the destination, then try again."

The service rejected the transactions. The message starts with the cause, for example "Rejected (HTTP 404)".

These are some problems that can stop the history:

- On the Airtable Free plan, a base can have a maximum of 1,000 records.
- If a Make scenario is not active, Make keeps the transactions in a queue. On the Make Free plan, the queue can have a maximum of 50 items.
- If a Zap is off, Zapier rejects the transactions. Zapier can start to reject them some hours after you set the Zap to off.

1. Correct the problem in the service.
2. In WalletFeed, tap the destination in **Destinations**.
3. Tap **Try Again**.

WalletFeed also tries again after approximately 1 hour, and then after longer periods, to a maximum of 24 hours.

### If the history shows "Paused"

WalletFeed does not send the history at this time.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Make sure that **Enabled** is on.
3. Make sure that you have WalletFeed Pro. In **Settings**, the **Subscription** section shows your plan.
4. Keep WalletFeed open.

   When WalletFeed continues the history, numbers replace "Paused".

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/siri-and-shortcuts/ -->
# Siri and Shortcuts

You can use Siri and the Shortcuts app with WalletFeed on your iPhone. Siri can open **Spending** or **Search** in WalletFeed. The WalletFeed actions in Shortcuts can send your Apple Card transactions to your [destinations](/docs/destinations/), or give them to a shortcut.

You can use **Show Spending** and **Search Transactions** without WalletFeed Pro. For the other actions and the **Sync Transactions** control, you must have [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/). WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.

## WalletFeed actions

WalletFeed gives these actions to Siri and the Shortcuts app:

| Action | Result | WalletFeed Pro |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Show Spending** | Opens **Spending** in WalletFeed. | Not necessary |
| **Search Transactions** | Opens **Search** with the transactions that you tell Siri to find. | Not necessary |
| **Sync Transactions** | Sends new and changed transactions to your destinations. WalletFeed does not open. | Necessary |
| **Sync New Purchase** | Sends your last purchase after Wallet records it. WalletFeed does not open. This action is for a **Transaction** automation. | Necessary |
| **Get Recent Card Transactions** | Gives your transactions from the last 7 days to the shortcut. You can change the number of days. | Necessary |

## Use Siri with WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, start Siri.
2. Tell Siri one of the instructions in the table that follows.

| Tell Siri | Result |
| --- | --- |
| "Show my spending in WalletFeed" or "Open my spending in WalletFeed" | WalletFeed opens **Spending**. |
| "Search WalletFeed" or "Find a transaction in WalletFeed" | You hear "What are you looking for?" You tell Siri the transactions to find. Then WalletFeed opens **Search**. |
| "Sync WalletFeed" or "Send my card transactions with WalletFeed" | WalletFeed sends new and changed transactions to your destinations. |
| "Get card transactions from WalletFeed" | Siri receives your transactions from the last 7 days. |

When you tell Siri "Sync WalletFeed", WalletFeed does not open. After WalletFeed sends the transactions, Siri gives a short message, for example "Changes sent: 3." Refer to [Messages from the sync actions](#messages-from-the-sync-actions).

## Find transactions with Siri

1. On your iPhone, start Siri.
2. Tell Siri "Search WalletFeed".

   You hear "What are you looking for?"

3. Tell Siri the transactions to find, for example "dining over $50 last month".

   **Search** opens in WalletFeed, with your instruction in the search field.

   ![The Search screen with the filters Groceries, Over $50.00 and Last 30 days, and 4 transactions with a total of $277.57.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/siri-and-shortcuts/walletfeed-search.webp)

With Apple Intelligence, WalletFeed reads your instruction on your iPhone. Then **Search** shows the transactions and their total. Search with Apple Intelligence is available only on an iPhone that can use Apple Intelligence, with Apple Intelligence on.

Without Apple Intelligence, **Search** shows the results that you get when you type the same instruction in the search field. For more information, refer to [Search](/docs/search/).

## The Sync control

WalletFeed has a control with the name **Sync Transactions**. You can add it to Control Center, the Lock Screen or the Action button. The control shows **Sync**.

When you use the control, WalletFeed opens. With WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed then sends new and changed transactions to your destinations. While WalletFeed is open, your destinations receive changes in seconds.

## Use your transactions in a shortcut

**Get Recent Card Transactions** gives your transactions to the next action in a shortcut. For example, a shortcut can send them to Notes or Mail.

1. On your iPhone, open the Shortcuts app.
2. Tap **•••** on your shortcut.
3. Tap **Search Actions**.
4. Type WalletFeed in the search field.
5. Tap **Get Recent Card Transactions**.

   The action shows "Get card transactions from the last 7 days".

6. To change the number of days, tap **7**.
7. Type the number of days.
8. Add the actions that use the transactions.

The action gives the transactions of the [Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/) that you share with WalletFeed. WalletFeed reads them from Wallet when the action operates. WalletFeed does not keep a copy.

The action gives this information for each transaction:

| Name in Shortcuts | Data |
| --- | --- |
| **Merchant** | The name of the merchant. If Wallet has no merchant name, **Merchant** has the description of the transaction. |
| **Amount** | The value of the transaction, with its currency. This value is more than zero for debits and for credits. |
| **Date** | The date of the transaction. |
| **Category** | The WalletFeed category, for example **Groceries** or **Dining**. |
| **Status** | The status in Wallet, for example `pending`, `authorized`, `booked` (posted) or `rejected` (declined). |
| **Credit** | Shows if the transaction is a credit, for example a refund or a payment. |

## Send transactions with an automation

An automation in the Shortcuts app can send your transactions while WalletFeed is closed. iOS does not let apps make automations. Thus, you make the automation in Shortcuts, with the steps that WalletFeed shows.

If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, **Settings** does not show the **Sync** section. Refer to [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/).

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In the **Sync** section, tap **Automations**.

   ![The WalletFeed Settings screen with Background Sync and Automations in the Sync section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/siri-and-shortcuts/walletfeed-settings.webp)

4. Do the steps in the **After Each Card Tap** section.

   ![The Automations screen with Last Run, Copy Description and Open Shortcuts in the After Each Card Tap section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/siri-and-shortcuts/walletfeed-automations.webp)

The steps on the screen are different on iOS 26 and iOS 27. On iOS 27 with Apple Intelligence on, step 1 is **Copy Description**. You paste this description in Shortcuts. Then you make sure that the automation is correct.

On iOS 27, the other method is below the steps, in **Set It Up Yourself** or **Describe It Instead**. For the steps of each method, refer to [Run a shortcut after each Apple Card purchase](/guides/apple-card-shortcuts/).

**Automations** can show these automations:

| Automation | WalletFeed action | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **After Each Card Tap** | **Sync New Purchase**, in a **Transaction** automation | Sends each purchase some seconds after you make it with your iPhone. |
| **Every Day** | **Sync Transactions**, in a **Time of Day** automation | Sends other changes, for example purchases on the internet and posted charges. |

**Every Day** shows only if **Background Sync** is off or **Sample Data** is on. When **Background Sync** is on and WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. Thus, **After Each Card Tap** is optional. Refer to [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/).

If you made an **Every Day** automation, it continues to operate when the **Automations** screen does not show **Every Day**.

After **Sync New Purchase** starts, it waits a maximum of 18 seconds for Wallet to record the purchase. If Wallet records the purchase after this time, WalletFeed sends it at the next sync.

### **Last Run** and the **Automations** value

On the **Automations** screen, the section of each automation starts with **Last Run**. **Last Run** shows the last time that the action operated, for example "2 hr. ago". If the action did not operate, **Last Run** shows **Never**. For **Every Day**, **Last Run** also changes when you use **Sync Transactions** with Siri or in a different shortcut.

The **Automations** value in **Settings** shows if each automation operated in its period. The period of **After Each Card Tap** is the last 14 days. The period of **Every Day** is the last 3 days. The value is one of these:

| Value | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| **On** | Each automation on the **Automations** screen operated in its period. |
| **1 of 2** | One of the two automations operated in its period. |
| **Set Up** | No automation operated in its period, and **Background Sync** is off or **Sample Data** is on. |
| **Off** | **Background Sync** is on, **Sample Data** is off, and **After Each Card Tap** did not operate in its period. |

iOS does not tell WalletFeed about your automations. To change or delete an automation, open it in the Shortcuts app.

## Messages from the sync actions

Siri shows or speaks the message from a sync action. In an automation, Shortcuts can show the message as a notification. When **Sync Transactions** or **Sync New Purchase** stops, it gives one of these messages:

| Message | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| "Changes sent: 3." | WalletFeed sent 3 changes. The number is the total for all your destinations. |
| "Nothing new to send." | **Sync Transactions** did not find a new change. |
| "Nothing new yet." | **Sync New Purchase** did not find a new change. |
| "Changes sent: 3. One destination needs attention." | WalletFeed cannot send to one destination. If more destinations have this problem, the message gives the number of destinations. |
| "Sync requires WalletFeed Pro." | WalletFeed Pro is not active on this iPhone. |
| "Open WalletFeed and allow Wallet access." | WalletFeed cannot read your Wallet accounts. |
| "Add a destination in WalletFeed first." | WalletFeed has no destination that is on. |

Without WalletFeed Pro, **Get Recent Card Transactions** shows "This action requires WalletFeed Pro."

## Your data in Siri and Shortcuts

When you use **Show Spending** or **Search Transactions** with Siri, Siri opens WalletFeed. Siri does not receive your transactions or the totals on **Spending**. For **Search Transactions**, Siri receives only your instruction.

**Get Recent Card Transactions** gives your transactions to the shortcut or to Siri. The other actions in the shortcut can send the transactions to other apps.

On your iPhone, WalletFeed records the last time that each sync action operated. **Settings** uses these times to show the **Automations** value.

## If there is a problem

### If **Last Run** shows **Never**

The automation did not start the WalletFeed action on this iPhone.

1. On your iPhone, open the Shortcuts app.
2. If your iPhone has iOS 26, tap **Automation**.
3. Find the automation. On iOS 27, an automation is a trigger at the top of a shortcut.
4. If you cannot find the automation, do the steps in [Send transactions with an automation](#send-transactions-with-an-automation) again.
5. Make sure that the automation starts **Sync New Purchase** or **Sync Transactions**.
6. On iOS 26, make sure that the automation uses **Run Immediately**.
7. On iOS 27, make sure that **Confirm Before Run** is off.

### If the message is "Sync requires WalletFeed Pro."

WalletFeed Pro is not active on this iPhone. This is also the cause when **Get Recent Card Transactions** shows "This action requires WalletFeed Pro."

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In the **Subscription** section, tap the **WalletFeed Pro** row that shows **Upgrade**.
4. If you have a plan, tap **Restore Purchases** below the plans.
5. If you do not have a plan, get WalletFeed Pro. Refer to [Get WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/#get-walletfeed-pro).

### If the message is "Open WalletFeed and allow Wallet access."

WalletFeed cannot read your Wallet accounts.

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. Share your Wallet accounts with WalletFeed. Refer to [Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/).

### If the message is "Add a destination in WalletFeed first."

WalletFeed has no destination that is on.

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. If a destination shows **Off**, do these steps:
   1. Tap the destination.
   2. Set **Enabled** to on.
4. If there is no destination, do these steps:
   1. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.
   2. Add a destination. Refer to [Destinations](/docs/destinations/).

### If the message is "Changes sent: 3. One destination needs attention."

WalletFeed cannot send to one or more destinations.

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Find the destination that shows a message below its name, for example "Authentication failed".

   ![The Destinations screen with Authentication failed and a warning symbol for the n8n destination.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/siri-and-shortcuts/walletfeed-destinations-failure.webp)

4. Tap the destination.
5. In [Guides](/guides/), open the guide for that destination.
6. In the guide, find the message that the destination shows.
7. Do the steps for that message.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/spending-widget/ -->
# Spending widget

The Spending widget shows this month's total on your Home Screen or Lock Screen. You can use the widget without [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/) and without a [destination](/docs/destinations/).

## Totals in the widget

The widget and the [**Spending**](/docs/spending/) tab use the same totals from all the [Wallet accounts that WalletFeed reads](/docs/wallet-accounts/). The **This Month** total is from the start of this month to the last update. The **Same Point Last Month** total is from the start of last month to the same day and time last month.

The totals include pending purchases. Refunds decrease the totals. Transfers, bill payments and declined transactions are not in the totals.

## Widget shapes

The widget has these shapes:

| Widget | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| Small, on the Home Screen | **This Month** and **Same Point Last Month**. |
| Medium, on the Home Screen | **This Month**, **Same Point Last Month** and the change from last month. |
| On the Lock Screen | **Spending**, this month's total and the change from last month. |
| One line on the Lock Screen | This month's total, for example "$1,234.56 this month". |

The medium widget and the Lock Screen widget show the change from last month with an arrow, for example "↓ 14% vs Sep". The arrow points down when the **This Month** total is less than the **Same Point Last Month** total. It points up when the **This Month** total is the same or more. If the **Same Point Last Month** total is $0.00 or less, the widget does not show the change.

iOS can also show the widget in [StandBy](https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/use-standby-iph878d77632/ios) while your iPhone charges on its side.

## Add the widget to your Home Screen

1. On your iPhone, go to the Home Screen page where you want the widget.
2. Touch and hold an area with no apps until the apps start to move.
3. Tap **Edit** at the top of the screen.
4. Tap **Add Widget**.
5. In the search field, type `WalletFeed`.
6. Tap **WalletFeed**.

   iOS shows the small **Spending** widget. Until WalletFeed has your totals, the widget on this screen shows example totals.

7. To add the medium widget, swipe to it.
8. Tap **Add Widget**.
9. To move the widget, drag it to a different position.
10. Tap **Done**.

Apple gives more information in [Add, edit, and remove widgets on iPhone](https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/add-edit-and-remove-widgets-iphb8f1bf206/ios).

## Add the widget to your Lock Screen

1. To show the Lock Screen, push the side button of your iPhone.
2. If the Lock Screen does not show, push the side button again.
3. Touch and hold the Lock Screen until **Customize** shows at the bottom of the screen.
4. Tap **Customize**.
5. Tap **Add Widgets**.
6. In the list of apps, tap **WalletFeed**.
7. Tap the **Spending** widget.
8. To close the list of widgets, swipe down.
9. Tap **Done**.

Apple gives more information in [Create a custom iPhone Lock Screen](https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/create-a-custom-lock-screen-iph4d0e6c351/ios).

## Updates to the widget

WalletFeed updates the widget when you open WalletFeed. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. WalletFeed then updates the widget.

WalletFeed Pro is not necessary for these updates. The [**Background Sync**](/docs/background-sync/) switch in **Settings** › **Sync** has no effect on the widget.

At the start of a month, the widget shows $0.00 for this month. It does not show the **Same Point Last Month** total or the change. After the next update, the widget shows the totals again.

> **Note:** When **Sample Data** is on in **Settings**, the widget shows the totals of the sample transactions.

## Privacy

For the widget, WalletFeed keeps only this information on your iPhone:

- The two totals.
- The currency of the totals.
- The time of the last update.

iOS keeps a copy of the information that the widget shows. Because of this, the widget has only the two totals. It has no transactions, merchants or categories.

On a locked iPhone, iOS can remove the totals and the change from the widget.

If you stop WalletFeed's access to Wallet, WalletFeed removes the totals from the widget the next time that you open WalletFeed.

## If there is a problem

### If the widget shows "Open WalletFeed"

The widget shows this text before WalletFeed reads Wallet for the first time, and after WalletFeed's access to Wallet stops.

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. If WalletFeed shows **No Cards** or **Wallet Access Off**, give WalletFeed [access to Wallet](/docs/wallet-accounts/).

### If the widget does not show a new purchase

When WalletFeed is closed, the widget can show a new purchase in approximately 1 hour or less.

To update the widget, open WalletFeed.

### If the widget shows no totals on a locked iPhone

On a locked iPhone, iOS can remove the totals and the change from the widget.

Make sure that your iPhone is not locked.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/spending/ -->
# Spending

Spending in WalletFeed shows the total of your Apple Card and Apple Cash purchases for this month on your iPhone. It also shows a bar for each day, your largest categories and merchants, and the charges that occur each month or each week. You can use Spending without [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/).

## Open Spending

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. At the bottom of the screen, tap **Spending**.

   ![Spending with the October total of $1,317.68, a chart with a bar for each day, and the Monthly Summary.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/spending/walletfeed-spending.webp)

   Result: WalletFeed reads your transactions from Wallet. Then Spending shows the total and the chart for this month.

WalletFeed calculates the values for Spending on your iPhone. It does not keep your transactions. If Spending does not show a total, refer to [If something goes wrong](#if-something-goes-wrong).

## The total for this month

The first section of Spending has these parts:

- The name of the month.
- The change from the same time last month, for example "70% VS SEP" with an up arrow. An up arrow shows that the total increased, and a down arrow shows that it decreased.
- The total for this month.
- A chart with one bar for each day of the month. The line with the label "Avg" shows the average for each day, for example "Avg $45".
- The Monthly Summary, below the chart.

The total includes purchases that are pending. Refunds decrease the total. Transfers, bill payments and declined transactions are not in the total.

WalletFeed compares this month with the same days and time of last month. For example, on October 15 at 2:00 PM, WalletFeed compares the total with the total from September 1 to September 15 at 2:00 PM. If that total for last month is zero or less, Spending does not show the change.

The average is the total for this month, divided by the number of days from the first day of the month to this day.

## See the total for one day

1. On the chart, put your finger on the bar for a day.

   Result: the top of the section shows the date and the total for that day. The other bars become dim.
2. To see a different day, move your finger along the chart.

## Monthly Summary

The Monthly Summary is below the chart. It tells you the important facts about this month.

Apple Intelligence writes the Monthly Summary if your iPhone can use Apple Intelligence and Apple Intelligence is on. It uses facts that WalletFeed calculates, for example the total and your largest purchase. A Monthly Summary from Apple Intelligence has the Apple Intelligence symbol.

> **Note:** Apple Intelligence can write an incorrect value in the Monthly Summary. WalletFeed calculates all other values on Spending.

Apple Intelligence operates on your iPhone. WalletFeed does not send your transactions to a server for the Monthly Summary.

WalletFeed shows its first two facts with a light bulb symbol in these conditions:

- Apple Intelligence is not available on your iPhone.
- **Summarize Spending** is off in **Settings**.
- Apple Intelligence does not give a Monthly Summary.

An example of the two facts is "You've spent $1,318 so far this month. That's 70% more than at this point last month."

## Stop the Monthly Summary from Apple Intelligence

1. On Spending, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. Below **Privacy & Security**, set **Summarize Spending** to off.

   ![Settings with Summarize Spending set to on in the Privacy & Security section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/spending/walletfeed-settings-2.webp)

   Result: the Monthly Summary shows the two facts from WalletFeed.
3. Tap **Done**.

**Settings** shows **Summarize Spending** only when Apple Intelligence is available on your iPhone. When **Summarize Spending** is off, [Ask Spending](/docs/ask-spending/) also shows two facts from WalletFeed. To start the Monthly Summary from Apple Intelligence again, set **Summarize Spending** to on.

## Categories and merchants

The **Categories** section shows the five categories with the largest totals this month. **Other** shows the total of all other categories. At the top of the section, a bar has a color for each category. The length of each color shows the part of the total for that category.

The **Merchants** section, at the bottom of Spending, shows the five merchants with the largest totals this month.

## Recurring Charges

The **Recurring Charges** section shows charges that occur again each month or each week, for example subscriptions. The section shows only when WalletFeed finds one or more of these charges. For each charge, the section shows the name, **Monthly** or **Weekly**, and the value of the last charge.

To find these charges, Spending reads this month and the two months before it. Apple Intelligence can give each charge a clear name and a type. For example, "NETFLIX.COM 866-579" becomes "Netflix", with the type "Streaming". Then the section shows "Apple Intelligence suggested these names."

![Recurring Charges with three monthly charges, and Merchants with five merchants.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/spending/walletfeed-recurring.webp)

For more information, refer to [Recurring Charges](/docs/recurring-charges/).

## Monthly Installments

If you have Apple Card Monthly Installments, the **Monthly Installments** section shows your installment charges. It shows the charges for the last month that has installment charges, with the largest charge first. For each charge, the section shows the name, the date, for example "Sep 30", and the value.

Each installment charge has the date of the last day of a month. Thus, until the last day of this month, the section shows the charges from last month. These charges do not show in **Recurring Charges**.

Wallet does not give WalletFeed the remaining payments or the remaining balance. Thus, the section does not show them.

## Use Ask Spending

With Apple Intelligence, **Ask about your spending** is at the top of Spending.

1. Tap **Ask about your spending**.
2. Type what you want to see, for example "Dining this month vs last".
3. On the keyboard, tap **Go**.

   ![Spending with Dining this month vs last at the top, a total of $188.70 and a chart of this month and last month.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/spending/walletfeed-ask-spending.webp)

   Result: Spending shows the total, the chart, the categories and the transactions for what you typed.
4. To see the total for this month again, tap **Clear** (the x button).

For more information, refer to [Ask Spending](/docs/ask-spending/).

## Show new transactions

To show new transactions on Spending, pull the screen down.

## If something goes wrong

### If Spending shows "No Cards"

WalletFeed does not have access to your Wallet accounts.

1. Tap **Choose Accounts**.
2. Select the Wallet accounts for WalletFeed.

For more information, refer to [Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/).

### If Spending shows "Wallet Access Off"

Wallet access for WalletFeed is off in the Settings app on your iPhone.

1. Tap **Open Settings**.
2. In the Settings app, go to **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet**.
3. Give WalletFeed access to your Wallet accounts.

### If Spending shows "No Spending"

The Wallet accounts that WalletFeed can read have no purchases this month, or your refunds are more than your purchases. For the transactions in the total, refer to [The total for this month](#the-total-for-this-month).

If **Spending** does not include a Wallet account, refer to [Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/).

### If Spending shows "Couldn't Read Wallet"

WalletFeed cannot read your transactions from Wallet. To read Wallet again, pull the screen down.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/transactions/ -->
# Transactions

The **Transactions** tab in WalletFeed shows your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions by month on your iPhone. WalletFeed reads the transactions from Wallet and does not keep them.

## Open your transactions

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Transactions** at the bottom of the screen.

   ![The Transactions tab with the October transactions and a pending charge at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/transactions/walletfeed-transactions.webp)

The list has a section for each month. The month of your last transaction is at the top. Each section starts with the last transaction of its month. The name of a month before this year also shows the year, for example "September 2025".

## Transaction rows

Each row shows these items:

- An icon for the category
- The merchant name
- The amount
- The date.

The icon shows the category, for example a car for **Transport**. WalletFeed sets the category from the merchant category code (MCC).

If Wallet gives no merchant name, the row shows the description of the transaction. Some rows have a second line below the merchant name. This line shows **Pending** until the transaction posts. If most transactions in the list are from a different account, the line also shows the account name. For example, Apple Cash rows show "Apple Cash" when most transactions are from Apple Card.

A credit, for example a refund, is green and has a plus sign (+).

For the last 7 days, the date is **Today**, **Yesterday** or the name of the day, for example "Tuesday". For a date before these 7 days, the row shows the month and the day, for example "Oct 3". A date before this year also shows the year.

The category name is not on the row, but VoiceOver reads it with the other items in the row. The row also does not show the person who used the card, because Wallet does not give this information to apps.

## Apple Card Monthly Installments

If you use Apple Card Monthly Installments, the list shows the charge for each month with your other transactions. Apple adds these charges on the last day of the month. In [Spending](/docs/spending/), the **Monthly Installments** section also shows the charges of the last month that has them. Wallet does not give apps other installment information, for example the item that you bought or the remaining balance.

## Show more transactions

WalletFeed reads 200 transactions first. When you scroll to the end of the list, WalletFeed reads 200 more transactions.

1. Scroll down the list.
2. Continue to scroll until a message shows at the end of the list.

   The message gives the date of the last row, for example "Showing transactions from March 4, 2025."

   If **Sample Data** is on, the message does not show.

Wallet shares the transactions of each account from a start date. You select this date for each account when you [share the account with WalletFeed](/docs/wallet-accounts/).

## Change the accounts or the start dates

You select the accounts and their start dates on the Wallet access screen, which iOS shows only one time. After that, you change them in the Settings app.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select the accounts to share with WalletFeed.
4. To get transactions from before the start date of an account, change its start date.
5. Open WalletFeed.

   When WalletFeed opens, it reads Wallet again.

## Update the list

WalletFeed reads your transactions again each time you open WalletFeed or the **Transactions** tab.

1. At the top of the list, swipe down.

   WalletFeed reads your transactions from Wallet again. If WalletFeed cannot read Wallet, the list does not change.

## Find a transaction

To find a transaction by its merchant, category or amount, use [Search](/docs/search/). Search shows its results in the same rows and month sections as **Transactions**.

## If there is a problem

### If WalletFeed shows "No Cards"

You did not share Wallet accounts with WalletFeed.

1. Tap **Choose Accounts**.

   iOS shows the Wallet access screen.

2. Select each account to share.
3. For each account, select the start date.
4. Tap **Share**.

### If WalletFeed shows "Wallet Access Off"

You did not let WalletFeed read Wallet, or you stopped its access to Wallet in the Settings app. The Wallet access screen opens only one time.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select the accounts to share with WalletFeed.
4. Open WalletFeed.

### If WalletFeed shows "No Transactions"

The accounts that you share with WalletFeed have no transactions. WalletFeed also shows this message if it cannot read Wallet.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select more accounts to share with WalletFeed.
4. Open WalletFeed.

   When WalletFeed opens, it reads Wallet again.

### If WalletFeed shows "Wallet Unavailable"

This iPhone cannot share Wallet data with apps. WalletFeed cannot show transactions on it. WalletFeed is for iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version, and it is available only in the US.

### If a transaction is not in the list

WalletFeed shows only the Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions that Wallet shares with it.

1. At the top of the list, swipe down.
2. Scroll down the list until you find the transaction or until you are at the end of the list.
3. In the Wallet app, find the account and the date of the transaction.
4. If you do not share the account, or the date is before its start date, do the steps in [Change the accounts or the start dates](#change-the-accounts-or-the-start-dates).

### If the list shows transactions that you did not make

**Sample Data** is on. While it is on, WalletFeed shows two months of sample transactions and does not show your Wallet transactions.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Data** section, set **Sample Data** to off.
3. Tap **Done**.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/troubleshooting/ -->
# Troubleshooting

WalletFeed shows a message when it cannot read Wallet or send transactions to a destination. To correct a problem with WalletFeed on your iPhone, find the message or the problem on this page, then do the steps below it.

## Correct problems with Wallet and Apple Intelligence

### If WalletFeed does not show your cards

WalletFeed shows only the Wallet accounts that you share with it, and it reads only Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings in the US.

Until you tap **Share** or **Don't Share** on the iOS screen **Share Wallet Data**, **Settings** › **Wallet** shows **Choose Accounts**. To share your accounts, do these steps:

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Wallet** section, tap **Choose Accounts**.

   ![WalletFeed Settings, with Choose Accounts in the Wallet section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/troubleshooting/walletfeed-settings.webp)

   iOS shows **Share Wallet Data**.

3. For each account that WalletFeed can read, set the switch to on.

   ![The Share Wallet Data screen, with switches for Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings, and the Share button.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/troubleshooting/walletfeed-wallet-access.webp)

4. Tap **Share**.

After that, iOS does not show **Share Wallet Data** again, and **Settings** › **Wallet** shows **Open Settings**. To change the accounts that you share, do these steps:

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select the accounts that WalletFeed can read.
4. Select the start date of each account.
5. Open WalletFeed.

For more information, refer to [Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/).

### If WalletFeed does not show Ask Spending

WalletFeed shows Ask Spending only on an iPhone that can use Apple Intelligence, with Apple Intelligence on.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Set Apple Intelligence to on.
3. Open WalletFeed.
4. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
5. In the **Privacy & Security** section, find **Summarize Spending**.

   ![WalletFeed Settings, with the Summarize Spending switch in the Privacy & Security section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/troubleshooting/walletfeed-settings-2.webp)

   WalletFeed shows **Summarize Spending** only when it can use Apple Intelligence. Then **Spending** shows the field **Ask about your spending**. If WalletFeed does not show **Summarize Spending**, it cannot use Apple Intelligence at this time.

When **Summarize Spending** is off, **Spending** shows no summaries, but it continues to show Ask Spending.

Without Apple Intelligence, **Spending** and **Search** continue to operate. **Search** then finds the words that you type. Refer to [Ask Spending](/docs/ask-spending/).

## Correct problems with destinations

### If a destination shows "Authentication failed"

The service did not accept the key, the token or the sign-in of the destination.

For example, someone deleted the key, or the key is expired. A key that can only read, such as a **Read Only** key in Sure, also causes this message. BankSync stops a key after 90 days if you do not select a different **Expiration** when you make it.

The screen of the destination has a button to correct the problem:

| Destination | Button |
| --- | --- |
| A destination with an API key, for example Sure | **Replace Key** |
| A destination with a token, for example Lunch Money | **Replace Token** |
| A destination with a sign-in, for example Google Sheets | **Sign In Again** |
| Zapier or Make | **Replace URL** |
| Webhook | **URL** and **Authorization** |

To use a new key, token or URL, do these steps:

1. In the service, make a new key, token or URL. The [guide for your destination](/guides/) gives the steps.
2. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.

   ![The Destinations screen, with "Authentication failed" below the n8n destination.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/troubleshooting/walletfeed-destinations-failure.webp)

3. Tap the destination.

   ![The n8n destination screen, with "Authentication failed" below Last Sync, and the URL and Authorization rows.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/troubleshooting/walletfeed-destination-failure.webp)

4. Tap **Replace Key**, **Replace Token** or **Replace URL**.
5. Paste the new key, token or URL.
6. Tap **Replace**.

For a webhook, tap **URL** or **Authorization** in step 4. Type the new value. Then tap **Save**.

A destination with a sign-in can also show "Signed out. Sign in again in the destination's settings." To sign in again, do these steps:

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Sign In Again**.
4. Sign in to the same account that you used before.

You do not have to delete the destination. After you correct the problem, WalletFeed sends the changes that the destination did not receive. If the screen shows **Sending History** and **Try Again**, tap **Try Again**.

### If Destinations shows "Sync Requires Pro"

You do not have WalletFeed Pro at this time, and WalletFeed sends transactions to destinations only with WalletFeed Pro.

1. In **Destinations**, tap **Upgrade**.
2. Select a plan.
3. Complete the purchase.

The WalletFeed Pro screen also has **Restore Purchases**. For the plans, refer to [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/).

### If a destination shows "Off"

The **Enabled** switch of the destination is off, and WalletFeed does not send transactions to it.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Set the **Enabled** switch to on.
