   ![The Lunch Money destination screen, with the Enabled switch on.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/troubleshooting/walletfeed-destination-detail.webp)

### If destinations receive changes only while WalletFeed is open

**Background Sync** is off, or your iPhone started again and you did not type its passcode after that.

While WalletFeed is open, destinations receive changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Sync** section, set the **Background Sync** switch to on.

   ![WalletFeed Settings, with the Background Sync switch on in the Sync section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/troubleshooting/walletfeed-background-sync.webp)

3. After your iPhone starts again, type its passcode one time.

**Settings** shows the **Sync** section only with WalletFeed Pro. For more information, refer to [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/).

To send each purchase seconds after you tap your iPhone to pay, do these steps:

1. In **Settings** › **Sync**, tap **Automations**.

   ![The Automations screen, with the steps for After Each Card Tap.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/troubleshooting/walletfeed-automations.webp)

2. In **After Each Card Tap**, do the steps on the screen.

### If you get the notification "Sync Stopped"

WalletFeed did not complete a sync for 3 days, and **Remind If Sync Stops** is on in **Settings** › **Sync**.

The notification tells you "WalletFeed hasn't synced in 3 days. Open it to catch up."

1. Open WalletFeed.

   While WalletFeed is open, it sends the changes to your destinations.

2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. If a destination shows a message, find the message on this page.

**Remind If Sync Stops** stays off until you let WalletFeed send notifications.

### If a destination shows "Can't open the folder. Choose it again."

WalletFeed cannot open the folder of a CSV, OFX or QIF file at this time.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Change Folder**.
4. Select the same folder again.

WalletFeed then writes all the transactions of the destination to the folder again. If WalletFeed shows "Couldn't open this folder.", select a different folder.

### If a file changes only when you open WalletFeed

WalletFeed did not get access to the folder in the background. WalletFeed does not show a message for this.

1. Open WalletFeed.

   The file changes while WalletFeed is open.

WalletFeed also changes the file while your iPhone charges. An automation from **Settings** › **Sync** › **Automations** also changes it.

### If BankSync does not make the Apple Card table

BankSync did not make the table in approximately 30 seconds, for example because the workspace has the maximum number of tables for its plan.

WalletFeed shows "You're signed in, but BankSync hasn't created or shared the Apple Card table."

The message also gives the table limit of your plan, for example "The Free plan allows one table."

1. Tap **Open BankSync**.
2. In BankSync, delete a table that you do not use, or change to a plan that has more tables.
3. In WalletFeed, tap **Try Again**.
4. If WalletFeed continues to show the message, tap **Sign In Again**.
5. Give your approval as the owner or an admin of the workspace.
6. Tap **Add**.

To use an API key, tap **Use an API Key Instead**. API keys are available only on the Standard plan of BankSync or higher. Refer to [Send Apple Card transactions to BankSync](/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/).

> **Note:** Sign In with BankSync uses the referral link of WalletFeed. The form tells you this with the text "WalletFeed may earn a commission if you pay for BankSync."

## Prevent copies of transactions

### If Zapier, Make or a webhook receives a transaction two times

If a sync stops before it sends all the changes, WalletFeed sends the same changes again at the next sync.

Zapier and Make do not find copies. Thus, a Zap or a scenario that adds a row for each change can add a transaction two times. **Send History** also sends previous transactions again.

1. Open the Zap or the scenario.
2. Before the step that adds a row, add a step that finds the row by its `id`.
3. If the step finds the row, update that row.
4. If the step does not find the row, add a new row.

A webhook server must update the row that has the same `id`. To find a request that WalletFeed sent two times, use its `webhook-id` header. Refer to [Webhook format](/docs/webhooks/).

### If your app shows each transaction two times after an import

You imported the same QIF file two times, and a QIF file has no transaction ID.

1. In your app, delete the transactions that you imported the second time.
2. Import each QIF file only one time, after the end of its month.

An OFX file has an ID for each transaction. Actual, GnuCash and Moneydance use this ID and do not import a transaction two times. A CSV file has a **WalletFeed ID** column, but only some apps use it to find copies.

### If a destination shows a transaction two times

WalletFeed finds each transaction by the ID that it wrote, and it adds the transaction again if it cannot find that ID.

WalletFeed keeps the ID in these locations:

- Google Sheets: column A, **WalletFeed ID**
- Airtable, Notion and Coda: the **WalletFeed ID** field, property or column
- PocketSmith: the `wf:` note
- Linear: the **WalletFeed ID** row and the WalletFeed attachment, in the team that you selected

In Notion, WalletFeed also cannot find a row that you moved to the archive.

1. In the service, find the two copies of the transaction.
2. Delete the copy that has no ID, or a changed ID.
3. Do not change or delete the ID of the other transactions.

## Send an email to support

If the steps on this page do not correct the problem, send an email to [support@walletfeed.app](mailto:support@walletfeed.app). In the email, include these items:

- The model of your iPhone
- The version of iOS on your iPhone
- For a problem with a destination, the type of destination, for example Google Sheets

Do not send API keys, tokens or the details of your transactions. In WalletFeed, **Settings** › **Support** opens the support page.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/wallet-accounts/ -->
# Select the Wallet accounts that WalletFeed reads

WalletFeed reads the transactions of the Wallet accounts that you share with it on your iPhone. It can read your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings accounts. You select the accounts when you open WalletFeed for the first time. After that, you change them in the Settings app.

## Share your accounts for the first time

When you open WalletFeed for the first time, it shows **Welcome to WalletFeed**.

1. Tap **Continue**.

   ![The Welcome to WalletFeed screen, with the text "Next, choose the Wallet accounts to share." above the Continue button.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/wallet-accounts/walletfeed-welcome.webp)

   **Transactions** opens, and iOS shows the Wallet access screen.

2. Select each account to share.
3. For each account, select the start date.

   From that date, WalletFeed can read the transactions of the account.

4. Tap **Share**.

   **Transactions** shows the transactions of the accounts that you shared.

If you tap **Don't Share**, WalletFeed cannot read Wallet, and **Transactions** shows **Wallet Access Off**. To share accounts after that, use the Settings app. Refer to [Change the accounts that you share](#change-the-accounts-that-you-share).

## Share accounts from WalletFeed

Until you tap **Share** or **Don't Share** on the Wallet access screen, WalletFeed shows **Choose Accounts**. **Choose Accounts** is in **Settings** › **Wallet**. It also shows below **No Cards** in **Transactions**, **Spending** and **Search**.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Wallet** section, tap **Choose Accounts**.

   ![WalletFeed Settings, with Choose Accounts in the Wallet section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/wallet-accounts/walletfeed-settings.webp)

   iOS shows the Wallet access screen.

3. Do steps 2 to 4 in [Share your accounts for the first time](#share-your-accounts-for-the-first-time).

## Change the accounts that you share

After you tap **Share** or **Don't Share**, iOS does not show the Wallet access screen again. You change the accounts and their start dates in the Settings app.

At the end of the **Transactions** list, WalletFeed shows the date of the first transaction that it can read. If you select a start date before this date in step 4, WalletFeed can also read the transactions before this date.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select the accounts that WalletFeed can read.
4. Select the start date of each account.
5. Open WalletFeed.

   When WalletFeed opens, it reads the change.

If you do not select an account in step 3, WalletFeed cannot read the transactions of that account. A destination keeps the transactions that it received before this change.

> **Note:** After you tap **Share** or **Don't Share**, **Settings** › **Wallet** in WalletFeed shows **Open Settings**. **Open Settings** opens the WalletFeed page in the Settings app.

## Accounts and destinations

With [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), WalletFeed sends transactions to [destinations](/docs/destinations/), for example to Lunch Money or Google Sheets. A destination receives the transactions of the accounts that you share.

Before a new destination receives transactions, WalletFeed shows a message. The message tells you which data the destination receives and from which accounts. It also gives the start date, or tells you that the destination receives all the transactions from these accounts. After you tap **Send**, the destination starts to receive transactions. For a CSV, OFX or QIF file, the button is **Save**.

If you set the **Filter** switch of a destination to on, you can use **Accounts** to select the accounts that the destination receives. Refer to [Choose what a destination receives](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).

## Correct problems with Wallet access

### If WalletFeed shows Wallet Access Off

WalletFeed cannot read Wallet, because you tapped **Don't Share** or you stopped its access in the Settings app.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select the accounts that WalletFeed can read.
4. Open WalletFeed.

### If WalletFeed shows No Transactions

The accounts that you share have no transactions from their start dates. WalletFeed shows "To share more Wallet accounts, open Settings › Privacy & Security › Wallet."

If you did not share all your accounts, share more accounts. If an account has transactions before its start date, select a start date before these transactions. Refer to [Change the accounts that you share](#change-the-accounts-that-you-share).

### If an account does not show in WalletFeed

WalletFeed reads only your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings accounts. It does not show other cards in Wallet.

If the account is one of these accounts, share it in the Settings app. Refer to [Change the accounts that you share](#change-the-accounts-that-you-share).

### If WalletFeed shows Wallet Unavailable

This iPhone cannot share Wallet data with WalletFeed. WalletFeed is for iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version, and it is available only in the US.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/walletfeed-pro/ -->
# WalletFeed Pro

WalletFeed Pro lets WalletFeed send your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions to [destinations](/docs/destinations/), for example a budget app or a spreadsheet. WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.

You can use these functions without WalletFeed Pro:

- [Spending](/docs/spending/)
- [Ask Spending](/docs/ask-spending/)
- [Search](/docs/search/)
- [Recurring Charges](/docs/recurring-charges/)
- The [Spending widget](/docs/spending-widget/)
- [Export CSV](/docs/export-csv/).

## Functions of WalletFeed Pro

With WalletFeed Pro, you can add destinations, for example Lunch Money or Google Sheets. WalletFeed sends your transactions to each destination. While WalletFeed is open, a destination receives changes in seconds.

When WalletFeed is closed, [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) also sends changes to your destinations. iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet.

A new destination also receives previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. If **Send** is **Each Transaction** for Zapier, Make or Linear, the destination receives a maximum of 30 days of previous transactions. On the destination screen, [Send History](/docs/send-history/) sends more of them.

WalletFeed Pro adds the **Sync** section to **Settings**.

## Plans and prices

The **WalletFeed Pro** screen shows these plans:

| Plan | Price | Free trial |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Yearly** | $4.99 a year ($0.42 a month) | 1 week |
| **Monthly** | $0.99 a month | 1 week |
| **Lifetime** | $19.99, one time | No free trial |

**Yearly** and **Monthly** are subscriptions. **Lifetime** is a one-time purchase.

You can get one free trial of WalletFeed Pro, for **Yearly** or for **Monthly**. After the free trial, the subscription continues at the price of the plan. If you cannot get a free trial, the button at the bottom of the screen shows **Subscribe** for **Yearly** and **Monthly**.

You can use Family Sharing with WalletFeed Pro.

## Get WalletFeed Pro

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.

   ![The Transactions screen with the gear button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/walletfeed-pro/walletfeed-transactions.webp)

3. In the **Subscription** section, tap the **WalletFeed Pro** row that shows **Upgrade**.

   **Settings** closes, and the **WalletFeed Pro** screen opens. It shows the plans and their prices. **Yearly** has the check mark.

   ![The WalletFeed Pro screen with a check mark on the Yearly plan, and the Start Free Trial button at the bottom.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/walletfeed-pro/walletfeed-pro.webp)

4. Tap a plan.

   The text below the button at the bottom gives the terms, for example "1 week free, then $4.99/year."

5. Tap the button at the bottom of the screen, for example **Start Free Trial** or **Buy Lifetime**.
6. Complete the purchase on the App Store screen.

   The **WalletFeed Pro** screen closes. When you open **Settings** again, the **Subscription** section shows your plan, for example **Yearly**.

## Get WalletFeed Pro when you add a destination

Without WalletFeed Pro, you can see all the destinations in **Add Destination**. When you tap a destination, WalletFeed shows the **WalletFeed Pro** screen.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   The **Add Destination** screen opens.

   ![The Add Destination screen with the Budgeting section and the Sheets & Databases section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/walletfeed-pro/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

3. Tap a destination, for example PocketSmith.

   The **WalletFeed Pro** screen opens. It shows the icon of the destination above the title.

   ![The WalletFeed Pro screen with the PocketSmith icon above the title.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/walletfeed-pro/walletfeed-store-destination.webp)

4. Tap a plan.
5. Tap the button at the bottom of the screen, for example **Start Free Trial**.
6. Complete the purchase on the App Store screen.

   The **WalletFeed Pro** screen changes to the setup form of the destination.

If you have a plan, you can tap **Restore Purchases** below the plans as an alternative to steps 4 to 6. When WalletFeed finds your plan, the setup form opens.

## Get WalletFeed Pro on a different iPhone

When WalletFeed starts, it gets your plan from the App Store. If you have a plan but **Settings** shows **Upgrade**, for example on a new iPhone, you can get WalletFeed Pro again with **Restore Purchases**.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Subscription** section, tap the **WalletFeed Pro** row that shows **Upgrade**.
3. Tap **Restore Purchases** below the plans.

   If the App Store finds your plan, the **WalletFeed Pro** screen closes. If the App Store finds no plan, WalletFeed shows "No purchases to restore."

   If an error occurs, WalletFeed shows "Couldn't restore purchases."

## Change your plan

You can change from **Yearly** to **Monthly**, or from **Monthly** to **Yearly**. You can also change from a subscription to **Lifetime**. If you have **Lifetime**, you cannot select a subscription.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Subscription** section, tap **Change Plan**.

   ![The Settings screen with Yearly in the WalletFeed Pro row, and Change Plan and Manage Subscription below it.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/walletfeed-pro/walletfeed-settings.webp)

   **Settings** closes, and the **WalletFeed Pro** screen opens. Your plan shows **Current**.

3. Tap a different plan.
4. Tap the button at the bottom of the screen, for example **Subscribe** or **Buy Lifetime**.
5. Complete the purchase on the App Store screen.

   The **WalletFeed Pro** screen closes.

If you get **Lifetime** while you have a subscription, the subscription continues until you cancel it. After you get **Lifetime**, WalletFeed does not show **Change Plan** or **Manage Subscription**. To cancel the subscription, use the steps for the Settings app in [Cancel your subscription](#cancel-your-subscription).

## Cancel your subscription

A subscription continues automatically at the end of each period, for example at the end of the free trial or of a month. If you cancel it a minimum of 24 hours before the end of a period, it stops at the end of that period. WalletFeed Pro stays active until that time.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Subscription** section, tap **Manage Subscription**.

   The subscriptions screen of the App Store opens.

3. Cancel your WalletFeed Pro subscription.

You can also cancel the subscription in the Settings app:

1. Open the Settings app.
2. Tap your name.
3. Tap **Subscriptions**.
4. Tap WalletFeed.
5. Cancel the subscription.

## After WalletFeed Pro stops

When WalletFeed Pro stops, WalletFeed keeps your destinations, but it does not send transactions to them. These changes also occur:

- The **Destinations** screen shows **Sync Requires Pro** and an **Upgrade** button.
- If WalletFeed did not send all the history to a destination, the destination screen shows "Paused" below **Sending History**.
- The **Settings** screen does not show the **Sync** section.

The transactions that WalletFeed sent to a destination stay there. The other functions of WalletFeed continue to operate.

## If there is a problem

### If the Destinations screen shows **Sync Requires Pro**

WalletFeed Pro is not active on this iPhone.

1. On the **Destinations** screen, tap **Upgrade**.
2. Tap a plan.
3. Tap the button at the bottom of the screen, for example **Subscribe**.
4. Complete the purchase on the App Store screen.

If you have a plan, you can tap **Restore Purchases** below the plans as an alternative to steps 2 to 4.

### If the WalletFeed Pro screen shows "Couldn't load prices."

WalletFeed cannot get the plans from the App Store.

1. Make sure that your iPhone has a connection to the internet.
2. Tap **Try Again**.

### If WalletFeed shows "Waiting for approval."

The purchase must get approval through Ask to Buy in Family Sharing.

Wait for the approval. After the approval, WalletFeed Pro starts on your iPhone.

### If WalletFeed shows "Couldn't complete the purchase."

The App Store did not complete the purchase.

1. Make sure that your iPhone has a connection to the internet.
2. Tap the button at the bottom of the **WalletFeed Pro** screen again.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-api/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to your app or server

There is no web API for your Apple Card transactions. Apple lets an app on your iPhone read them with the FinanceKit API, but only after you give your approval.

WalletFeed is an iPhone app that reads your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions with FinanceKit. With WalletFeed Pro, it sends each change from your iPhone to your server, AWS, Supabase or BankSync.

## FinanceKit on iPhone

FinanceKit is the part of iOS that lets apps read data from Wallet. It is available only on iPhone. In the US, FinanceKit gives access to your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings accounts.

Before an app can read your data, iOS shows your Wallet accounts. You select the accounts that the app can read, and a start date for each account. After that, you can change them in the Settings app, in **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet**.

Apple has no bank feed for your Apple Card transactions, and a server cannot get them from Apple.

If you make an iPhone app, Apple must give approval before your app can use FinanceKit. To get this approval, the app must be in the Finance category of the App Store, for iPhone in the US or the UK. Apple also tells developers that the app must "provide financial management tools". For more information, refer to [FinanceKit on the Apple Developer site](https://developer.apple.com/financekit/).

## Destinations for your app or server

WalletFeed can send your transactions to the destinations in this table:

| Destination | Data that it receives |
| --- | --- |
| **Webhook** | JSON in a `POST` request to your HTTPS URL, with a maximum of 100 transactions in each request |
| **Amazon S3** | One CSV or JSON Lines file for each month, in your bucket |
| **Amazon SQS** | One message for each change |
| **Kinesis Data Streams** | One record for each change |
| **DynamoDB** | One item for each transaction |
| **EventBridge** | One event for each change |
| **Supabase** | One row for each transaction, in a Postgres table in your Supabase project |
| **BankSync** | One row for each transaction, in a BankSync table that your AI agents can read |

In the **Add Destination** list, **Amazon S3**, **Amazon SQS**, **Kinesis Data Streams**, **DynamoDB** and **EventBridge** are all in **AWS**. You can add more than one destination.

These pages give the full procedure for each destination:

- [Send Apple Card transactions to a webhook](/guides/apple-card-to-webhook/)
- [Send Apple Card transactions to AWS](/guides/apple-card-to-aws/)
- [Send Apple Card transactions to Supabase](/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/)
- [Send Apple Card transactions to BankSync](/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/).

## Before you start

You must have:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version
- WalletFeed on that iPhone
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase
- For a webhook, a server with an HTTPS URL that your iPhone can connect to from the internet
- For AWS, an AWS account in which you can make an IAM user and an access key
- For Supabase, a Supabase project
- For BankSync, a BankSync workspace in which you are the owner or an admin.

WalletFeed is available only in the US.

## Step 1: Give WalletFeed access to your Wallet accounts

If WalletFeed shows your transactions, go to [Step 2](#step-2-add-the-destination).

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. On the **Welcome to WalletFeed** screen, tap **Continue**. iOS shows your Wallet accounts.

   ![The Welcome to WalletFeed screen, with the Continue button at the bottom.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-api/walletfeed-welcome.webp)
3. Select the accounts that WalletFeed can read.
4. For each account, select the start date of the transactions that WalletFeed can read.
5. Tap **Share**. **Transactions** shows the transactions of the accounts that you shared.

If WalletFeed shows **No Cards**, tap **Choose Accounts**. iOS shows your Wallet accounts. Then do steps 3 to 5. For more information, refer to [Choose the Wallet accounts WalletFeed reads](/docs/wallet-accounts/).

## Step 2: Add the destination

1. Tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with no destinations, and the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-api/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)
3. Find the destination in the **Add Destination** list. You can also type its name in the search field.

   ![The Add Destination list, with the Budgeting section and the start of the Sheets & Databases section.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-api/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

   The **Developers** section has **Webhook** and **AWS**. **Supabase** is in **Sheets & Databases**, and **BankSync** is in **Budgeting**.
4. Tap the destination.
5. If WalletFeed shows **WalletFeed Pro**, get WalletFeed Pro. Then WalletFeed shows the setup screen of the destination.

## Step 3: Connect the destination

Do the steps for your destination. WalletFeed keeps each URL, key and secret in the Keychain on your iPhone.

### Webhook

1. **Optional:** In **Name**, type a different name for the destination.

   ![The Webhook screen in WalletFeed, with Name, the URL field, Authorization (Optional), Share Signing Secret, Send Test and the steps.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-api/walletfeed-setup-webhook.webp)
2. Type the HTTPS URL of your server in the field that shows `https://example.com/hook`.
3. If your server must get an `Authorization` header, type its value in **Authorization (Optional)**.
4. Tap **Share Signing Secret**. iOS shows the share sheet.
5. Tap **Copy**, or send the secret to your computer, for example with AirDrop.
6. Add the secret to your server. Your server uses the secret to make sure that WalletFeed sent each request.
7. Tap **Send Test**. Your server receives a request with the type `walletfeed.test` and one test transaction.
8. Tap **Add**.

For the JSON fields and the signature check, refer to [Webhook format](/docs/webhooks/). WalletFeed uses [Standard Webhooks](https://www.standardwebhooks.com) signatures.

### AWS

For DynamoDB, the table must have a String partition key with the name `id`, and no sort key.

WalletFeed accepts only the access key of an IAM user. It does not accept temporary keys that have a session token.

1. In **Service**, select **Amazon S3**, **Amazon SQS**, **Kinesis Data Streams**, **DynamoDB** or **EventBridge**.

   ![The AWS screen in WalletFeed, with Service set to Amazon S3, and the Access Key ID, Secret Access Key, Region, Endpoint, Bucket, Prefix and Format fields.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-api/walletfeed-setup-amazon-s3.webp)
2. If your service is not in the AWS region `us-east-1`, type its region in **Region**.
3. If you use Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2 or a different service that is compatible with S3, type its URL in **Endpoint**.
4. Type the value for your service in **Bucket**, **Queue URL**, **Stream**, **Table** or **Event Bus**.
5. Tap **Share IAM Policy**.
6. Send the policy to your computer, for example with AirDrop.
7. On your computer, open [IAM in the AWS console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/iam/home#/users).
8. Make an IAM user that has the policy from WalletFeed.
9. Make an access key for the user.
10. Send the access key ID and the secret access key to your iPhone, for example with AirDrop.
11. In WalletFeed, paste the access key ID in **Access Key ID**.
12. Paste the secret access key in **Secret Access Key**.
13. Tap **Add**. WalletFeed does a test before it adds the destination.

For the test, WalletFeed writes and deletes a test file in S3. For DynamoDB, it makes sure that the table has the correct partition key. SQS, Kinesis Data Streams and EventBridge receive one test event.

### Supabase

1. In your Supabase project, open the **Connect** dialog.
2. If the project has no publishable key, make one in **Settings** › **API Keys**.
3. Copy the project URL and the publishable key. The key starts with `sb_publishable_`.
4. If Supabase is open on your computer, send the URL and the key to your iPhone, for example with AirDrop.
5. In WalletFeed, paste the key in **Publishable Key**.

   ![The Supabase screen in WalletFeed, with the Publishable Key field, the project URL field, Share SQL and the steps.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-api/walletfeed-setup-supabase.webp)
6. Paste the project URL in the field below the key. When this field is empty, it shows `https://abcd.supabase.co`.
7. Tap **Share SQL**.
8. Tap **Copy**, or send the SQL to your computer, for example with AirDrop.
9. Paste the SQL in the **SQL Editor** of your Supabase project.
10. Click **Run**.
11. In WalletFeed, tap **Add**.

The SQL makes the table `walletfeed_transactions`. It also adds a policy that lets only this destination read and write the table. WalletFeed does not accept a secret key, which starts with `sb_secret_`.

### BankSync

1. Tap **Sign In with BankSync**.

   ![The BankSync screen in WalletFeed, with Sign In with BankSync and Use an API Key Instead.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-api/walletfeed-setup-banksync.webp)
2. On the BankSync page, tap **Continue with Google**, or type your email address in **Email** and tap **Continue with email**.

   ![The BankSync sign-in page with Continue with Google, an Email field and Continue with email.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-api/banksync-sign-in-with-banksync.webp)
3. If BankSync has no account for your email address, do the steps on the BankSync page to make one.
4. Give your approval to WalletFeed as the owner or an admin of the workspace. BankSync makes the **Apple Card** table, and WalletFeed shows **Signed In**.
5. Tap **Add**.

The **Sign In with BankSync** button uses WalletFeed's referral link. Below the button, WalletFeed shows the message "WalletFeed may earn a commission if you pay for BankSync."

On the Free plan, a workspace can have only one table. If the workspace has a different table, BankSync cannot make the **Apple Card** table. Then WalletFeed shows **Try Again** and **Open BankSync**.

As an alternative, you can tap **Use an API Key Instead**. API keys are available only on BankSync's Standard plan or a higher plan. In BankSync, the keys are in **Settings** › **Developers** › **API Keys**. [Send Apple Card transactions to BankSync](/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/) gives the steps for an API key.

## Step 4: Start to send transactions

After you tap **Add**, WalletFeed shows a message before it sends data. The message tells you the data that the destination receives. It also gives the accounts and the start date. For a webhook, the title of the message is "Send Transactions to Your Server?"

1. Read the message.
2. Tap **Send**. WalletFeed adds the destination and starts to send your transactions.

If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed does not add the destination.

## Transaction data

Each destination receives this data for a transaction:

- An ID that stays the same when the transaction changes
- The account name, for example Apple Card
- The date, the currency and the value of the transaction
- The description, the merchant name and the merchant category code (MCC), if Wallet has them
- The WalletFeed category, for example groceries or travel
- The status in Wallet, for example `pending` or `booked`
- For a purchase in a different currency, the value in that currency.

The table that follows gives the value of a purchase at each destination, and what WalletFeed does when Wallet removes a transaction.

| Destination | Value of a purchase | Removed transaction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Webhook** | A number more than zero, with `direction` set to `debit` | WalletFeed puts the ID of the transaction in `deletedIDs`. |
| **Amazon S3** | A number less than zero | WalletFeed writes the file of the month again, without the transaction. |
| **Amazon SQS**, **Kinesis Data Streams**, **EventBridge** | A number less than zero | WalletFeed sends an event with `event` set to `deleted` and only the `id`. |
| **DynamoDB** | A number less than zero | WalletFeed deletes the item. |
| **Supabase** | A number less than zero | WalletFeed deletes the row. |
| **BankSync** | A number less than zero | WalletFeed deletes the row, and BankSync moves it to its trash. |

If you do not change **Prefix** or **Format**, the S3 file for October 2026 is `walletfeed/transactions/2026-10.csv`.

In EventBridge, the `source` of each event is `app.walletfeed`. The `detail-type` is `Transaction Created`, `Transaction Updated` or `Transaction Deleted`.

Your transactions go from your iPhone directly to your server or service. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. After a service has the data, the terms of that service are applicable to the data.

## Sync times and pending charges

- While WalletFeed is open, a destination receives changes in seconds.
- When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. This occurs only if [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**. **Background Sync** is on until you set it to off.
- A pending charge has the status `pending` or `authorized`. When the status changes to `booked`, the destination receives the transaction again, with the same ID and the value of the booked transaction.
- WalletFeed removes declined charges, expired charges and the transactions that Wallet removes.
- A refund is a different transaction. Its type is `refund`.
- For a webhook, if your server does not send a status code from 200 to 299, WalletFeed sends the same changes again at the next sync.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. WalletFeed sends the transactions from the last date to the first date.

To send previous transactions again, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Send History**.
4. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

While WalletFeed sends the history, you can stop it:

1. Tap **Send History**.
2. Tap **Stop Sending**.

WalletFeed can send only the transactions that iOS lets it read. To let WalletFeed read more previous transactions, change the start date in the Settings app, in **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.

## Change or stop the destination

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.

Then do one of these steps:

- To send only some transactions, set **Filter** to on (refer to [Choose what a destination receives](/docs/choose-what-to-send/)).
- To stop the destination for a period, set **Enabled** to off.
- To change the URL or the `Authorization` value of a webhook, tap **URL** or **Authorization**.
- To use a new AWS, Supabase or BankSync API key, tap **Replace Key**.

To remove the destination:

1. Tap **Delete**. WalletFeed shows the message "Transactions already sent stay at the destination."
2. Tap **Delete** again.

To remove the transactions that WalletFeed sent, delete them on your server or in the service.

## If something goes wrong

### If WalletFeed shows "Wallet Access Off"

WalletFeed cannot read Wallet, because you tapped **Don't Share** or you stopped its access in the Settings app.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select the accounts that WalletFeed can read.
4. Open WalletFeed.

### If WalletFeed does not show your Apple Card transactions

You did not select your Apple Card when iOS showed your Wallet accounts, or you are a participant in Apple Card Family. FinanceKit does not give participants access to the Apple Card account.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select your Apple Card.
4. Open WalletFeed.

### If the destination shows "Authentication failed"

Your server or the service did not accept the key, the sign-in or the `Authorization` value. The HTTP status code was 401 or 403.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.

   ![The Destinations list, with the destination n8n, which shows Authentication failed.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-api/walletfeed-destinations-failure.webp)
2. Tap the destination.

   ![The screen of the webhook destination n8n, with Authentication failed below Last Sync, and the URL and Authorization rows.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-api/walletfeed-destination-failure.webp)
3. Do the steps for your destination:

   - For a webhook, tap **Authorization**. Type the correct value. Then tap **Save**.
   - For AWS, tap **Replace Key**. Paste the access key ID and the secret access key. Then tap **Replace**.
   - For Supabase or a BankSync API key, tap **Replace Key**. Paste the correct key. Then tap **Replace**.
   - For Sign In with BankSync, tap **Sign In Again**.

4. Tap **Send Test**.

### If the destination shows "Can't connect"

WalletFeed did not get a response from your server or the service.

1. Make sure that your iPhone can connect to the internet.
2. For a webhook, make sure that your server is on and that it accepts HTTPS requests.
3. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
4. Tap the destination.
5. For a webhook, tap **URL** to make sure that the URL is correct.
6. Tap **Send Test**.

### If AWS shows "Wrong region for this bucket."

The S3 bucket is in a different AWS region.

1. In **Region**, type the region of the bucket.
2. Tap **Add**.

### If AWS shows "Key rejected"

AWS did not accept the access key, or the IAM policy of the user does not include the necessary action.

1. On your computer, open IAM.
2. Make sure that the user has the policy from **Share IAM Policy**.
3. In WalletFeed, paste the access key ID in **Access Key ID** again.
4. Paste the secret access key in **Secret Access Key** again.
5. Tap **Add**.

### If your software receives an event two times

SQS, Kinesis Data Streams and EventBridge can receive the same event again. This occurs when WalletFeed sends the same changes again. A FIFO queue in SQS removes the second copy of an event if the queue receives it 5 minutes or less after the first copy.

1. In the software that reads the events, use the `id` of the transaction as the key.
2. If an event has the same `event` and `status` as the last event for that `id`, ignore the event.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-shortcuts/ -->
# Run a shortcut after each Apple Card purchase

A Shortcuts automation on your iPhone can send each of your Apple Card purchases to your WalletFeed destinations in seconds. In Shortcuts, it is a **Transaction** automation. It starts when you tap your iPhone to pay with your Apple Card or Apple Cash card.

iOS does not let apps make automations. You make the automation one time in the Shortcuts app. WalletFeed shows the steps.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version
- WalletFeed, with access to your Wallet accounts
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase
- One or more [destinations](/docs/destinations/) in WalletFeed, for example Google Sheets or Lunch Money
- Your Apple Card or Apple Cash card in Wallet on your iPhone
- The Shortcuts app on your iPhone.

WalletFeed is available only in the US. You must have WalletFeed Pro to send transactions to destinations.

## Step 1: Open Automations in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.

   Result: WalletFeed shows **Settings**.
3. If **Settings** does not show **Sync**, get WalletFeed Pro. Refer to [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/).
4. Below **Sync**, tap **Automations**.

   ![WalletFeed Settings with Background Sync and Automations below Sync.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-shortcuts/walletfeed-settings.webp)

   Result: WalletFeed shows **Automations**. **After Each Card Tap** is at the top of the screen.

## Step 2: Make the automation in Shortcuts

In **After Each Card Tap**, WalletFeed shows the steps for your iPhone. The steps for iOS 26, iOS 27 and iOS 27 with Apple Intelligence are different. Do only the procedure that is applicable to your iPhone.

### iOS 27 with Apple Intelligence

On iOS 27 with Apple Intelligence, Shortcuts can make a shortcut from text that you give it. WalletFeed gives you the text. In WalletFeed, step 1 is **Copy Description**.

1. In **After Each Card Tap**, tap **Copy Description**.

   ![The Automations screen with Copy Description and its text below After Each Card Tap.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-shortcuts/walletfeed-automations.webp)

   Result: WalletFeed copies the text below **Copy Description** and shows **Copied**. The text is "When I tap my Apple Card or Apple Cash card, run Sync New Purchase from WalletFeed without asking."
2. Tap **Open Shortcuts**.

   Result: The Shortcuts app opens.
3. Tap **+**.

   Result: Shortcuts shows a new shortcut. You can type the task that the shortcut must do.
4. Paste the text.
5. Make sure that the shortcut uses your Apple Card or Apple Cash card.
6. Tap the arrow adjacent to the trigger at the top of the shortcut.
7. Make sure that **Confirm Before Run** is off.
8. Tap **Done**.

If Shortcuts does not let you type the task that the shortcut must do, do these steps:

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Set It Up Yourself**.
2. Below **Set It Up Yourself**, tap **Open Shortcuts**.
3. Do steps 2 to 11 in [iOS 27 without Apple Intelligence](#ios-27-without-apple-intelligence).

### iOS 27 without Apple Intelligence

On iOS 27, an automation is a trigger at the top of a shortcut. In WalletFeed, step 1 is **Open Shortcuts**, and **Describe It Instead** is below the steps.

1. In **After Each Card Tap**, tap **Open Shortcuts**.

   Result: Shortcuts opens a new shortcut.
2. Tap **Add Action**.
3. Type WalletFeed in the search field.
4. Tap **Sync New Purchase**.
5. In the action list, tap **Automation** › **Transaction**.
6. Select your cards.
7. Tap the arrow adjacent to the trigger.
8. Set **Confirm Before Run** to off.
9. Tap the information button **ⓘ** › **Privacy**.
10. Set **Allow Running When Locked** to on.
11. Tap **Done**.

### iOS 26

On iOS 26, automations have a tab in Shortcuts. Your other devices do not get these automations. In WalletFeed, step 1 is **Open Shortcuts**.

1. In **After Each Card Tap**, tap **Open Shortcuts**.

   Result: The Shortcuts app opens.
2. Tap **Automation**.
3. If you have no automations, tap **New Automation**.
4. If you have one or more automations, tap **+**.
5. Tap **Transaction**.
6. Select your cards.
7. Select **Run Immediately**.
8. Tap **Next**.
9. Tap **New Blank Automation** › **Add Action**.
10. Type WalletFeed in the search field.
11. Tap **Sync New Purchase**.
12. Tap **Done**.
13. If you use WalletFeed on a different iPhone, do this procedure on that iPhone also.

## Step 3: Make sure that the automation operates

After you tap your iPhone to pay with your Apple Card or Apple Cash card, do these steps:

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. Below **Sync**, look at the value adjacent to **Automations**.

   Result: **Automations** shows **On** or **1 of 2**. The table that follows gives each value.
4. Tap **Automations**.
5. In **After Each Card Tap**, look at **Last Run**.

   Result: **Last Run** shows the time of the last operation of **Sync New Purchase**, for example "2 hr. ago".
6. If **Last Run** shows **Never**, refer to [If Last Run shows Never after a purchase](#if-last-run-shows-never-after-a-purchase).

**Automations** in **Settings** shows if each automation operated in its period. The period of **After Each Card Tap** is the last 14 days. The period of **Every Day** is the last 3 days. This table gives the values of **Automations**.

| **Automations** shows | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| **On** | Each automation on the **Automations** screen operated in its period. |
| **1 of 2** | Only one of the two automations operated in its period. |
| **Set Up** | No automation operated in its period, and **Background Sync** is off or **Sample Data** is on. |
| **Off** | **After Each Card Tap** did not operate in the last 14 days, **Background Sync** is on, and **Sample Data** is off. |

When **Background Sync** is on, the automation is optional. Without the automation, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet.

## Time to send each purchase

When you tap your iPhone to pay with your Apple Card or Apple Cash card, the automation starts **Sync New Purchase**. This WalletFeed action operates in the background. It does not open WalletFeed.

At that time, Wallet does not have the purchase. First, WalletFeed sends the changes that it did not send previously. Then it waits for Wallet to record the purchase. When Wallet records the purchase, WalletFeed sends the purchase to your destinations.

WalletFeed waits for the purchase until 18 seconds after the action starts. If Wallet records the purchase after that time, WalletFeed sends it at the next sync. While WalletFeed is open, it sends each change in seconds. When WalletFeed is closed and **Background Sync** is on, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. Refer to [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/).

The automation starts only when you tap your iPhone to pay. WalletFeed sends other changes at the next sync, for example online purchases and posted charges. Your Savings account has no card. Thus, the automation does not start for Savings transactions.

The automation does not change the data that WalletFeed sends to your destinations. WalletFeed also uses the filter of each destination. Refer to [filters for destinations](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).

After your iPhone starts again, WalletFeed cannot send to destinations until you type your passcode one time.

When the action stops, it gives a short message. Shortcuts can show the message as a notification. This table gives the messages.

| Message | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| "Changes sent: 2." | WalletFeed sent 2 changes. The number is the total for all your destinations. |
| "Nothing new yet." | WalletFeed did not find a new change to send. |
| "Changes sent: 1. One destination needs attention." | WalletFeed cannot send to one destination. If two or more destinations have a problem, the message gives the number of these destinations. |
| "Sync requires WalletFeed Pro." | WalletFeed Pro is not active on this iPhone. |
| "Open WalletFeed and allow Wallet access." | WalletFeed does not have access to your Wallet accounts. |
| "Add a destination in WalletFeed first." | WalletFeed has no destination that is on. |

To correct a problem, refer to [If there is a problem](#if-there-is-a-problem).

## Send other changes each day

If **Background Sync** is off, **Automations** also shows **Every Day**. An **Every Day** automation starts **Sync Transactions** at a time that you select. This action sends new and changed transactions to your destinations, for example online purchases and posted charges.

For **Every Day**, the text to paste is "Every day at 9 PM, run Sync Transactions from WalletFeed without asking."

To make the automation, do [Step 2](#step-2-make-the-automation-in-shortcuts) with these changes:

- Use the steps below **Every Day** in WalletFeed.
- If you paste the text, make sure that the time in Shortcuts is correct.
- Tap **Sync Transactions**, not **Sync New Purchase**.
- Tap **Time of Day**, not **Transaction**.
- Select a time, not your cards.

If **Background Sync** is on, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. Thus, WalletFeed does not show **Every Day**. An **Every Day** automation that you made previously continues to operate.

## Stop or change the automation

iOS does not tell WalletFeed about your automations. To change the cards or the time, open the automation in the Shortcuts app.

To stop the automation, delete it in the Shortcuts app. After you delete it, WalletFeed sends new purchases at the next sync. The transactions that WalletFeed sent stay at each destination.

## Other WalletFeed actions in Shortcuts

WalletFeed has more actions for the Shortcuts app. For example, **Get Recent Card Transactions** gives your transactions from the last 7 days to the next action in a shortcut. You can change the number of days. Refer to [Siri and Shortcuts](/docs/siri-and-shortcuts/).

## If there is a problem

### If Last Run shows Never after a purchase

The automation did not start, or it did not start the WalletFeed action.

1. Open the Shortcuts app.
2. If you cannot find the automation, do [Step 2](#step-2-make-the-automation-in-shortcuts) again.
3. Make sure that the automation uses your Apple Card or Apple Cash card.
4. Make sure that the automation starts **Sync New Purchase**.
5. On iOS 26, make sure that the automation uses **Run Immediately**.
6. On iOS 27, make sure that **Confirm Before Run** is off.
7. On iOS 27, make sure that **Allow Running When Locked** is on.

### If the message is "Nothing new yet."

WalletFeed did not send the purchase before the action stopped. For example, Wallet recorded the purchase more than 18 seconds after the action started.

1. If the destination has a filter, make sure that the filter includes the purchase.
2. To send the purchase at this time, open WalletFeed.
3. If you do not open WalletFeed, wait for the next sync.

> **Note:** When WalletFeed is closed and **Background Sync** is on, the next sync occurs in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet.

### If the message is "Sync requires WalletFeed Pro."

WalletFeed Pro is not active on this iPhone.

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. Tap **WalletFeed Pro**.
4. If you got WalletFeed Pro previously, tap **Restore Purchases**.
5. If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, get it. Refer to [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/).

### If the message is "Open WalletFeed and allow Wallet access."

WalletFeed does not have access to your Wallet accounts.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select the accounts that WalletFeed can read. Refer to [Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/).
4. Open WalletFeed.

### If the message is "Add a destination in WalletFeed first."

WalletFeed has no destination that is on.

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. If a destination shows **Off**, do these steps:

   1. Tap the destination.
   2. Set **Enabled** to on.

4. If there is no destination, tap **+** to add a destination. Refer to [Destinations](/docs/destinations/).

### If the message includes "One destination needs attention."

WalletFeed cannot send to one or more destinations.

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Find the destination with the problem. Below its name, WalletFeed shows the cause, for example "Authentication failed".

   ![The Destinations screen with Authentication failed and a warning symbol for the n8n destination.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-shortcuts/walletfeed-destinations-failure.webp)
4. Tap the destination.
5. In the guide for that destination, do the steps for this cause. Refer to [Guides](/guides/).

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-spending-by-category/ -->
# See Apple Card spending by category

WalletFeed shows your Apple Card spending by category on your iPhone. The [**Spending**](/docs/spending/) tab shows this month's total, a chart with a bar for each day, the categories and the merchants with the largest totals.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- WalletFeed. You can use **Spending** without [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/).
- An iPhone that can use Apple Intelligence, with Apple Intelligence turned on. This is necessary only to see a different month.

## Step 1: Give WalletFeed access to your Apple Card

If WalletFeed shows your transactions, go to [Step 2](#step-2-read-the-total-for-this-month).

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. If WalletFeed shows **Welcome to WalletFeed**, tap **Continue**.

   ![The Welcome to WalletFeed screen with the Continue button at the bottom.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-spending-by-category/walletfeed-welcome.webp)

3. If WalletFeed shows **No Cards**, tap **Choose Accounts**.
4. When iOS shows your Wallet accounts, make sure that your Apple Card is on.

   ![The Share Wallet Data screen with Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings turned on.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-spending-by-category/walletfeed-wallet-access.webp)

5. Tap **Share**.

WalletFeed can read only the accounts that you share. You can change the accounts later in the Settings app, in **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.

## Step 2: Read the total for this month

1. Tap **Spending** at the bottom of the screen.

   ![The Spending screen with the October total of $1,317.68, a chart with a bar for each day and the top of Categories.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-spending-by-category/walletfeed-spending.webp)

2. To see the total for one day, touch the chart and move your finger to that day.

   **Spending** shows the date and the total for that day.

The top part of **Spending** shows these items:

- The name of the month and the total of your purchases in this month.
- An arrow and the change from the same time last month, for example "70% vs Sep".
- A chart with a bar for each day of the month. The line with the label "Avg $45" shows the average for each day, from the first day of the month to today.
- The Monthly Summary, a short text below the chart.

WalletFeed compares this month with the same days of last month. For example, on October 20, it compares October 1 to 20 with September 1 to 20.

If your iPhone can use Apple Intelligence, Apple Intelligence writes the Monthly Summary from the results that WalletFeed calculates. WalletFeed does not examine the text that Apple Intelligence writes. Without Apple Intelligence, WalletFeed writes the Monthly Summary. It usually gives the total and the change from last month.

To get the Monthly Summary from WalletFeed on an iPhone with Apple Intelligence, do these steps:

1. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In **Privacy & Security**, turn off **Summarize Spending**.

   ![Settings with Summarize Spending turned on in the Privacy & Security section.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-spending-by-category/walletfeed-settings-2.webp)

The Spending widget shows the total for this month and the total at the same time last month. You can put the widget on the Home Screen or the Lock Screen.

## Step 3: See the categories and the merchants

1. On **Spending**, scroll down to **Categories**.

   **Categories** shows a bar with one color for each category. Below the bar, each row shows a category and its total for this month.

2. Scroll down to **Merchants**.

   **Merchants** shows the five merchants with the largest totals this month.

   ![Spending with Other at the bottom of Categories, then Recurring Charges and Merchants.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-spending-by-category/walletfeed-recurring.webp)

In **Categories**, WalletFeed shows your five largest categories, then **Other**. **Other** is the total of the remaining categories and of the transactions without a category. Between **Categories** and **Merchants**, **Spending** can also show **Recurring Charges** and **Monthly Installments**.

## Step 4: See a different month

If your iPhone can use Apple Intelligence, with Apple Intelligence turned on, **Spending** has the field **Ask about your spending** at the top. The name of this feature is [Ask Spending](/docs/ask-spending/). Without Apple Intelligence, **Spending** shows only this month.

1. Tap **Ask about your spending**.
2. Type what you want to see, for example `Spending by category last month`.
3. Tap **Go** on the keyboard.

   The result has a chart with a bar for each category. Below the chart, WalletFeed shows **Categories**, **Merchants** and the transactions.

4. To see one category, type the category and a period, for example `Dining this month vs last`.
5. Tap **Go**.

   ![The result for Dining this month vs last, with 9 transactions, a total of $188.70 and a line chart of this month and last month.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-spending-by-category/walletfeed-ask-spending.webp)

6. To see this month again, tap **Clear** (the x button) in the field.

Above the result, WalletFeed shows how it read your text, for example "Dining · This month · vs last month". When no result shows, WalletFeed shows an example below the field. If you tap the example, WalletFeed puts its text in the field.

You can type a period, for example `today`, `this week`, `last 30 days`, `last month`, `last 3 months`, `this year` or the name of a month. To compare with last month, you can add `vs last month`.

Apple Intelligence operates on your iPhone. When it reads what you type, it gets only that text. WalletFeed calculates the totals, the charts and the lists. Apple Intelligence then writes the short text below the chart from the results that WalletFeed calculates.

## See the transactions in a category

1. Tap **Search** at the bottom of the screen.
2. In **Categories**, tap a category.

   Search puts the name of the category in the search field and shows the transactions that it finds, by month. Search looks at all the transactions that you share.

3. If your iPhone can use Apple Intelligence, type a category and a period, for example `Groceries last month`.
4. Tap **Search** on the keyboard.

   Above the transactions, Search shows the number of transactions and their total.

   ![Search with the result Groceries · Over $50.00 · Last 30 days, 4 transactions and a total of $277.57.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-spending-by-category/walletfeed-search.webp)

## Categories and totals

WalletFeed sets the category of each transaction from its merchant category code (MCC). Wallet supplies the MCC with the transaction. If a transaction has no MCC, or an MCC that WalletFeed does not know, its category is **Other**.

WalletFeed uses these categories:

- **Groceries**
- **Dining**
- **Transport**
- **Fuel**
- **Travel**
- **Shopping**
- **Entertainment**
- **Subscriptions**
- **Utilities**
- **Health**
- **Services**
- **Cash & Transfers**
- **Other**

These rules apply to all the totals in **Spending**:

- WalletFeed adds purchases and fees, and subtracts refunds.
- Transfers and payments are not in the totals.
- Pending purchases are in the totals. Declined purchases are not.
- The totals include the purchases from all the Wallet accounts that you share, for example Apple Cash.

WalletFeed reads your transactions from Wallet on your iPhone when it shows **Spending**. It does not keep a copy of them.

## If something goes wrong

### If Spending shows "Wallet Access Off"

WalletFeed does not have access to Wallet. After the first time, you can give access only in the Settings app.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Go to **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet**.
3. Give WalletFeed access to your Apple Card.

### If Spending shows "No Spending"

WalletFeed found no purchases for this month in the accounts that you share. This can occur on the first days of a month.

1. If your iPhone can use Apple Intelligence, type `Spending by category last month` in **Ask about your spending**.
2. Tap **Go**.
3. To share more Wallet accounts, go to **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** in the Settings app.

### If Spending shows "Couldn't Read Wallet"

WalletFeed did not get your transactions from Wallet. In **Ask about your spending**, the same problem shows as "Couldn't read Wallet. Pull down to try again."

1. Pull down on **Spending**.

WalletFeed then reads Wallet again.

### If Spending does not show "Ask about your spending"

This field shows only on an iPhone that can use Apple Intelligence, with Apple Intelligence turned on.

1. Make sure that your iPhone can use Apple Intelligence.
2. In the Settings app on your iPhone, turn on Apple Intelligence.

Without Apple Intelligence, **Spending** shows this month. **Search** shows the transactions in a category.

### If WalletFeed shows "Couldn't read this."

WalletFeed could not read your text, or WalletFeed cannot show that result. WalletFeed cannot show these results:

- Two categories compared with each other, for example `Dining vs Groceries`.
- A result that does not include a category or a merchant, for example `not Uber` or `except Dining`.
- Two limits for a purchase, for example `over $20 and under $50`.

To get a result, do these steps:

1. Type a shorter text with one category and one period, for example `Travel this year`.
2. Tap **Go**.

### If a previous month shows no transactions

Wallet shares the history of an account only from the date that you selected when you gave access.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Go to **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Share more of the history of your Apple Card.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-spending-widget/ -->
# Add an Apple Card spending widget

The WalletFeed [Spending widget](/docs/spending-widget/) shows your Apple Card spending for this month on the Home Screen or the Lock Screen of your iPhone. It compares this total with the same day and time last month, and you can use it without [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/).

## Before you start

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- Your Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account in Wallet on your iPhone.
- WalletFeed, from the App Store.

WalletFeed Pro and destinations are not necessary for the widget.

## Step 1: Give WalletFeed access to Wallet

The widget shows totals only after WalletFeed gets [access to your Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/) and reads your transactions. If WalletFeed shows your transactions, go to Step 2.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. If WalletFeed shows **Welcome to WalletFeed**, tap **Continue**.

   ![The Welcome to WalletFeed screen with the Continue button at the bottom.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-spending-widget/walletfeed-welcome.webp)

3. For each account to include, set the switch to on.

   ![The Share Wallet Data screen with switches for Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings, and the Share button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-spending-widget/walletfeed-wallet-access.webp)

4. Tap **Share**.

WalletFeed then reads your transactions and calculates the totals for the widget.

## Step 2: Add the widget to the Home Screen

1. On your iPhone, go to the Home Screen page for the widget.
2. Touch and hold an empty area of the screen until the apps move.
3. Tap **Edit** at the top of the screen.
4. Tap **Add Widget**.
5. In the search field, type `WalletFeed`.
6. Tap **WalletFeed**.
7. Swipe to the small or the medium **Spending** widget.
8. Tap **Add Widget**.
9. To move the widget, drag it to a different position.
10. Tap **Done**.

> **Note:** The **Sync Status** widget in the same list shows the status of destinations, which are part of WalletFeed Pro.

## Add the widget to the Lock Screen

On the Lock Screen, the **Spending** widget can be below the time or above it.

1. Push the side button of your iPhone two times.
2. Touch and hold the Lock Screen until **Customize** shows at the bottom of the screen.
3. Tap **Customize**.
4. If iOS shows the Lock Screen and the Home Screen, tap the Lock Screen.
5. Select a position for the widget:
   - For the widget below the time, tap **Add Widgets**, or the widgets that are there.
   - For the one-line widget above the time, tap the date above the time.
6. Tap **WalletFeed**.
7. Tap the **Spending** widget.
8. Tap **Done**.

## Totals in each widget

The **Spending** widgets show these totals:

| Widget | Position | Totals |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Small | Home Screen | The **This Month** total, with the **Same Point Last Month** total below it. |
| Medium | Home Screen | The **This Month** and **Same Point Last Month** totals, and the change from last month, for example “↓ 14% vs Sep”. |
| Rectangular | Lock Screen, below the time | The total for this month and the change from last month. |
| One line | Lock Screen, above the time | The total for this month, for example “$1,234.56 this month”. |

The arrow points down if the **This Month** total is less than the **Same Point Last Month** total. If the **Same Point Last Month** total is 0, the widget does not show the change.

The widget shows the same totals as the [Spending](/docs/spending/) tab in WalletFeed. The total for this month starts on the first day of the month. The total for last month is from the first day of last month to the same day and time last month. Purchases and other charges increase the totals, and refunds decrease them. The totals do not include transfers, payments or declined purchases.

The totals include each account that you gave WalletFeed access to in Step 1. When a new month starts, the widget shows 0 for this month, without the other totals, until WalletFeed updates it.

To see the same totals with a chart for each day:

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Spending**.

   ![The Spending tab with the total for October, the change from September and a chart for each day.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-spending-widget/walletfeed-spending.webp)

## Widget updates

WalletFeed updates the widget when you open WalletFeed. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. WalletFeed then updates the widget.

WalletFeed Pro and [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) are not necessary for these updates.

## Data in the widget

For the widget, WalletFeed keeps only two totals on your iPhone, with their currency and the time of the update. The widget has no transactions, merchants or categories. iOS also keeps the data that the widget shows.

While your iPhone is locked, iOS can show the widget without the totals and the change.

## Change or remove the widget

To change the accounts in the totals:

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security**.
3. Tap **Wallet**.
4. Tap **WalletFeed**.
5. For each account, set the switch to on or off.

If you set all the switches to off, WalletFeed clears the totals from the widget the next time that it starts.

To remove the widget from the Home Screen:

1. Touch and hold the widget.
2. Tap **Remove Widget**.
3. If iOS shows a message, tap **Remove**.

To change the small widget to the medium widget, remove it. Then add the medium widget, as in Step 2.

To remove the widget from the Lock Screen:

1. Touch and hold the Lock Screen until **Customize** shows at the bottom of the screen.
2. Tap **Customize**.
3. Tap the widgets below the time.
4. Tap **−** on the **Spending** widget.
5. Tap **Done**.

## If something goes wrong

### If the widget shows “Open WalletFeed to see your spending.”

WalletFeed did not read your transactions in Wallet, or it does not have access to Wallet. The one-line widget shows only “Open WalletFeed”.

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Transactions**.

If **Transactions** shows your transactions, WalletFeed updated the widget when it opened. If **Transactions** shows **No Cards**, do these steps:

1. Tap **Choose Accounts**.
2. For each account to include, set the switch to on.
3. Tap **Share**.

If **Transactions** shows **Wallet Access Off**, do the steps in the next section.

### If WalletFeed shows “Wallet Access Off”

WalletFeed does not have access to Wallet, and iOS shows the question about Wallet access only one time.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security**.
3. Tap **Wallet**.
4. Tap **WalletFeed**.
5. For each account to include, set the switch to on.
6. Open WalletFeed.

### If the widget does not show a new purchase

WalletFeed did not update the widget after the purchase. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet.

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. Go to the Home Screen.

WalletFeed updates the widget when it opens.

### If the widget shows totals that are not yours

**Sample Data** is on, so the widget shows the totals of the sample transactions.

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. Set **Sample Data** to off.

WalletFeed then clears the sample totals and calculates your totals from Wallet.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/ -->
# Import Apple Card transactions into Actual Budget

To import Apple Card transactions into Actual Budget, WalletFeed saves them from your iPhone to iCloud Drive as one OFX file for each month. Then, on a computer, you import the file into an Apple Card account in Actual Budget.

## Before you start

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- Apple Card in Wallet on that iPhone, and WalletFeed with [access to your Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/).
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), which is necessary for destinations. WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.
- iCloud Drive on your iPhone.
- A computer with access to your iCloud Drive. On a Mac, iCloud Drive is in Finder. On Windows, you can use iCloud for Windows or iCloud.com.
- Actual Budget, open in a web browser on that computer.

Actual Budget does not show the **Import** button on a phone screen. Thus, you import the files on a computer.

## Step 1: Add an OFX file in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with no destinations and the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In the **Destinations** search field, type `Actual`.

   ![The Add Destination screen with the Destinations search field above the Budgeting list.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

5. Tap **OFX File**.

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, the **WalletFeed Pro** screen opens. After you get WalletFeed Pro, the **Files** screen opens.

6. Make sure that **Format** is **OFX**.

   ![The Files screen with Format set to OFX, the Folder row, the name WalletFeed and three steps.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/walletfeed-setup-ofx-file.webp)

   Do not use **QIF** for Actual Budget. A QIF file has no transaction IDs. If you import a QIF file two times, Actual Budget adds each transaction two times.

7. Tap **Folder**.
8. Select a folder in iCloud Drive.

   The name of the folder shows next to **Folder**. You open this folder on your computer in Step 3.

9. To use a different name for the files, type it in **Name**.

   Each month has one file. The files get names such as `WalletFeed 2026-10.ofx`.

10. Tap **Add**.
11. When WalletFeed shows **Save Transactions to Files?**, tap **Save**.

    The message tells you which data the folder receives, from which accounts and from which date. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes the new destination.

WalletFeed adds the destination to **Destinations** with the name **WalletFeed**, or the name that you typed. Then it writes a file for each month that has posted transactions.

If WalletFeed has access to Apple Cash or Savings, the files also contain their transactions. To write only Apple Card transactions, refer to [Change or remove the destination](#change-or-remove-the-destination).

## Step 2: Make an Apple Card account in Actual Budget

You do this step one time.

1. On your computer, open Actual Budget in a web browser.
2. If Actual Budget shows **Sign in to this Actual instance**, sign in with the password of your server.
3. If Actual Budget shows **Welcome to Actual**, click **Start budgeting**.

   ![The Actual Budget welcome page with the Start budgeting button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/actual-budget-start-budgeting.webp)

   Actual Budget makes a budget with the name **My Finances**. Do not click **Import my budget**, because that link is not for OFX files.

4. At the bottom of the sidebar, click **Add account**.

   ![The Actual Budget sidebar with the Add account button at the bottom.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/actual-budget-add-account.webp)

5. Click **Create a local account**.

   ![The Add account dialog with the Create a local account button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/actual-budget-create-local-account.webp)

6. In **Name:**, type `Apple Card`.
7. Make sure that **Off budget** is clear.

   You cannot change **Off budget** after you make the account.

8. Make sure that **Balance:** is `0`.
9. Click **Create**.

   ![The Create Local Account dialog with the name Apple Card, a clear Off budget box, a balance of 0 and the Create button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/actual-budget-account-name-apple-card.webp)

Actual Budget opens the **Apple Card** account page. The sidebar shows **Apple Card** below **On budget**.

## Step 3: Import the file in Actual Budget

Do these steps each time that you want the new transactions in Actual Budget.

> **Note:** On a phone screen, Actual Budget does not show **Import**.

1. On your computer, in the Actual Budget sidebar, click **Apple Card**.

   Actual Budget puts all the transactions from the file into the account that is open.

2. Click **Import**.

   ![The Apple Card account page in Actual Budget with the Import button above the empty list of transactions.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/actual-budget-account-import-button.webp)

3. In the window that your browser opens, go to the folder in iCloud Drive that you selected in Step 1.
4. Open the file of the month, such as `WalletFeed 2026-10.ofx`.

   You can open only one file at a time. Do not open `WalletFeed Test.ofx`, because it has only a sample transaction.

5. In **Import transactions (OFX)**, make sure that each new transaction has a blue **+** icon.
6. Click **Import 6 transactions**.

   ![The Import transactions (OFX) window with six new Apple Card transactions and the Import 6 transactions button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/actual-budget-import-preview.webp)

   The number in the button is the number of new transactions. It is not necessary to change the check boxes below the list.

7. Make sure that the transactions show on the **Apple Card** page.

   ![The Apple Card account in Actual Budget with six imported transactions in the Payment and Deposit columns.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/actual-budget-imported-transactions.webp)

   At the top of the page, Actual Budget shows the number of transactions without a category, such as **6 uncategorized transactions**.

## Import the same month again

WalletFeed updates the file of the month when your transactions change. You can import the file again at any time, also before the end of the month. Actual Budget uses the ID of each transaction to find the transactions that you imported before. It adds only the new transactions.

1. In the Actual Budget sidebar, click **Apple Card**.
2. Click **Import**.
3. Open the file of the month again, such as `WalletFeed 2026-10.ofx`.
4. Make sure that only the new transactions have a blue **+** icon.

   ![The Import transactions (OFX) window with one new transaction, Shell, and six dim rows that Actual Budget has from before.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/actual-budget-reimport-updated-month.webp)

   The transactions that you imported before show as dim rows with a clear check box.

5. Click the import button, such as **Import 1 transactions**.

   ![The Apple Card account in Actual Budget with seven different transactions.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/actual-budget-after-second-import.webp)

A transaction goes into the file of the month of the purchase. A purchase at the end of a month can post in the next month. WalletFeed then adds it to the file of the month of the purchase. Thus, import the file of each month again some days after the end of the month.

## Data that Actual Budget receives

Each OFX file has the posted transactions of one month. This table shows the column in Actual Budget for each Wallet field.

| Wallet | Actual Budget |
| --- | --- |
| Posted date | **Date**. This date can be one day after the date of the purchase in Wallet. |
| Merchant, or the description if Wallet has no merchant | **Payee**, with 32 characters at most |
| Description, card statement text and the value in a foreign currency | **Notes** |
| A purchase or a fee | **Payment**, without a minus sign |
| A refund, a payment or a deposit | **Deposit** |
| Transaction ID | Not shown. Actual Budget uses it to find the transactions that you imported before. |
| Category | Not in the file. **Category** shows **Categorize**. |

Purchases make the balance of the **Apple Card** account less than zero, such as -549.61.

When Actual Budget adds a new payee, it can change the letters of the name. For example, NETFLIX.COM 866-579 becomes Netflix.Com 866-579.

If **Notes** shows the same text as **Payee**, you can clear **Import notes from file** in the import window. Then **Notes** stays empty. Actual Budget then does not import the card statement text or the foreign value.

If WalletFeed has access to more than one Wallet account, each file has the transactions of all these accounts. Actual Budget puts all of them into the account that is open.

WalletFeed writes the files only to the folder that you select. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers.

## Changes to the files

While WalletFeed is open, the file of the month receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. For this, [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) must be on in **Settings** › **Sync**. If WalletFeed cannot open the folder at that time, the file changes the next time that you open WalletFeed, or while your iPhone charges.

Actual Budget gets the changes only when you import the file again.

WalletFeed writes only posted transactions to an OFX file. A pending charge goes into the file after it posts, with the same ID. A declined charge does not post, so it is not in the file. A refund is a different transaction, in **Deposit**.

If Wallet deletes a transaction, WalletFeed removes it from the file. If you imported the transaction before, delete it in Actual Budget.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. WalletFeed then writes a file for each month with posted transactions. You can import only the months that you want.

To change **Initial History**, do these steps before you add the destination:
