1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In **Sync**, tap **Initial History**, then select **Today**, **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

   ![Settings, with Initial History set to All in the Sync section.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/walletfeed-settings.webp)

To write the files of previous months again, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. In **Destinations**, tap your OFX destination, such as **WalletFeed**.
2. Tap **Send History**, then select **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

WalletFeed writes the file of each month in that period again. When you import a file again, Actual Budget adds only the transactions that it does not have.

## Change or remove the destination

In **Destinations**, tap your OFX destination. Then use this table:

| Change | On the destination screen |
| --- | --- |
| Stop the changes to the files for a time | Set **Enabled** to off. |
| Write only Apple Card transactions | Set **Filter** to on, then select Apple Card in **Accounts**. Then tap **Send History** › **All**. |
| Write only some transactions | Set **Filter** to on. Then set **Include**, **Minimum**, **Accounts**, **Categories** or **Exclude**. |
| Use a different folder | Tap **Change Folder**, then select the folder. WalletFeed then writes all the files again in the new folder. |
| Make sure that WalletFeed can write to the folder | Tap **Send Test**. The folder gets `WalletFeed Test.ofx` with a sample transaction. Do not import this file. |
| Remove the destination | Tap **Delete**, then tap **Delete** again. The files stay in the folder, and the transactions stay in Actual Budget. |

To import Apple Cash or Savings into a different account in Actual Budget, add one more **OFX File** destination with a different **Name**. Then set its filter to that Wallet account.

For more information about the filter, refer to [Choose what a destination receives](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).

## If there is a problem

### If Actual Budget does not show Import

**Import** shows only on the page of an account, and not on a phone screen.

1. Open Actual Budget in a web browser on a computer.
2. In the sidebar, click **Apple Card**.

### If the button shows “Import 0 transactions”

Actual Budget has all the transactions in the file. This is not an error.

1. Click **×** to close the window.

   ![When you import the same file again, Actual Budget shows all the rows as dim, and you cannot click Import 0 transactions.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/actual-budget-reimport-same-file.webp)

### If a transaction that you deleted in Actual Budget shows again

Actual Budget selects **Reimport deleted transactions** if you do not change it. Thus, it shows deleted transactions as new when you import a month again.

1. In **Import transactions (OFX)**, clear **Reimport deleted transactions**.

   ![With Reimport deleted transactions clear, the deleted Nopa transaction is dim and the button shows Import 0 transactions.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/actual-budget-reimport-deleted-off.webp)

   You can also clear the check box of the deleted transaction.

2. Click the import button. If it shows **Import 0 transactions**, click **×**.

### If Apple Cash or Savings transactions are in the Apple Card account

The file has the transactions of all the Wallet accounts that the destination receives, and Actual Budget puts them into the open account.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap your OFX destination, such as **WalletFeed**.
3. Set **Filter** to on.
4. Tap **Accounts**, then select Apple Card.
5. On the destination screen, tap **Send History**, then tap **All**.
6. In Actual Budget, delete the transactions that are not from Apple Card.

### If the dates are one day after the dates in Wallet

Actual Budget shows the date that the charge posted, and Wallet shows the date of the purchase. This is not an error.

### If a pending charge is not in Actual Budget

WalletFeed writes a charge to the file only after it posts.

1. After the charge posts in Wallet, import the file of the month again.

### If the folder has no file for a month

WalletFeed writes a file only for a month that has posted transactions.

1. In WalletFeed, open the destination.
2. Tap **Send Test**.

   The folder then gets `WalletFeed Test.ofx`. If this file is in the folder, WalletFeed can write there.

3. To write the files of all months, tap **Send History**, then tap **All**.

### If WalletFeed shows “Couldn't open this folder.”

WalletFeed cannot get access to the folder that you selected on the **Files** screen.

1. Tap **Folder**.
2. Select a different folder in iCloud Drive.

### If the destination shows “Can't open the folder. Choose it again.”

WalletFeed does not have access to the folder of the destination.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Change Folder**.
4. Select the folder again.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to Airtable

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a table in Airtable. You make a personal access token in Airtable, then paste it into WalletFeed.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- WalletFeed, with access to your Wallet accounts. Refer to [First steps with WalletFeed](/docs/get-started/).
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/). Destinations are part of WalletFeed Pro. WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.
- An Airtable account. You can make one at [airtable.com](https://airtable.com/signup).
- A web browser for the Airtable steps. The screenshots show Airtable on a computer.

> **Note:** A new Airtable account starts with a 14-day trial of the Team plan. On the Airtable Free plan, a base can contain a maximum of 1,000 records. Each workspace has a limit of 1,000 API calls each month.

## Step 1: Make a base in Airtable

A base is an Airtable database. If you have a base for your transactions, go to [Step 2](#step-2-make-a-personal-access-token-in-airtable).

1. On your computer, sign in to [Airtable](https://airtable.com).
2. On **Home**, click **+ Create** at the bottom of the sidebar.

   ![The Airtable Home page with the Create button at the bottom of the sidebar.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-home-create.webp)

3. Click **Build an app on your own**.

   ![The dialog "How do you want to start?" with the highlighted card "Build an app on your own".](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-build-on-your-own.webp)

   Airtable opens a new base with the name **Untitled Base**. In this dialog, Airtable uses "app" for a base. The other Airtable pages use "base".
4. If Airtable shows a message with a **Skip** or **Dismiss** button, click the button.
5. Click **Untitled Base**, at the top of the page.

   ![A new Airtable base with the highlighted name Untitled Base at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-new-base.webp)

6. Delete **Untitled Base** from the name box.

   Airtable puts the cursor after the old name. If you do not delete the old name, Airtable adds your text to it. The base then has the name `Untitled BaseWalletFeed`.
7. Type a name for the base, for example `WalletFeed`.

   ![The Airtable base panel with WalletFeed Docs as the new base name.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-rename-base.webp)

8. Press Return or Enter.

> **Note:** A new base can show an Omni panel on the left side. The **«** button closes the Omni panel.

> **Note:** The new base also has a table with the name **Table 1**. WalletFeed does not change this table.

## Step 2: Make a personal access token in Airtable

1. On your computer, open [Airtable](https://airtable.com).
2. On **Home**, click your account picture, in the top right corner.
3. Click **Builder hub**.

   ![The Airtable account menu with the highlighted Builder hub item.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-account-menu.webp)

   Airtable opens **Builder hub** in a new browser tab, on the **Personal access tokens** page.
4. Click **Create token**.

   ![The Personal access tokens page with the highlighted Create token button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-personal-access-tokens.webp)

5. In **Name**, type `WalletFeed`.

   ![The new token form with WalletFeed in the Name box.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-token-name.webp)

   Airtable shows this name in the revision history of the records that WalletFeed writes. The form also tells you not to give the token to third-party apps. Refer to [The Airtable text about third-party apps](#the-airtable-text-about-third-party-apps).
6. Below **Scopes**, click **+ Add a scope**.
7. In **Find a scope**, type `data.records`.
8. Select `data.records:read` and `data.records:write`.

   ![The scope list for data.records with the selected read and write scopes.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-scopes-records.webp)

9. In **Find a scope**, replace the text with `schema.bases`.
10. Select `schema.bases:read` and `schema.bases:write`.

    ![The scope list for schema.bases with the selected read and write scopes.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-scopes-schema.webp)

11. To close the list, press Esc.
12. Make sure that the four scopes show below **Scopes**.
13. Below **Access**, click **+ Add a base**.

    ![The token form with four scopes and the highlighted Add a base link.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-scopes-added.webp)

14. Click your base, below the name of its workspace.

    ![The base list with the highlighted WalletFeed Docs base.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-add-base.webp)

    The token has access only to this base. If you click **All current and future bases in this workspace**, the token gets access to all the bases in the workspace. WalletFeed uses this access only to add a new base when your base is full. Refer to [Send more than 1,000 transactions](#send-more-than-1-000-transactions).
15. Click **Create token**.

    ![The completed token form with the highlighted Create token button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-create-token.webp)

16. In the **Your token has been created** dialog, click the clipboard button on the right side of the token.

    ![The dialog "Your token has been created" with the highlighted clipboard button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-token-created.webp)

    Airtable shows the token only one time. You cannot click **Done** until you copy the token.
17. Click **Done**.
18. Do not copy other text until you paste the token in [Step 3](#step-3-add-airtable-in-walletfeed).

> **Note:** If you use a Mac with the same Apple Account as your iPhone, you can paste the token on the iPhone with [Universal Clipboard](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102430).

### The Airtable text about third-party apps

In the token form and in the token dialog, Airtable shows the text "Only use this token for your own development. Don't share it with third-party services and applications." WalletFeed is a third-party app. The list that follows gives information about the token in WalletFeed:

- WalletFeed keeps the token in the Keychain on your iPhone. The token does not go to iCloud Keychain.
- WalletFeed sends the token only in requests to the Airtable API. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. Your transactions go from your iPhone directly to Airtable.
- The token has access only to the base or the workspace that you added in [Step 2](#step-2-make-a-personal-access-token-in-airtable). It can do only the actions that its four scopes let it do.
- If you delete the token in Airtable, WalletFeed has no access to your base. Refer to [Change or stop the destination](#change-or-stop-the-destination).

## Step 3: Add Airtable in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The empty Destinations screen with the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. Tap **Airtable**, in **Sheets & Databases**.

   ![The Add Destination list with Airtable in the Sheets & Databases group.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed shows the **WalletFeed Pro** screen first.
5. If WalletFeed shows **Sign In with Airtable**, tap **Use a Token Instead**.
6. Tap **Personal Access Token**.

   ![The Airtable screen in WalletFeed with the Personal Access Token field and the steps for Airtable.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/walletfeed-setup-airtable.webp)

7. Paste the token.

   The form then shows **Base** and **Table**. **Base** shows the bases that the token can change.
8. In **Base**, select your base.
9. Do not change **Table**.

   **Table** shows **New Table**, and the form shows "Adds a WalletFeed Transactions table to the base." If the base has a **WalletFeed Transactions** table from a previous destination, **Table** shows that table.
10. Tap **Add**.

    The message **Send Transactions to Airtable?** gives the data that Airtable receives, the accounts, and the start date.
11. Tap **Send**.

    If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed sends nothing and removes the destination.

The new destination is in **Destinations**. Its name has two parts, for example **Airtable · WalletFeed**. The second part is the name of your base. WalletFeed starts to send your transactions.

## Step 4: See your transactions in Airtable

1. On your computer, open your base in Airtable.
2. Click the **WalletFeed Transactions** tab.

   ![The WalletFeed Transactions table in Airtable with six sample transactions that WalletFeed sent.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-walletfeed-result.webp)

3. To see all the fields of a transaction, move the pointer onto its row.
4. Click the expand icon that shows in the row.

   ![One expanded transaction record with its fields and a check mark in the Pending box.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-result-record.webp)

5. Optional: On your iPhone, tap **Send Test** on the destination screen in WalletFeed.

   The table gets a test record with WalletFeed in **Merchant** and -4.20 in **Amount**. You can delete this record in Airtable.

## Fields in Airtable

Each transaction is one record in the **WalletFeed Transactions** table. WalletFeed makes these fields:

| Airtable field | Data |
| --- | --- |
| **WalletFeed ID** | The ID of the transaction in Wallet. WalletFeed uses it to find and change the same record. |
| **Date** | The date of the transaction in your time zone, for example 2026-10-30. |
| **Merchant** | The name of the merchant. If Wallet has no merchant name, this field contains the description. |
| **Amount** | A number with two decimal places. A purchase or a fee is less than zero, and a refund or a payment is more than zero. |
| **Currency** | The currency code, for example `USD`. |
| **Category** | The WalletFeed category, for example Groceries or Fuel. |
| **Status** | The status in Wallet, for example `pending` or `booked`. |
| **Pending** | A check box. WalletFeed selects it while the status is `pending` or `authorized`. |
| **Account** | The name of the Wallet account, for example Apple Card. |
| **Description** | The description from Wallet. |
| **Type** | The type of transaction in Wallet, for example `pointOfSale` or `refund`. |
| **MCC** | The merchant category code, as a number. If Wallet has no code, this field is empty. |
| **Foreign Amount** | The value in the currency of the merchant, with a minus sign when **Amount** has one. It is empty for a purchase in US dollars. |
| **Foreign Currency** | The currency code of the merchant. It is empty for a purchase in US dollars. |

WalletFeed does not change fields that you add to the table. If you change a WalletFeed field in a record, WalletFeed replaces your change when that transaction changes again.

You can also select a different table in **Table**. **Table** shows only the tables that have a field with the name **WalletFeed ID**. WalletFeed writes only to the WalletFeed fields that the table has. If you add a WalletFeed field to the table, WalletFeed writes to it after you tap **Send Test**.

## New and changed transactions

WalletFeed sends each change in Wallet to Airtable:

- While WalletFeed is open, Airtable receives changes in seconds.
- When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. Then WalletFeed sends the change. This occurs only if [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**. **Background Sync** is on until you set it to off.
- When your iPhone starts again, WalletFeed cannot send changes until you enter the passcode.

WalletFeed changes the same record when a transaction changes:

- WalletFeed adds a pending charge as a record, and selects **Pending**. When its status changes to `booked`, WalletFeed changes the same record and removes the check mark from **Pending**.
- A refund is a new record, and its **Amount** is more than zero.
- If the status of a pending charge changes to `rejected`, WalletFeed removes its record. Wallet gives this status to a declined or expired charge.
- If Wallet removes a transaction, WalletFeed also removes its record.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it.

To send previous transactions after you add the destination, do these steps:

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap your Airtable destination.
3. Tap **Send History**.
4. Select **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

To stop WalletFeed while it sends these transactions, tap **Send History** › **Stop Sending**. For more information, refer to [Send previous transactions](/docs/send-history/).

On the Airtable Free plan, a base can contain a maximum of 1,000 records. To decrease the number of records in Airtable, set a shorter **Initial History** before you add Airtable.

## Send more than 1,000 transactions

Each Airtable plan has a maximum number of records in a base. On the Free plan, the maximum is 1,000. When your base is full, WalletFeed can add a new base with the name **WalletFeed (2)** to the same workspace. The new base has the same table and fields. When that base is full, WalletFeed adds **WalletFeed (3)**.

WalletFeed can add a base only in these conditions:

- The destination has the ID of the workspace in **Workspace ID**.
- The token has access to the workspace. For this access, the token must have **All current and future bases in this workspace** below **Access**. You can click it in step 14 of [Step 2](#step-2-make-a-personal-access-token-in-airtable).
- You have the Creator permission in the workspace.

To add the workspace ID to the destination, do these steps:

1. On your computer, open the [Airtable workspaces](https://airtable.com/workspaces) page.
2. Click the workspace of your base.
3. Copy the address from the address bar of the browser.

   The address contains the workspace ID. The ID starts with `wsp` and stops before the question mark.
4. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
5. Tap **Destinations**.
6. Tap your Airtable destination.
7. Tap **Workspace ID**.
8. Paste the address.
9. Tap **Save**.

When WalletFeed adds a base, the destination shows "Airtable base full. Now writing to WalletFeed (2)." **Current Base** on the destination screen shows the name of the new base. If a transaction changes after that, WalletFeed changes its record in the base that contains the record.

> **Note:** On the Free plan, the limit of 1,000 API calls each month is for all the bases in the workspace. A new base does not change this limit.

## Change or stop the destination

To open the destination, tap **Destinations** in WalletFeed. Then tap your Airtable destination. On the destination screen, you can make these changes:

- To send only some transactions, set **Filter** to on. You can set **Include**, **Minimum**, **Include Pending**, **Accounts**, **Categories** and **Exclude**. Refer to [Choose what a destination receives](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).
- To stop the destination for a period, set **Enabled** to off.
- To let WalletFeed add a new base when your base is full, tap **Workspace ID**. Refer to [Send more than 1,000 transactions](#send-more-than-1-000-transactions).
- To use a new token, tap **Replace Token**. Paste the new token. Then tap **Replace**. WalletFeed keeps the new token only if the new token lets WalletFeed read the table.
- To remove the destination, tap **Delete**. Then tap **Delete** again. WalletFeed removes the destination and its token from your iPhone.

The records that WalletFeed sent stay in Airtable after you delete the destination. The terms of Airtable are applicable to these records.

To delete the token in Airtable, do these steps on your computer:

1. On Airtable **Home**, click your account picture, in the top right corner.
2. Click **Builder hub**.

   Airtable opens the **Personal access tokens** page.
3. In the row of the token, click **…**.

   ![The token list with the WalletFeed token and its highlighted menu button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-token-list.webp)

4. Click **Delete token**.

   ![The token menu with the highlighted Delete token item.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-token-menu.webp)

5. Click **Delete**.

   ![The dialog that asks if you want to delete the token, with the highlighted Delete button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-delete-token.webp)

   After this step, Airtable does not accept the token from WalletFeed.

## If something goes wrong

### If you cannot click Done in the token dialog

Airtable does not let you click **Done** until you copy the token.

1. Click the clipboard button on the right side of the token.
2. Click **Done**.

### If you closed the token dialog before you copied the token

Airtable shows a token only one time. The **Token ID** in the token list is not the token.

1. Delete the token that you cannot use, with the procedure in [Change or stop the destination](#change-or-stop-the-destination).
2. Make a new token with the procedure in [Step 2](#step-2-make-a-personal-access-token-in-airtable).

### If WalletFeed shows "Token rejected (HTTP 401). Check it and try again."

Airtable did not accept the token.

1. Make sure that you paste the full token from the **Your token has been created** dialog.
2. If you do not have the full token, make a new token with the procedure in [Step 2](#step-2-make-a-personal-access-token-in-airtable).

### If WalletFeed shows "The token has no base you can edit"

The token has no base, or you cannot change the bases that it has.

1. In Airtable, make a new token with the procedure in [Step 2](#step-2-make-a-personal-access-token-in-airtable).
2. In WalletFeed, delete the text in **Personal Access Token**.
3. Paste the new token.

### If WalletFeed shows "The token can't reach this base"

The token does not have the base or one of the four scopes.

1. In Airtable, make a new token with the procedure in [Step 2](#step-2-make-a-personal-access-token-in-airtable).
2. In WalletFeed, delete the text in **Personal Access Token**.
3. Paste the new token.

WalletFeed can add the **WalletFeed Transactions** table only if you have the Creator permission for the base. If you tap **Add** without this permission, WalletFeed can also show this message.

### If WalletFeed shows "Airtable is limiting requests. Try again in 30 seconds."

Airtable accepts a maximum of five requests each second for one base. After too many requests, Airtable rejects requests for 30 seconds.

1. Wait 30 seconds.
2. In WalletFeed, do the last step again.

### If Destinations shows "Authentication failed"

Airtable does not accept the token. This occurs if you delete the token, or if the token does not have the base or a scope.

![The Destinations list with Authentication failed below the name of a destination.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/walletfeed-destinations-failure.webp)

1. In Airtable, make a new token with the procedure in [Step 2](#step-2-make-a-personal-access-token-in-airtable).
2. In WalletFeed, tap the destination.
3. Tap **Replace Token**.
4. Paste the new token.
5. Tap **Replace**.

### If Destinations shows "Add your workspace ID to this destination"

The base has the maximum number of records for your Airtable plan, and the destination has no workspace ID. WalletFeed sends no more transactions until you add the ID.

Add the workspace ID with the procedure in [Send more than 1,000 transactions](#send-more-than-1-000-transactions). After you tap **Save**, WalletFeed tries again to add a new base.

### If Destinations shows "Check the workspace ID"

Airtable did not let WalletFeed add a new base. The workspace ID is not correct, the token has no access to the workspace, or you do not have the Creator permission in the workspace.

1. Do the procedure in [Send more than 1,000 transactions](#send-more-than-1-000-transactions) again.
2. In Airtable, make a new token with the procedure in [Step 2](#step-2-make-a-personal-access-token-in-airtable). In step 14, click **All current and future bases in this workspace**.
3. In WalletFeed, tap the destination.
4. Tap **Replace Token**.
5. Paste the new token.
6. Tap **Replace**.

### If some transactions are not in the table

The cause can be a filter, the **Initial History** start, or a full base.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap your Airtable destination.
3. Make sure that **Filter** is off, or that the filter includes these transactions.
4. If the destination screen shows **Current Base**, look for the transactions in that base in Airtable.
5. To send previous transactions, tap **Send History**.
6. Select a period.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-aws/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to AWS

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to Amazon S3, Amazon SQS, Kinesis Data Streams, DynamoDB or EventBridge in your AWS account. You make a user in AWS with a policy from WalletFeed, then you paste its access key into WalletFeed.

## Before you start

You must have:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version
- WalletFeed, with access to your [Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/)
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase
- An AWS account that lets you make users and access keys in AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
- A web browser, on a computer or on your iPhone

WalletFeed is available only in the US.

WalletFeed can use only the commercial AWS Regions. It cannot use the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions or the China Regions.

## Step 1: Make the AWS resource

WalletFeed sends your transactions to a bucket, a queue, a stream, a table or an event bus in your AWS account. Each of these is a resource in AWS. Do the steps for the service that you will use. If you have the resource, go to [Step 2](#step-2-open-the-aws-screen-in-walletfeed).

### Amazon S3: make a bucket

1. On your computer, open the [Amazon S3 console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/s3/).
2. In the navigation bar, select the AWS Region for the bucket.
3. Click **General purpose buckets**.
4. Click **Create bucket**.
5. In **Bucket name**, type a name for the bucket.
6. Do not change the other values on the page. When the page opens, all four controls in **Block Public Access settings for this bucket** are on.
7. Click **Create bucket**.
8. Record the bucket name and the code of the region, for example `us-east-1`.

For more information, refer to [Creating a general purpose bucket](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/create-bucket-overview.html) in the AWS documentation.

### Amazon SQS: make a queue

1. On your computer, open the [Amazon SQS console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/sqs/).
2. In the navigation bar, select the AWS Region for the queue.
3. Click **Create queue**.
4. For **Type**, keep **Standard**.
5. In **Name**, type a name for the queue.
6. Click **Create queue**. The **Details** page of the queue opens.
7. Copy the URL of the queue, for example `https://sqs.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/123456789012/MyQueue`.

You can also use a FIFO (first-in-first-out) queue. If the name of the queue has `.fifo` at the end, WalletFeed uses it as a FIFO queue. For more information, refer to [Creating an Amazon SQS standard queue](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/creating-sqs-standard-queues.html).

### Kinesis Data Streams: make a stream

1. On your computer, open the [Kinesis console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/kinesis).
2. In the navigation bar, select the AWS Region for the stream.
3. Click **Create data stream**.
4. Type a name for the data stream.
5. Keep the **On-demand** capacity mode, or select **Provisioned**.
6. If you selected **Provisioned**, type the number of shards.
7. Click **Create Kinesis stream**.
8. Wait for the **Status** of the stream to change to **Active**.
9. Record the stream name and the code of the region. You can also use the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the stream.

For more information, refer to [Create a stream using the AWS Management Console](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/how-do-i-create-a-stream.html).

### DynamoDB: make a table

WalletFeed can write only to a table with the partition key `id` of the type String, and with no sort key.

1. On your computer, open the [DynamoDB console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/dynamodb/).
2. In the navigation bar, select the AWS Region for the table.
3. Click **Tables**.
4. Click **Create table**.
5. In **Table name**, type a name for the table.
6. In **Partition key**, type `id`.
7. Make sure that the type of the partition key is String.
8. Do not type a value in **Sort key**.
9. For **Table settings**, keep **Default settings**.
10. Click **Create table**.

For more information, refer to [Create a table in DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/getting-started-step-1.html).

### EventBridge: make a rule on the event bus

WalletFeed sends events to the `default` event bus, or to a different bus that you type in WalletFeed. A rule selects events with an event pattern. EventBridge sends an event to a target only when a rule on the bus selects the event. Thus, you must make a rule for the WalletFeed events.

1. On your computer, open the [EventBridge console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/events/).
2. In the navigation bar, select the AWS Region for the rule.
3. Click **Rules**.
4. Click **Create rule**.
5. Click **Advanced Builder**.
6. In **Name**, type a name for the rule.
7. For **Event bus**, select the event bus that WalletFeed sends to. In this list, the `default` bus is **AWS default event bus**.
8. For **Rule type**, select **Rule with an event pattern**.
9. Click **Next**.
10. For **Event source**, select **AWS events or EventBridge partner events**.
11. In the **Creation method** section, for **Method**, select **Custom pattern (JSON editor)**.
12. In **Event pattern**, paste this pattern. It selects all the events from WalletFeed:

    ```json
    {"source": ["app.walletfeed"]}
    ```
13. Click **Next**.
14. For **Target type**, select **AWS service**.
15. For **Select a target**, select the service that receives the events, for example Amazon SQS.
16. Select the resource of that service, for example your queue.
17. Click **Next**.
18. Click **Next** again.
19. Click **Create rule**.

For more information, refer to [Creating rules using the Advanced Builder](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-create-rule-wizard.html).

## Step 2: Open the AWS screen in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with no destinations, and the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-aws/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)
4. Scroll down to the **Developers** section. It is the last section in the list.
5. Tap **AWS**. Below its name, WalletFeed shows **S3, SQS, Kinesis, DynamoDB, EventBridge**.
6. If WalletFeed shows the **WalletFeed Pro** screen, get WalletFeed Pro. Then the AWS screen opens.
7. Tap **Service**.
8. Tap the service of your resource.
9. If your resource is not in `us-east-1`, replace `us-east-1` in **Region** with the code of its region.
10. If you selected **Amazon S3**, type the bucket name in **Bucket**.

    ![The AWS screen with Amazon S3 selected, with the fields Access Key ID, Secret Access Key, Region, Endpoint, Bucket, Prefix and Format.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-aws/walletfeed-setup-amazon-s3.webp)
11. If you selected **Amazon S3**, do not type a value in **Endpoint**.
12. If you selected **Amazon SQS**, paste the queue URL in **Queue URL**. WalletFeed uses the region in the queue URL.

    ![The AWS screen with Amazon SQS selected, with the Queue URL field and Share IAM Policy.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-aws/walletfeed-setup-amazon-sqs.webp)
13. If you selected **Kinesis Data Streams**, type the stream name or ARN in **Stream**.

    ![The AWS screen with Kinesis Data Streams selected, with the Stream field and Share IAM Policy.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-aws/walletfeed-setup-kinesis-data-streams.webp)
14. If you selected **DynamoDB**, type the table name or ARN in **Table**.

    ![The AWS screen with DynamoDB selected, with the Table field and the message "The partition key must be a string named id."](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-aws/walletfeed-setup-dynamodb.webp)
15. If you selected **EventBridge**, keep `default` in **Event Bus**, or type the name or ARN of your bus.

    ![The AWS screen with EventBridge selected, with the value default in the Event Bus field.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-aws/walletfeed-setup-eventbridge.webp)

For Amazon S3, you can also change **Prefix** and **Format**. The prefix is the folder in the bucket. At the start, the prefix is `walletfeed/`. The format is **CSV** or **JSON Lines**. The policy in Step 3 contains the prefix. Thus, you must set the prefix before you get the policy.

> **Note:** **Endpoint** is for a different storage service that uses the S3 API, for example Cloudflare R2 or Backblaze B2. The IAM steps on this page are only for AWS.

## Step 3: Make an IAM user with the policy

WalletFeed makes an IAM policy for the resource on the AWS screen. The policy lets the key do only these actions on that resource:

| Service | Actions in the policy |
| --- | --- |
| Amazon S3 | `s3:PutObject` and `s3:DeleteObject` on the prefix in the bucket. WalletFeed deletes only its test file. |
| Amazon SQS | `sqs:SendMessage` on the queue |
| Kinesis Data Streams | `kinesis:PutRecords` on the stream |
| DynamoDB | `dynamodb:BatchWriteItem` and `dynamodb:DescribeTable` on the table |
| EventBridge | `events:PutEvents` on the event bus |

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Share IAM Policy**. The share sheet opens with the policy.
2. If you use IAM on your computer, send the policy to your computer, for example with AirDrop.
3. If you use IAM on your iPhone, tap **Copy** in the share sheet.
4. Open the [IAM console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/iam/). On the AWS screen in WalletFeed, **Open IAM** also opens it.
5. Click **Users**.
6. Click **Create user**.
7. In **User name**, type a name for the user, for example `walletfeed`.
8. Click **Next**.
9. On the **Set Permissions** page, click **Next**. You add the policy after you make the user.
10. Click **Create user**.
11. Click **View user**.
12. Click the **Permissions** tab.
13. Click **Add permissions**.
14. Click **Create inline policy**.
15. In the **Policy editor**, select **JSON**.
16. Delete all the JSON in the editor.
17. If you sent the policy to your computer, copy it there.
18. Paste the policy from WalletFeed.
19. Click **Next**.
20. In **Policy Name**, type a name for the policy, for example `walletfeed`.
21. Click **Create policy**.

> **Note:** For a person who uses AWS, AWS recommends temporary credentials. For an app that cannot use an IAM role, the AWS documentation gives the steps to make an IAM user. WalletFeed accepts only the access key of an IAM user. It does not accept temporary credentials.

For more information, refer to [Create an IAM user for workloads that can't use IAM roles](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/getting-started-workloads.html).

## Step 4: Make an access key

1. On the page of the user, click the **Security credentials** tab.
2. In the **Access keys** section, click **Create access key**.
3. On the **Access key best practices & alternatives** page, select **Other**.
4. Click **Next**.
5. **Optional:** Type a description for the key, for example `WalletFeed on iPhone`.
6. Click **Create access key**.
7. Click **Show** to see the secret access key.
8. If you use IAM on your computer, send the access key ID and the secret access key to your iPhone. For example, you can use AirDrop.
9. Keep this page open until WalletFeed has the two values.

> **Note:** AWS shows the secret access key only one time. If you do not have it, you can make a new access key.

For more information, refer to [How an IAM administrator can manage IAM user access keys](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access-keys-admin-managed.html).

## Step 5: Paste the key and start to send

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed again.
2. If the AWS screen is not open, do Step 2 again.
3. Copy the access key ID.
4. In WalletFeed, paste the access key ID in **Access Key ID**. The first letters of this ID are `AKIA`.
5. Copy the secret access key.
6. In WalletFeed, paste the secret access key in **Secret Access Key**.
7. Tap **Add**. WalletFeed uses the key to do a check of the resource.
8. If WalletFeed shows an error message below **Share IAM Policy**, refer to [If there is a problem](#if-there-is-a-problem).
9. Read the message, for example **Send Transactions to Amazon S3?**

   The message tells you the data that the service will receive, the accounts and the start date.
10. Tap **Send**. WalletFeed adds the destination and starts to send your transactions.

The check after you tap **Add** is different for each service:

- For Amazon S3, WalletFeed writes a test file in the prefix, for example `walletfeed/walletfeed-test.csv`. Then it deletes the file.
- For Amazon SQS, Kinesis Data Streams and EventBridge, WalletFeed sends one test event with the description `WalletFeed test transaction`.
- For DynamoDB, WalletFeed reads the keys of the table. It does not write an item.

If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed does not add the destination. The AWS screen stays open.

The name of the new destination has the name of the service and the name of the resource, for example **Amazon S3 · my-bucket**.

> **Note:** WalletFeed keeps the key in the Keychain on your iPhone. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. Your transactions go from your iPhone directly to your AWS account. After AWS receives the data, the AWS terms are applicable to it.

## Data that AWS receives

The table shows the data that each service receives:

| Service | Data |
| --- | --- |
| Amazon S3 | One file for each month, for example `walletfeed/transactions/2026-10.csv`, or `.jsonl` for JSON Lines. |
| Amazon SQS | One message for each change. The body of the message is the event. |
| Kinesis Data Streams | One record for each change. The data is the event, and the partition key is the `id` of the transaction. |
| DynamoDB | One item for each transaction, with the key `id`. A change replaces the item. |
| EventBridge | One event for each change, from the source `app.walletfeed`. The `detail` field is the WalletFeed event. |

In an EventBridge event, `detail-type` is `Transaction Created`, `Transaction Updated` or `Transaction Deleted`.

Each event is a JSON object with these fields:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `event` | `created` the first time, then `updated` after each change. `deleted` if a transaction becomes declined or expired, or Wallet removes it. |
| `id` | The WalletFeed ID of the transaction. |
| `date` | The day of the transaction, in the time zone of your iPhone. |
| `merchant` | The merchant name, or the description if Wallet has no merchant name. |
| `amount` | The value of the transaction. For purchases and fees, the value is less than zero. For payments and refunds, it is more than zero. |
| `currency` | The currency code, for example `USD`. |
| `category` | The WalletFeed category, for example `Groceries` or `Dining`. |
| `status` | The status in Wallet, for example `pending`, `authorized` or `booked`. |
| `pending` | `true` when the status is `pending` or `authorized`, and `false` at other times. |
| `account` | The account name, for example Apple Card. |
| `description` | The description of the transaction in Wallet. |
| `type` | The transaction type in Wallet, for example `pointOfSale` or `refund`. |
| `mcc` | The merchant category code. |
| `foreignAmount` | For a purchase in a different currency, the value in that currency. It has the same sign (plus or minus) as `amount`. |
| `foreignCurrency` | The code of that different currency. |

If Wallet does not give a value, the value is `null`, for example `foreignAmount` for a purchase in dollars. A `deleted` event has only `event` and `id`.

WalletFeed sends the test event on one line. The `date` is the day of the test. For Amazon SQS, Kinesis Data Streams and EventBridge, the test event has these values:

```json
{
  "account": "Sample Card",
  "amount": -4.2,
  "category": "Shopping",
  "currency": "USD",
  "date": "2026-10-30",
  "description": "WalletFeed test transaction",
  "event": "created",
  "foreignAmount": null,
  "foreignCurrency": null,
  "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
  "mcc": 5734,
  "merchant": "WalletFeed",
  "pending": true,
  "status": "pending",
  "type": "purchase"
}
```

In DynamoDB, each field is an attribute of the item. Strings are type S, numbers are type N, and `true` or `false` is type BOOL. WalletFeed does not write the fields that have no value.

In Amazon S3, a JSON Lines file has one line for each transaction. Each line is an object with the same fields, but with no `event`. A CSV file has 16 columns. The first columns are Date, Posted Date, Merchant, Description, Original Description, Amount, Currency and Direction. The last columns are Status, Type, Category, MCC, Account, Foreign Amount, Foreign Currency and WalletFeed ID.

## Sync times and changes

While WalletFeed is open, AWS receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is off in **Settings** › **Sync**, iOS does not start WalletFeed. **Background Sync** is on until you set it to off.

When the status of a pending transaction changes to `booked`, WalletFeed sends the same transaction again. If a transaction becomes declined or expired, or if Wallet removes it, WalletFeed sends a `deleted` event. A refund is a different transaction, and its `amount` is more than zero.

In Amazon S3, WalletFeed writes the full file of each month that changed. The next time that WalletFeed writes a month, it removes the deleted transactions from the file of that month. In DynamoDB, a change replaces the item, and a `deleted` event deletes the item. Thus, Amazon S3 and DynamoDB keep one copy of each transaction.

Amazon SQS, Kinesis Data Streams and EventBridge can receive the same event more than one time. You can use `id` to find the transaction in your data. If the `event` and `status` did not change, you can ignore the event. If WalletFeed sends a transaction to a FIFO queue again with no changes in 5 minutes or less, the queue ignores it.

If AWS does not accept some records, WalletFeed sends them again after 1 second. If AWS does not accept them again, the destination shows "AWS rejected" and the number of records. WalletFeed tries again at the next sync.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it.

To send transactions from a different period, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the AWS destination. The first part of its name is the name of the service, for example **Amazon S3 ·**.
3. Tap **Send History**.
4. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

Amazon SQS, Kinesis Data Streams and EventBridge receive each transaction again, as a `created` event. Amazon S3 and DynamoDB keep one copy of each transaction. To stop, tap **Send History** › **Stop Sending**.

## Change or stop the destination

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the AWS destination.

   ![The screen of a Lunch Money destination, with Name, Enabled, Last Sync, Replace Token, Filter, Send History, Send Test and Delete.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-aws/walletfeed-destination-detail.webp)

The screen of an AWS destination has the same controls, but it has no **Replace Token**. It shows the resource, for example **Bucket** or **Queue**. Below the resource, it shows **Region**, **Share IAM Policy** and **Replace Key**.

To send only some transactions:

1. Set **Filter** to on.
2. Select the transactions with **Accounts**, **Categories**, **Minimum** and the other controls.

For more information, refer to [Choose what to send](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).

To stop the destination temporarily, set **Enabled** to off.

To use a different access key:

1. Tap **Replace Key**.
2. Paste the access key ID.
3. Paste the secret access key.
4. Tap **Replace**.

WalletFeed does the same check as **Add**. It keeps the new key only if the check is satisfactory. For Amazon SQS, Kinesis Data Streams and EventBridge, this check sends one test event.

You cannot change the region or the resource of a destination. To use a different resource, add a new AWS destination. Then delete the destination that you do not use. You can have more than one AWS destination, for example a bucket and a queue.

To remove the destination:

1. Tap **Delete**.
2. Tap **Delete** again.

WalletFeed tells you "Transactions already sent stay at the destination." The data stays in your AWS account until you delete it in AWS.

If no destination uses the access key, delete the key in IAM:

1. In the IAM console, click **Users**.
2. Click the name of the user.
3. Click the **Security credentials** tab.
4. In the **Access keys** section, click **Actions** for the key.
5. Click **Deactivate**.
6. In the dialog, click **Deactivate** again.
7. Click **Actions** for the key.
8. Click **Delete**.
9. In the dialog, type the access key ID.
10. Click **Delete**.

## If there is a problem

### If you cannot tap Add

WalletFeed lets you tap **Add** only when all the necessary fields have a value. **Region** must contain only letters, numbers and hyphens.

1. Make sure that **Access Key ID** and **Secret Access Key** are not empty.
2. Make sure that **Region** has a code, for example `us-east-1`, and not a name, for example US East.
3. For Amazon S3, make sure that **Bucket** is not empty.
4. If **Endpoint** has a value, make sure that its first part is not `http://`. WalletFeed accepts only HTTPS.
5. For Amazon SQS, paste the full queue URL again. The first part of the URL is `https://sqs.`.
6. For Kinesis Data Streams or DynamoDB, make sure that **Stream** or **Table** is not empty.

### If WalletFeed shows "Key rejected"

AWS did not accept the key, or the IAM policy of the user does not let the key do the action. WalletFeed shows the HTTP code, for example "Key rejected (HTTP 403). Check the key and its IAM policy."

1. In WalletFeed, paste the access key ID again.
2. Paste the secret access key again.
3. In the IAM console, open the user.
4. On the **Permissions** tab, make sure that the user has the policy from **Share IAM Policy**.
5. If you changed the resource or the region after you got the policy, tap **Share IAM Policy** again.
6. If you got a new policy, replace the policy of the user with the new policy.
7. In WalletFeed, tap **Add**.

### If WalletFeed shows "Wrong region for this bucket."

The bucket is in a different region from the code in **Region**.

1. In the Amazon S3 console, find the region of the bucket.
2. In WalletFeed, type the code of that region in **Region**.
3. Tap **Add**.

### If WalletFeed shows "Not found. Check the name and the region."

AWS did not find a bucket with the name in **Bucket**.

1. In WalletFeed, make sure that the name in **Bucket** is the same as the bucket name in AWS.
2. Make sure that **Region** has the code of the region of the bucket.
3. Tap **Add**.

### If WalletFeed shows a message about the partition key

The DynamoDB table has a different partition key, or it has a sort key. WalletFeed then shows "The table's partition key must be a string named id."

1. Make a new DynamoDB table with the partition key `id` of the type String, and no sort key.
2. In WalletFeed, type the name of the new table in **Table**.
3. Tap **Share IAM Policy**.
4. Replace the policy of the user with the new policy.
5. Tap **Add**.

### If WalletFeed shows "Couldn't connect" with HTTP 400

The full message is "Couldn't connect: The server returned an error (HTTP 400)." AWS did not accept the data from WalletFeed. For example, the name of the queue, the stream, the table or the event bus is not correct. The resource can also be in a different region.

1. In the AWS console, find the resource and its region.
2. In WalletFeed, type the name of the resource again, or paste the queue URL again.
3. In **Region**, type the code of the region of the resource.
4. Tap **Add**.

### If the destination shows "Authentication failed"

AWS did not accept the key at the last sync. For example, a person deactivated or deleted the key, or removed the policy from the user.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.

   ![The Destinations list, with an n8n destination that shows Authentication failed.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-aws/walletfeed-destinations-failure.webp)
2. Tap the AWS destination.

   ![The screen of an n8n destination, with Authentication failed below Last Sync.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-aws/walletfeed-destination-failure.webp)
3. If the user has no active access key, make a new access key (refer to [Step 4](#step-4-make-an-access-key)).
4. Tap **Replace Key**.
5. Paste the access key ID.
6. Paste the secret access key.
7. Tap **Replace**.

### If the destination shows "AWS rejected" or "AWS throttled"

AWS did not accept some records, and it did not accept them again after 1 second. "AWS throttled" tells you that the resource received data too frequently. WalletFeed tries again at the next sync.

1. Open the AWS destination.
2. Tap **Send Test**.
3. If **Send Test** shows HTTP 403, do the steps in [If the destination shows "Authentication failed"](#if-the-destination-shows-authentication-failed).
4. If the error message stays after the next sync, examine the resource in the AWS console.

### If the EventBridge target receives no events

EventBridge sends an event to a target only when a rule on the event bus selects the event.

1. In the EventBridge console, make sure that the rule is on the same event bus as **Event Bus** in WalletFeed.
2. Make sure that the rule is in the same region as the destination.
3. Make sure that the event pattern of the rule is `{"source": ["app.walletfeed"]}`.
4. In WalletFeed, open the AWS destination.
5. Tap **Send Test**.

### If no new data shows in AWS

WalletFeed sends changes while it is open, or when iOS starts it in the background.

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. Make sure that **Background Sync** is on in **Settings** › **Sync**.
3. Open the AWS destination.
4. Make sure that the destination shows no error message below **Last Sync**.
5. Tap **Send Test**. AWS receives the test transaction with the description `WalletFeed test transaction`.

   For Amazon S3, **Send Test** writes the test file in the prefix, for example `walletfeed/walletfeed-test.csv`, and keeps it. For DynamoDB, **Send Test** writes an item with the `id` `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000`.
6. For Amazon S3 or DynamoDB, delete the test file or the test item in AWS.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to BankSync

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a table in BankSync. Then your AI agents can read the table through BankSync's MCP tools or its REST API.

You can connect with Sign In with BankSync, or with a BankSync API key.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- WalletFeed, with access to your Wallet accounts. Refer to [Choose the Wallet accounts WalletFeed reads](/docs/wallet-accounts/).
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), which is necessary for destinations. WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.
- A BankSync account. If you do not have one, you can make it when you sign in from WalletFeed.
- Owner or admin access to your BankSync workspace.
- A workspace that can have one more table. On the Free plan, a workspace can have only one table.
- For an API key, BankSync's Standard plan or higher.

## Step 1: Open BankSync in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed and tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

3. In the **Budgeting** section, tap **BankSync**.

   ![The Add Destination list with BankSync at the top of the Budgeting section.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed shows the WalletFeed Pro screen before the BankSync form.

## Step 2: Sign in with BankSync

Sign In with BankSync is available on all BankSync plans, which include the Free plan. With Sign In with BankSync, WalletFeed can see only its Apple Card table.

Sign In with BankSync goes through WalletFeed's referral link. The form tells you this with the text "WalletFeed may earn a commission if you pay for BankSync."

1. Tap **Sign In with BankSync**.

   ![The BankSync form in WalletFeed with Sign In with BankSync and Use an API Key Instead.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/walletfeed-setup-banksync.webp)

2. On the BankSync page, tap **Continue with Google**, or type your email address in **Email** and tap **Continue with email**.

   ![The BankSync sign-in page with Continue with Google, an Email field and Continue with email.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/banksync-sign-in-with-banksync.webp)

3. If you have a BankSync account, complete the sign-in.
4. If you do not have a BankSync account, do these steps:

   1. Type a password in **Password** and in **Confirm password**.
   2. Tap **Create account**.

      ![The BankSync Create your password form with the Create account button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/banksync-create-password.webp)

   3. In Mail, open the email "Verify your email for BankSync" and tap its link.
   4. Go back to WalletFeed and tap **I've verified my email**.

      ![The BankSync Check your inbox screen with the I've verified my email button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/banksync-check-inbox.webp)

5. On the BankSync page about WalletFeed, give your approval as the owner or an admin of the workspace.

   BankSync adds WalletFeed to the workspace and makes the **Apple Card** table. WalletFeed waits a maximum of approximately 30 seconds for the table. Then the form shows **Signed In** and your workspace.

6. Tap **Add**.

## Step 3: Start the first sync

After you tap **Add**, WalletFeed shows the message "Send Transactions to BankSync?". The message tells you the data that BankSync receives, the Wallet accounts, and the date that the transactions start from.

1. Read the message.
2. Tap **Send**.

If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes BankSync from your destinations.

## Step 4: Find the table in BankSync

1. On a computer, go to [app.banksync.io](https://app.banksync.io) and sign in.
2. Click **Tables** at the top of the page.
3. Click the **Apple Card** table. If you used an API key, the table has the name that you typed in WalletFeed.

   ![The BankSync Tables page with the Apple Card (WalletFeed) table.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/banksync-tables.webp)

4. Optional: To see only the columns that have data, click **Fields** and remove the empty columns from the view.

   ![Six sample transactions in the BankSync table, with the Amount, Category, Account Name, Pending and Wallet Status columns.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/banksync-result-walletfeed-columns.webp)

## Connect with an API key

An API key is an alternative to Sign In with BankSync. API keys are available only on BankSync's Standard plan or higher. With a key, WalletFeed makes the table, with the name that you type.

The screenshots show BankSync in a web browser on a computer.

### Make an API key in BankSync

1. On a computer, go to [app.banksync.io](https://app.banksync.io) and sign in as the owner or an admin of the workspace.
2. Click the workspace name at the top left of the page.
3. Click **Settings**.

   ![The BankSync workspace menu with Settings selected.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/banksync-workspace-menu.webp)

4. In the sidebar, in the **WORKSPACE** group, click **Developers**.

   ![The BankSync Settings page with Developers in the sidebar.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/banksync-settings-developers.webp)

5. Click the **API Keys** tab.

   ![The BankSync Developer Settings page with the API Keys tab.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/banksync-developer-settings.webp)

6. Click **Create Key**.
7. In **Key Name**, type `WalletFeed`.
8. In **Expiration**, select **1 year** or **Never**.

   At first, BankSync selects **90 days**. After that period, the key is expired and WalletFeed cannot send to BankSync.

9. In **Permissions**, in the **tables** row, select **read** and **write**.
10. Click **Create API Key**.
11. Click the **Copy to clipboard** button adjacent to the `bsk_` key.
12. Click **Done**.

> **Note:** BankSync shows the key only one time. **Select all** gives the key full access to your workspace. WalletFeed uses only **read** and **write** in the **tables** row.

### Add the key in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open the BankSync form. Refer to [Step 1](#step-1-open-banksync-in-walletfeed).
2. Tap **Use an API Key Instead**.
3. Paste the key in **API Key**.
4. Optional: In **Table**, type a different name for the table.

   At first, **Table** contains **Apple Card (WalletFeed)**.

5. Tap **Add**.
6. In the message "Send Transactions to BankSync?", tap **Send**.

## Data that BankSync receives

WalletFeed writes one row for each transaction. The table that follows shows the BankSync column for each part of a Wallet transaction.

| Data from Wallet | BankSync column |
| --- | --- |
| The transaction ID | **ID** |
| The posted date, or the purchase date while the charge is pending | **Date** |
| The purchase date | **Authorized Date** |
| The value, less than 0 for a purchase and more than 0 for a credit, for example a refund | **Amount** |
| The value of a purchase, or 0 | **Debit Amount** |
| The value of a credit, or 0 | **Credit Amount** |
| The currency, for example USD | **Currency** |
| The description that Wallet shows | **Description** |
| The card statement text | **Original Description** |
| The merchant name, if Wallet has one | **Merchant Name** |
| The category, for example Dining or Groceries | **Category** |
| The account name, for example Apple Card or Apple Cash | **Account Name** |
| Selected while the charge is pending | **Pending** |
| The Wallet status, for example `pending` or `booked` | **Wallet Status** |
| The merchant category code | **MCC** |
| For a purchase in a different currency, the value in that currency | **Foreign Amount** |
| For a purchase in a different currency, that currency | **Foreign Currency** |

BankSync's transactions table has more columns, for example **Card Last 4** and **Bank**. WalletFeed does not put data in them.

## Read the table with an AI agent

BankSync has a REST API and an MCP server. An AI agent that you connect to BankSync can read the Apple Card table with the BankSync table tools, for example `query_table_rows` and `aggregate_table_rows`. Thus the agent can see your Apple Card transactions together with your other banks in BankSync.

- BankSync includes API and MCP access on the Standard plan or higher.
- On the Free plan, the **API Keys** tab shows "API & MCP aren't included on your plan".
- To connect an AI agent, make an API key for the agent on the **API Keys** tab. BankSync tells you "Create a key to access the REST API or connect an MCP client".

For more information, refer to [BankSync's guide to API keys](https://banksync.io/docs/api/api-keys).

## Sync times and pending charges

- While WalletFeed is open, BankSync receives changes in seconds.
- When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. This occurs only if [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on.
- BankSync receives a pending charge with **Pending** selected. When the charge posts, WalletFeed changes the same row. **Date** changes to the posted date, and **Pending** is not selected.
- A refund gets a new row, with a value of more than 0 in **Amount**.
- If a pending charge does not post, WalletFeed removes its row. BankSync moves the row to its trash.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. On the Free plan, a BankSync workspace can have a maximum of 5,000 rows in all its tables.

To send more previous transactions after you add BankSync, use **Send History**. Refer to [Send previous transactions](/docs/send-history/).

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap your BankSync destination.
3. Tap **Send History**.
4. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

To stop, tap **Send History**, then tap **Stop Sending**.

## Change or remove the destination

To change the destination, tap **Destinations** in WalletFeed, then tap your BankSync destination. Its name is "BankSync ·" and then the name of your BankSync workspace.

- To send only some transactions, turn on **Filter**. Refer to [Choose what a destination receives](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).
- To stop the sync for a period, turn off **Enabled**.
- To change the name, type a new name in **Name**.
- If the destination uses an API key, tap **Replace Key** to use a new key. Then paste the key and tap **Replace**.
- If the destination uses Sign In with BankSync, tap **Sign In Again** to sign in again.
- To remove the destination, tap **Delete**, then tap **Delete** again.

When you remove the destination, the table and its rows stay in BankSync. WalletFeed tells you "Transactions already sent stay at the destination."

To remove the access that WalletFeed has to your workspace, go to **Settings** › **Developers** in BankSync. The **Connected Apps** tab shows the apps that have your approval. The **API Keys** tab shows your keys.

![The BankSync Connected Apps tab with no connected apps.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/banksync-connected-apps.webp)

## If a problem occurs

### If BankSync shows "Upgrade to create API keys"

The Free and Starter plans do not include API keys.

![The BankSync API Keys page on the Free plan, with Upgrade to create API keys.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/banksync-api-keys-free-plan.webp)

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Sign In with BankSync Instead**.
2. Do the steps in [Step 2](#step-2-sign-in-with-banksync).

As an alternative, change to the Standard plan or higher in BankSync.

### If WalletFeed shows "Key rejected"

BankSync did not accept the key. Possibly the key is incorrect or expired, or it does not have **read** and **write** in the **tables** row. Also, the Free and Starter plans do not include API keys.

1. Make a new key. Refer to [Make an API key in BankSync](#make-an-api-key-in-banksync).
2. In WalletFeed, paste the new key in **API Key**, or tap **Replace Key** on the destination.

### If WalletFeed shows "hasn't created or shared the Apple Card table"

The workspace has the maximum number of tables for its plan, or BankSync did not make the table in time. WalletFeed tells you the limit of your plan, for example "The Free plan allows one table."

The table limit is 1 on Free, 2 on Starter, 5 on Standard, 25 on Professional and 100 on Business.

1. Tap **Open BankSync**.
2. Delete a table that you do not use, or change to a plan that has more tables.
3. In WalletFeed, tap **Try Again**.
4. If WalletFeed continues to show the message, tap **Sign In Again**.

### If BankSync does not accept the sign-in

Only the owner or an admin of the workspace can give approval to WalletFeed. WalletFeed shows "BankSync didn't accept the sign-in", or BankSync shows a message on its page.

1. Tap **Sign In with BankSync** again.
2. Sign in as the owner or an admin of the workspace.
3. If BankSync does not accept the sign-in again, use an API key. Refer to [Connect with an API key](#connect-with-an-api-key).

### If the destination shows "Authentication failed"

BankSync did not accept the key or the sign-in. For example, the API key is expired.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**, then tap your BankSync destination.
2. If the destination uses an API key, make a new key, then tap **Replace Key** and paste it.
3. If the destination uses Sign In with BankSync, tap **Sign In Again**.

WalletFeed can also show "Signed out. Sign in again in the destination's settings." Do step 3 to correct this.

### If BankSync shows only its logo after the email link

After you open the link in the BankSync email, the BankSync page can stay on the BankSync logo.

1. Reload the page.

### If BankSync has no Tables tab

BankSync's documentation tells you that Tables is in beta, and that BankSync turns it on for each workspace.

1. Contact BankSync and tell them that your workspace has no **Tables** tab.

### If many columns in the table are empty

A BankSync transactions table has 24 columns, and WalletFeed puts data in 12 of them. WalletFeed also adds 5 columns, for example **Pending** and **Wallet Status**, at the right end of the table.

1. In the table, click **Fields**.
2. Remove the empty columns from the view.
3. Click **Save view**.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to Coda

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a table in Coda, which changed its name to Superhuman Docs. You make the table and an API token in Superhuman Docs, and then you paste the token into WalletFeed.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- WalletFeed, and an Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account that WalletFeed can read.
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), which is necessary for [destinations](/docs/destinations/). It is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.
- A Superhuman Docs account. You can make an API token on the Free plan.
- A computer with a web browser, for the steps in Superhuman Docs.

## Step 1: Make a doc and a table in Superhuman Docs

1. On your computer, open [Superhuman Docs](https://docs.superhuman.com/).
2. Sign in.
3. Click **+ New doc**.

   ![The Superhuman Docs home page, with the New doc button at the top of the sidebar.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-docs-home.webp)

4. If a message or the **Docs AI** panel opens, close it.
5. If you cannot see the sidebar with the list of pages, click the sidebar button at the top left.
6. Click the doc name, **Untitled doc**, at the top of the sidebar.

   ![A new doc in Superhuman Docs, with its name, Untitled doc, at the top of the sidebar.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-new-doc.webp)

7. Type a name for the doc, for example `WalletFeed`.
8. Press Return.
9. Click in the page, below **Add page title**. If you do not click in the page, the text that you type goes into the doc name.
10. Type `/table`.
11. In the menu, below **Tables**, click **Table**.

    ![The menu that opens when you type /table, with the Table item at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-insert-table.webp)

12. In the **New table** panel, click **Start blank**.

    ![The New table panel, with Start blank at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-start-blank.webp)

13. Double-click the table name, **Table**. This selects all of the name.
14. Type `WalletFeed Transactions`. In Step 4, WalletFeed selects the table that has this name.

    ![The table with its new name, WalletFeed Transactions.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-name-table.webp)

15. Press Return.
16. Keep the doc in **My Docs**.
17. Do not use **Share** on the doc.

> **Note:** On the Free plan, a doc that other persons can open has a limit of 1,000 table rows. If such a doc has more rows than the limit for 14 days, Superhuman Docs stops all changes to it. A doc that only you can open has no such limit.

## Step 2: Make the columns

WalletFeed writes to the columns that have these names, and ignores other columns. Only the **WalletFeed ID** column is necessary. Each name must have the same letters and spaces as in this table, but the letters can be uppercase or lowercase.

| Column name | Column type |
|---|---|
| WalletFeed ID | Text |
| Date | Date |
| Merchant | Text |
| Amount | Number |
| Currency | Text |
| Category | Text |
| Status | Text |
| Pending | Checkbox |
| Account | Text |
| Description | Text |
| Type | Text |
| MCC | Number |
| Foreign Amount | Number |
| Foreign Currency | Text |

A new table has four columns: **Name**, **Column 2**, **Column 3** and **Notes**. You change their names first, and then you add the other 10 columns.

1. Click the column name **Name**. This selects the column.
2. Click **Name** again.
3. Type `WalletFeed ID`.

   ![The first column, with its new name, WalletFeed ID.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-rename-first-column.webp)

4. Press Return.
5. Change the name of **Column 2** to `Date`, as in steps 1 to 4.
6. Put the pointer on **Date**. The type button (**T**) shows on the right side of the column name.
7. Click the type button.
8. Click **Column type** › **Date** › **Date**.

   ![The menu of the Date column, with Column type, Date and Date.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-column-type-date.webp)

9. Change the name of **Column 3** to `Merchant`.
10. Change the name of **Notes** to `Amount`.
11. Put the pointer on **Amount**.
12. Click the type button.
13. Click **Column type** › **Number** › **Number**. This step is necessary because **Notes** is a **Canvas** column, not a number column.

    ![The menu of the Amount column, with Column type, Number and Number.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-column-type-number.webp)

14. Put the pointer on the column names. The **+** button shows at the right end of the column names.
15. If you cannot see **+**, scroll the table to the right until you can see it. This occurs when the table is wider than the window.
16. Click **+**.

    ![The plus button at the end of the column names, which adds a column.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-add-column.webp)

17. In **Pick column type**, click **Text**.

    ![The Pick column type menu, with Text at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-pick-column-type.webp)

18. Type `Currency`. If you do not type a name, the column has the name **Text**, and WalletFeed ignores it.

    ![A new column with the name Currency.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-name-new-column.webp)

19. Press Return.
20. Do steps 14 to 19 again for each of the other columns, from `Category` to `Foreign Currency`. In step 17, click the type of the column:

    - **Checkbox** for **Pending**
    - **Number** › **Number** for **MCC** and **Foreign Amount**
    - **Text** for all other columns

21. Put the pointer on the table.
22. Click **Options**.
23. Click **Columns**. The panel shows the 14 columns and their types.

    ![The Columns panel, with all 14 WalletFeed columns and their types.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-all-columns.webp)

You can delete the three empty rows of the new table. For each empty row, do these steps:

1. Right-click the row.
2. If you cannot see **Delete row** at the bottom of the menu, scroll down the menu.
3. Click **Delete row**.

## Step 3: Make an API token in Superhuman Docs

1. On your computer, open the [Superhuman Docs home page](https://docs.superhuman.com/).
2. Click your name at the bottom of the sidebar.
3. Click **Account settings**.

   ![The account menu, with Account settings.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-account-menu.webp)

4. In the list on the left side, click **API connections**.

   ![The Account settings page, with API connections in the list on the left side.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-account-settings.webp)

5. In **API tokens**, click **Generate API token**.

   ![The API tokens section, with the Generate API token button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-api-connections.webp)

6. In **Name**, type `WalletFeed`.
7. Click **Permission**. Its value is **Read only** until you change it.
8. Click **Read and write**. If the token is **Read only**, WalletFeed does not add the destination.

   ![The New API token dialog, with Read and write in the Permission list.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-token-permission.webp)

9. In **Scopes**, keep **Content** and **All** selected. With **Selected content**, WalletFeed cannot find your doc.

   ![The New API token dialog with the name WalletFeed, Read and write in Permission, Content and All in Scopes, and the Generate token button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-token-settings.webp)

10. Click **Generate token**.
11. In **API token generated**, click **Copy**. Superhuman Docs shows the token only one time.

    ![The API token generated dialog, with the Copy button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-token-created.webp)

12. If you closed the dialog before you clicked **Copy**, do steps 5 to 11 again.

> **Note:** If you use a Mac with the same Apple Account as your iPhone, you can paste the token on the iPhone with [Universal Clipboard](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102430).

> **Note:** On your iPhone, the **Open Account Settings** link in WalletFeed opens **Account settings** › **API connections** in Superhuman Docs.

## Step 4: Add Coda in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The empty Destinations screen, with the plus button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. Below **Sheets & Databases**, tap **Coda**. If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed first shows the **WalletFeed Pro** screen.
5. Paste the token in **API Token**.

   ![The Coda setup form in WalletFeed, with the API Token field and the setup steps.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/walletfeed-setup-coda.webp)

6. Make sure that **Doc** shows your doc. If it shows a different doc, select your doc in **Doc**.
7. Make sure that **Table** shows **WalletFeed Transactions**. If it shows a different table, select **WalletFeed Transactions** in **Table**.
8. Tap **Add**. If a message in red shows below the fields, refer to [If there is a problem](#if-there-is-a-problem).
9. Read the **Send Transactions to Coda?** message.

   The message tells you which data the destination receives, from which accounts, and from which date. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes the destination.

10. Tap **Send**.

    ![A Superhuman Docs table with six sample transactions in the 14 WalletFeed columns.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-walletfeed-result.webp)

After some seconds, the rows show in your table. In **Destinations**, the new destination has the name of your doc after Coda, for example **Coda · WalletFeed**.

## Data in each column

WalletFeed writes these values to the columns:

| Column | Value |
|---|---|
| WalletFeed ID | The ID of the transaction in Wallet. WalletFeed uses it to find the row again. |
| Date | The date of the transaction, in the time zone of your iPhone. |
| Merchant | The merchant name, or the description if Wallet has no merchant name. |
| Amount | The value of the transaction. |
| Currency | The currency code, for example USD. |
| Category | The WalletFeed category, for example Dining or Groceries. |
| Status | The status in Wallet, for example `pending` or `booked`. |
| Pending | A check mark while the charge is pending. |
| Account | The account name, for example Apple Card or Apple Cash. |
| Description | The description from Wallet. |
| Type | The transaction type from Wallet, for example `pointOfSale`. |
| MCC | The merchant category code. A **Number** column shows 5814 as 5,814. |
| Foreign Amount | The value in the currency of the merchant. |
| Foreign Currency | The currency code of the merchant. |

A value in **Amount** or **Foreign Amount** is less than zero for money that goes out of the account. It is more than zero for money that goes into the account. **Foreign Amount** and **Foreign Currency** are empty for a transaction in US dollars.

Your transactions go from your iPhone directly to Superhuman Docs. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. WalletFeed keeps the token in the Keychain on your iPhone. After Superhuman Docs receives your transactions, its terms are applicable to them.

## New and changed transactions
