While WalletFeed is open, the table receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. This occurs only if [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**.

A pending charge has a check mark in **Pending**. When the charge changes from pending to posted, WalletFeed updates the same row.

For a refund or a payment, WalletFeed adds a new row with a value more than zero in **Amount**. It deletes the row of a declined charge. When Wallet removes a transaction, WalletFeed also deletes the row of that transaction.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › [Initial History](/docs/send-history/). **Initial History** is **All** until you change it.

To send history from the screen of the destination, do these steps:

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Coda destination.
2. Tap **Send History**.
3. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

While WalletFeed sends the history, it shows **Sending History**. It does not add a second row for a transaction that is in the table.

## Change or remove the destination

In WalletFeed, you change the destination on its screen. To open this screen, tap the Coda destination in **Destinations**.

To send only some transactions, set **Filter** to on. Then set **Include**, **Minimum**, **Include Pending**, **Accounts**, **Categories** or **Exclude**. For more information, refer to [Choose what a destination receives](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).

To stop the destination for some time, set **Enabled** to off.

To use a new token:

1. Tap **Replace Token**.
2. Paste the new token.
3. Tap **Replace**. WalletFeed makes sure that the token can read and write the table.

To use a column that you add after setup:

1. In Superhuman Docs, give the column a name from the table in Step 2.
2. In WalletFeed, tap **Send Test**. WalletFeed reads the columns again and adds a test row with the merchant WalletFeed. You can delete that row.

You can change the name of a column after setup. WalletFeed continues to write to the same column.

To remove the destination:

1. Tap **Delete**.
2. Tap **Delete** again. The rows that WalletFeed sent stay in the table.

To stop the token in Superhuman Docs:

1. On your computer, open **Account settings** › **API connections** in Superhuman Docs.
2. On the **WalletFeed** token, click **⋮**.
3. Click **Revoke**.

   ![The token menu, with Revoke.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-token-revoke-menu.webp)

4. In **Revoke token?**, click **Revoke**. After this, WalletFeed cannot send to the table.

   ![The Revoke token dialog, with the Revoke button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-token-revoke-confirm.webp)

## If there is a problem

### If WalletFeed shows "This token is Read only"

The token has **Read only** in **Permission**. WalletFeed can read your doc with this token, but it cannot add rows.

1. On your computer, open **Account settings** › **API connections** in Superhuman Docs. A **Read only** token shows **Read only - Content** below its name.

   ![A token in the API tokens list with the line Read only - Content.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-T1-token-read-only.webp)

2. Make a new token with **Read and write**, as in [Step 3](#step-3-make-an-api-token-in-superhuman-docs).
3. In WalletFeed, paste the new token in the same field as the **Read only** token.
4. Tap **Add** or **Replace** again.

### If WalletFeed shows "Authentication failed"

Superhuman Docs does not accept the token. For example, you used **Revoke** on it.

1. In Superhuman Docs, make a new token, as in Step 3.
2. On your iPhone, tap the Coda destination in **Destinations**.
3. Tap **Replace Token**.
4. Paste the new token.
5. Tap **Replace**.

### If WalletFeed shows "The token can't reach this doc"

The token has **Selected content** in **Scopes**. With this token, WalletFeed cannot find your docs.

1. In Superhuman Docs, make a new token with **Content** and **All**, as in Step 3.
2. In WalletFeed, paste the new token in the same field as the token with **Selected content**.
3. Tap **Add** or **Replace** again.

### If WalletFeed shows "Token rejected (HTTP 401). Check it and try again."

The token is not correct, or you used **Revoke** on it.

1. In Superhuman Docs, make a new token, as in Step 3.
2. Click **Copy** to copy the token. The dots in the dialog are not the token.
3. In WalletFeed, paste the new token.

### If WalletFeed shows "No docs yet"

WalletFeed cannot find a doc in your Superhuman Docs account.

1. In Superhuman Docs, make the doc and the table, as in Step 1 and Step 2.
2. In WalletFeed, tap the back button.
3. Tap **Coda** again.
4. Paste the token again.

### If WalletFeed shows "This table needs a column named WalletFeed ID."

No column in the table has the name WalletFeed ID with the same letters and spaces.

1. In WalletFeed, make sure that **Table** shows **WalletFeed Transactions**.
2. In Superhuman Docs, change the name of the first column to `WalletFeed ID`.
3. In WalletFeed, tap **Add** again.

### If a column stays empty

The column name is not the same as a name in Step 2, or you added the column after setup. WalletFeed also does not write to a column that has a formula.

1. In Superhuman Docs, correct the name of the column.
2. On your iPhone, tap the Coda destination in **Destinations**.
3. Tap **Send Test**. WalletFeed reads the columns again and adds a test row.

### If WalletFeed shows "Server error (503)"

Superhuman Docs did not add or change the rows in one minute. WalletFeed sends them again at the next sync.

1. To send the rows at this time, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of **Destinations**.
2. Tap **Sync Now**.

### If WalletFeed shows "Coda doc full"

The full message is "Coda doc full. To add the next doc, use a token with no scopes." Other persons can open your doc, and its tables have 1,000 rows or more. On the Free plan, Superhuman Docs then stops changes to the doc. WalletFeed can continue in a copy of the doc, but only a token with no scopes can make the copy.

1. On your computer, do steps 1 to 8 of [Step 3](#step-3-make-an-api-token-in-superhuman-docs).
2. In **Scopes**, click **Content** to remove its check mark. **Packs** and **MCP** must also have no check mark.
3. Click **Generate token**.
4. Click **Copy**.
5. On your iPhone, tap the Coda destination in **Destinations**.
6. Tap **Replace Token**.
7. Paste the new token.
8. Tap **Replace**.

At the next sync, WalletFeed makes a copy of your doc, **WalletFeed (2)**, in the same folder. Then it sends the new rows to that doc, and the destination shows "Coda doc full. Now writing to WalletFeed (2)."

> **Note:** Superhuman Docs lets only a Doc Maker in the workspace make docs. WalletFeed also makes the doc **WalletFeed Template**, a copy of your doc with an empty table, for the next copies.

### If Amount shows -23.4 and not -23.40

A **Number** column does not show a zero at the end of a value.

1. Put the pointer on **Amount**.
2. Click the type button on the right side of the column name.
3. Click **Column type** › **Number** › **Currency**.

### If Table shows a table that you deleted

Superhuman Docs can keep the table of a deleted page in its list of tables.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Table**.
2. Tap **WalletFeed Transactions**.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-csv/ -->
# Export Apple Card transactions to a CSV file automatically

WalletFeed exports your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a CSV file, and updates the file automatically when your transactions change. You select a folder, for example in iCloud Drive, and WalletFeed writes one row for each transaction to `WalletFeed Transactions.csv` in that folder.

## Before you start

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- WalletFeed, with access to your Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account.
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), for a file that WalletFeed updates. WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.
- A folder for the file. The folder can be in iCloud Drive, in **On My iPhone** or in a different file app, for example Dropbox.

Without WalletFeed Pro, you can [export one CSV file](#export-one-csv-file-without-walletfeed-pro). WalletFeed does not update that file.

## Step 1: Add a CSV file in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with no destinations and the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-csv/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In the search field, type `CSV`.

   ![The Add Destination screen with the Destinations search field above the Budgeting list.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-csv/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

5. Tap **CSV File**.

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, the **WalletFeed Pro** screen opens. After you get WalletFeed Pro on that screen, the **Files** screen opens.

6. Make sure that **Format** is **CSV**.
7. Make sure that **Save As** is **One File**.

   ![The Files screen with Format set to CSV, Save As set to One File and the name WalletFeed Transactions.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-csv/walletfeed-setup-csv-file.webp)

   With **One File**, WalletFeed writes all your transactions to one file. The newest transaction is at the top. To get one file for each month, tap **Save As**. Then select **One File per Month**. Each file then has its month in the name, for example `WalletFeed 2026-10.csv`.

8. Tap **Folder**.
9. Select a folder, for example in iCloud Drive.

   **Folder** then shows the name of the folder.

10. To use a different file name, type it in **Name**.

    The name of the file then has `.csv` at the end. For example, if you type `Budget` or `Budget.csv`, the file is `Budget.csv`.

11. Tap **Add**.

    You can tap **Add** only after you select a folder.

12. When WalletFeed shows **Save Transactions to Files?**, tap **Save**.

    The message tells you the folder, the data that the folder receives, the accounts and the period. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes the new destination.

WalletFeed then writes your transactions to the file. WalletFeed does not keep your transactions in the app.

## Step 2: Open the file

1. On your iPhone, open the Files app.
2. Open the folder that you selected in Step 1.
3. Tap the file, for example `WalletFeed Transactions.csv`.

   With **One File per Month**, each month has a file, for example `WalletFeed 2026-10.csv`.

If the folder is in iCloud Drive, you can also open the file on a computer that has access to your iCloud Drive. For the steps to use the file in a spreadsheet, refer to [the Numbers guide](/guides/apple-card-to-numbers/) or [the Excel guide](/guides/apple-card-to-excel/).

## Export one CSV file without WalletFeed Pro

[Export CSV](/docs/export-csv/) makes one CSV file with the transactions from a period that you select. You can use Export CSV without WalletFeed Pro. The file does not change after you export it.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. Tap **Export CSV**.

   ![The Settings screen with Export CSV in the Data section.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-csv/walletfeed-settings-3.webp)

4. Tap **Range**.

   ![The Export CSV screen with Range set to This Month, 29 transactions and the Export button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-csv/walletfeed-export-csv.webp)

5. Select **This Month**, **Last Month**, **Last 90 Days**, **This Year** or **All**.

   **Transactions** shows the number of transactions in that period.

6. Tap **Export**.
7. In the share sheet, tap **Save to Files**.
8. Select a folder.
9. Tap **Save**.

The name of the file has the period in it, for example `Apple Card Last Month.csv`. The name starts with `Apple Card`, also for a file with Apple Cash or Savings transactions. The file has the same columns as the file that WalletFeed updates.

## Columns in the file

Each CSV file from WalletFeed has one row for each transaction, and these columns:

| Column | Data |
| --- | --- |
| **Date** | The date of the transaction in the time zone of your iPhone, for example 2026-10-28. |
| **Posted Date** | The date when the charge posted. This cell is empty while the charge is pending. |
| **Merchant** | The merchant name. If Wallet has no merchant name, this cell has the description. |
| **Description** | The description of the transaction in Wallet. |
| **Original Description** | The text of the transaction from the card network. |
| **Amount** | The value, for example -23.40. Purchases and fees are negative numbers. Payments and refunds are positive numbers. |
| **Currency** | The currency code, for example USD. |
| **Direction** | `debit` for purchases and fees, or `credit` for payments and refunds. |
| **Status** | The status in Wallet: `authorized`, `pending`, `booked` (posted) or `memo`. A file from **Export CSV** can also have `rejected` (declined). |
| **Type** | The transaction type in Wallet, for example `pointOfSale`, `refund` or `transfer`. |
| **Category** | The WalletFeed category, for example **Groceries**, **Dining** or **Cash & Transfers**. |
| **MCC** | The merchant category code from the card network. |
| **Account** | The Wallet account, for example Apple Card. |
| **Foreign Amount** | For a purchase in a different currency, the value in that currency. |
| **Foreign Currency** | The code of that different currency. |
| **WalletFeed ID** | The ID of the transaction. WalletFeed uses it to find and update each row. |

The file is UTF-8 text in the RFC 4180 CSV format. If you move the columns in `WalletFeed Transactions.csv`, WalletFeed can continue to update the file, because WalletFeed finds each column by its name. WalletFeed then writes the columns in the sequence that the table shows.

> **Note:** WalletFeed writes only these columns. When WalletFeed updates `WalletFeed Transactions.csv`, it removes all other columns and all rows that have no **WalletFeed ID**.

## Changes to the file

While WalletFeed is open, the file receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. This occurs only if [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**.

If WalletFeed cannot open the folder at that time, the file does not change. WalletFeed then updates the file at these times:

- When you open WalletFeed.
- When an automation from **Settings** › **Sync** › **Automations** starts a sync.
- While your iPhone charges, at a time that iOS selects.

A pending charge is in the file with the status `pending` or `authorized`. When the charge posts, WalletFeed updates the same row, and the status changes to `booked`. The row stays in the same position.

WalletFeed removes the rows of declined charges and the rows of transactions that Wallet deletes. A refund is a different transaction. In its row, **Amount** is a positive number and **Direction** is `credit`.

With **One File per Month**, WalletFeed writes the full file of a month again when a transaction in that month changes. A month with no transactions gets no file.

## Send previous transactions

A new CSV file also receives your previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. You can select **Today**, **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

To add transactions from before that date, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination, for example **WalletFeed Transactions**.
3. Tap **Send History**.
4. Select **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

Because WalletFeed finds each row by its **WalletFeed ID**, the file has only one row for each transaction.

## Change or remove the destination

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination, for example **WalletFeed Transactions**.
3. Do one of these steps:
   - To write only some transactions to the file, set **Filter** to on. Then set **Include**, **Minimum**, **Include Pending**, **Accounts**, **Categories** or **Exclude**.
   - To put the file in a different folder, tap **Change Folder**. Then select the folder.
   - To stop the changes to the file, set **Enabled** to off.
   - To remove the destination, tap **Delete**. Then tap **Delete** again.

After you change the folder, WalletFeed writes the transactions from the first date to a file in the new folder. If you change **Name** on this screen, the name of the file does not change.

After you delete the destination, the file stays in the folder. WalletFeed does not remove the transactions that it wrote to the file.

## If there is a problem

### If WalletFeed shows “Couldn't open this folder.”

WalletFeed cannot get access to the folder that you selected.

1. Tap **Folder**, or tap **Change Folder** on the screen of the destination.
2. Select a different folder.

### If WalletFeed shows “Can't open the folder. Choose it again.”

WalletFeed does not have access to the folder of the destination at this time.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Change Folder**.
4. Select the same folder again.

### If WalletFeed shows “The file has no WalletFeed ID column.”

WalletFeed does not change a file that has no **WalletFeed ID** column.

1. On your iPhone, open the Files app.
2. Open the folder of the destination.
3. Change the name of `WalletFeed Transactions.csv`, for example to `WalletFeed Transactions 1.csv`.
4. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
5. Tap the destination.
6. Tap **Send History**.
7. Tap **All**.

WalletFeed makes a new `WalletFeed Transactions.csv` with all your transactions.

### If the folder has no CSV file

WalletFeed did not write the file to the folder.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Send Test**.

   The folder then gets `WalletFeed Test.csv` with a sample transaction. If this file is in the folder, WalletFeed can write to the folder.

4. To write all your transactions to the file, tap **Send History**.
5. Tap **All**.

### If new transactions are not in the file

WalletFeed did not update the file, or the app that shows the file did not read it again after WalletFeed changed it.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button).
3. Tap **Sync Now**.
4. Open the file again, for example `WalletFeed Transactions.csv`.

### If a name or description starts with an apostrophe

WalletFeed puts an apostrophe (`'`) before text that starts with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@`. With the apostrophe, a spreadsheet does not use the text as a formula.

### If you cannot tap Export

**Export** is not available while WalletFeed reads the transactions, or when the period has no transactions.

1. Wait until **Transactions** shows a number.
2. If the number is 0, tap **Range**.
3. Select a different period, for example **All**.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-excel/ -->
# Open Apple Card transactions in Excel

WalletFeed exports your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a CSV file that Excel opens on a Mac or a PC. You can export a file with [**Export CSV**](/docs/export-csv/), or get [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/) and let WalletFeed update a file in iCloud Drive for you.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version
- WalletFeed on your iPhone
- Excel on a Mac or a PC
- iCloud Drive on your iPhone and on your computer
- WalletFeed Pro, for a file that WalletFeed updates.

WalletFeed is available only in the US. WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase. You can also use a different location in Files, for example Dropbox.

## Step 1: Make a CSV file on your iPhone

Use one of these methods.

### Export a file one time

WalletFeed Pro is not necessary for **Export CSV**.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. At the top of the screen, tap **Settings** (the gear button).
3. In the **Data** section, tap **Export CSV**.

   ![The Settings screen shows Export CSV below Data.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-excel/walletfeed-settings-3.webp)

4. Tap **Range**.
5. Select **This Month**, **Last Month**, **Last 90 Days**, **This Year** or **All**.

   **Transactions** shows the number of transactions in the range.

   ![The Export CSV screen shows the range This Month and 29 transactions.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-excel/walletfeed-export-csv.webp)

6. Tap **Export**.

   The share sheet opens.

7. Tap **Save to Files**.
8. Save the file in a folder in iCloud Drive.

   The name of the file includes the range, for example `Apple Card This Month.csv`.

> **Note:** In the share sheet, you can also tap a different app to send the file to your computer. WalletFeed keeps no copy of the file. The file goes only to the location that you select.

### Update a file in iCloud Drive (WalletFeed Pro)

With WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed writes your transactions to a CSV file in a folder that you select. When your transactions change, WalletFeed updates the file.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+**.

   ![The Destinations screen has no destinations and shows the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-excel/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In the search field, type `Excel`.
5. Tap **CSV File**.

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed shows the WalletFeed Pro screen first. After you start the free trial or get WalletFeed Pro, the **Files** screen opens.

6. Make sure that **Format** is **CSV**.
7. Make sure that **Save As** is **One File**.

   With **One File**, all your transactions are in one file, and WalletFeed puts the newest transaction first.

   ![The Files screen shows CSV in Format and One File in Save As.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-excel/walletfeed-setup-csv-file.webp)

   > **Note:** With **One File per Month**, each month has a different file, for example `WalletFeed 2026-10.csv`.

8. Tap **Folder**.
9. Select a folder in iCloud Drive.

   **Add** is available after you select a folder.

10. If you want a different name for the file, type the name in **Name**.

    If you do not change the name, the file is `WalletFeed Transactions.csv`.

11. Tap **Add**.

    The message **Save Transactions to Files?** opens. It shows the data that the folder receives, the accounts and the start date.

12. Tap **Save**.

    Then, WalletFeed writes your transactions to the file.

> **Note:** WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. WalletFeed keeps no copy of the file. The file is in the folder that you selected.

## Step 2: Open the file in Excel

1. On your Mac or PC, find the file, for example in iCloud Drive.
2. Open the file in Excel.

   Excel shows one row for each transaction.

3. If WalletFeed updates the file for you, save your changes in a copy that has a different name.

> **Note:** When WalletFeed updates the file, it removes the columns that it does not write. It also removes the rows that have no WalletFeed ID. With **One File per Month**, WalletFeed writes the full file for a month again, and your changes to that file do not stay.

## Columns in the file

The first row has the names of the columns. Each row after it is one transaction. The file has these columns:

| Column | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Date | The date of the transaction, for example 2026-10-30. |
| Posted Date | The date that the transaction posted. This cell is empty while the transaction is pending. |
| Merchant | The name of the merchant. If Wallet has no merchant name, this cell has the text from Description. |
| Description | The description of the transaction from Wallet. |
| Original Description | The text of the transaction from the card network. |
| Amount | The value, for example `-23.40`. It is less than zero for a purchase and more than zero for a payment or a refund. |
| Currency | The currency code, for example USD. |
| Direction | `debit` if Amount is less than zero, or `credit` if Amount is more than zero. |
| Status | The status from Wallet, for example `pending`, or `booked` for a posted transaction. A file from **Export CSV** can also have `rejected` for a declined transaction. |
| Type | The type from Wallet, for example `pointOfSale` or `refund`. |
| Category | The WalletFeed category, for example Groceries. |
| MCC | The merchant category code, for example 5411. |
| Account | The name of the Wallet account, for example Apple Card. |
| Foreign Amount | For a transaction in a different currency, the value in that currency. |
| Foreign Currency | The code of the currency in Foreign Amount, for example EUR. |
| WalletFeed ID | The ID of the transaction. WalletFeed uses it to find the row of a transaction that changes. |

If the first character in a text cell is `=`, `+`, `-` or `@`, WalletFeed puts an apostrophe (`'`) before the text. As a result, Excel reads the cell as text and does not use it as a formula.

## Changes to the file

While WalletFeed is open, the file in iCloud Drive receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. For this, [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) must be on in **Settings** › **Sync**.

If WalletFeed cannot open the folder at that time, the file receives the changes when one of these conditions occurs:

- You open WalletFeed.
- A Shortcuts automation starts WalletFeed.
- iOS starts WalletFeed while your iPhone charges.

A pending transaction is in the file with the status `pending` or `authorized`. When the transaction posts, WalletFeed changes the same row. WalletFeed removes declined transactions from the file. A refund is a new row that has a value more than zero in Amount.

With **One File per Month**, WalletFeed writes the file for a month again each time that a transaction in that month changes.

## Send previous transactions

A new CSV File destination also receives your previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. You can select **Today**, **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

To send previous transactions to a destination after you add it:

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap the destination, for example **WalletFeed Transactions**.
4. Tap **Send History**.
5. Select **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

WalletFeed does not make two rows for one transaction. With **One File**, it finds the row that has the WalletFeed ID of the transaction and changes that row. For more information, refer to [Send History](/docs/send-history/).

## Change or remove the destination

To change the destination, tap it in [**Destinations**](/docs/destinations/). You can make these changes:

- To write only some transactions to the file, set **Filter** to on. Then, select accounts in **Accounts** or categories in **Categories**, or type a value in **Minimum**.
- To use a different folder, tap **Change Folder**. WalletFeed then writes your transactions from the start date to a file in that folder.
- To stop the updates to the file but keep the destination, set **Enabled** to off.
- To change the name of the destination, type a different name in **Name**. The name of the file does not change.

With **One File**, WalletFeed does not remove the rows that it wrote before you changed the filter. With **One File per Month**, WalletFeed uses the filter each time that it writes the file for a month again. It then removes the transactions that the filter does not include.

To remove the destination:

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap **Delete**.
3. In the message, tap **Delete** again.

The file and the transactions that WalletFeed wrote to it stay in the folder.

## If there is a problem

### If you cannot tap Export

You cannot tap **Export** while WalletFeed reads the transactions, or if the range has no transactions.

1. Wait until **Transactions** shows a number.
2. If the number is 0, tap **Range**.
3. Select a longer range, for example **All**.

### If the destination shows "Can't open the folder. Choose it again."

WalletFeed cannot open the folder that you selected.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap **Change Folder**.
3. Select the folder again.

WalletFeed writes your transactions to the file again. It does not make two rows for one transaction.

### If the destination shows "The file has no WalletFeed ID column."

WalletFeed cannot find the rows that it wrote, because the file has no WalletFeed ID column. For example, this problem occurs if you remove the column in Excel.

1. On your computer, change the name of the file.
2. On your iPhone, in **Destinations**, tap the destination.
3. Tap **Send History**.
4. Select **All**.

WalletFeed makes a new file and writes your transactions to it.

### If the file on your computer does not show new transactions

WalletFeed did not update the file after the last change in Wallet.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. At the top of the screen, tap **Settings** (the gear button).
3. In the **Sync** section, tap **Sync Now**.

   **Sync Now** shows the time of the last sync.

4. On your computer, open the file in Excel again.

### If Destinations shows "Sync Requires Pro"

You do not have WalletFeed Pro at this time. WalletFeed keeps the destination, but it does not update the file.

1. In **Destinations**, tap **Upgrade**.
2. Start the free trial, or get WalletFeed Pro.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to Firefly III

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to one account on your Firefly III server. You make a personal access token in Firefly III. Then you paste the token and the address of your server into WalletFeed.

## Before you start

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings in Wallet on that iPhone, and WalletFeed with [access to your Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/).
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), which is necessary for destinations. WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.
- Your Firefly III server, and a user account on it.
- An `https://` address for the server, with a certificate that iOS accepts. Your iPhone must connect to this address from all locations, not only on your home Wi-Fi.
- Your time zone in `TZ` on the server.

WalletFeed cannot use an `http://` address. The Firefly III image for Docker uses `http://` on port 8080. To get an `https://` address with a certificate that iOS accepts, you can use one of these:

- Tailscale HTTPS, with an address that ends in `.ts.net`
- A reverse proxy with a certificate from Let's Encrypt
- Cloudflare Tunnel

You can also make a root certificate and install it on your iPhone. Then, in **Settings** › **General** › **About** › **Certificate Trust Settings**, set the switch for that certificate to on.

WalletFeed sends the time of each transaction as the time on your iPhone, without a time zone. If the server uses a different time zone, a new transaction can have a time after the time on the server. Then Firefly III does not include the transaction in **Current balance** for some hours. If `TZ` has no value, Firefly III uses UTC.

## Step 1: Make a personal access token in Firefly III

You can do these steps on a computer, or in Safari on your iPhone. With Universal Clipboard, you can copy the token on a Mac and paste it on your iPhone. Do not send the token to yourself in a message or an email.

1. On your computer, sign in to Firefly III in a web browser.
2. Click the person icon at the top right of the page. The icon has no text.

   ![The Firefly III home page with the person icon at the top right highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/firefly-iii-user-icon.webp)

3. Click **Remote access and tokens**.

   ![The Firefly III account menu, with Remote access and tokens highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/firefly-iii-user-menu.webp)

4. In the **Personal Access Tokens** section, click **Create new token**.

   ![The Remote access and tokens page, with the Create new token button in the Personal Access Tokens section highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/firefly-iii-remote-access-page.webp)

   Do not click **Create New Client** in the **OAuth Clients and Applications** section. WalletFeed does not use OAuth clients.

5. In **Name**, type `WalletFeed`.
6. Click **Create**.

   ![The Create token dialog, with WalletFeed in the Name field and the Create button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/firefly-iii-create-token.webp)

7. Click in the large box that shows the token.
8. To select all the text in the box, press Command-A on a Mac, or Ctrl-A on Windows.
9. Copy the text.

   ![The Personal Access Token dialog with the new token, blurred here, in a large text box.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/firefly-iii-token-created.webp)

   > **Note:** Firefly III shows the token only one time. The token is very long, and the dialog has no copy button.

10. Click **Close**.

The token gives full access to your Firefly III data. WalletFeed keeps the token in the Keychain on your iPhone.

## Step 2: Add Firefly III in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen in WalletFeed with no destinations, and the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In the **Budgeting** section, tap **Firefly III**.

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed first shows the **WalletFeed Pro** screen. After you get WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed shows the Firefly III screen.

5. Paste the token into **Personal Access Token**.

   ![The Firefly III screen in WalletFeed, with the Personal Access Token field, the server address field and three steps.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/walletfeed-setup-firefly-iii.webp)

   > **Note:** The steps on this screen and the **Firefly III Docs** link give the path **Options** › **Profile** › **OAuth**. Firefly III 6.7.9 does not have this path. Step 1 on this page gives the path for Firefly III 6.7.9.

6. In the field that shows `https://firefly.example.com`, type the address of your server.

   Use the address that you use to open Firefly III in a browser. WalletFeed removes a `/` or `/api/v1` at the end. Then WalletFeed makes sure that the token and the address are correct, and shows **Account**.

7. Make sure that **Account** shows **New Apple Card**.

   With **New Apple Card**, WalletFeed makes an asset account with the name Apple Card in Firefly III. Its role is **Credit card**, and its currency is US dollars.

   If you made an account for your card in Firefly III, select that account. The list shows the active asset accounts and liabilities in Firefly III. If Firefly III has an account with the name Apple Card, WalletFeed selects it, and **New Apple Card** is not in the list.

8. Tap **Add**.
9. When WalletFeed shows **Send Transactions to Firefly III?**, tap **Send**.

   The message tells you which data Firefly III receives, from which Wallet accounts and from which date. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes the destination and sends nothing.

WalletFeed adds **Firefly III · Apple Card** to **Destinations**, and starts to send your transactions.

## Step 3: Find your transactions in Firefly III

1. On your computer, in the Firefly III sidebar, click **Accounts**.
2. Click **Asset accounts**.

   ![The Firefly III sidebar, with Accounts open and Asset accounts highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/firefly-iii-accounts-menu.webp)

3. Click **Apple Card**. Its role is **Credit card**.

   ![The Asset accounts list, with the Apple Card credit card account highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/firefly-iii-apple-card-account.webp)

4. Look at the **Transactions** section on the **Apple Card** page.

   ![The Apple Card account in Firefly III, with six card transactions and their amounts, dates, merchants and categories.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/firefly-iii-result-transactions.webp)

## Data that Firefly III receives

WalletFeed puts the transactions from all the Wallet accounts that you share into the one Firefly III account. This table shows the Firefly III field for each Wallet field.

| Wallet | Firefly III |
| --- | --- |
| A purchase | A withdrawal from your account to an expense account |
| A refund or a different credit | A deposit into your account from a revenue account |
| Merchant | The name of the expense account or revenue account. If Wallet has no merchant, WalletFeed uses the description. |
| Amount | **Amount**, with two decimals |
| Date | **Date**, in the time of your iPhone |
| Posted date | Book date |
| Description | **Description**. If Wallet has no description, WalletFeed uses the merchant. |
| Category, but not Other | **Category**. Firefly III adds the category if it is new. |
| Amount in a foreign currency | Foreign amount and foreign currency |
| Card statement text, merchant category code and foreign amount | **Notes** |
| The WalletFeed ID of the transaction | **External ID** |
| No Wallet field | The `walletfeed` tag. A pending charge also has the `pending` tag. |

![A Firefly III transaction from WalletFeed, with its category, external ID, notes, and the walletfeed and pending tags.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/firefly-iii-result-transaction-detail.webp)

WalletFeed sets the category and the notes only when it adds a transaction. When it updates a transaction, it changes only the amounts, the dates and the `pending` tag. Your changes to the description, the category, the notes and your tags stay.

Firefly III applies your rules to each new transaction. Firefly III receives a payment to your card as a deposit from a revenue account. You can change it to a transfer in Firefly III, or with a rule.

If Firefly III does not have the foreign currency, WalletFeed sends the transaction again without the foreign amount. The notes also show the foreign amount.

Your transactions go from your iPhone directly to your Firefly III server. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers.

## Sync times and changes

While WalletFeed is open, Firefly III receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. For this, [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) must be on in **Settings** › **Sync**.

A pending charge goes to Firefly III with the `pending` tag. When Wallet shows the charge as posted, WalletFeed updates the same transaction and removes the `pending` tag. If a transaction has more than one split in Firefly III, WalletFeed does not change it.

If Wallet shows a charge as declined or expired, WalletFeed deletes the transaction in Firefly III.

If Firefly III does not accept a change, WalletFeed tries to send it again the next time that it syncs.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. To change it, do these steps before you add Firefly III:

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In **Sync**, tap **Initial History**, then select **Today**, **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

   ![Settings, with Initial History set to All in the Sync section.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/walletfeed-settings.webp)

To send more previous transactions to your Firefly III destination, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. In **Destinations**, tap your Firefly III destination, such as **Firefly III · Apple Card**.
2. Tap **Send History**, then select **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

WalletFeed does not add a transaction two times. Before it adds a transaction, it looks for the **External ID** in Firefly III. While WalletFeed sends, the destination shows **Sending History** and the progress. To stop, tap **Send History** › **Stop Sending**.

## Change or remove the destination

In **Destinations**, tap your Firefly III destination. Then use this table:

| Change | On the destination screen |
| --- | --- |
| Stop the destination for a time | Set **Enabled** to off. |
| Send only some transactions | Set **Filter** to on. Then set **Include**, **Minimum**, **Include Pending**, **Accounts**, **Categories** or **Exclude**. |
| Send only one Wallet account, such as Apple Card | Set **Filter** to on, then select the account in **Accounts**. |
| Use a new token | Tap **Replace Token**, paste the token, then tap **Replace**. WalletFeed makes sure that Firefly III accepts the token. |
| Make sure that WalletFeed can send | Tap **Send Test**. Firefly III receives a test withdrawal of $4.20, with the merchant WalletFeed. You can delete it in Firefly III. |
| Remove the destination | Tap **Delete**, then tap **Delete** again. The transactions that WalletFeed sent stay in Firefly III. |

For more information about the filter, refer to [Choose what a destination receives](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).

### Replace the token after one year

You can use a personal access token for one year. In Firefly III, **Expires at** shows the last date of the token.

![The Personal Access Tokens list with one token named WalletFeed and its Expires at date.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/firefly-iii-token-list.webp)

1. Make a new token, as in [step 1](#step-1-make-a-personal-access-token-in-firefly-iii).
2. In WalletFeed, on the destination screen, tap **Replace Token**.
3. Paste the new token, then tap **Replace**.

### Delete the token in Firefly III

When you remove the destination, the token stays in Firefly III. To delete the token:

1. In Firefly III, click the person icon, then click **Remote access and tokens**.
2. In the **WalletFeed** row of **Personal Access Tokens**, click **Delete**.

   ![The Personal Access Tokens list, with the Delete button for the WalletFeed token highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/firefly-iii-delete-token.webp)

Firefly III deletes the token when you click **Delete**, and does not show a message first. The row stays on the page until you load the page again.

## If there is a problem

### If WalletFeed shows "Use your server's HTTPS address."

The address does not start with `https://`.

1. Type the `https://` address of your server. If your server has no `https://` address, refer to [Before you start](#before-you-start).

### If WalletFeed shows "iOS doesn't trust your server's certificate."

iOS does not accept the certificate of your server. A self-signed certificate gives this message.

1. Give your server a certificate that iOS accepts, as in [Before you start](#before-you-start).

### If WalletFeed shows "Can't reach your server."

Your iPhone cannot connect to the address. WalletFeed cannot use `localhost`, or an address on your home network such as `192.168.1.20`.

1. Use an `https://` address that your iPhone can connect to from all locations.

### If WalletFeed shows "No Firefly III API at this address."

The address does not go to Firefly III.

1. Type the address that you use to open Firefly III in a browser.

### If WalletFeed shows "Token rejected (HTTP 401)"

Firefly III does not accept the token. You did not copy all of the token, you deleted the token, or the token is expired. The number can also be 403.

1. Make a new token, as in [step 1](#step-1-make-a-personal-access-token-in-firefly-iii).
2. Make sure that you copy all the text in the token box.
3. Paste the new token into **Personal Access Token**.

### If you closed the token dialog before you copied the token

Firefly III shows a token only one time.

1. In **Personal Access Tokens**, click **Delete** in the row of that token.
2. Make a new token, as in [step 1](#step-1-make-a-personal-access-token-in-firefly-iii).

### If the destination shows "Authentication failed"

Firefly III does not accept the token now. The token can be expired, or you deleted it in Firefly III.

1. Make a new token, as in [step 1](#step-1-make-a-personal-access-token-in-firefly-iii).
2. In WalletFeed, on the destination screen, tap **Replace Token**.
3. Paste the new token, then tap **Replace**.

### If the destination shows "Can't connect"

Your iPhone cannot connect to the server, for example when you are not on your home Wi-Fi. WalletFeed tries again the next time that it syncs.

1. Make sure that your iPhone can open the `https://` address of the server from all locations.

### If a new transaction is not in Current balance

The server uses a different time zone from your iPhone. The transaction has a time after the time on the server.

1. Set `TZ` on the server to your time zone.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-gnucash/ -->
# Import Apple Card transactions into GnuCash

You can import your Apple Card transactions into GnuCash with the OFX files that WalletFeed writes from your iPhone. WalletFeed writes one file for each month to a folder that you select, and you import each file in GnuCash on your computer.

## Before you start

You must have:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version
- WalletFeed, with [access to your Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account](/docs/wallet-accounts/)
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase
- GnuCash on your computer
- iCloud Drive on your iPhone and on your computer, or a different location that Files shows, for example Dropbox.

WalletFeed is available only in the US.

## Step 1: Add an OFX file in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with no destinations and the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-gnucash/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In the **Destinations** search field, type `GnuCash`.

   ![The Add Destination screen with the Destinations search field above the Budgeting list.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-gnucash/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

   The list shows **OFX File** and **QIF File**. With an OFX file, GnuCash uses the transaction ID and does not import a transaction two times. A QIF file has no transaction ID.

5. Tap **OFX File**.

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed shows the **WalletFeed Pro** screen. After you get WalletFeed Pro, the **Files** screen opens.

6. Make sure that **Format** is **OFX**.

   ![The Files screen with OFX in Format, Choose… in Folder and WalletFeed in Name.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-gnucash/walletfeed-setup-ofx-file.webp)

7. Tap **Folder**.
8. Select a folder in iCloud Drive, or in the other location that you use.

   The **Folder** row shows the name of the folder. You can tap **Add** only after you select a folder.

9. To use a different name for the files, type it in **Name**.

   Each file name is that name with the month, for example `WalletFeed 2026-10.ofx`.

10. Tap **Add**.
11. When WalletFeed shows **Save Transactions to Files?**, tap **Save**.

    The message gives the folder, the data that the folder receives, the accounts and the period. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes the new destination.

WalletFeed then writes one file for each month that has posted transactions, for example `WalletFeed 2026-09.ofx` and `WalletFeed 2026-10.ofx`.

> **Note:** WalletFeed writes the files only to the folder that you selected. It does not keep a copy of the files.

## Step 2: Import the file in GnuCash

1. On your computer, open GnuCash.
2. Click **File** › **Import** › **Import OFX/QFX…**.
3. Open the folder that you selected in WalletFeed.
4. Select the file for a month, for example `WalletFeed 2026-10.ofx`.

   To import more than one month, you can select more than one file.

5. Click **Import**.
6. In the **Select Account** window, select the GnuCash account for your Apple Card.

   You can also add a GnuCash account with **New Account…**. GnuCash shows this window only when it imports a Wallet account for the first time. If the file also has Apple Cash or Savings, GnuCash shows the window for each of them.

7. Click **OK**.

   GnuCash records the account that you selected. Then, GnuCash shows the transactions from the file in the **Generic import transaction matcher** window.

8. To set the transfer account of a new transaction, double-click its row.

   The transfer account is the account for the other part of the transaction, for example `Expenses:Groceries`.

9. Select the transfer account.
10. Click **OK**.
11. Do steps 8, 9 and 10 again for each new transaction.
12. In the **Generic import transaction matcher** window, click **OK**.

    GnuCash adds the transactions to your Apple Card account.

> **Note:** If a new transaction has no transfer account when you click **OK**, GnuCash puts it in an Imbalance account.

The next time that you import a file, GnuCash can set the transfer account of a new transaction from the accounts that you selected previously. For more information, refer to [Importing Transactions from Files](https://www.gnucash.org/docs/v5/C/gnucash-manual/trans-import.html) in the GnuCash manual.

## Data that GnuCash receives

Each OFX file has one statement for each Wallet account. Apple Card has a credit card statement. Apple Cash has a checking account statement, and Savings has a savings account statement.

Each transaction in the file has this data:

| Data | In the OFX file |
| --- | --- |
| Date | The date of the transaction in Wallet. |
| Posted date | The date that the transaction posted. GnuCash uses this date as the date of the transaction. |
| Merchant | The merchant name, or the description if Wallet has no merchant name. WalletFeed writes only the first 32 characters. |
| Amount | The amount of the transaction. Purchases have a minus sign. Payments and refunds have no minus sign. |
| Currency | The currency of the statement, for example USD. |
| Memo | The description and the card network text, if they are different from the merchant. The amount in a different currency, if there is one. |
| Type | The type of transaction, for example a purchase, a payment or a transfer. |
| Transaction ID | The ID of the transaction in Wallet. GnuCash uses it to find the transactions that it imported previously. |

The file does not include the WalletFeed category or the balance of the account. You set the transfer account of each transaction in GnuCash.

WalletFeed changes curly quotes, dashes and ellipses to ASCII characters. Some other characters change to a character that is almost the same, or to a question mark.

## New transactions and changes

While WalletFeed is open, the folder receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. For this, [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) must be on in **Settings** › **Sync**.

If WalletFeed cannot open the folder at that time, it writes the files when one of these occurs:

- You open WalletFeed.
- A Shortcuts automation starts WalletFeed.
- iOS starts WalletFeed while your iPhone charges.

At each sync, WalletFeed writes the full file again for each month that has a change. You can import the file of a month more than one time, for example the file of this month. GnuCash uses the transaction ID to find the transactions that it imported previously. It does not import them again. If GnuCash previously imported all the transactions in a file, it shows a message that the file has no new transactions.

An OFX file includes a transaction only after it posts. When a pending charge posts, WalletFeed adds it to the file with the same transaction ID. A charge that does not post, for example a declined charge, is not in the file.

A refund is a different transaction from the purchase. Its amount has no minus sign.

If Wallet removes a transaction from this month or last month, WalletFeed removes it from the file of that month. If GnuCash previously imported the transaction, the transaction stays in GnuCash until you delete it.

## Send previous transactions

A new OFX File destination also receives your previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it.

[Send History](/docs/send-history/) writes the files again for a period that you select:

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **WalletFeed**, or the name that you typed in **Name**.
4. Tap **Send History**.
5. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.
6. On your computer, import the files for the months in that period in GnuCash, as in [Step 2](#step-2-import-the-file-in-gnucash).

GnuCash does not import a transaction two times.

## Change or stop the destination

### Open the destination

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **WalletFeed**, or the name that you typed in **Name**.

If you change **Name** on this screen, the names of the files stay the same.

### Send only some transactions

1. Open the destination.
2. Set **Filter** to on.
3. Set **Include**, **Minimum**, **Accounts**, **Categories** or **Exclude**.

For more information, refer to [Choose what to send](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).

### Use a different folder

1. Open the destination.
2. Tap **Change Folder**.
3. Select the new folder.

At the next sync, WalletFeed writes the files again in the new folder, from the same start date.

### Stop the destination temporarily

1. Open the destination.
2. Set **Enabled** to off.

### Remove the destination

1. Open the destination.
2. Tap **Delete**.
3. Tap **Delete** again.

The files stay in the folder. The transactions that you imported stay in GnuCash.

## If there is a problem

### If you cannot tap Add

You did not select a folder on the **Files** screen.

1. Tap **Folder**.
2. Select a folder in iCloud Drive.

### If WalletFeed shows “Couldn't open this folder.”

WalletFeed cannot get access to the folder that you selected on the **Files** screen.

1. Tap **Folder**.
2. Select a different folder in iCloud Drive.

### If the destination shows “Can't open the folder. Choose it again.”

WalletFeed does not have access to the folder of the destination.

1. Open the destination.
2. Tap **Change Folder**.
3. Select the folder again.

WalletFeed writes the files again. GnuCash does not import a transaction two times.

### If the folder has no file for a month

WalletFeed writes a file for a month only when the month has posted transactions.

1. Open the destination.
2. Tap **Send Test**.

   WalletFeed writes `WalletFeed Test.ofx` with one test transaction to the folder. This file shows that WalletFeed can write to the folder.

3. Do not import `WalletFeed Test.ofx` into GnuCash.
4. Tap **Send History**.
5. Tap **All**.

### If GnuCash does not show new transactions

WalletFeed did not write the file after the last change in Wallet, or the new charges are pending.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. Tap **Sync Now**.

   ![The Settings screen with Background Sync, Initial History and Sync Now in the Sync section.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-gnucash/walletfeed-settings.webp)

4. On your computer, import the file of the month again in GnuCash.

If the new charges are pending, WalletFeed adds them to the file after they post.

### If Destinations shows “Sync Requires Pro”

You do not have WalletFeed Pro at this time. WalletFeed keeps the destination, but it does not write the files.

1. In **Destinations**, tap **Upgrade**.
2. Select a plan.
3. Tap **Start Free Trial**, **Subscribe** or **Buy Lifetime**.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-google-sheets/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to Google Sheets

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to Google Sheets. After you sign in to Google in WalletFeed, WalletFeed makes a spreadsheet in your Google Drive and updates it automatically.

## Before you start

You must have:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- WalletFeed, with access to your Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase. WalletFeed Pro is necessary for all destinations.
- A Google Account.

## Step 1: Add Google Sheets in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The empty Destinations screen with the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-google-sheets/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In **Sheets & Databases**, tap **Google Sheets**.

   ![The Add Destination list with Google Sheets below Sheets & Databases.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-google-sheets/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, the **WalletFeed Pro** screen opens first. Do these steps on that screen:

   1. Select a plan.
   2. Complete the purchase.

   Then the Google Sheets screen opens.

## Step 2: Sign in to Google

1. Tap **Sign In with Google**.

   ![The Google Sheets screen with the Sign In with Google button and the Spreadsheet field.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-google-sheets/walletfeed-setup-google-sheets.webp)

2. On the Google page, sign in to the Google Account that you want to use.
3. Give WalletFeed access to the files that it makes.

   Then WalletFeed shows **Signed In**.

> **Note:** WalletFeed keeps the sign-in in the Keychain on your iPhone. With this sign-in, WalletFeed can open only the spreadsheets that it makes. Google shows this access with the description "See, edit, create, and delete only the specific Google Drive files you use with this app."

## Step 3: Make the spreadsheet

1. If you want a different name for the spreadsheet, type the name in **Spreadsheet**.

   The name is **WalletFeed Transactions** until you change it.

2. Tap **Add**.

   WalletFeed makes the spreadsheet in your Google Drive. Then WalletFeed shows the message **Send Transactions to Google Sheets?**

   The message tells you the data that Google Sheets receives, the Wallet accounts and the start date.

3. Tap **Send**.

   WalletFeed starts to send your transactions to the spreadsheet.

If you tap **Cancel** in the message, WalletFeed sends nothing and removes the destination. The spreadsheet stays in your Google Drive. It has only the header row.

## Step 4: Open the spreadsheet

1. In **Destinations**, tap the name of your spreadsheet, for example **WalletFeed Transactions**.
2. Tap **Open in Google Sheets**.

   The spreadsheet has one tab, **Transactions**. Row 1 has the headers. Each row below row 1 has one transaction.

On a computer, you can also find the spreadsheet in your Google Drive.

## Columns in the spreadsheet

This table shows the columns that WalletFeed writes, from A to N:

| Column | Header | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| A | **WalletFeed ID** | The ID of the transaction in WalletFeed |
| B | **Date** | The date of the transaction, in your time zone |
| C | **Merchant** | The merchant name. If Wallet has no merchant name, this column has the same data as **Description**. |
| D | **Amount** | Money out of the account is a negative number. Money into the account, for example a refund or a payment, is a positive number. |
| E | **Currency** | The currency code, for example USD |
| F | **Category** | The WalletFeed category, for example Groceries or Dining |
| G | **Status** | The status from Wallet, for example `booked` or `pending` |
| H | **Pending** | A checkbox that shows a check mark while the transaction is pending |
| I | **Account** | The name of the Wallet account, for example Apple Card |
| J | **Description** | The description of the transaction from Wallet |
| K | **Type** | The type of transaction from Wallet, for example `pointOfSale` |
| L | **MCC** | The merchant category code, as a number |
| M | **Foreign Amount** | For a transaction in a different currency, the amount in that currency. It is empty for other transactions. |
| N | **Foreign Currency** | For a transaction in a different currency, the code of that currency. It is empty for other transactions. |

WalletFeed writes numbers in **Amount** and **Foreign Amount**, and dates in **Date**. You can use them in formulas.

Do not change column A. WalletFeed uses the **WalletFeed ID** to find each row again.

WalletFeed writes each row from column A to column N. If you add columns, put them after column N.

You can change the name of the spreadsheet and the name of the **Transactions** tab. WalletFeed does not change the colors or fonts that you set.

Your transactions go from your iPhone directly to Google. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. After Google Sheets receives your transactions, Google's terms are applicable to them.

## New and changed transactions

While WalletFeed is open, the spreadsheet receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet.

For changes while WalletFeed is closed, [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) in **Settings** › **Sync** must be on. It is on until you set it to off.

WalletFeed adds each new transaction as a new row at the end of the tab. If a purchase is pending, its row has a check mark in **Pending**. When the purchase posts, WalletFeed updates the same row.

WalletFeed removes the rows of declined transactions and of transactions that Wallet removes. A refund is a new row with a positive number in **Amount**.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it.

To send transactions from before that start date, or to send them again, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. In **Destinations**, tap your spreadsheet.
2. Tap **Send History**.
3. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

   While WalletFeed sends the transactions, the screen shows **Sending History**.

If a transaction is in the spreadsheet, WalletFeed updates its row and does not add a second row. To stop before WalletFeed sends all the transactions, tap **Send History** › **Stop Sending**.

## Change or remove the destination

### Send only some transactions

1. In **Destinations**, tap your spreadsheet.
2. Set **Filter** to on.
3. Set the rules that you want, for example **Accounts**, **Categories** or **Minimum**.

   If Apple Intelligence is on, you can also type a rule, for example "Travel over $50, not Uber", and tap **Create Rule**.

### Stop and start the destination

1. In **Destinations**, tap your spreadsheet.
2. Set **Enabled** to off.

To start again, set **Enabled** to on.

### Remove the destination

1. In **Destinations**, tap your spreadsheet.
2. Tap **Delete**.
3. In the message, tap **Delete**.

   WalletFeed sends no more transactions to the spreadsheet. WalletFeed also removes the Google sign-in for the spreadsheet from your iPhone.

The spreadsheet and the transactions in it stay in your Google Drive. When you remove the destination, WalletFeed does not delete the data that it sent.

### Remove WalletFeed's access to your Google Account

To also remove the access that you gave WalletFeed in your Google Account, do these steps:

1. On a computer, open the [linked apps page](https://myaccount.google.com/linkedapps) of your Google Account.
2. Click **Access to your Google Account**.
3. Click WalletFeed.
4. Click **See details**.
5. Click **Remove access**.
6. Click **Confirm**.

## If there is a problem

### If WalletFeed shows "Signed out" or "Authentication failed"

Google does not accept the sign-in that you gave WalletFeed. This occurs if you remove WalletFeed's access on the linked apps page, or if WalletFeed does not use the sign-in for 6 months.

1. In **Destinations**, tap your spreadsheet.
2. Tap **Sign In Again**.
3. Sign in to the Google Account that you used to make the spreadsheet.
4. Give WalletFeed access to the files that it makes.

If you use a different Google Account, WalletFeed shows "This Google account can't open the spreadsheet. Use the one you set it up with."

### If WalletFeed shows "Google rejected the sign-in"

Google did not accept the sign-in when WalletFeed tried to make the spreadsheet.

1. On the **Google Sheets** screen, tap **Use Another Account**.
2. Sign in to your Google Account again.
3. Give WalletFeed access to the files that it makes.
4. Tap **Add**.

### If the spreadsheet does not receive new transactions

When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. This occurs only if **Background Sync** is on.

1. Open WalletFeed.

   While WalletFeed is open, it sends changes in seconds.

2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. Make sure that **Background Sync** is on.
4. Tap **Sync Now**.

### If Destinations shows "Sync Requires Pro"

Your WalletFeed Pro subscription stopped. WalletFeed Pro is necessary for destinations.

1. Tap **Upgrade**.
2. Select a plan.
3. Complete the purchase.

If you have a previous WalletFeed Pro purchase with the same Apple Account, tap **Restore Purchases** on the **WalletFeed Pro** screen.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-linear/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to Linear

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to Linear. It makes one issue for each month, or one issue for each transaction. You make a personal API key in Linear, then paste it into WalletFeed.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- WalletFeed, with access to your [Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/).
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase. You must have WalletFeed Pro to send transactions to Linear.
- A Linear account. To make one, open [Linear's sign-up page](https://linear.app/signup). You can use the Free plan of Linear.

> **Note:** On Linear's Free plan, a workspace with more than 250 issues cannot get new issues. With **Monthly**, WalletFeed makes one issue for each month. With **Each Transaction**, WalletFeed makes one issue for each transaction. [Step 3](#step-3-set-a-filter) shows how to send only some transactions.

## Step 1: Make a personal API key in Linear

A personal API key is a code that lets WalletFeed make issues in your Linear workspace.

1. On your iPhone, open [Linear's Security & Access settings](https://linear.app/settings/account/security). In WalletFeed, the **Security & Access** link on the Linear screen opens the same page.
2. If Linear shows its login page, log in with your email address or your Google account. Linear does not use passwords.
3. If Linear shows **Verifying it’s you**, tap the **Verify you are human** checkbox.

   ![The Linear page with the heading Verifying it’s you and the Verify you are human checkbox.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-linear/linear-verify-human.webp)

4. If you log in with your email address, open the email from Linear.
5. To log in, use the link or the code in the email.
6. If Linear shows a different page after you log in, open [Linear's Security & Access settings](https://linear.app/settings/account/security) again.
7. On the **Security & Access** page, find the API section.
8. In the API section, tap the button for a new personal API key.
9. If Linear shows a field for a name, type `WalletFeed`.
10. Give the key full access, or only **Read** and **Write** access. If you select only **Create issues**, WalletFeed cannot change or archive issues.
11. Optional: Give the key access to only the team that will receive the issues.
12. Tap the button that makes the key.
13. Copy the key. The key starts with `lin_api_`.
14. Keep this page open until you paste the key into WalletFeed.

## Step 2: Add Linear in WalletFeed

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. Optional: If your workspace is on Linear's Free plan and you select **Each Transaction** in step 10, set **Initial History** to **Today**. Then the new destination receives no transactions from before today. **Settings** shows the **Sync** section only with WalletFeed Pro.
   1. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
   2. In the **Sync** section, set **Initial History** to **Today**.

      ![WalletFeed Settings with the Sync section and Initial History set to All.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-linear/walletfeed-settings.webp)

   3. Tap **Done**.
3. Tap **Destinations**.
4. Tap **+**.

   ![The Destinations screen in WalletFeed with the + button and no destinations.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-linear/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

5. Under **Sheets & Databases**, tap **Linear**. You can also type `Linear` in the search field.
6. If WalletFeed shows the **WalletFeed Pro** screen, get WalletFeed Pro on that screen. Then the **Linear** screen opens.
7. Paste the key into the **API Key** field. WalletFeed keeps the key in the Keychain on your iPhone.

   ![The Linear screen in WalletFeed with the API Key field, three steps and the Security & Access link.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-linear/walletfeed-setup-linear.webp)

8. After WalletFeed reads the key, select a team in **Team**. This team receives the issues.
9. Optional: In **Project**, select a project. If you do not select a project, **Project** stays at **None**. A project must be in Linear before WalletFeed can show it.
10. In **Send**, select **Monthly** or **Each Transaction**.

    With **Monthly**, each month becomes one issue, with a table of its transactions. **Monthly** is the default.

    With **Each Transaction**, each transaction becomes one issue.

11. Tap **Add**.
12. Read the message **Send Transactions to Linear?** It tells you the fields that Linear receives. It also gives the accounts and the start date of the transactions.
13. Tap **Send**. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed does not add the destination.

**Destinations** then shows the new destination with the name of the team, for example “Linear · Finance”.

## Step 3: Set a filter

With a [filter](/docs/choose-what-to-send/), WalletFeed sends only some transactions to Linear. If **Send** is **Each Transaction** and your workspace is on Linear's Free plan, set a filter.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Linear destination.
2. Set the **Filter** switch to on.

   ![The destination screen for Lunch Money in WalletFeed, with the Filter switch set to off.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-linear/walletfeed-destination-detail.webp)

3. Optional: Set **Include** to **Purchases**. Then Linear receives no refunds or payments.
4. Optional: In **Minimum**, type an amount, for example `25`. Then Linear receives only transactions of $25 or more.
5. Optional: In **Accounts** or **Categories**, select only the accounts or categories to send to Linear.
6. Optional: To send previous transactions with this filter, tap **Send History**. Refer to [Send previous transactions](#send-previous-transactions).

## Data that Linear receives

Your transactions go from your iPhone directly to Linear. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. After Linear receives your transactions, Linear's terms are applicable to them.

WalletFeed puts each issue in the team that you selected, and in the project if you selected one. If Triage is on for the team, a new issue goes to Triage. If Triage is off, the issue goes to the first Backlog status of the team.

### Monthly

Each month becomes one issue. The title has the accounts of the transactions and the month, for example `Apple Card transactions, October 2026`.

The description starts with the number of transactions and their total, for example `42 transactions · Total $1,234.56`. Then it has a table of the transactions of the month, newest first. The table has these columns:

- **Date**
- **Merchant**, with `· Pending` after the merchant until the charge posts
- **Amount**, with + before the amount of a refund or a payment
- **Category**
- **Account**, only if the month has transactions from more than one Wallet account

The last line of the description starts with `WalletFeed ID:`. WalletFeed uses this line and an attachment with the title WalletFeed to find the issue again.

If a month has more than approximately 400 transactions, the table shows only the newest transactions. Then the description shows, for example, “Showing the newest 412 of 530 transactions. The count and total include all of them.”

### Each Transaction

Each transaction becomes one issue. The title of the issue has the amount and the merchant, for example `$6.75 · Blue Bottle Coffee`. The description of the issue is a table with these rows:

| Row in the description | Value from Wallet |
| --- | --- |
| **Date** | The date of the transaction, for example 2026-10-29 |
| **Merchant** | The merchant name, or the description if Wallet has no merchant name |
| **Amount** | Less than zero for a charge, for example -84.12, and more than zero for a refund or a payment |
| **Currency** | The currency code, for example USD |
| **Category** | The WalletFeed category, for example Groceries |
| **Status** | The Wallet status, for example `pending`, or `booked` after the charge posts |
| **Pending** | Yes or No |
| **Account** | The Wallet account, for example Apple Card |
| **Description** | The description from Wallet |
| **Type** | The type of transaction, for example `pointOfSale` or `refund` |
| **MCC** | The merchant category code, for example 5411 |
| **Foreign Amount** and **Foreign Currency** | The amount and the currency of a charge in a different currency |
| **WalletFeed ID** | The transaction ID, in the last row |

WalletFeed does not write a row that has no value. In the description, an amount has no zeros at the end, for example -23.4 for $23.40.

Each issue also has an attachment with the title WalletFeed. WalletFeed uses this attachment and the **WalletFeed ID** row to find the issue again.

## Sync times and changes

While WalletFeed is open, Linear receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. For this, [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) must be on.

**Background Sync** is in **Settings** › **Sync**, and it is on until you set it to off. After your iPhone starts again, WalletFeed sends nothing to Linear until you type your iPhone passcode one time.

### Monthly

The first transaction of a month makes the issue of that month. After that, each change in the month changes the title and the description of the same issue. For example, a new transaction, a pending charge that posts and a declined charge all change the issue.

If no transactions stay in a month, for example after a declined charge, the issue of the month stays. Its description then shows “No transactions.”

### Each Transaction

A pending charge becomes an issue with `· Pending` at the end of the title. When the charge posts, WalletFeed changes the title and the description of the same issue.

A refund becomes a different issue from the charge. The title of a refund or a payment has + before the amount, for example `+$49.00 · Apple Store`.

If the bank rejects a pending charge, or Wallet removes a transaction, WalletFeed archives the issue. The archived issue stays in Linear.

### Changes that you make in Linear

When a transaction changes, WalletFeed writes the title and the description of its issue again. If you changed them in Linear, WalletFeed replaces your changes. WalletFeed does not change the status or the assignee of the issue.

## Send previous transactions

A new Linear destination also receives previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it.

With **Each Transaction**, a Linear destination receives a maximum of 30 days of previous transactions. With **Monthly**, there is no limit of 30 days. The start date moves back to the first day of its month, and each previous month becomes one issue. WalletFeed sends the newest month first.

To send transactions from a longer period, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Linear destination.
2. Tap **Send History**.
3. Select a period: **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.
4. Read the message **Send History to Linear?**

   With **Monthly**, the message shows “Each month becomes one issue.” With **Each Transaction**, it shows “Each transaction can become an issue.”

5. Tap **Send**.

WalletFeed sends the newest transactions first, and the destination screen shows the number of transactions that WalletFeed sent. **Send History** also uses the filter. With **Monthly**, the period starts on the first day of its month.

One year can have more than 250 transactions. If **Send** is **Each Transaction** and your workspace is on Linear's Free plan, set a filter before you use **Send History**.

To stop **Send History**:

1. On the destination screen, tap **Send History**.
2. Tap **Stop Sending**. The issues that WalletFeed sent stay in Linear.

## Change or delete the destination

To change the transactions that go to Linear, change the **Filter** settings on the destination screen.

The destination screen shows the **Team** and the **Project**, but you cannot change them. To use a different team or project, add Linear again with the new team and project. Then delete the previous Linear destination.

To change what becomes an issue, select **Monthly** or **Each Transaction** in **Send** on the destination screen. With **Monthly**, the issue of a month then shows all the transactions of the month. These include the transactions that have an issue from **Each Transaction**. With **Each Transaction**, each new transaction becomes an issue, and the month issues stay. With **Each Transaction** and no filter, you can tap **Turn On Filter** below **Send**.

To stop the destination temporarily, set the **Enabled** switch to off.

To replace the key, for example after you revoke it in Linear:

1. In Linear, make a new personal API key, as in [Step 1](#step-1-make-a-personal-api-key-in-linear).
2. In WalletFeed, tap the Linear destination in **Destinations**.
3. Tap **Replace Key**.
4. Paste the new key into **API Key**.
