5. Tap **Replace**. Before WalletFeed keeps the new key, it makes sure that the key can get access to the team.

To delete the destination:

1. In WalletFeed, tap the Linear destination in **Destinations**.
2. Tap **Delete**.
3. In the message, tap **Delete**. The issues that WalletFeed sent stay in Linear.
4. Optional: In Linear, revoke the key in **Settings** › **Account** › **Security & Access**.

## If there is a problem

### If WalletFeed shows “Key rejected”

Linear did not accept the key because the key is not correct, or because a person revoked it in Linear.

1. In Linear, make a new personal API key, as in [Step 1](#step-1-make-a-personal-api-key-in-linear).
2. If WalletFeed shows the message on the Linear screen, paste the new key into the **API Key** field.
3. If WalletFeed shows the message on the destination screen, replace the key, as in [Change or delete the destination](#change-or-delete-the-destination).

### If the destination shows “Authentication failed”

Linear did not accept the key, or the key cannot make or change issues in the team.

1. In Linear, make a new personal API key with full access, or with **Read** and **Write**.
2. In WalletFeed, tap the Linear destination in **Destinations**.
3. Tap **Replace Key**.
4. Paste the new key into **API Key**.
5. Tap **Replace**.

### If WalletFeed shows “Give the key Read and Write access”

Linear does not let the key get access to the team.

1. In Linear, make a new personal API key with full access, or with **Read** and **Write**.
2. If you give the key access to only some teams, include the team that you use with WalletFeed.
3. If WalletFeed shows the message on the Linear screen, paste the new key into the **API Key** field.
4. If WalletFeed shows the message on the destination screen, replace the key, as in [Change or delete the destination](#change-or-delete-the-destination).

### If WalletFeed shows “This key can't see any teams”

The key has access to no team in Linear.

1. In Linear, make a new personal API key with access to your team.
2. Paste the new key into the **API Key** field.

### If WalletFeed shows “Linear is limiting requests”

Linear has a limit for each user in each hour, and you are at that limit.

1. Wait for one minute.
2. If WalletFeed shows the message on the Linear screen, tap **Try Again**.
3. If WalletFeed shows the message on the destination screen, replace the key again, as in [Change or delete the destination](#change-or-delete-the-destination).

### If new transactions do not become issues

On Linear's Free plan, a workspace with more than 250 issues cannot get new issues.

1. To make fewer issues, set **Send** to **Monthly** on the destination screen. Then each month becomes one issue.
2. To send all your transactions to Linear, change your workspace to a different Linear plan, for example Basic. Basic has no limit on issues.
3. To send only some transactions, set a filter, as in [Step 3](#step-3-set-a-filter).

### If one transaction has two issues

With **Each Transaction**, WalletFeed finds an issue in the team that you selected by its **WalletFeed ID** row and its WalletFeed attachment. If a person removes the row and the attachment, or moves the issue to a different team, WalletFeed makes a new issue.

1. In Linear, archive or delete the issue that has no **WalletFeed ID** row, or the issue in the different team. WalletFeed continues to change the other issue.
2. Keep the **WalletFeed ID** row and the WalletFeed attachment in each issue.

### If Linear receives changes only while WalletFeed is open

**Background Sync** is off, or your iPhone started again and you did not type its passcode.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Sync** section, set the **Background Sync** switch to on.
3. Tap **Done**.
4. After your iPhone starts again, type its passcode one time.

### If Linear does not let you make an API key

An admin of your Linear workspace does not let members make API keys. Admins can always make API keys. On the Free plan, all users are admins.

1. Tell an admin of the workspace to change **Member API keys** in **Settings** › **Administration** › **API**.
2. After the admin changes **Member API keys**, make the key, as in [Step 1](#step-1-make-a-personal-api-key-in-linear).

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to Lunch Money

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to Lunch Money. You get an access token in Lunch Money, then paste it into WalletFeed.

## Before you start

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- WalletFeed, with access to your Wallet accounts.
- WalletFeed Pro. You must have it to send transactions to Lunch Money. It is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase. Refer to [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/).
- A Lunch Money budget. Lunch Money has a 30-day free trial, and you can start the trial without a credit card.

## Step 1: Select Lunch Money in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The empty Destinations screen with the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. Tap **Lunch Money**, below **Budgeting**.

   ![The Add Destination screen with Lunch Money in the Budgeting list.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

   Result: WalletFeed shows the Lunch Money screen. If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, it shows **WalletFeed Pro** first.
5. If WalletFeed shows **WalletFeed Pro**, get WalletFeed Pro. Refer to [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/).

## Step 2: Get an access token in Lunch Money

An access token lets WalletFeed send transactions to one Lunch Money budget. The token is for the budget that is open when you get it.

1. On the Lunch Money screen in WalletFeed, tap **Open Developers**.

   ![The Lunch Money screen in WalletFeed with the Access Token field and the Open Developers link.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/walletfeed-setup-lunch-money.webp)

   Result: your iPhone shows the Lunch Money **Developers** page.
2. If Lunch Money shows its login page, log in with your Lunch Money email address and password.
3. If you have more than one budget, tap the circle at the top right of the page.

   Result: Lunch Money shows **Switch Accounts**.
4. In **Switch Accounts**, select the budget for your transactions.
5. In **New Access Token**, type a label for the token, such as WalletFeed.
6. Tap **Request new access token**.

   Result: Lunch Money shows the token.
7. Tap **Copy**.

> **Note:** Lunch Money shows the token one time only. If you close the page before you paste the token, get a new token.

## Step 3: Paste the token in WalletFeed

1. Go back to WalletFeed.

   Result: WalletFeed shows the Lunch Money screen.
2. If WalletFeed shows a different screen, do [Step 1](#step-1-select-lunch-money-in-walletfeed) again.
3. Paste the token into **Access Token**.

   Result: WalletFeed connects to Lunch Money and shows **Account**.
4. In **Account**, select the Lunch Money account for your transactions.

   If you select **New Apple Card Account**, WalletFeed makes a credit account with the name Apple Card. Its balance is 0.

   If your budget has an account with the name Apple Card, WalletFeed selects that account.

   The list does not show closed accounts, or accounts that cannot have transactions.
5. Tap **Add**.

   Result: WalletFeed shows **Send Transactions to Lunch Money?** with a message. The message tells you what Lunch Money receives, from which Wallet accounts, and from which date.

   If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes the new destination and sends nothing.
6. Tap **Send**.

   Result: WalletFeed starts to send transactions to Lunch Money.

   ![The Destinations screen with Lunch Money and three other destinations.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/walletfeed-destinations.webp)

In Lunch Money, the transactions show on the **Transactions** page.

## Data that Lunch Money receives

WalletFeed adds each transaction to the Lunch Money account that you selected. This table shows where each item goes in Lunch Money.

| WalletFeed sends | Lunch Money field |
| --- | --- |
| Date of the transaction, in your time zone | Date |
| Merchant name, or the description if there is no merchant name | Payee |
| Card statement text | Original payee name |
| Amount | Amount |
| Currency | Currency |
| Transaction ID | External ID |
| Wallet status, transaction type, merchant category code and WalletFeed category | Custom metadata |

A purchase goes to Lunch Money as money out. A payment goes as money in. WalletFeed uses the external ID to find the transaction again when it changes. Apps that use the Lunch Money API can read the custom metadata.

WalletFeed does not set the Lunch Money category. Lunch Money applies your rules for the account to each new transaction. Thus, a rule can set the category. Each new transaction starts as unreviewed.

After WalletFeed adds a transaction, it does not change the payee, category, notes, tags or review status. It changes only the date, amount, currency and Wallet status, when these change in Wallet.

WalletFeed does not change the balance of the Lunch Money account. To correct the balance, change it on the Lunch Money **Accounts** page.

Lunch Money receives transactions from all the Wallet accounts that you share with WalletFeed. They all go to the one Lunch Money account. To send transactions from only some Wallet accounts, use a filter. Refer to [Send only some transactions](#send-only-some-transactions).

Your transactions go from your iPhone directly to Lunch Money. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. WalletFeed keeps the token in the Keychain on your iPhone. After Lunch Money receives your transactions, the Lunch Money terms of service are applicable to them.

## New and changed transactions

While WalletFeed is open, Lunch Money receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. Then WalletFeed sends the change. For this, [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) must be on in **Settings** › **Sync**.

Wallet shows a new charge as pending until the charge posts. Lunch Money does not mark transactions in a manual account as pending. Thus, a pending charge shows in Lunch Money as a usual transaction. WalletFeed records the Wallet status in the custom metadata.

When the charge posts, WalletFeed changes the same transaction in Lunch Money. The date stays the same. If the posted amount is different, WalletFeed changes the amount. To send charges only after they post, set **Include Pending** to off in the filter.

A refund goes to Lunch Money as money in. If Wallet shows a charge as declined or expired, WalletFeed deletes it from Lunch Money. WalletFeed also deletes a transaction that Wallet removes. But WalletFeed does not delete a transaction that you split or put in a group in Lunch Money.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. To start from a different date, set **Initial History** before you add Lunch Money.

To send more previous transactions after you add Lunch Money, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Lunch Money destination.

   ![The Lunch Money destination in WalletFeed with Replace Token, Filter, Send History, Send Test and Delete.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/walletfeed-destination-detail.webp)

2. Tap **Send History**.
3. Select **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

   Result: WalletFeed shows **Sending History**, with the number of transactions that it sent.

WalletFeed sends previous transactions to Lunch Money in groups of 50. It waits 45 seconds between groups. Lunch Money does not receive the same transaction two times. To stop, tap **Send History**, then tap **Stop Sending**.

## Change or remove the destination

### Send only some transactions

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Lunch Money destination.
2. Set **Filter** to on.
3. Set the filter. The table that follows gives the controls.

| Control | Result |
| --- | --- |
| **Include** | Sends all transactions, only purchases or only credits. |
| **Minimum** | Sends only transactions of this amount or more. |
| **Include Pending** | When off, sends charges only after they post. |
| **Accounts** | Sends only transactions from the Wallet accounts that you select. |
| **Categories** | Sends only transactions in the categories that you select. |
| **Exclude** | Does not send transactions from the merchants that you type. Put a comma between merchants. |

If Apple Intelligence is on, you can also type a rule in words, for example "Travel over $50, not Uber". Then tap the Apple Intelligence symbol to make the rule.

A filter applies only to the transactions that WalletFeed sends after you set it.

### Replace the token

1. Get a new access token for the same budget, as in [Step 2](#step-2-get-an-access-token-in-lunch-money).
2. In **Destinations**, tap the Lunch Money destination.
3. Tap **Replace Token**.
4. Paste the new token into **Access Token**.
5. Tap **Replace**.

   Result: WalletFeed shows a green check mark.

The new token must come from the same budget. A token from a different budget cannot get access to the account.

### Stop or delete the destination

To stop the destination for a period, set **Enabled** to off in the destination.

To delete the destination, do these steps:

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Lunch Money destination.
2. Tap **Delete**.
3. Tap **Delete** again.

The transactions that WalletFeed sent stay in Lunch Money. If you do not use the token again, revoke it in Lunch Money:

1. On your iPhone, open [the Lunch Money Developers page](https://my.lunchmoney.app/developers).
2. In **Active Access Tokens**, tap **Revoke** for the WalletFeed token.

## If something goes wrong

### If WalletFeed shows "Token rejected" or "Authentication failed"

Lunch Money does not accept the token. This occurs if someone revoked the token, or if the pasted text is not the full token.

1. Get a new access token, as in [Step 2](#step-2-get-an-access-token-in-lunch-money).
2. If WalletFeed shows the Lunch Money screen, paste the new token into **Access Token**.
3. If you added Lunch Money before, replace the token. Refer to [Replace the token](#replace-the-token).

### If WalletFeed shows "The account is gone from Lunch Money"

The Lunch Money account for this destination does not exist, or the token is for a different budget.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Lunch Money destination.
2. Tap **Delete**.
3. Tap **Delete** again.
4. Do [Step 1](#step-1-select-lunch-money-in-walletfeed), Step 2 and Step 3 again.

### If the transactions go to an incorrect budget

The token is for the budget that was open when you got the token.

1. Delete the Lunch Money destination. Refer to [Stop or delete the destination](#stop-or-delete-the-destination).
2. In Lunch Money, select the correct budget in **Switch Accounts**.
3. Do [Step 1](#step-1-select-lunch-money-in-walletfeed), Step 2 and Step 3 again.

The transactions in the incorrect budget stay there. You can delete them in Lunch Money.

### If Lunch Money does not receive new transactions

WalletFeed cannot send to Lunch Money. For example, the destination is off, or **Background Sync** is off.

1. Open WalletFeed. While WalletFeed is open, it sends changes in seconds.
2. If **Destinations** shows **Sync Requires Pro**, tap **Upgrade**.
3. If the Lunch Money destination shows **Off**, set **Enabled** to on in the destination.
4. If **Filter** is on, make sure that the filter includes the transaction.
5. Tap **Settings** at the top of **Destinations**.
6. Make sure that **Background Sync** is on.
7. Tap **Sync Now**.

After your iPhone restarts, WalletFeed cannot send to destinations until you type your passcode one time.

To make sure that the connection operates, tap **Send Test** in the destination. If Lunch Money receives the test transaction, WalletFeed shows a green check mark.

> **Note:** **Send Test** adds a test transaction of $4.20 from the payee WalletFeed to the Lunch Money account. You can delete it in Lunch Money.

### If the balance in Lunch Money is not correct

WalletFeed does not change the balance of the Lunch Money account.

1. In Lunch Money, open the **Accounts** page.
2. Change the balance of the account that receives your transactions.

### If WalletFeed shows "Too many requests" or "Rejected (HTTP 429)"

Lunch Money accepts a maximum of 100 requests each minute. WalletFeed waits, then tries again.

1. Wait. WalletFeed tries again at the time that it shows, or at the next sync.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-make/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to Make

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a scenario in Make (previously Integromat). You add a Custom webhook in Make, then paste its URL into WalletFeed.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.
- A Make account. To get an account, open [Make's sign-up page](https://www.make.com/en/register). The Free plan has the Webhooks app.
- A computer with a web browser for the steps in Make. The screenshots show Make on a computer.

> **Note:** Make's Free plan has 1,000 credits each month. Each time that the webhook starts the scenario, the webhook uses 1 credit. Each module after the webhook uses more credits.

## Step 1: Add a Custom webhook in Make

The webhook gives you a URL. WalletFeed sends your transactions to this URL.

1. On your computer, sign in to [Make](https://www.make.com).
2. Click **+ Create scenario**.

   ![The Make dashboard with the Create scenario button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-make/make-dashboard.webp)

3. If a **Scheduling** message opens, click **Got it**.
4. If the Maia panel opens, click **X** on the panel.

   Maia is not necessary for these steps.

5. In the scenario editor, click the large **+**.

   ![An empty Make scenario with the large plus button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-make/make-new-scenario.webp)

6. In **Search all apps or modules**, type `Webhooks`.
7. Click the **Webhooks** app with the red icon.

   Make shows the app **Make** first, with its webhook modules below it, for example **List webhooks**. The app **Make** is not correct for these steps.

   ![The Make app search with the Webhooks app highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-make/make-search-webhooks.webp)

8. In **Triggers**, click **Custom webhook**.

   **Custom mailhook** is above **Custom webhook**. **Custom mailhook** is not correct for these steps.

   ![The Webhooks app in Make with the Custom webhook trigger highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-make/make-custom-webhook.webp)

9. Below **Webhook**, click **Create a webhook**.

   ![The webhook panel in Make with the Create a webhook button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-make/make-create-a-webhook.webp)

10. In **Webhook name**, replace the name with `WalletFeed`.
11. Do not click **+ Add API key**.

    If the webhook has an API key, Make accepts only the requests that contain the key. WalletFeed cannot send an API key.

12. Click **Save**.

    ![The Create a webhook dialog with WalletFeed as the name and the Save button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-make/make-name-webhook.webp)

13. Below **Webhook URL**, click the copy button at the end of the URL.

    Make does not show the full URL. If you select the text, you copy only a part of the URL.

    ![The webhook panel in Make with the copy button for the webhook URL highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-make/make-copy-webhook-url.webp)

14. Do not give the URL to other persons.

    With the URL, a person can send data to your scenario.

15. Keep the scenario open.

    Make must show **Listening for data** when you tap **Add** in WalletFeed.

> **Note:** If you use a Mac with the same Apple Account as your iPhone, you can paste the URL on your iPhone with [Universal Clipboard](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102430).

## Step 2: Add Make in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Optional: If you use Make's Free plan and select **Each Transaction** in step 8, set **Initial History** to **Today**.

   With **Today**, Make receives only the transactions of this day. While the scenario is not active, Make keeps the transactions in a queue. On the Free plan, this queue can contain a maximum of 50 transactions. **Settings** shows the **Sync** section only with WalletFeed Pro.

   1. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
   2. In the **Sync** section, set **Initial History** to **Today**.

      ![WalletFeed Settings with the Sync section and Initial History set to All.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-make/walletfeed-settings.webp)

   3. Tap **Done**.
3. Tap **Destinations**.
4. Tap **+**.

   ![The Destinations screen in WalletFeed with the + button and no destinations.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-make/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

5. In **Automations**, tap **Make**. You can also type `Make` in the search field.
6. If WalletFeed shows the **WalletFeed Pro** screen, get WalletFeed Pro on that screen. WalletFeed then opens the **Make** screen.
7. Paste the URL into **Webhook URL**. WalletFeed keeps the URL in the Keychain on your iPhone.
8. In **Send**, select **Monthly** or **Each Transaction**.

   With **Monthly**, Make receives one request 5 days after the end of each month. The request contains all the transactions of that month. **Monthly** is the default.

   With **Each Transaction**, Make receives one request for each new or changed transaction. Each request starts the scenario and uses credits.

9. Tap **Add**. WalletFeed sends a sample to Make.

   With **Each Transaction**, the sample is one transaction, with `merchant` WalletFeed and `amount` -4.2. With **Monthly**, the sample is one month that contains the same transaction.

10. Read the message **Send Transactions to Make?**

    The message tells you what Make receives, the Wallet accounts of the transactions and the start date.

11. Tap **Send**. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed does not add the destination.

**Destinations** then shows the new destination with the name Make.

## Step 3: Save the scenario in Make

1. On your computer, make sure that Make shows **Detected data** with the fields of the sample.

   With **Monthly**, Make shows “6 values detected and ready to map”. These values include `month` and `transactions`. With **Each Transaction**, Make shows “15 values detected and ready to map”.

   ![Make shows the 15 fields that it found in WalletFeed's sample, with the Save button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-make/make-data-detected.webp)

2. Click **Save** in the webhook panel.
3. Optional: At the top of the editor, replace the scenario name with `WalletFeed`.
4. Click **Save** in the toolbar at the bottom of the editor.

   If a webhook is not in a scenario for more than 5 days, Make deactivates the webhook. Then WalletFeed cannot send transactions to it.

   ![The WalletFeed scenario in Make with the Save button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-make/make-save-scenario.webp)

## Step 4: Add modules and activate the scenario

With **Monthly**, you can add an Iterator as the first module after the webhook. The Iterator divides the transactions of the month into bundles. Each bundle contains one transaction. Each module after the Iterator then receives one bundle at a time. The Iterator uses 1 credit, and each module after it uses 1 credit for each transaction.

To add an Iterator, do these steps:

1. Click the small **+** on the right side of the webhook module.
2. In **Search all apps or modules**, type `Iterator`.
3. Below **Flow Control**, click **Iterator**.
4. In the **Array** field, select `transactions[]`.
5. Click **Save** in the Iterator panel.

To complete the scenario, do these steps:

1. Add the other modules of the scenario.

   With **Each Transaction**, or after an Iterator, these modules can use each field of a transaction, for example `amount` or `merchant`. Without an Iterator, the modules can use the fields of the month, for example `month` or `total`.

2. Click **Save** in the toolbar at the bottom of the editor.
3. Optional: To start the scenario one time, click **Run once**.

   If the queue of the webhook is empty, Make shows **Waiting for data...** until it receives a request.

   ![The Make editor with Waiting for data... and a red Stop button after Run once.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-make/make-waiting-for-data.webp)

4. If Make shows **Unprocessed data in webhook queue**, click **Use existing data**.

   Make starts the scenario one time with the first request in the queue.

5. Optional: Look at the fields in **Output**.

   ![The Make output for one WalletFeed month, with the fields of the month and 6 sample transactions.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-make/make-walletfeed-result.webp)

6. To activate the scenario, click the **Inactive** switch at the top of the editor.

   With **Immediately as data arrives**, the scenario starts each time that Make receives a request.

7. If Make shows **Unprocessed data in webhook queue**, click **Process old data**.

   Make then starts the scenario one time for each request in the queue. If you click **Delete old data**, Make removes these requests, and the scenario does not get their transactions.

## Data that Make receives

Your transactions go from your iPhone directly to Make. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. After Make receives your transactions, Make's terms are applicable to them.

With **Monthly**, WalletFeed sends one HTTP request for each month. The request has these fields:

| Field in Make | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `event` | `month` |
| `month` | The month in your time zone, for example `2026-10` |
| `count` | The number of transactions in `transactions` |
| `total` | All the `amount` values of the month, added together, for example -16.95 |
| `currency` | The currency code of `total`, for example USD |
| `transactions` | The transactions of the month, newest first. Each transaction has the fields in the next table, but not `event`. |

If the month has more than one currency, `total` and `currency` have no value.

With **Each Transaction**, WalletFeed sends one HTTP request for each change. The request has these 15 fields, and Make shows a field without a value as empty:

| Field in Make | Value from Wallet |
| --- | --- |
| `event` | `created` the first time that WalletFeed finds the transaction in Wallet, and `updated` after a change |
| `id` | The transaction ID from Wallet, which stays the same when the transaction changes |
| `date` | The day of the purchase in your time zone, for example 2026-10-30 |
| `merchant` | The merchant name, or the description if Wallet has no merchant name |
| `amount` | A negative number for a purchase, for example -6.75, and a positive number for a refund or a payment |
| `currency` | The currency code, for example USD |
| `category` | The WalletFeed category, for example Dining |
| `status` | The Wallet status, for example `pending`, or `booked` after the charge posts |
| `pending` | `true` when `status` is `pending` or `authorized`, and `false` after the charge posts |
| `account` | The Wallet account, for example Apple Card |
| `description` | The description from Wallet |
| `type` | The type of transaction, for example `pointOfSale` or `refund` |
| `mcc` | The merchant category code, for example 5814 |
| `foreignAmount` | For a purchase in a different currency, the value in the currency of the merchant |
| `foreignCurrency` | The currency code of `foreignAmount` |

`foreignAmount` is also a negative number for a purchase and a positive number for a refund. With **Each Transaction**, if the bank rejects a pending charge or Wallet removes a transaction, Make receives a request with only two fields. These fields are `id`, and `event` with the value `deleted`.

## Sync times and changes

To send transactions to Make while WalletFeed is closed, [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) must be on in **Settings** › **Sync**. **Background Sync** is on until you set it to off. After your iPhone starts again, WalletFeed does not send transactions until you type your iPhone passcode one time.

### Monthly

WalletFeed sends each month at the first sync on or after the 6th day of the next month. For example, Make receives October on or after November 6. If the filter keeps no transactions of a month, Make receives nothing for that month.

If a charge is pending when WalletFeed sends the month, its `pending` value is `true`. WalletFeed does not send the charge again after it posts. After WalletFeed sends a month, it does not send changes to that month.

If a sync stops after WalletFeed sends a month, Make can receive the same month two times. A scenario can use a Make data store to find a `month` value that it received before.

### Each Transaction

While WalletFeed is open, Make receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet.

Make receives a pending charge again when it posts. Then `event` is `updated` and `status` is `booked`, with the same `id`. For a refund, `amount` is a positive number and `type` is `refund`.

Each request starts the scenario one time. Thus, an update also uses credits. If WalletFeed stops during a sync, WalletFeed can send the same changes again, with the same `event` value. A scenario that adds rows must first try to find a row with the same `id`. If the scenario finds that row, it must change the row.

## Send previous transactions

A new Make destination also receives previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it.

With **Each Transaction**, Make receives a maximum of 30 days of previous transactions. With **Monthly**, there is no limit of 30 days. The start date moves back to the first day of its month, and Make receives one request for each previous month. WalletFeed sends the newest month first.

To send more transactions, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. On your computer, make sure that the scenario is active in Make.
2. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
3. In **Destinations**, tap the Make destination.
4. Tap **Send History**.
5. Tap a period: **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.
6. In the message **Send History to Make?**, tap **Send**.

   With **Monthly**, the message shows “Each month runs your scenario once.” With **Each Transaction**, it shows “Each transaction runs your scenario.”

WalletFeed sends the newest transactions first. While it sends, the destination screen shows **Sending History** and a count, for example 20 of 50. With **Monthly**, the period starts on the first day of its month, and **Send History** also sends the months that Make received before. WalletFeed uses the filter for **Send History**. Each request uses credits in Make, and the Free plan has 1,000 credits each month.

To stop **Send History**, do these steps:

1. Tap **Send History**.
2. Tap **Stop Sending**.

The transactions that Make received stay in Make.

## Change or remove the destination

To change the transactions that go to Make, change the [filter](/docs/choose-what-to-send/) of the Make destination. With **Each Transaction** and no filter, you can tap **Turn On Filter** below **Send**. To stop the destination for a period, set the **Enabled** switch to off.

To change **Send**, do these steps:

1. In WalletFeed, open the Make destination.
2. In **Send**, select **Monthly** or **Each Transaction**.

   With **Monthly**, Make receives the month of the change 5 days after the end of that month. The request contains all the transactions of the month. These include the transactions that Make received before. With **Each Transaction**, Make receives the changes from that time. To send previous transactions, use **Send History**.

3. On your computer, open the scenario in Make.
4. If Make shows **Edit**, click **Edit**.
5. Click the webhook module.
6. Click **Detect new values**.
7. On your iPhone, tap **Send Test** on the Make destination screen.

   The sample has the fields of your new selection in **Send**.

8. On your computer, click **Save** in the webhook panel.
9. Make sure that the modules of the scenario use the new fields.

   With **Each Transaction**, the requests have no `transactions` field, and an Iterator is not necessary.

10. If you selected **Each Transaction** and the scenario has an Iterator, right-click the Iterator.
11. Click **Delete**.
12. Click **Save** in the toolbar at the bottom of the editor.

In **Webhook**, the destination screen shows only the first part of the URL, for example `hook.us2.make.com`.

To find the URL of the webhook again, do these steps:

1. On your computer, in the Make sidebar, click **Webhooks**.
2. Click **WalletFeed**.

   ![The Make Webhooks page with the WalletFeed webhook highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-make/make-webhooks-list.webp)

3. Below **Webhook URL**, click the copy button.

   ![The Detail page of the WalletFeed webhook in Make, with the copy button for the webhook URL highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-make/make-webhook-detail.webp)

To replace the URL, for example after you add a new webhook, do these steps:

1. In WalletFeed, open the Make destination.
2. Tap **Replace URL**.
3. Paste the URL into **Webhook URL**.
4. Tap **Replace**.

   Before WalletFeed keeps the new URL, it sends a sample. If Make does not accept the sample, WalletFeed keeps the previous URL.

To remove the destination, do these steps:

1. In WalletFeed, open the Make destination.
2. Tap **Delete**.
3. In the message **Delete Make?**, tap **Delete**.

The transactions that WalletFeed sent stay in Make.

To also remove the webhook, do these steps on your computer:

1. In the Make sidebar, click **Webhooks**.
2. Click **⋮** for the WalletFeed webhook.
3. Click **Delete**.
4. In **Please confirm**, click **Delete**.
5. In **Confirmation required**, click **OK**.

Make also removes the transactions that are in the queue of the webhook, and the scenario stops.

## If there is a problem

### If you cannot tap Add

The text in **Webhook URL** is not a Make webhook URL. A Make webhook URL starts with `https://hook.`, for example `https://hook.us2.make.com/`.

1. In Make, copy the URL again with the copy button.
2. Paste the full URL into **Webhook URL**.

### If WalletFeed shows “The webhook refused the test”

Make did not accept the sample, for example because the webhook has an API key, or because Make removed or deactivated the webhook.

1. In Make, add a new Custom webhook without an API key, as in Step 1.
2. Copy the URL of the new webhook with the copy button.
3. In WalletFeed, paste the URL into **Webhook URL**.
4. Tap **Add**.

### If WalletFeed shows “Too many requests. Try again in a few minutes.”

Make accepts a maximum of 300 requests in 10 seconds.

1. Wait some minutes.
2. Tap **Add** again.

### If Make does not show the fields

Make did not show **Listening for data** when WalletFeed sent the sample.

1. On your computer, in the webhook panel, click **Detect new values**.
2. On your iPhone, open the Make destination in WalletFeed.
3. Tap **Send Test**.
4. On your computer, make sure that Make shows the fields of the sample.
5. Click **Save** in the webhook panel.

### If WalletFeed shows “Rejected (HTTP 400)”

Make rejects requests when the queue of the webhook is full. While the scenario is not active, Make keeps the requests in the queue. On the Free plan, the queue can contain a maximum of 50 requests. The **Webhooks** page in Make shows the number of requests in the queue, for example 50/50.

1. On your computer, open the scenario in Make.
2. To activate the scenario, click the **Inactive** switch.
3. If Make shows **Unprocessed data in webhook queue**, click **Process old data**.

   With **Run once**, Make starts the scenario for only one request in the queue.

4. On your iPhone, open **Settings** › **Sync** in WalletFeed.
5. Tap **Sync Now**.
6. If the Make destination shows **Try Again**, tap **Try Again**.

### If WalletFeed shows “Rejected (HTTP 410)”

Make removed or deactivated the webhook. If a webhook is not in a scenario for more than 5 days, Make deactivates it.

1. In Make, add a new Custom webhook, as in Step 1.
2. Save the scenario, as in Step 3.
3. In WalletFeed, open the Make destination.
4. Tap **Replace URL**.
5. Paste the new URL into **Webhook URL**.
6. Tap **Replace**.

### If the scenario starts only one time each month

**Send** is **Monthly**, which is the default. With **Monthly**, Make receives each month 5 days after the end of the month.

To receive each transaction after a change, do these steps:

1. In WalletFeed, open the Make destination.
2. In **Send**, select **Each Transaction**.
3. On your computer, open the scenario in Make.
4. If Make shows **Edit**, click **Edit**.
5. Click the webhook module.
6. Click **Detect new values**.
7. On your iPhone, tap **Send Test** on the Make destination screen.
8. On your computer, click **Save** in the webhook panel.
9. If the scenario has an Iterator, right-click the Iterator.
10. Click **Delete**.
11. Click **Save** in the toolbar at the bottom of the editor.

### If the scenario does not start for new transactions

The scenario is not active. Make keeps the transactions in the queue of the webhook.

1. On your computer, open the scenario in Make.
2. To activate the scenario, click the **Inactive** switch.
3. If Make shows **Unprocessed data in webhook queue**, click **Process old data**.

### If Make receives transactions only while WalletFeed is open

**Background Sync** is off, or your iPhone started again and you did not type its passcode.

1. In WalletFeed, open **Settings** › **Sync**.
2. Set the **Background Sync** switch to on.
3. After your iPhone starts again, type its passcode one time.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to Notion

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a database in Notion. You make a connection in Notion and share a page with it. WalletFeed then makes a database on that page and adds one row for each transaction. You can use this database for a budget in Notion.

## Before you start

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings in Wallet on that iPhone.
- WalletFeed, with [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/). WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.
- A Notion account. You must be a Workspace Owner in the workspace that receives your transactions, because only a Workspace Owner can make a connection.
- A computer with a web browser, for step 1 and step 2.

## Step 1: Make a connection in Notion

1. On your computer, open [Notion's Developer portal](https://app.notion.com/developers/connections).
2. Sign in to Notion.
3. In the **Build** section of the sidebar, click **Internal connections**.
4. Click **Create a new connection**.
5. Type a name for the connection, for example WalletFeed.
6. Select the workspace for your transactions.
7. Save the connection.
8. Open the **Configuration** tab of the connection.
9. In the content capabilities, select **Read content**, **Update content** and **Insert content**.
10. For user capabilities, select **No user information**. WalletFeed does not use user information or comments.

The **Configuration** tab also shows the **API token**. You copy the token on your iPhone in step 3.

## Step 2: Share a page with the connection

A new connection cannot open pages in Notion. WalletFeed makes its database on a page that you share with the connection.

> **Note:** When you share a page, the connection also gets access to all the child pages of that page. If you share a new page for WalletFeed, the connection cannot open your other pages.

1. In Notion, make a new page for your transactions, for example Budget.
2. In the Developer portal, open your connection.
3. Click the **Content access** tab.
4. Click **Edit access**.
5. Select the page that you made.
6. Save the change.

You can also share the page from Notion:

1. Open the page in Notion.
2. Click **•••** at the top right of the page.
3. Find **Connections** in the menu. If you cannot find it, click **More**.
4. Click **+ Add connection** or **Add connections**.
5. Type the name of your connection.
6. Select your connection.
7. If Notion shows a message about access to the child pages, accept the access.

## Step 3: Paste the token in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with no destinations, and the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In **Sheets & Databases**, tap **Notion**.

   ![The Add Destination list, with Notion in the Sheets & Databases section.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed first shows the **WalletFeed Pro** screen. After you get WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed shows the Notion screen.

5. Tap **Developer Portal**. Notion's Developer portal opens in your web browser.

   ![The Notion screen in WalletFeed, with the Token field, four steps and the Developer Portal link.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/walletfeed-setup-notion.webp)

6. If Notion shows its sign-in page, sign in.
7. Tap **Internal connections**.
8. Tap your connection.
9. On the **Configuration** tab, copy the **API token**.
10. Open WalletFeed again.
11. Paste the token in **Token**. WalletFeed shows **Database** and **Page** below **Token**.

WalletFeed keeps the token in the Keychain on your iPhone.

## Step 4: Select the page and add Notion

1. Make sure that **Database** shows **New**.
2. In **Page**, select the page that you shared in step 2. WalletFeed shows "Adds a WalletFeed Transactions database to the page."
3. Tap **Add**. WalletFeed makes the **WalletFeed Transactions** database on the page.
4. On the message **Send Transactions to Notion?**, tap **Send**.

   The message tells you which data Notion receives, from which Wallet accounts and from which date. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes the destination and sends nothing. The empty database stays on the page.

WalletFeed starts to send your transactions to the **WalletFeed Transactions** database.

> **Note:** **Database** also shows the databases that the connection can open and that have a text property with the name **WalletFeed ID**. If you select one of these databases, WalletFeed writes to it. WalletFeed fills each property that has the same name as a property in the next section.

## Properties in the database

WalletFeed makes the **WalletFeed Transactions** database with these properties. Each row is one transaction.

| Property | Type | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Merchant** | Title | The merchant name. If Wallet has no merchant name, the description. |
| **Date** | Date | The day of the transaction, in the time zone of your iPhone. |
| **Amount** | Number, in dollars | Less than zero for money out, for example a purchase. More than zero for money in, for example a payment or a refund. |
| **Currency** | Select | The currency code, for example USD. |
| **Category** | Select | The WalletFeed category, for example Groceries or Dining. |
| **Status** | Select | The status of the transaction in Wallet, for example pending or booked. |
| **Pending** | Checkbox | Selected while the charge is pending. |
| **Account** | Select | The name of the Wallet account, for example Apple Card. |
| **Description** | Text | The description of the transaction in Wallet. |
| **Type** | Select | The type of transaction in Wallet. |
| **MCC** | Number | The merchant category code. This number identifies the type of business. |
| **Foreign Amount** | Number | The amount in the currency of the merchant. It is less than zero for money out. It is empty for a purchase in dollars. |
| **Foreign Currency** | Select | The code of that currency. It is empty for a purchase in dollars. |
| **WalletFeed ID** | Text | The ID that WalletFeed uses to find the row again. |

WalletFeed writes only to these properties. You can add other properties to the database, and WalletFeed does not change them. WalletFeed finds each property by its name, and each row by its **WalletFeed ID**. Thus, these names and values must stay the same.

Your transactions go from your iPhone directly to Notion. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. After Notion receives your transactions, the terms of Notion are applicable to them.

## Sync times and changes

While WalletFeed is open, Notion receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. For this, [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) must be on in **Settings** › **Sync**.

A pending charge goes to Notion with **Pending** selected. When the charge posts, WalletFeed changes **Status** and **Pending** in the same row. A refund is a new row, with an **Amount** that is more than zero.

If a pending charge does not post, WalletFeed moves its row to the trash in Notion. WalletFeed also moves a row to the trash when Wallet removes the transaction. You can restore a row from the trash.

Notion has a limit on requests. Thus, WalletFeed sends not more than three requests each second, and a long history can be slow.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. To change it, do these steps before you add Notion:

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In **Sync**, tap **Initial History**.
3. Select **Today**, **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

   ![Settings, with Initial History set to All in the Sync section.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/walletfeed-settings.webp)

To send more previous transactions to a Notion destination that you have, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. In **Destinations**, tap your Notion destination. Its name starts with Notion.
2. Tap **Send History**.
3. Select **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

   ![A destination screen, here for Lunch Money, with Send History below Filter.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/walletfeed-destination-detail.webp)

Rows that are already in the database do not show two times. WalletFeed finds them by **WalletFeed ID** and changes them. While WalletFeed sends the history, the destination shows **Sending History** and a progress bar. You can stop it with **Send History** › **Stop Sending**. When WalletFeed has sent all of the history, **History** shows **All sent**, or **Sent from** and the start date.

## Change or remove the destination

To change the destination, tap it in **Destinations**. On the destination screen, you can do these tasks:

| Task | On the destination screen |
| --- | --- |
| Stop for a time | Set **Enabled** to off. To start again, set **Enabled** to on. |
| Send only some transactions | Set **Filter** to on. Then set **Include**, **Minimum**, **Include Pending**, **Accounts**, **Categories** or **Exclude**. |
| Use a new token | Tap **Replace Token**. Paste the token. Tap **Replace**. WalletFeed makes sure that the token can read the database. |
| Make sure that WalletFeed can write | Tap **Send Test**. WalletFeed adds a sample row, with the merchant WalletFeed and the account Sample Card. |
| Remove the destination | Tap **Delete**. Tap **Delete** again. The rows that WalletFeed sent stay in Notion. |

If your iPhone can use Apple Intelligence and Apple Intelligence is on, you can also type a filter rule in words:

1. Set **Filter** to on.
2. In the field below **Filter**, type a rule, for example "Travel over $50, not Uber".
3. Tap **Create Rule**, the button with the Apple Intelligence symbol.

The connection in Notion stays after you remove the destination. To stop its access to your pages, disconnect the connection from the page in Notion.

## If something goes wrong

### If WalletFeed shows "Token rejected. Copy it again from the Developer portal."

Notion did not accept the token. For example, you did not copy all of the token.

1. On your iPhone, open [Notion's Developer portal](https://app.notion.com/developers/connections).
2. Open your connection.
3. On the **Configuration** tab, copy all of the **API token** again.
4. In WalletFeed, paste the token in **Token**.

### If WalletFeed tells you to share a page

The connection has no access to the page or the database. WalletFeed shows "Share a page with your connection, then try again." or "Share the page or database with your connection, then try again."

1. Share a page with the connection, as in [step 2](#step-2-share-a-page-with-the-connection).
2. In WalletFeed, tap **Try Again**.

### If WalletFeed shows "Give the connection read, update and insert content capabilities."

The connection does not have the three content capabilities that WalletFeed uses.

1. In the Developer portal, open your connection.
2. Open the **Configuration** tab.
3. Select **Read content**, **Update content** and **Insert content**.
4. In WalletFeed, tap **Try Again**.

### If WalletFeed shows "Notion is limiting requests. Try again in a minute."

Notion received too many requests from the connection in a short time.

1. Wait for one minute.
2. Tap **Try Again**.

### If the destination shows "Authentication failed"

Notion rejected the token. For example, a person removed the connection, or deselected one of its content capabilities.

1. On your iPhone, open [Notion's Developer portal](https://app.notion.com/developers/connections).
2. Open your connection.

   If you cannot find the connection, make a new one as in step 1. Then share the page with it as in step 2.

3. On the **Configuration** tab, make sure that the connection has **Read content**, **Update content** and **Insert content**.
4. Copy the **API token**.
5. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.

   ![The Destinations list, where a destination with a problem shows Authentication failed.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/walletfeed-destinations-failure.webp)

6. Tap your Notion destination.
7. Tap **Replace Token**.
8. Paste the token in **Token**.
9. Tap **Replace**.

On the Free plan of Notion, a workspace can get to its block limit. Then Notion can reject new rows, and WalletFeed shows "Authentication failed".

### If the destination shows "Rejected (HTTP 404)"

The connection cannot find the database. For example, a person disconnected the connection from the page.

1. Share the page with the connection again, as in [step 2](#step-2-share-a-page-with-the-connection).
2. In WalletFeed, open your Notion destination.
3. Tap **Send Test**.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-numbers/ -->
# Open Apple Card transactions in Numbers

WalletFeed saves your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a CSV file that you open in Numbers as a spreadsheet. With WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed updates the file when your transactions change.

## Before you start

To do the steps on this page, you must have:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version
- WalletFeed, with access to your Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account
- Numbers on your iPhone, or on a Mac that has access to your iCloud Drive
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), for a file that WalletFeed updates.

WalletFeed is available only in the US. WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase. Without WalletFeed Pro, you can [export one CSV file](#export-one-csv-file-without-walletfeed-pro), but WalletFeed does not update that file.

## Step 1: Add a CSV file in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with no destinations and the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-numbers/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In the search field, type `Numbers`.

   ![The Add Destination screen with the Destinations search field above the Budgeting list.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-numbers/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

5. Tap **CSV File**.

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, the **WalletFeed Pro** screen opens. After you get WalletFeed Pro, the **Files** screen opens.

6. Make sure that **Format** is **CSV**.
7. Make sure that **Save As** is **One File**.

   ![The Files screen with Format set to CSV, Save As set to One File and the name WalletFeed Transactions.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-numbers/walletfeed-setup-csv-file.webp)

   With **One File**, WalletFeed writes all your transactions to one file. The rows are in date sequence, and the row with the last date is at the top. You can also select **One File per Month**. Then each file has its month in the name, for example `WalletFeed 2026-10.csv`.

8. Tap **Folder**.
9. Select a folder in iCloud Drive.

   **Folder** then shows the name of the folder.

10. To use a different file name, type it in **Name**.

    WalletFeed adds `.csv` to the name, for example `WalletFeed Transactions.csv`.

11. Tap **Add** at the top of the screen.

    You can tap **Add** only after you select a folder.

12. When WalletFeed shows **Save Transactions to Files?**, tap **Save**.

    The message tells you the data that the folder receives. It also gives the accounts and the period of the transactions. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes the new destination.

WalletFeed then writes your transactions to the file.

## Step 2: Open the file in Numbers

1. On your iPhone, open Numbers.
2. Tap **Browse** at the bottom of the screen.
3. Open the folder that you selected in Step 1.
4. Tap `WalletFeed Transactions.csv`, or the file with the name that you typed.

Numbers shows each transaction as a row in the spreadsheet. If WalletFeed changes the file after you open it, Numbers shows the changes only after you open the file again.

## Export one CSV file without WalletFeed Pro

[Export CSV](/docs/export-csv/) makes one CSV file with the transactions from a period that you select. You can use Export CSV without WalletFeed Pro. The file does not change after you export it.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. Tap **Export CSV**.

   ![Settings with Export CSV in the Data section.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-numbers/walletfeed-settings-3.webp)

4. Tap **Range**.
5. Select a period: **This Month**, **Last Month**, **Last 90 Days**, **This Year** or **All**.

   ![The Export CSV screen with Range set to This Month, 29 transactions and the Export button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-numbers/walletfeed-export-csv.webp)

   **Transactions** shows the number of transactions in the period.

6. Tap **Export**.
7. In the share sheet, tap **Save to Files**.
8. Select a folder in iCloud Drive.
9. Save the file in that folder.

   The name of the file has the period in it, for example `Apple Card Last Month.csv`.

10. To open the file in Numbers, do the steps in [Step 2](#step-2-open-the-file-in-numbers).

## Columns in the file

Each CSV file from WalletFeed has one row for each transaction, and these columns:

| Column | Data |
| --- | --- |
| **Date** | The date of the transaction, for example 2026-10-28. |
| **Posted Date** | The date that the charge posted. It is empty while the charge is pending. |
| **Merchant** | The merchant name. If Wallet has no merchant name, this column has the text from **Description**. |
| **Description** | The text of the transaction in Wallet. |
| **Original Description** | The card statement text from the card network. |
| **Amount** | The value of the transaction, for example -23.40. It has a minus sign for purchases and fees, and no minus sign for payments and refunds. |
| **Currency** | The currency code, for example USD. |
| **Direction** | `debit` for purchases and fees, or `credit` for refunds, payments and deposits. |
| **Status** | The condition of the transaction in Wallet: `authorized`, `pending`, `booked` (posted) or `memo`. A file from **Export CSV** can also have `rejected`, for a declined charge. |
| **Type** | The transaction type in Wallet, for example `pointOfSale` (a purchase), `refund`, `billPayment` (a payment) or `transfer`. |
| **Category** | The WalletFeed category, for example Groceries, Dining or Cash & Transfers. |
| **MCC** | The merchant category code from the card network. |
| **Account** | The Wallet account, for example Apple Card. |
| **Foreign Amount** | For a purchase in a different currency, the value in that currency. |
| **Foreign Currency** | The code of that different currency. |
| **WalletFeed ID** | The ID of the transaction. WalletFeed uses it to find and update each row. |

> **Note:** WalletFeed writes only these columns. When it updates `WalletFeed Transactions.csv`, it removes all other columns.

## Changes to the file

While WalletFeed is open, `WalletFeed Transactions.csv` receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. WalletFeed then updates the file. For this, [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) must be on in **Settings** › **Sync**. If WalletFeed cannot open the folder at that time, the file changes the next time that you open WalletFeed, or while your iPhone charges.

A pending charge is in the file with `pending` or `authorized` in **Status**. When the charge posts, WalletFeed updates the same row. WalletFeed removes declined charges and the transactions that Wallet deletes. A refund is a different transaction. Its **Amount** has no minus sign.

## Send previous transactions

A new CSV file also receives your previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. To add transactions from before that date, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap **WalletFeed Transactions**, or the name that you typed.
3. Tap **Send History**.
4. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

Because WalletFeed finds each row by its **WalletFeed ID**, a transaction does not get a second row.

## Change or remove the destination

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap **WalletFeed Transactions**, or the name that you typed.
3. Do one of these steps:
   - To send only some transactions, turn on **Filter**. Then set **Include**, **Minimum**, **Accounts**, **Categories** or **Exclude**.
   - To put the file in a different folder, tap **Change Folder**. Then select the folder.
   - To stop the changes to the file, turn off **Enabled**.
   - To remove the destination, tap **Delete**. Then tap **Delete** again.

After you select a different folder, WalletFeed writes the file again in the new folder the next time that it updates the destination. If you delete the destination, the file and its transactions stay in the folder.

## If there is a problem

### If WalletFeed shows “Couldn't open this folder.”

WalletFeed cannot get access to the folder that you selected on the **Files** screen.

1. Tap **Folder**.
2. Select a different folder in iCloud Drive.

### If WalletFeed shows “Can't open the folder. Choose it again.”

WalletFeed does not have access to the folder of the destination.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Change Folder**.
4. Select the folder again.

### If WalletFeed shows “The file has no WalletFeed ID column.”

Because the file in the folder does not have the **WalletFeed ID** column, WalletFeed cannot find its rows.

1. On your iPhone, open the Files app.
2. Open the folder of the destination.
3. Touch and hold `WalletFeed Transactions.csv`.
4. Tap **Rename**.
5. Type a different name, for example `WalletFeed Transactions 1`.
6. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
7. Tap the destination.
8. Tap **Send History**.
9. Tap **All**.

WalletFeed makes a new `WalletFeed Transactions.csv` with all your transactions.

### If the folder has no CSV file

WalletFeed writes the file only when there are transactions to put in the file.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Send Test**.

   WalletFeed then writes `WalletFeed Test.csv` to the folder. This file has a sample transaction. If this file is in the folder, WalletFeed can write to the folder.

4. To write all your transactions to the file, tap **Send History**.
5. Tap **All**.

### If new transactions are not in Numbers

WalletFeed did not update the file, or Numbers does not show the changes that WalletFeed made after you opened the file.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. Tap **Sync Now**.
4. In Numbers, open `WalletFeed Transactions.csv` again.

### If text in a cell starts with an apostrophe

WalletFeed puts an apostrophe (`'`) before text that starts with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@`. Because of the apostrophe, a spreadsheet does not use the text as a formula.

### If you cannot tap Export

**Export** is not available while WalletFeed reads the transactions, or when the period has no transactions.

1. Look at **Transactions**.
2. If it shows 0, select a different **Range**.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-ofx/ -->
# Save Apple Card transactions as OFX files

WalletFeed saves your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone in one OFX file for each month. WalletFeed updates the files automatically in a folder that you select, and you import them into your app, for example Quicken for Mac or Actual.

## Before you start

You must have:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version
- WalletFeed, with [access to your Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account](/docs/wallet-accounts/)
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), which is necessary for destinations (a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase)
- An app that can import OFX files, for example Quicken for Mac, Actual, GnuCash, Moneydance, Banktivity, Goodbudget or YNAB
- If your app is on a computer, a folder that your iPhone and that computer can both open, for example in iCloud Drive

WalletFeed is available only in the US.

> **Note:** Quicken for Windows cannot import the OFX files from WalletFeed. WalletFeed does not write QFX files. Quicken for Windows can import a CSV file from WalletFeed. The [Quicken guide](/guides/apple-card-to-quicken/) has more information.

## Step 1: Add an OFX file in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with no destinations and the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-ofx/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In the **Destinations** search field, type `OFX`.

   ![The Add Destination screen with the Destinations search field above the Budgeting list.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-ofx/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

5. Tap **OFX File**.

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, the **WalletFeed Pro** screen opens. After you get WalletFeed Pro, the **Files** screen opens.

6. Make sure that **Format** is **OFX**.

   ![The Files screen with OFX in Format, no folder in Folder and WalletFeed in Name.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-ofx/walletfeed-setup-ofx-file.webp)

7. Tap **Folder**.
8. Select a folder in iCloud Drive.

   **Folder** then shows the name of the folder.

9. To use a different name for the files, type the name in **Name**.

   Each file name contains this name, the month and `.ofx`. For example, the file for October 2026 is `WalletFeed 2026-10.ofx`.

10. Tap **Add**.
11. When WalletFeed shows **Save Transactions to Files?**, tap **Save**.

    The message tells you the data that the folder receives from each posted transaction. This data includes the date, the merchant and the amount. The message also tells you the accounts and the period. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes the new destination.

WalletFeed then writes one file for each month that has posted transactions.

## Step 2: Import a file into your app

1. On your computer, open the folder that you selected in Step 1.
2. Find the file for the month, for example `WalletFeed 2026-10.ofx`.
3. In your app, import the file into the account for your Apple Card.

   In Quicken for Mac, **Bank or Brokerage File (OFX, QFX)** is in **File** › **Import**. In Actual, **Import** is on the page of the account. Actual does not show **Import** on a phone.

4. Make sure that the transactions are in the correct account.

   ![The Apple Card account in Actual with five transactions from an OFX file.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-ofx/actual-budget-walletfeed-result.webp)

> **Note:** If a file has Apple Card transactions, Actual imports only the Apple Card transactions from it. Actual does not import the Apple Cash or Savings transactions in that file. With one destination for each account, Actual can import the transactions of each account. The steps are in [If Apple Cash or Savings transactions are not in the correct account](#if-apple-cash-or-savings-transactions-are-not-in-the-correct-account).

The file uses the same account ID each time. Thus, your app can put the transactions from each file into the same account.

You can import the file for a month again after WalletFeed updates it. Actual, GnuCash and Moneydance use the transaction ID to find the transactions that you imported previously. They do not import these transactions again.

## Data in the file

Each file has one statement for each Wallet account that has posted transactions in that month. A statement shows Apple Card as a credit card, Apple Cash as a checking account and Savings as a savings account. Each statement also has the currency code, for example USD, and an ID for the Wallet account. This ID is the same in each file.

Each transaction in a statement has this data:

| Data in the file | From Wallet |
| --- | --- |
| Type | The type of the transaction, for example a purchase, a fee, a payment or a transfer. |
| Posted date | The date when the transaction posted. |
| Transaction date | The date of the transaction in Wallet. |
| Amount | The value of the transaction, for example -23.40. Purchases have a minus sign. Payments and refunds have no minus sign. |
| Transaction ID | The ID of the transaction in Wallet. Apps use it to find the transactions that they imported previously. |
| Name | The merchant name, or the description if Wallet has no merchant name. The file keeps the first 32 characters. |
| Memo | The description and the card statement text, if they are different from the name. The memo also has any value in a different currency. |

Each date is the calendar day on your iPhone. The files do not include the account balance.

## Changes to the files

While WalletFeed is open, the files receive changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. WalletFeed then updates the files. For this, [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) must be on in **Settings** › **Sync**. If WalletFeed cannot open the folder at that time, the files change when you open WalletFeed, when an automation starts, or while your iPhone charges.

The files contain only posted transactions. After a pending charge posts, WalletFeed writes it to the file with the same transaction ID. WalletFeed does not write declined charges to the files. A refund has no minus sign.

When a transaction in a month changes, WalletFeed writes the full file for that month again. For a month without posted transactions, WalletFeed writes no file. If Wallet deletes a transaction, WalletFeed removes it from the file. But a transaction that you imported previously stays in your app.

## Send previous transactions

A new OFX destination also receives your previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. With [Send History](/docs/send-history/), WalletFeed writes the files again for a period that you select:

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap **WalletFeed**, or the name that you typed in **Name**.
3. Tap **Send History**.
4. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

WalletFeed then writes the file for each month in that period. If your app uses the transaction ID, it does not import a transaction two times.

## Change or remove the destination

You make all the changes in this section on the screen of the destination. The destination has the name **WalletFeed**, or the name that you typed in **Name**. A change to **Name** on that screen does not change the names of the files.

### Send only some transactions

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Set the **Filter** switch to on.
3. Set **Include**, **Minimum**, **Accounts**, **Categories** or **Exclude**.

### Put the files in a different folder

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap **Change Folder**.
3. Select the folder.

   At the next sync, WalletFeed writes all the files in the new folder.

### Stop the updates to the files

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Set the **Enabled** switch to off.

### Remove the destination

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap **Delete**.
3. Tap **Delete** again.

   The files stay in the folder.

## If there is a problem

### If WalletFeed shows “Couldn't open this folder.”

WalletFeed cannot open the folder that you selected.

1. Tap **Folder**, or **Change Folder** on the screen of the destination.
2. Select a different folder in iCloud Drive.

### If WalletFeed shows “Can't open the folder. Choose it again.”

WalletFeed cannot open the folder that the destination uses.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Change Folder**.
4. Select the folder again.

### If the folder has no OFX file

WalletFeed writes a file only for a month that has posted transactions.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Send Test**.

   The folder then gets `WalletFeed Test.ofx` with a sample transaction. If this file is in the folder, WalletFeed can write there.

4. Do not import `WalletFeed Test.ofx` into your app.
5. To write all your transactions to the files, tap **Send History**.
6. Tap **All**.

### If a pending charge is not in the file

The files contain only posted transactions.

1. Wait until the charge posts in Wallet.
2. Import the file for that month again.

### If Quicken for Windows does not import the file

Quicken for Windows cannot import the OFX files from WalletFeed.

1. In WalletFeed, add a **CSV File** destination.
2. Import the CSV file into Quicken for Windows.

The [Quicken guide](/guides/apple-card-to-quicken/) has more information.

### If a transaction has a different date in your app

Each transaction in the file has a posted date and a transaction date. Some apps show the posted date. For example, Actual shows the posted date, which can be one or more days after the date in Wallet.

### If a transaction that Wallet deleted stays in your app

WalletFeed removes the transaction from the file. But your app keeps the transactions that you imported previously.

1. In your app, find the transaction.
2. Delete the transaction.
3. If you use Actual and you import that month again, clear **Reimport deleted transactions**.

   If you do not clear **Reimport deleted transactions**, Actual shows the deleted transaction again as a new transaction.

### If Apple Cash or Savings transactions are not in the correct account

One file contains the transactions of all the Wallet accounts that WalletFeed reads. Some apps, for example YNAB, put all the transactions from one file into one account. If a file has Apple Card transactions, Actual imports only the Apple Card transactions from it.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Set the **Filter** switch to on.
4. Tap **Accounts**.
5. Select one account.
6. Go back to the destination.
7. Tap **Send History**.
8. Tap **All**.
9. For each of your other accounts, do [Step 1](#step-1-add-an-ofx-file-in-walletfeed) again with a different name in **Name**.
10. For each new destination, do steps 1 thru 8 again with a different account in step 5.

    Each destination then writes the files for one account only.

11. In your app, import the files of each destination into a different account.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-pocketsmith/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to PocketSmith

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to PocketSmith. You make a developer key in PocketSmith, then you paste the key in WalletFeed.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- WalletFeed on your iPhone, with access to your Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account.
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase. You must have WalletFeed Pro to send transactions to PocketSmith.
- A PocketSmith account and its password. You can use the Free plan of PocketSmith.

If you make a new PocketSmith account, select your time zone on the sign-up form. WalletFeed can find a transaction in PocketSmith only after its date starts in that time zone.

## Step 1: Open the PocketSmith form in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of **Destinations**.

   ![The Destinations screen with no destinations, and the + icon at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-pocketsmith/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In the search field, type `PocketSmith`.
5. Tap **PocketSmith**.

   ![The search for PocketSmith, with the PocketSmith row below the search field.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-pocketsmith/walletfeed-add-destination-search.webp)

6. If WalletFeed shows **WalletFeed Pro**, get [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/).

   After you get WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed shows the PocketSmith form.

## Step 2: Make a developer key in PocketSmith

PocketSmith shows a warning on its developer keys page. The warning tells you that a developer key gives full access to your PocketSmith data until you delete the key. It tells you not to paste a key into "a third-party website or hosted service". It also tells you that PocketSmith does not recommend keys if you are not a software developer.

These facts are about the key in WalletFeed:

- WalletFeed keeps the key in the Keychain on your iPhone.
- WalletFeed sends the key directly from your iPhone to PocketSmith. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers.
- WalletFeed uses the key to get the list of your PocketSmith accounts, and to make the Apple Card account. It also uses the key to add, change and delete the transactions that it sends.
- You can delete the key in PocketSmith. After that, WalletFeed cannot connect to PocketSmith with the key. Refer to [Delete the key in PocketSmith](#delete-the-key-in-pocketsmith).

To make the key on your iPhone, do these steps:

1. In the PocketSmith form, tap **Manage Developer Keys**.

   Your web browser opens PocketSmith.

   ![The PocketSmith form in WalletFeed, with the Developer Key field and the Manage Developer Keys link.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-pocketsmith/walletfeed-setup-pocketsmith.webp)

2. If PocketSmith shows **Sign in to PocketSmith**, sign in with your PocketSmith email address and password.
3. In **Confirm your password**, type your PocketSmith password.

   PocketSmith shows this box each time that you open **Manage developer keys**.

   ![PocketSmith on an iPhone, with a message about the password above the Confirm your password box.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-pocketsmith/pocketsmith-alt-iphone-confirm-password.webp)

4. Tap **CONFIRM PASSWORD**.

   PocketSmith shows **Manage developer keys** and the warning. If the password is not correct, PocketSmith shows "Sorry, your password was incorrect. Try again."

5. In **Create a new key**, type `WalletFeed` in **Name**.

   The name helps you find the WalletFeed key in the list of keys.

   ![The form for a new key in PocketSmith, with the name WalletFeed and the CREATE KEY button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-pocketsmith/pocketsmith-create-key.webp)

6. Tap **CREATE KEY**.

   PocketSmith shows the key one time, in a box below a green message.

7. If you cannot see the key, scroll up to the green message.

   ![PocketSmith on an iPhone, with the new developer key in a box below the green message.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-pocketsmith/pocketsmith-alt-iphone-key-created.webp)

8. Touch and hold the key.
9. Make sure that the highlighted text includes all of the key.

   The key has 128 letters and numbers. PocketSmith has no button to copy the key.

10. Tap **Copy**.

> **Note:** PocketSmith also shows this page from its account menu. The account menu is the person icon at the top right, and it has no label. The path is **Security & integrations** › **Manage developer keys**.

## Step 3: Paste the key in WalletFeed

1. Open WalletFeed again.

   If WalletFeed does not show the PocketSmith form, do [Step 1](#step-1-open-the-pocketsmith-form-in-walletfeed) again.

2. Touch and hold **Developer Key**.
3. Tap **Paste**.

   WalletFeed connects to PocketSmith with the key. Then it shows **Account**.

4. In **Account**, select the account that receives your transactions.

   If you select **New Apple Card Account**, WalletFeed makes a credit card account with the name Apple Card in PocketSmith. If PocketSmith has an account with the name Apple Card, WalletFeed selects that account.

5. Tap **Add**.

   WalletFeed shows **Send Transactions to PocketSmith?** The message tells you the data that PocketSmith receives, the Wallet accounts and the start date.

6. Tap **Send**.
