   WalletFeed starts to send your transactions to PocketSmith. In **Destinations**, the name of the new destination is PocketSmith · and the account name, for example PocketSmith · Apple Card. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed does not send transactions.

## Step 4: Find the transactions in PocketSmith

1. On a computer, open PocketSmith in a web browser.
2. Click **Transactions** at the top of the page.
3. Click the panel icon adjacent to the **Transactions** title.

   PocketSmith shows **Accounts**.

4. In **Accounts**, click **Apple Card**, or the account that you selected in WalletFeed.

   The title changes to **Transactions** › **Apple Card**. Below each merchant, PocketSmith shows `wf:` and an ID.

   ![The Apple Card account in PocketSmith, with six sample transactions.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-pocketsmith/pocketsmith-result-transactions.webp)

5. Click a transaction.
6. Click **Memo**.

   PocketSmith shows the card statement text.

   ![An open transaction in PocketSmith, with the wf: note and the card statement text in Memo.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-pocketsmith/pocketsmith-result-transaction-note.webp)

## The data that PocketSmith receives

WalletFeed adds each transaction to the account that you selected in PocketSmith. This table shows the data that PocketSmith receives:

| From Wallet | In PocketSmith |
| --- | --- |
| The merchant name, or the description if there is no merchant name | **MERCHANT** |
| The amount, negative for a purchase and positive for a refund | **AMOUNT** |
| The date of the transaction, in the time zone of your iPhone | **DATE** |
| The card statement text, if it is different from the merchant name | **Memo** |
| `wf:` and the ID of the transaction in Wallet | The note below the merchant |

PocketSmith shows a purchase in parentheses, for example ($84.12). It shows a refund in green, for example $49.00.

PocketSmith receives no category and no balance. You can give each transaction a category in PocketSmith. After WalletFeed sends a transaction, WalletFeed changes only its amount and its date. Your changes to the merchant, the category and the labels stay.

The new Apple Card account starts with a balance of $0.00. PocketSmith calculates the **BALANCE** column from that balance. Thus, the **BALANCE** column can be different from the balance of your card.

Do not change or delete the `wf:` note. WalletFeed uses the note to find the transaction again. If the note changes, WalletFeed adds the transaction again the next time that the transaction changes in Wallet.

## New transactions and changes

While WalletFeed is open, PocketSmith receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. For this, [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) must be on in **Settings** › **Sync**.

PocketSmith also receives pending charges. When a pending charge becomes posted, WalletFeed changes the amount and the date of the same transaction in PocketSmith. PocketSmith does not show a pending status for transactions from WalletFeed. To send only posted charges, set **Filter** to on, then set **Include Pending** to off. Refer to [Send only some transactions](#send-only-some-transactions).

WalletFeed deletes a declined charge from PocketSmith. It also deletes a transaction that Wallet removes. PocketSmith receives a refund as a different transaction, with a positive amount.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. To change this start date, change **Initial History** before you add PocketSmith.

To send previous transactions again, do these steps:

1. In **Destinations**, tap the PocketSmith destination.
2. Tap **Send History**.
3. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

   WalletFeed shows **Sending History** and the number of transactions that it sent. To stop, tap **Send History**, then **Stop Sending**.

WalletFeed sends a small number of previous transactions to PocketSmith, waits, and then sends more. If you have many transactions, WalletFeed can take a long time to send them all.

**Send History** does not add a transaction two times. WalletFeed finds each transaction by its `wf:` note, and it changes the transaction that it finds. If you deleted a transaction in PocketSmith, **Send History** adds the transaction again.

## Change or stop the PocketSmith destination

You change the PocketSmith destination on its screen in **Destinations**. For more about this screen, refer to [Destinations](/docs/destinations/).

### Send only some transactions

1. In **Destinations**, tap the PocketSmith destination.
2. Set **Filter** to on.
3. Change **Include**, **Minimum**, **Include Pending**, **Accounts**, **Categories** or **Exclude**.

   **Accounts** selects the Wallet accounts that PocketSmith receives. With Apple Intelligence, you can also write the rule in words, for example "Travel over $50, not Uber". Then tap the Apple Intelligence icon.

### Stop the destination for a time

1. In **Destinations**, tap the PocketSmith destination.
2. Set **Enabled** to off.

   WalletFeed does not send transactions to PocketSmith until you set **Enabled** to on again.

### Replace the key

Replace the key after you delete it in PocketSmith, or if PocketSmith does not accept the key.

1. Make a new key in PocketSmith. Refer to [Step 2](#step-2-make-a-developer-key-in-pocketsmith).
2. In **Destinations**, tap the PocketSmith destination.
3. Tap **Replace Key**.
4. Paste the new key in **Developer Key**.
5. Tap **Replace**.

   WalletFeed connects to PocketSmith with the new key before it puts the key in the Keychain. Then **Replace Key** shows a green check mark.

### Remove PocketSmith from WalletFeed

1. In **Destinations**, tap the PocketSmith destination.
2. Tap **Delete**.
3. Tap **Delete** again.

   WalletFeed removes the destination and deletes the key from your iPhone. The transactions that WalletFeed sent stay in PocketSmith. PocketSmith continues to accept the key until you delete the key in PocketSmith.

### Delete the key in PocketSmith

1. On a computer, open [Manage developer keys in PocketSmith](https://my.pocketsmith.com/security/manage_keys).
2. In **Confirm your password**, type your PocketSmith password.
3. Click **CONFIRM PASSWORD**.
4. In the row for WalletFeed, click **Revoke**.

   PocketSmith deletes the key, and it does not tell you to confirm. It shows "Successfully deleted your WalletFeed key."

   ![The list of developer keys in PocketSmith, with the Revoke link for the WalletFeed key.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-pocketsmith/pocketsmith-revoke-key.webp)

After you delete the key, the PocketSmith destination in WalletFeed shows "Authentication failed" when WalletFeed tries to send. To send transactions again, make a new key. Then [replace the key](#replace-the-key) in WalletFeed.

## If there is a problem

### If WalletFeed shows "Key rejected"

WalletFeed shows "Key rejected (HTTP 401). Create a new one in PocketSmith." when PocketSmith does not accept the key, for example because the copied key is not complete.

1. Make a new key in PocketSmith. Refer to [Step 2](#step-2-make-a-developer-key-in-pocketsmith).
2. When you copy the new key, make sure that the highlighted text includes all of the key.
3. Paste the new key in **Developer Key**.

### If the destination shows "Authentication failed"

PocketSmith does not accept the key of the destination, for example because someone deleted the key in PocketSmith.

1. Make a new key in PocketSmith. Refer to [Step 2](#step-2-make-a-developer-key-in-pocketsmith).
2. Replace the key in WalletFeed. Refer to [Replace the key](#replace-the-key).

### If you did not copy the key

PocketSmith shows a key only one time.

1. In PocketSmith, open **Manage developer keys** again.
2. In the row for WalletFeed, tap **Revoke**.
3. Make a new key. Refer to [Step 2](#step-2-make-a-developer-key-in-pocketsmith).

### If PocketSmith shows only the Welcome page

A new PocketSmith account shows the Welcome page until you complete one of its start paths.

1. On the Welcome page, click a start path, for example **Take guided mode**.
2. Complete all the steps of that path.

You can make the developer key before you complete a start path. Guided mode also makes an account with the name Main account. WalletFeed shows this account in **Account**.

### If a transaction shows two times in PocketSmith

WalletFeed did not find the first transaction, because its `wf:` note changed.

1. In PocketSmith, find the transaction that has no `wf:` note.
2. Delete that transaction in PocketSmith.

### If PocketSmith receives transactions only while WalletFeed is open

When **Background Sync** is off, WalletFeed sends transactions only while it is open.

1. Tap the gear icon at the top of **Destinations**.
2. In **Settings** › **Sync**, set **Background Sync** to on.

For more information, refer to [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/).

### If WalletFeed shows "The account is gone from PocketSmith"

Someone deleted the PocketSmith account that the destination uses.

1. Delete the destination. Refer to [Remove PocketSmith from WalletFeed](#remove-pocketsmith-from-walletfeed).
2. Add PocketSmith again. Refer to [Step 1](#step-1-open-the-pocketsmith-form-in-walletfeed).

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-qif/ -->
# Save Apple Card transactions as QIF files

WalletFeed writes your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to QIF files in a folder that you select. There is one file for each month. You import each file into an app, for example GnuCash or Banktivity.

## Before you start

You must have:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version
- WalletFeed, with [access to your Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account](/docs/wallet-accounts/)
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/) (a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase)
- A folder in iCloud Drive, in **On My iPhone** or in a different app that the Files app shows, for example Dropbox
- An app that can import QIF files, for example GnuCash, Moneydance, Banktivity, Actual or YNAB.

WalletFeed is available only in the US. If your app is on a computer, the computer must have access to the folder.

> **Note:** Quicken for Windows cannot import a QIF file into a credit card, checking or savings account. The [Quicken guide](/guides/apple-card-to-quicken/) tells you the files that Quicken can import.

## Step 1: Add a QIF file in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with no destinations and the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-qif/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In the **Destinations** search field, type `QIF`.

   ![The Add Destination screen with the Destinations search field above the Budgeting list.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-qif/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

5. Tap **QIF File**.

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, the **WalletFeed Pro** screen opens. After you get WalletFeed Pro, the **Files** screen opens.

6. Make sure that **Format** is **QIF**.

   ![The Files screen with QIF in Format, no folder in Folder and WalletFeed in Name.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-qif/walletfeed-setup-qif-file.webp)

7. Tap **Folder**.
8. Select a folder, for example a folder in iCloud Drive.

   **Folder** then shows the name of the folder.

9. To use a different name for the files, type it in **Name**.

   Each file gets the name, the month and `.qif`, for example `WalletFeed 2026-10.qif`.

10. Tap **Add**.
11. When WalletFeed shows **Save Transactions to Files?**, tap **Save**.

    The message tells you the data that the folder receives, the accounts and the period. It also tells you that the folder receives only posted transactions. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes the new destination.

WalletFeed then writes a QIF file for each month that has posted transactions. WalletFeed keeps no copy of the files.

## Step 2: Import a QIF file into your app

A QIF file has no ID for each transaction. Thus, your app can import the same transaction two times.

1. Wait until the end of the month.

   Each charge goes into the file for the month of its date, but only after the charge posts. As a result, the file can change after the end of the month.

2. Open your app on the computer or iPhone that has access to the folder.
3. In your app, import the file for the month, for example `WalletFeed 2026-10.qif`.
4. If your app lets you select a date format, select month, day, year (`MM/DD/YYYY`).
5. If your app lets you select an account, select the account for the transactions in the file.
6. Do not import the file for that month again.

   If you import a month two times, your app can show each transaction two times.

> **Note:** Actual shows its **Import** button only on a computer, not on a phone. Actual can import a QIF file only if the file has one Wallet account. [Get one file for each account](#get-one-file-for-each-account) tells you how to make these files.

## Data in the QIF files

Each file contains the posted transactions of one month from the Wallet accounts that the destination gets. Each transaction has these fields:

| Field | Data |
| --- | --- |
| Date (`D`) | The date of the transaction, as month, day, year, for example `10/28/2026`. |
| Amount (`T`) | The amount of the transaction. Purchases have a minus sign, for example `-23.40`. Payments and refunds have no minus sign. |
| Cleared (`C`) | `*` for each transaction, because each transaction in the file posted. |
| Payee (`P`) | The merchant name. If Wallet has no merchant name, the payee is the description. |
| Memo (`M`) | The description and the card statement text, if they are different from the payee. |
| Category (`L`) | The WalletFeed category, for example Groceries or Dining. A transaction in Other has no category. |

For a transaction in a different currency, the memo also contains the amount in that currency and the currency code. The file does not contain the currency, the posted date, the merchant category code or a transaction ID.

A file with one Wallet account has one section. In the file, your Apple Card is a credit card account (`CCard`). Your Apple Cash and Savings accounts are bank accounts (`Bank`). A file with more than one Wallet account has one section for each account. Each section starts with the name of the account.

## Changes to the files

While WalletFeed is open, the files receive changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. For this, [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) must be on in **Settings** › **Sync**. If WalletFeed cannot open the folder at that time, the files change when you open WalletFeed, when an [automation](/docs/siri-and-shortcuts/#send-transactions-with-an-automation) starts, or while your iPhone charges.

A pending charge is not in the file. When the charge posts, WalletFeed adds it to the file for the month of its date. Declined charges do not go into the file. A refund is a different transaction. Its amount has no minus sign.

When a transaction in a month changes, WalletFeed writes the full file for that month again. Changes that you make to a file stay only until WalletFeed writes the file again. If Wallet deletes a transaction from this month or last month, WalletFeed removes it from the file. If you previously imported that transaction into your app, it stays in your app until you delete it.

## Send previous transactions

A new QIF destination also receives your previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. With [Send History](/docs/send-history/), WalletFeed writes the files again for a period that you select:

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap **WalletFeed**, or the name that you typed in **Name**.
3. Tap **Send History**.
4. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

WalletFeed then writes the files of those months again.

> **Note:** If you import a month again after **Send History**, your app can show each transaction of that month two times.

## Change or remove the destination

In WalletFeed, the destination has the name **WalletFeed**, or the name that you typed in **Name**. A change to **Name** on the screen of the destination does not change the names of the files.

### Send only some transactions

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Set the **Filter** switch to on.
3. Set **Include**, **Minimum**, **Accounts**, **Categories** or **Exclude**.

WalletFeed uses the new [filter](/docs/choose-what-to-send/) for the files that it writes after the change. QIF files contain only posted transactions. **Include Pending** does not change this.

### Get one file for each account

Each file of a destination contains the transactions of all the Wallet accounts that the destination gets. To get a different file for each account, use one destination for each account:

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the QIF destination.
3. Set the **Filter** switch to on.
4. Tap **Accounts**.
5. Tap the account that this destination gets.
6. On your iPhone, open the Files app.
7. In the folder, delete the QIF files of this destination, for example `WalletFeed 2026-10.qif`.
8. In WalletFeed, on the screen of the destination, tap **Send History**.
9. Tap **All**.
10. For each of the other accounts, do [Step 1](#step-1-add-a-qif-file-in-walletfeed) again with a different name in **Name**.
11. For each new destination, do steps 1 to 9 of this list again.

### Put the files in a different folder

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap **Change Folder**.
3. Select the folder.

   Then WalletFeed writes all the files again in the new folder.

### Stop the changes to the files

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Set the **Enabled** switch to off.

### Remove the destination

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap **Delete**.
3. Tap **Delete** again.

   The files stay in the folder.

## If there is a problem

### If your app shows each transaction two times

Your app cannot find the transactions that you imported before, because a QIF file has no transaction ID.

1. In your app, delete the transactions that you imported the second time.
2. Do not import that month again.

An OFX file has an ID for each transaction. GnuCash, Moneydance and Actual use this ID and do not import a transaction two times. If your app can import OFX files, you can use an [OFX file](/guides/apple-card-to-ofx/).

### If Actual shows "Failed parsing: doesn't look like a valid QIF file."

Actual cannot import a QIF file that has more than one Wallet account.

1. Do the steps in [Get one file for each account](#get-one-file-for-each-account).
2. In Actual, import each file into a different account.

### If your app puts the transactions of all accounts into one account

Some apps, for example YNAB, put all the transactions of a file into one account.

1. Do the steps in [Get one file for each account](#get-one-file-for-each-account).
2. In your app, import each file into a different account.

### If a charge is not in the file

The charge is pending. A QIF file includes a charge only after it posts.

1. Wait until the charge posts in Wallet.
2. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. Tap **Sync Now**.

If the destination has a filter, make sure that the filter includes the charge.

### If the folder has no QIF file

WalletFeed writes a file only for a month that has posted transactions.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Send Test**.

   The folder then gets `WalletFeed Test.qif` with a sample transaction. If this file is in the folder, WalletFeed can write there.

4. Do not import `WalletFeed Test.qif` into your app.
5. To write all your transactions to the files, tap **Send History**.
6. Tap **All**.

### If the dates in your app are not correct

The file uses US dates in the sequence month, day, year (`MM/DD/YYYY`).

1. In your app, delete the transactions with the incorrect dates.
2. Import the file again.
3. If your app lets you select a date format, select month, day, year.

### If WalletFeed shows "Couldn't open this folder."

WalletFeed cannot open the folder that you selected.

1. Tap **Folder**, or **Change Folder** on the screen of the destination.
2. Select a different folder.

### If the destination shows "Can't open the folder. Choose it again."

WalletFeed does not have access to the folder of the destination at this time.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Change Folder**.
4. Select the same folder again.

### If you cannot tap Add

**Add** is available only after you select a folder.

1. Tap **Folder**.
2. Select a folder.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-quicken/ -->
# Import Apple Card transactions into Quicken

WalletFeed saves your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to OFX files in iCloud Drive, and you import the files into Quicken for Mac. Quicken for Windows cannot import these OFX files, but it can import a CSV file from WalletFeed after you change a copy to Quicken's format.

## Before you start

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version
- WalletFeed, with [access to your Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/)
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase
- Quicken for Mac, or Quicken for Windows with a spreadsheet app
- iCloud Drive on your iPhone and on your computer

WalletFeed is available only in the US.

## Step 1: Add an OFX file in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with no destinations and the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-quicken/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In the search field at the top, type `Quicken`.

   ![The Add Destination screen with the Destinations search field above the Budgeting list.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-quicken/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

5. Tap **OFX File**.

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, the **WalletFeed Pro** screen opens first. After you start the free trial or get a plan, the **Files** screen opens.

6. Make sure that **Format** shows **OFX**.

   ![The Files screen with OFX in Format, Choose… in Folder and WalletFeed in Name.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-quicken/walletfeed-setup-ofx-file.webp)

   With OFX, WalletFeed writes one file for each month.

7. Tap **Folder**.
8. Select a folder in iCloud Drive.

   WalletFeed shows the name of the folder in the **Folder** row.

9. To use a different name for the files, type the name in **Name**.

   If you do not change the name, the file for October 2026 is `WalletFeed 2026-10.ofx`.

10. Tap **Add**.
11. When WalletFeed shows **Save Transactions to Files?**, tap **Save**.

    The message gives the name of the folder and the data that the folder receives. It also gives the Wallet accounts and the start date of the transactions, if there is one. Because an OFX file has only posted transactions, the message uses the words “posted transactions”. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes the new destination.

WalletFeed then writes a file for each month that has posted transactions. In **Destinations**, the new destination has the name **WalletFeed**, or the name that you typed.

## Step 2: Import a file into Quicken for Mac

Quicken for Mac imports the file with the same menu item as a file that you download from the website of a bank.

1. On your Mac, open Quicken.
2. Make a backup of your Quicken data file.
3. Click **File** › **Import** › **Bank or Brokerage File (OFX, QFX)**.
4. Click **Browse**.
5. In the iCloud Drive folder that you selected in WalletFeed, select the file for one month, for example `WalletFeed 2026-10.ofx`.
6. Click **Open**.
7. On the **Choose Your Accounts** screen, select the Quicken account that receives the transactions, for example your Apple Card account.
8. Make sure that the new transactions are in that account.
9. To import the file for a different month, do steps 3 to 8 again.

For more information about these steps, refer to [Quicken's instructions to download and import transactions](https://info.quicken.com/mac/downloading-transactions).

## Use a CSV file with Quicken for Windows

Quicken for Windows cannot import the OFX files from WalletFeed. It imports QFX files (Web Connect files) that you download from the website of a bank. WalletFeed does not write QFX files.

Quicken for Windows can import a CSV file only in Quicken's CSV format. The columns of a WalletFeed CSV file are in a different sequence, and its dates are in a different format. Thus, before you import a file, you must change a copy of it to Quicken's format.

1. On your iPhone, do [step 1](#step-1-add-an-ofx-file-in-walletfeed), with these changes on the **Files** screen:
   - In **Format**, select **CSV**.
   - In **Save As**, select **One File per Month**.

   WalletFeed then writes a CSV file for each month. If you do not change the name, the file for October 2026 is `WalletFeed 2026-10.csv`.

2. On your PC, open the iCloud Drive folder that has the files.
3. Make a copy of the file for one month.
4. Open the copy in a spreadsheet app.
5. In the copy, change the columns and the dates to Quicken's CSV format.

   For the columns and the date format, refer to [Quicken's instructions to import transactions from a CSV file](https://info.quicken.com/win/import-transactions-from-csv-file).

6. Save the copy as a CSV file.
7. In Quicken, click **File** › **File Import** › **Banking Transactions** › **From (.CSV) File**.
8. Click **Choose .CSV File to Import…**.
9. Select the copy of the file.
10. Click **OK**.

> **Note:** Quicken adds all the transactions in a CSV file each time that you import the file. It does not find the transactions that it imported previously.

The CSV file also has pending transactions. Its Status column shows if a transaction is pending. For the columns of the file, refer to the [page about CSV files](/guides/apple-card-to-csv/).

WalletFeed can also write QIF files, but Quicken for Windows cannot import a QIF file into a credit card, checking or savings account.

## Data that Quicken receives

This table shows the data in the OFX file for each Wallet field.

| Wallet | In the OFX file |
| --- | --- |
| Merchant | The name of the payee, with a maximum of 32 characters. If Wallet has no merchant name, WalletFeed uses the description. |
| Amount | The amount of the transaction. Purchases are less than zero. Payments and refunds are more than zero. |
| Currency | The currency of the statement, for example USD. |
| Date | The date of the transaction. |
| Posted date | The date that the transaction posted. |
| Type | The type of transaction, for example a purchase, a payment, a fee or a transfer. |
| Description, card statement text and foreign amount | The memo. WalletFeed does not add text that is the same as the name of the payee. |
| Transaction ID | The ID of the transaction. It stays the same each time that WalletFeed writes the file. |
| Account | A different statement for each of your accounts. The type is credit card for Apple Card, checking for Apple Cash and savings for Savings. |

The file does not include the WalletFeed category or the balance of the account.

## Changes to the files

While WalletFeed is open, the files receive changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. This occurs only if [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**.

If WalletFeed cannot open the folder at that time, the files get the changes when one of these occurs:

- You open WalletFeed.
- A Shortcuts automation starts WalletFeed.
- iOS starts WalletFeed while your iPhone is on its charger.

An OFX file has only posted transactions. WalletFeed adds a pending charge to the file after the charge posts. A declined charge does not post, and thus it is not in the file. A refund is a different transaction, with an amount that is more than zero.

WalletFeed puts each transaction in the file for the month of the transaction date. When a transaction in a month changes, WalletFeed writes the file for that month again. Thus, a file can change after the end of its month, for example when a charge from the last day of that month posts.

Each transaction keeps the same ID each time that WalletFeed writes the file. But Quicken's instructions tell you not to import transactions for the same dates two times, because Quicken can then show a transaction two times.

If Wallet removes a transaction, WalletFeed removes it from the file. WalletFeed cannot remove the transaction from Quicken.

WalletFeed keeps no copy of the files. The files are in your iCloud Drive. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers.

## Send previous transactions

A new OFX File destination also receives your previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. To change the start date, do these steps before you add the destination:

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In **Sync**, tap **Initial History**.

   ![The Settings screen with Initial History set to All in the Sync section.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-quicken/walletfeed-settings.webp)

3. Select **Today**, **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

After you add a destination, you can use [Send History](/docs/send-history/) to write previous transactions to its files:

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination, for example **WalletFeed**.
2. Tap **Send History**.
3. Select **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

   WalletFeed writes the files for those months again. While WalletFeed writes the files, the destination shows **Sending History** and a progress bar.

4. In Quicken, import the files for the months that you did not import previously.

To stop before WalletFeed writes all the files, tap **Send History** › **Stop Sending**.

## Change or remove the destination

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination, for example **WalletFeed**.
3. Make one of the changes in this table.

| Change | On the destination screen |
| --- | --- |
| Send only some transactions | Set **Filter** to on. Then set **Include**, **Minimum**, **Accounts**, **Categories** or **Exclude**. |
| Send only one Wallet account, for example Apple Card | Set **Filter** to on. Tap **Accounts**. Then select the account. |
| Use a different folder | Tap **Change Folder**. Then select the folder. WalletFeed writes all your transactions to the new folder. |
| Stop the changes to the files for a time | Set **Enabled** to off. |
| Change the name of the destination | Type a different name in **Name**. The names of the files stay the same. |
| Remove the destination | Tap **Delete**. Then tap **Delete** again. |

When you remove the destination, the files stay in the folder. Quicken keeps the transactions that you imported.

## If there is a problem

### If WalletFeed shows “Couldn't open this folder.”

WalletFeed cannot get access to the folder that you selected on the **Files** screen.

1. Tap **Folder**.
2. Select a different folder in iCloud Drive.

### If the destination shows “Can't open the folder. Choose it again.”

WalletFeed does not have access to the folder of the destination at this time.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap **Change Folder**.
3. Select the folder again.

### If the folder has no file for a month

WalletFeed writes a file for a month only when the month has posted transactions.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap **Send Test**.

   The folder then gets `WalletFeed Test.ofx`. This file has a sample purchase of $4.20. If this file is in the folder, WalletFeed can write files to the folder.

3. Do not import `WalletFeed Test.ofx` into Quicken.

### If the file does not have new transactions

WalletFeed did not write the file after the last change in Wallet.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** at the top of the screen.
3. In **Sync**, tap **Sync Now**.

### If a pending charge is not in Quicken

An OFX file has only posted transactions. WalletFeed adds the charge to the file after the charge posts.

1. Wait until the charge posts in Wallet.
2. Import the file for that month again, as in [step 2](#step-2-import-a-file-into-quicken-for-mac).
3. If Quicken then shows a transaction two times, delete one of the two transactions.

### If Quicken shows a transaction two times

Quicken imported the same transaction two times, for example when you imported the file for a month two times.

1. In Quicken, delete one of the two transactions.

### If Quicken has a transaction that Wallet removed

WalletFeed removes the transaction from the file, but it cannot remove the transaction from Quicken.

1. In Quicken, delete the transaction.

### If Quicken for Windows does not import the OFX file

Quicken for Windows cannot import the OFX files from WalletFeed.

1. Add a CSV file in WalletFeed, as in [Use a CSV file with Quicken for Windows](#use-a-csv-file-with-quicken-for-windows).

### If Quicken for Windows does not import the CSV file

The file is not in Quicken's CSV format. Quicken then shows a message that gives the necessary changes.

1. Change the copy of the file as the message tells you.
2. Import the copy again, as in [Use a CSV file with Quicken for Windows](#use-a-csv-file-with-quicken-for-windows).

### If Destinations shows “Sync Requires Pro”

You do not have WalletFeed Pro at this time. WalletFeed keeps the destination but does not write the files.

1. In **Destinations**, tap **Upgrade**.
2. Start the free trial, or get a plan.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to Supabase

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a Postgres database in your Supabase project. You copy two values from Supabase into WalletFeed, then you paste SQL from WalletFeed into the Supabase **SQL Editor**.

## Before you start

You must have:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version
- WalletFeed, with access to your [Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/)
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase
- A Supabase account, or an email address for a new account
- A web browser on a computer or on your iPhone.

WalletFeed is available only in the US.

## Step 1: Make a Supabase project

1. If you have a Supabase project for your transactions, go to [Step 2](#step-2-copy-the-project-url-and-the-publishable-key).
2. On your computer, open the [Supabase sign-up page](https://supabase.com/dashboard/sign-up) in a web browser.
3. Type your email address and a password.
4. Click **Sign up**. You can also click **Continue with GitHub**.

   ![The Supabase sign-up page, with the Sign up button highlighted below the Email and Password fields.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/supabase-sign-up.webp)
5. If Supabase sends you an email, open the link in that email.
6. In the [Supabase dashboard](https://supabase.com/dashboard), make a new project.
7. Type the details for the project.
8. Wait until the new database starts.

> **Note:** WalletFeed does not use a database password. It uses only the project URL and the publishable key.

## Step 2: Copy the project URL and the publishable key

1. In your Supabase project, open the **Connect** dialog.
2. Copy the project URL. The URL starts with `https://` and ends with `.supabase.co`.
3. If your project has no publishable key, make one in **Settings** › **API Keys**.
4. Copy the publishable key. The key starts with `sb_publishable_`.
5. If Supabase is open on your computer, send the URL and the key to your iPhone, for example with AirDrop.

> **Note:** WalletFeed does not accept a secret key, which starts with `sb_secret_`. With a secret key, Supabase ignores the Row Level Security policies of your project.

## Step 3: Add Supabase in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with no destinations, and the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)
4. In the **Sheets & Databases** section, tap **Supabase**.

   ![The Add Destination list, with the Budgeting section and the start of the Sheets & Databases section.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)
5. If WalletFeed shows the **WalletFeed Pro** screen, get WalletFeed Pro. Then the Supabase form opens.
6. Paste the publishable key in **Publishable Key**.

   ![The Supabase form in WalletFeed, with the Publishable Key field, the project URL field, Share SQL and the setup steps.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/walletfeed-setup-supabase.webp)
7. Paste the project URL in the field below the key. When this field is empty, it shows `https://abcd.supabase.co`.

> **Note:** WalletFeed keeps the key in the Keychain on your iPhone. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers.

## Step 4: Make the table in Supabase

The SQL from WalletFeed makes the table `walletfeed_transactions` in your project. It also adds a policy that lets only this WalletFeed destination read and write the table. Supabase tells you that the publishable key is [safe to show in an app](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/api/api-keys). With this policy, a person who has only the publishable key cannot read your transactions.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Share SQL**. The share sheet opens.
2. If Supabase is open on your computer, send the SQL to your computer, for example with AirDrop.
3. If Supabase is open on your iPhone, tap **Copy** in the share sheet.
4. In your Supabase project, open the **SQL Editor**.
5. Paste the SQL in the editor.
6. Click **Run**.

## Step 5: Start to send transactions

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed again.
2. Tap **Add**. WalletFeed reads one row of the table to make sure that the URL, the key and the SQL are correct.
3. If WalletFeed shows an error below **Share SQL**, refer to [If something goes wrong](#if-something-goes-wrong).
4. Read the message **Send Transactions to Supabase?** It tells you the data that Supabase receives, the accounts, and the start date.
5. Tap **Send**. WalletFeed adds the destination and starts to send your transactions.
6. In Supabase, open the **Table Editor**.
7. Select the table `walletfeed_transactions`. Each transaction is one row.

> **Note:** If you tap **Cancel** in step 4, WalletFeed does not add the destination. The Supabase form stays open.

## Columns in the Supabase table

Each transaction is one row in the table `public.walletfeed_transactions`. WalletFeed writes these values:

| Column | Postgres type | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `text` | The WalletFeed ID of the transaction. This column is the primary key. |
| `date` | `date` | The day of the transaction, in the time zone of your iPhone. |
| `merchant` | `text` | The merchant name, or the description if Wallet has no merchant name. |
| `amount` | `numeric` | The amount. Purchases and fees are negative numbers. Payments and refunds are positive numbers. |
| `currency` | `text` | The currency code, for example `USD`. |
| `category` | `text` | The WalletFeed category, for example Groceries or Travel. |
| `status` | `text` | The status in Wallet, for example `pending`, `authorized` or `booked`. |
| `pending` | `boolean` | `true` when the status is `pending` or `authorized`, and `false` at other times. |
| `account` | `text` | The account name, for example Apple Card. |
| `description` | `text` | The description of the transaction in Wallet. |
| `type` | `text` | The transaction type in Wallet, for example `pointOfSale` or `refund`. |
| `mcc` | `integer` | The merchant category code. |
| `foreign_amount` | `numeric` | For a purchase in a different currency, the amount in that currency, with the same sign as `amount`. |
| `foreign_currency` | `text` | The code of that different currency. |

For a purchase in dollars, `foreign_amount` and `foreign_currency` are empty (`null`). When a transaction changes, WalletFeed updates its row by `id`. Thus, each transaction has only one row.

Your transactions go from your iPhone directly to your Supabase project. After Supabase receives your transactions, the Supabase terms are applicable to them.

## Sync times and pending charges

While WalletFeed is open, Supabase receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. For this, [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) must be on in **Settings** › **Sync**. **Background Sync** is on until you set it to off.

A pending charge has the value `true` in `pending`. When its status changes to `booked`, WalletFeed updates the same row. If a charge becomes declined or expired, or if Wallet removes a transaction, WalletFeed deletes its row. A refund is a different transaction, with a positive number in `amount`.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it.

To send transactions from a different period, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the Supabase destination. Its name starts with **Supabase ·**.
3. Tap **Send History**.
4. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

Supabase keeps one row for each transaction. To stop, tap **Send History**, then tap **Stop Sending**.

## Change or stop the destination

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the Supabase destination.

   ![The screen of a Lunch Money destination, with Name, Enabled, Last Sync, Replace Token, Filter, Send History, Send Test and Delete.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/walletfeed-destination-detail.webp)

The screen of a Supabase destination has the same controls. It also has **Project**, **Share SQL** and **Replace Key**, but not **Replace Token**.

To send only some transactions, set **Filter** to on. Then select the transactions with **Accounts**, **Categories**, **Minimum** and the other controls. Refer to [Choose what to send](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).

To stop the destination for a time, set **Enabled** to off.

To use a different publishable key, tap **Replace Key**. Paste the new key, then tap **Replace**. WalletFeed keeps the new key only after it can read the table.

To get the SQL again, tap **Share SQL** in the destination. This SQL has the same token as the destination, so you can use it in the **SQL Editor** again. This SQL keeps the rows. It also adds the columns `foreign_amount` and `foreign_currency` if the table does not have them.

To remove the destination, tap **Delete**, then tap **Delete** again. The rows that WalletFeed sent stay in your Supabase table. To remove them, delete the rows or the table in Supabase.

## If something goes wrong

### If you cannot tap Add

WalletFeed lets you tap **Add** only when the form has a publishable key and a correct project URL. If the key is a secret key, WalletFeed also shows "Use the publishable key. Secret keys skip the table's policy."

1. Copy the publishable key from the **Connect** dialog again. The key starts with `sb_publishable_`.
2. Paste the key in **Publishable Key**.
3. Paste the project URL from the **Connect** dialog again.

### If WalletFeed shows "Key rejected. Copy the publishable key again."

Supabase did not accept the key, or the SQL that you used came from a different Supabase form. Each time you open the Supabase form, WalletFeed makes new SQL with a new token.

1. Copy the publishable key from the **Connect** dialog again.
2. Paste the key in **Publishable Key**.
3. Tap **Share SQL**.
4. Paste the new SQL in the **SQL Editor**.
5. Click **Run**.
6. In WalletFeed, tap **Add**.

### If WalletFeed shows "Table not found. Run the SQL, then try again."

The project has no `walletfeed_transactions` table. For example, you did not click **Run**, or you used the **SQL Editor** of a different project.

1. In Supabase, open the project that has the URL from Step 2.
2. Open the **SQL Editor**.
3. Paste the SQL from **Share SQL**.
4. Click **Run**.
5. In WalletFeed, tap **Add**.

### If the destination shows "Authentication failed" or "Rejected (HTTP 404)"

Supabase did not accept the key or the token, or the table is not in the project. For example, SQL from a different WalletFeed destination replaced the token in the table.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.

   ![The Destinations list, with a destination named n8n that shows Authentication failed.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/walletfeed-destinations-failure.webp)
2. Tap the Supabase destination.
3. Tap **Share SQL**.
4. Paste the SQL in the **SQL Editor**.
5. Click **Run**.
6. In WalletFeed, tap **Send Test**.
7. If **Send Test** shows an error, tap **Replace Key**.
8. Paste the publishable key from the **Connect** dialog, then tap **Replace**.

### If Supabase paused your project

The Supabase [pricing page](https://supabase.com/pricing) tells you that Free plan projects "are paused after 1 week of inactivity".

1. Open your project in the [Supabase dashboard](https://supabase.com/dashboard).
2. If the dashboard shows that Supabase paused the project, click the button that starts the project again.
3. In WalletFeed, open the Supabase destination.
4. Tap **Send Test**.

### If no new rows show in the table

WalletFeed sends changes while it is open, or when iOS starts it in the background.

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. Make sure that **Background Sync** is on in **Settings** › **Sync**.
3. Open the Supabase destination.
4. Make sure that the destination shows no error below **Last Sync**.
5. Tap **Send Test**. Supabase receives a test row with the description `WalletFeed test transaction`.
6. In the **Table Editor**, delete the test row.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to Sure

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to Sure, the self-hosted budget app that is a fork of Maybe Finance. You add a card account and make an API key in Sure. Then you paste the key into WalletFeed.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings in Wallet on that iPhone.
- WalletFeed with [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.
- A Sure server and an account on that server. Sure is open source, and you can get it without a purchase.
- An `https://` address for the Sure server. [Step 1](#step-1-get-an-https-address-for-your-sure-server) gives the conditions for this address.
- A computer with a web browser. You use it to add the card account and to make the key in Sure.

## Step 1: Get an HTTPS address for your Sure server

WalletFeed connects only to an address that starts with `https://`. [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) also sends transactions when your iPhone can be away from your home network. Thus, your iPhone must connect to the address from all locations.

If you install Sure with Docker and do not change its configuration, Sure uses an `http://` address on port 3000. WalletFeed cannot use this address.

1. If the address of your Sure server starts with `http://`, use a tunnel service to make an `https://` address. Tailscale and Cloudflare Tunnel are examples of tunnel services.
2. If a tunnel service gives Sure its `https://` address, set `RAILS_ASSUME_SSL: "true"` in the Sure configuration. For more information, refer to the HTTPS section of [the Docker instructions for Sure](https://github.com/we-promise/sure/blob/main/docs/hosting/docker.md).
3. Disconnect your iPhone from your home Wi-Fi.
4. On your iPhone, open the `https://` address of your Sure server in Safari.
5. Make sure that Sure opens.

## Step 2: Add a card account in Sure

WalletFeed writes the transactions into one account in Sure. The Sure API cannot make accounts. Thus, you must add the account in Sure first.

1. On your computer, open your Sure server in a web browser.
2. If a **What's new** dialog opens, click **Got it**.
3. On **Home** › **Dashboard**, click **Add account** or **New**.

   ![The Sure dashboard with no accounts and the Add account button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/sure-home-add-account.webp)

4. Click **Credit Card**.

   ![The Sure dialog that shows the account types, with Credit Card highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/sure-choose-credit-card.webp)

5. Click **Enter account balance**.

   ![The Sure dialog that shows the methods to add the card, with Enter account balance highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/sure-enter-account-balance.webp)

6. In **Account name**, type `Apple Card`.
7. In **Balance on date:**, type `0`, or type the card balance on the **Opening balance date**.
8. Click **Create Account**.

   ![The credit card form in Sure with the name Apple Card, and with the Create Account button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/sure-credit-card-details.webp)

> **Note:** Sure shows a credit card on the **Debts** tab of the account list. The **Assets** tab does not show it.

> **Note:** Sure calculates the card balance from the balance in **Balance on date:** and from the transactions that it receives. The balance in Sure agrees with Wallet only if the balance in **Balance on date:** is correct.

## Step 3: Make a Read/Write API key in Sure

WalletFeed uses the key to read your Sure accounts and to write transactions. With Universal Clipboard, you can copy the key on a Mac and paste it on your iPhone. Do not send the key to yourself in a message or an email.

1. On your computer, open your Sure server in a web browser.
2. At the bottom of the left bar, click the circular button that shows the first letters of your name.

   ![The Sure account page with the circular button at the bottom of the left bar highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/sure-open-account-menu.webp)

3. Click **Settings**.

   ![The Sure account menu, with Settings highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/sure-account-menu-settings.webp)

4. In the Settings list, scroll down to the **ADVANCED** group.
5. Click **API Keys**.

   ![The Sure Settings list with API Keys highlighted in the ADVANCED group.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/sure-settings-api-keys.webp)

6. Click **New API Key**.

   ![The API Keys page in Sure, with no keys and the New API Key button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/sure-api-keys-empty.webp)

7. In **API Key Name**, type `WalletFeed`.
8. In **Permissions**, click **Read/Write**.

   ![The page for a new key in Sure with the name WalletFeed, and with the Read/Write permission highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/sure-create-key-read-write.webp)

9. Click **Save API Key**.

   ![The page for a new key in Sure, with the Save API Key button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/sure-save-api-key.webp)

10. Click **Copy API Key**.

    ![The Sure page that shows the new key one time, with the Copy API Key button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/sure-key-created-copy.webp)

> **Note:** Sure shows the key on this page only. The `curl` example on the same page also contains the key, but WalletFeed cannot use the full `curl` line.

> **Note:** Sure does not select a permission for you. WalletFeed does not accept a **Read Only** key.

To make the key on your iPhone, do these steps:

1. In WalletFeed, do steps 1 to 6 of [Step 4](#step-4-add-sure-in-walletfeed).
2. Tap **Open API Keys**. WalletFeed opens the **API Keys** page of your Sure server.
3. If Sure shows its sign-in page, sign in.
4. If Sure then shows its dashboard, tap **Open API Keys** in WalletFeed again.
5. On the **API Keys** page, do steps 6 to 10 of the first procedure in Step 3.

## Step 4: Add Sure in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+**.

   ![The empty Destinations screen with the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In **Budgeting**, tap **Sure**. If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed first shows the WalletFeed Pro screen.

   ![The Add Destination list, with Sure and the text Self-hosted in the Budgeting group.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

5. In the field that shows `https://sure.example.com`, type the `https://` address of your Sure server.
6. If WalletFeed shows **Use an API Key Instead**, tap it.

   In Sure v0.7.6, WalletFeed does not connect with **Sign In with Sure**. For more information, refer to [If Sure opens the dashboard after you sign in](#if-sure-opens-the-dashboard-after-you-sign-in).

7. In **API Key**, paste the key. WalletFeed connects to Sure and shows **Account**.

   ![The Sure setup screen in WalletFeed with the server field, the API Key field and three steps.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/walletfeed-setup-sure.webp)

8. In **Account**, select your card account. If an account has Apple Card in its name, WalletFeed selects that account for you.
9. Tap **Add**.
10. In the **Send Transactions to Sure?** message, tap **Send**. The message tells you the data that Sure receives, the Wallet accounts and the start date.
11. On your computer, click **Transactions** in Sure. Sure shows the transactions from WalletFeed in the list.

    ![The Sure Transactions page with seven sample transactions from WalletFeed in the Apple Card account.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/sure-walletfeed-result.webp)

## Data that Sure receives

WalletFeed sends these fields for each transaction to the Sure account that you selected:

| From Wallet | In Sure |
| --- | --- |
| The date of the transaction, in your time zone | Date |
| The merchant name, or the description if there is no merchant name | Name |
| The amount | Amount. A purchase is an expense, and a refund or other credit is income. |
| The currency | Currency |
| The ID of the transaction in Wallet | An ID that WalletFeed uses to change the transaction |

WalletFeed does not send categories. Sure shows new transactions as **Uncategorized** until you give them a category.

Sure shows a purchase with a minus sign, for example -$6.75. It shows a refund in green without a minus sign. The **Debt balance** of the card increases with each purchase.

WalletFeed sends the transactions from your iPhone directly to your Sure server. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. The server address and the key stay in the Keychain on your iPhone.

## New and changed transactions

While WalletFeed is open, Sure receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. Then WalletFeed sends the change. For this, [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) must be on in **Settings** › **Sync**.

WalletFeed sends a pending charge to Sure as a usual transaction. When Wallet shows the charge as posted, WalletFeed changes the date and the amount in Sure to agree with Wallet. The name, category, merchant, tags and notes that you set in Sure stay the same.

If Wallet removes a pending charge, for example a declined charge, WalletFeed deletes the transaction from Sure. WalletFeed deletes only transactions from the last 90 days.

If WalletFeed sends a transaction again, Sure does not make a second copy. Sure keeps one transaction for each Wallet transaction.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it.

You can also send previous transactions with [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the Sure destination, for example **Sure · Apple Card**.
3. Tap **Send History**.
4. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

WalletFeed shows **Sending History** with the number of transactions that it sent. To stop, tap **Send History** › **Stop Sending**.

## Change or remove the destination

To open the Sure destination, do these steps:

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the Sure destination.

For more information, refer to [Destinations](/docs/destinations/).

### Send only some transactions

1. Set **Filter** to on.
2. Use **Include**, **Minimum**, **Include Pending**, **Accounts**, **Categories** and **Exclude** to select the transactions.

To send only Apple Card transactions to this destination, select Apple Card in **Accounts**. To send Apple Cash to a different Sure account, add Sure again. In **Account**, select that account.

For more information, refer to [Choose what a destination receives](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).

### Replace the key

> **Note:** Sure does not accept two active keys with the same name. While the previous key is active, the new key must have a different name. If you click **Revoke** for the previous key first, you can use the same name.

1. Make a new Read/Write key in Sure, as in [Step 3](#step-3-make-a-read-write-api-key-in-sure).
2. In the Sure destination, tap **Replace Key**.
3. In **API Key**, paste the new key.
4. Tap **Replace**.

WalletFeed keeps the new key only if the key lets WalletFeed read the card account and write transactions into it.

### Stop or remove the destination

To stop the destination temporarily, set **Enabled** to off.

To remove the destination, do these steps:

1. In the Sure destination, tap **Delete**.
2. In the **Delete Sure · Apple Card?** message, tap **Delete**.
3. On your computer, open **Settings** › **API Keys** in Sure.
4. Click **Revoke** for the WalletFeed key.

   ![The API Keys list in Sure, with the Revoke button for the WalletFeed key highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/sure-revoke-key.webp)

5. Click **Confirm**.

   ![The Sure dialog about the WalletFeed key, with Confirm highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/sure-revoke-confirm.webp)

The transactions that WalletFeed sent stay in Sure. If you remove the destination, WalletFeed does not delete them.

## If there is a problem

### If Sure opens the dashboard after you sign in

You tapped **Sign In with Sure**. In Sure v0.7.6, Sure opens its dashboard after you sign in, and WalletFeed does not connect. The dashboard starts with "Welcome back" and your name.

1. Close the Sure page.
2. Tap **Use an API Key Instead**.
3. Make a key, as in [Step 3](#step-3-make-a-read-write-api-key-in-sure).
4. Do steps 7 to 11 of [Step 4](#step-4-add-sure-in-walletfeed).

### If WalletFeed does not show Account or Open API Keys

The address starts with `http://`. WalletFeed connects only to `https://` addresses, and it shows no message for an `http://` address.

1. Get an `https://` address for your Sure server, as in [Step 1](#step-1-get-an-https-address-for-your-sure-server).
2. In WalletFeed, type the `https://` address.

### If WalletFeed shows "This server doesn't support sign-in"

WalletFeed shows "This server doesn't support sign-in. Use an API key." when it cannot find Sign In with Sure at the address. Then WalletFeed opens the API key form.

1. Make sure that the address is the same address that you use to open Sure in a web browser.
2. If the address is correct, paste the key in **API Key**, as in [Step 4](#step-4-add-sure-in-walletfeed).

### If WalletFeed shows "Sure signs in at"

WalletFeed shows "Sure signs in at", then a different address, when Sure gives a different address for Sign In with Sure. Sure gets this address from `APP_URL` in its configuration. An API key does not use this address.

1. Tap **Use an API Key Instead**.
2. Paste the key in **API Key**, as in [Step 4](#step-4-add-sure-in-walletfeed).

### If WalletFeed shows "Create an account in Sure"

When Sure has no account that WalletFeed can write into, WalletFeed shows "Create an account in Sure for your card, then try again."

1. Add a card account in Sure, as in [Step 2](#step-2-add-a-card-account-in-sure).
2. In WalletFeed, delete the key in **API Key**.
3. Paste the key in **API Key** again.
4. Make sure that WalletFeed shows **Account**.

### If WalletFeed shows "This key is Read Only"

WalletFeed shows "This key is Read Only. Create a Read/Write key." when you paste a **Read Only** key. WalletFeed must have a Read/Write key to write transactions into Sure.

1. On your computer, open **Settings** › **API Keys** in Sure.
2. Click **Revoke** for the key.
3. Click **Confirm**.
4. Make a new Read/Write key, as in [Step 3](#step-3-make-a-read-write-api-key-in-sure).
5. In WalletFeed, paste the new key in **API Key**.

### If WalletFeed shows "Key rejected (HTTP 401)"

When Sure does not accept the key, WalletFeed shows "Key rejected (HTTP 401). Check it, or create a new one in Sure." The key is not correct or expired, or you clicked **Revoke** for it in Sure.

1. Make sure that you copied the key with **Copy API Key**, and not the `curl` line.
2. If you copied the `curl` line, do the steps in [If you closed the key page before you copied the key](#if-you-closed-the-key-page-before-you-copied-the-key).
3. If you copied the key with **Copy API Key**, make a new Read/Write key in Sure, as in [Step 3](#step-3-make-a-read-write-api-key-in-sure).
4. In WalletFeed, paste the new key in **API Key**.

### If Destinations shows "Authentication failed" for Sure

Sure does not accept the key when WalletFeed sends transactions. For example, you clicked **Revoke** for the key in Sure.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.

   ![The Destinations screen, where one destination shows Authentication failed.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/walletfeed-destinations-failure.webp)

2. Tap the Sure destination.
3. Replace the key, as in [Replace the key](#replace-the-key).

### If WalletFeed shows "Can't connect" or "Couldn't connect"

WalletFeed cannot connect to your Sure server. The server is off, or your iPhone can connect to it only on your home network.

1. Make sure that your Sure server operates.
2. Disconnect your iPhone from your home Wi-Fi.
3. On your iPhone, open the `https://` address of your Sure server in Safari.
4. If Sure does not open, get an `https://` address for all locations, as in [Step 1](#step-1-get-an-https-address-for-your-sure-server).
5. If you added Sure in WalletFeed, tap **Send Test** in the Sure destination.

The test writes a transaction of $4.20 with the name WalletFeed into the card account in Sure. You can delete it in Sure after the test.

### If WalletFeed shows "No Sure API at this address"

WalletFeed shows "No Sure API at this address, or the account is gone." when the address is not correct. WalletFeed also shows this message if you deleted the card account in Sure.

1. Make sure that the address is the same address that you use to open Sure in a web browser.
2. If you deleted the card account in Sure, add a new card account, as in [Step 2](#step-2-add-a-card-account-in-sure).
3. If you added a new card account, add Sure again in WalletFeed, as in [Step 4](#step-4-add-sure-in-walletfeed).

### If you closed the key page before you copied the key

Sure shows a key one time only. Sure also does not accept two active keys with the same name.

1. On your computer, open **Settings** › **API Keys** in Sure.
2. Click **Revoke** for the WalletFeed key.
3. Click **Confirm**.
4. Make a new key, as in [Step 3](#step-3-make-a-read-write-api-key-in-sure).
5. In WalletFeed, paste the new key in **API Key**.

### If the card balance in Sure is not correct

Sure calculates the balance from the balance in **Balance on date:** and from the transactions. After many transactions in a short time, Sure can show a balance without the last transaction.

1. In Sure, open the card account.
2. On the right side of the account name, click the icon with two circular arrows.

   ![The Apple Card account in Sure, with the icon that has two circular arrows highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/sure-refresh-account-balance.webp)

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to Toshl Finance

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to Toshl Finance. You make a personal token in Toshl, then paste it into WalletFeed.

## Before you start

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- WalletFeed, with access to the [Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/) that you want to send.
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), because destinations are part of it. WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.
- Toshl Finance, with the email and password that you use to log in. You can make personal tokens on the Toshl Free plan.
- A computer with a web browser, to add an account in Toshl in Step 1.

## Step 1: Add an Apple Card account in Toshl

WalletFeed adds all entries to one Toshl account. If the name of an account includes "Apple", WalletFeed selects that account for you. If you have an account for your card in Toshl, go to Step 2.

1. On your computer, log in to the [Toshl web app](https://toshl.com/app/).
2. Click **All accounts**.

   ![The Toshl web app with a red frame around the All accounts button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/toshl-home-all-accounts.webp)

3. In the **Accounts** panel, click **ADD ACCOUNT**.

   ![The Toshl Accounts panel with a red frame around the ADD ACCOUNT button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/toshl-add-account.webp)

   If Toshl shows **Upgrade to Toshl Pro or Medici**, click **X**, then go to Step 2. The Toshl Free plan has a limit of 2 accounts.

4. Click **General financial account**.

   ![The Toshl Add account dialog with a red frame around General financial account.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/toshl-general-account.webp)

   Do not click **Connected financial account**. It is Toshl bank sync, which is only on the Medici plan.

5. In **Title**, type `Apple Card`.

   ![The Toshl Add account form with the title Apple Card and a red frame around the SAVE button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/toshl-account-title.webp)

6. Click **SAVE**. You can keep 0.00 in **New account balance** and **Account limit**.

   ![The Toshl Accounts panel with the new Apple Card account below Cash.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/toshl-account-added.webp)

## Step 2: Open the Toshl Finance form in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. In **Destinations**, tap **+**.

   ![The Destinations screen in WalletFeed with the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

3. Under **Budgeting**, tap **Toshl Finance**.

   ![The Add Destination list in WalletFeed with Toshl Finance in the Budgeting group.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed shows **WalletFeed Pro** first. After you get WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed shows the Toshl Finance form.

## Step 3: Make a personal token in Toshl

1. In the Toshl Finance form, tap **Open Apps**.

   ![The Toshl Finance form in WalletFeed with the Personal Token field and the Open Apps link.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/walletfeed-setup-toshl-finance.webp)

   The Toshl **Apps** page opens in your web browser.

2. If the page shows **Please login to proceed.**, do these steps:

   ![The Toshl Apps page with the message Please login to proceed and a red frame around login.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/toshl-apps-login.webp)

   1. Tap **login**.
   2. Type your Toshl email and password.
   3. Tap **Log in**. Toshl then opens its web app, not the **Apps** page.
   4. In WalletFeed, tap **Open Apps** again.

3. In **Description**, type `WalletFeed`.

   ![The Toshl Apps page with a red frame around the Description field.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/toshl-apps-page.webp)

4. In **Password**, type your Toshl password.
5. Tap **Create**.

   ![The new personal token form with the description WalletFeed and a red frame around the Create button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/toshl-create-token.webp)

6. Copy all of the token in the gray box under **Tokens list**.

   ![The Toshl Tokens list with the new token in a gray box, blurred in this picture, and the description WalletFeed.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/toshl-token-created.webp)

   Toshl shows all of the token only one time. The token has two lines, and the page has no copy button. The text WalletFeed in the same row is the description, not the token.

> **Note:** With the token, an app can read and change all of your Toshl data. Toshl does not let you limit what a token can do.

## Step 4: Add Toshl Finance in WalletFeed

1. Go back to WalletFeed.
2. In **Personal Token**, paste the token.

   WalletFeed does a check of the token, then shows **Account** with your Toshl accounts. The token stays in the Keychain on your iPhone.

3. Make sure that **Account** shows the Toshl account for your card, such as Apple Card.

   To use a different account, tap **Account**, then select the account.

4. Tap **Add**.

   WalletFeed shows **Send Transactions to Toshl Finance?** The message tells you that Toshl Finance receives the date, merchant, amount, currency and category of transactions. It also gives the Wallet accounts and the start date.

5. Tap **Send**.

   WalletFeed starts to send your transactions. **Destinations** shows the new destination, with a name such as **Toshl · Apple Card**. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed does not add the destination.

   ![The Toshl Expenses page with sample Apple Card purchases by date, each with its category and merchant.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/toshl-result-expenses.webp)

## Data that Toshl Finance receives

Each transaction becomes one entry in the Toshl account that you selected. Your transactions go from your iPhone directly to Toshl. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. After Toshl receives your transactions, the Toshl terms are applicable to them.

| In Wallet | In Toshl Finance |
|---|---|
| A purchase | An expense |
| A refund or other credit | An income |
| Amount | Amount. WalletFeed does not send a transaction with an amount of 0, because Toshl does not accept it. |
| Currency | Currency |
| Purchase date | Date, as the day in your time zone |
| Merchant, or the description if there is no merchant | Description, with a maximum of 255 characters |
| Category | Category, from the table that follows |
| Transaction ID | A WalletFeed ID that Toshl keeps but does not show |

Toshl does not receive the name of the Wallet account. All entries go into the one Toshl account.

For each new entry, WalletFeed compares your Toshl categories with the names in the second column, in sequence. It uses the first name that agrees with a Toshl category. Capital letters do not change the result. If no name agrees, WalletFeed uses **Other**.

| WalletFeed category | Toshl category names, in sequence | Result with the standard English categories in Toshl |
|---|---|---|
| Groceries | Groceries, Food & Drinks, Food | Food & Drinks |
| Dining | Restaurants, Dining, Food & Drinks, Food | Food & Drinks |
| Transport | Transport, Transportation | Transport |
| Fuel | Fuel, Car, Transport | Transport |
| Entertainment | Entertainment, Leisure | Leisure |
| Travel | Travel, Holidays | Other |
| Shopping | Shopping, Clothing | Other |
| Subscriptions | Subscriptions, Bills & Fees, Bills | Other |
| Utilities | Utilities, Bills & Fees, Bills, Home | Other |
| Health | Health, Healthcare, Health & Beauty | Other |
| Services | Services | Other |
| Cash & Transfers | Cash, Transfers | Other |
| Other | Other | Other |
| A refund or other credit | Refunds, Other (income categories) | Other |

WalletFeed sets the category only when it adds an entry. If you change the category, tags, location or reminders of an entry in Toshl, WalletFeed keeps your changes.

## Sync times and changes

While WalletFeed is open, Toshl receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. For this, [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) must be on in **Settings** › **Sync**.

Toshl has no pending status. In Toshl, a pending purchase is a usual expense. When the purchase posts, WalletFeed changes the amount, date and description of the same entry.

If a pending purchase does not post, for example after a decline, WalletFeed removes its entry from Toshl. WalletFeed does this only for entries from the last 90 days.

A refund is an income in Toshl, in the category **Refunds** or **Other**.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it.

To send a different period, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Toshl Finance destination.
2. Tap **Send History**.

   ![A destination screen in WalletFeed, here for Lunch Money, with Send History under Filter.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/walletfeed-destination-detail.webp)

3. Select **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

WalletFeed sends the history in small parts, at a speed that Toshl accepts. **Destinations** shows the progress. To stop, tap **Send History** › **Stop Sending**.

If you send a period again, WalletFeed finds the entries that it sent before. It changes them if it is necessary, and it does not add a second entry.

## Change or stop the destination

In **Destinations**, tap the Toshl Finance destination. Then use these controls:

- To stop the destination for a time, set **Enabled** to off.
- To send only some transactions, set **Filter** to on. Refer to [Choose what a destination receives](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).
- To use a new token, tap **Replace Token**, paste the token, then tap **Replace**.
- To remove the destination, tap **Delete**, then tap **Delete** again.

WalletFeed accepts a new token only if it can see the same Toshl account. The entries that WalletFeed sent before stay in Toshl, and WalletFeed does not add them again.

After you tap **Delete**, the transactions that WalletFeed sent stay in Toshl. To remove the token from Toshl too, do these steps:

1. On your computer, open the [Toshl Apps page](https://developer.toshl.com/apps/).
2. In **Tokens list**, click **Delete** in the row of the WalletFeed token.

   ![The Toshl Tokens list with a red frame around the Delete button for the WalletFeed token.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/toshl-delete-token.webp)

   Toshl removes the token and does not show a confirmation message.

## If something goes wrong

### If WalletFeed shows "Token rejected" or "Authentication failed"

Toshl does not accept the token, because you copied only part of it, or you removed it in Toshl.

1. Make a new personal token, as in [Step 3](#step-3-make-a-personal-token-in-toshl).
2. Copy all of the token in the gray box.
3. In WalletFeed, paste the token in **Personal Token**.

   For a destination that you added before, use **Replace Token**.

### If the token in Toshl ends with "..."

Toshl shows all of the token only one time, and WalletFeed cannot use the first part that Toshl shows after that.

1. Make a new personal token, as in [Step 3](#step-3-make-a-personal-token-in-toshl).
2. In **Tokens list**, tap **Delete** in the row of the token that ends with "...".

### If WalletFeed shows "Create an account in Toshl first."

Toshl has no active account for your login.

1. Add an account in Toshl, as in [Step 1](#step-1-add-an-apple-card-account-in-toshl).
2. In WalletFeed, remove the token from **Personal Token**.
3. Paste the token again.

### If WalletFeed shows "This token can't see" and the account name

The new token is from a different Toshl login, or the account is not in Toshl now.

1. Log in to Toshl with the email that has the account.
2. Make a new personal token, as in [Step 3](#step-3-make-a-personal-token-in-toshl).
3. In WalletFeed, tap **Replace Token** and paste the new token.

### If Toshl shows "Upgrade to Toshl Pro or Medici"

The Toshl Free plan has a limit of 2 accounts, and the account Cash is one of them.

1. Click **X**.
2. In WalletFeed, in **Account**, select an account that you have in Toshl.

### If you do not know your Toshl password

To make a token, you must type your Toshl password. If you log in to Toshl with Apple, Google or Facebook, possibly you have no Toshl password.

1. Open the [Toshl Log In page](https://toshl.com/login/).
2. Tap **Forgot password?** and set a password.

### If many entries are in Other

The standard Toshl categories do not have names for many WalletFeed categories.

1. On the Toshl **Expenses** page, click **Edit categories**.
2. Add an expense category with a name from the [category table](#data-that-toshl-finance-receives), such as `Shopping`.

WalletFeed uses the new category for new entries only. To change an entry that is in Toshl now, change its category in Toshl.

### If Toshl shows a negative balance

The new account starts at 0.00, and each purchase is an expense. Thus, the balance is less than zero after the first purchase. This is usual for a card account and does not show a sync problem.

### If no transactions show in Toshl

1. In WalletFeed, tap the Toshl Finance destination in **Destinations**.
2. Read **Last Sync**. If it shows a message, find that message on this page.
3. Tap **Send Test**.

   Toshl receives a test expense of $4.20 with the description WalletFeed. Remove it in Toshl after the test.

4. In Toshl, click the arrows adjacent to the month name to see a different month.

### If an entry shows two times in Toshl

Two iPhones that send the same card to Toshl at the same time can each add the entry.

1. Keep the Toshl Finance destination on one iPhone only.
2. In Toshl, remove the second entry.

### If WalletFeed shows "Toshl is limiting requests. Try again later."

Toshl received too many requests in a short time.

1. Wait some minutes.
2. Try again.

During a sync, WalletFeed stops and continues at the next sync.
