<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-webhook/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to a webhook

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a webhook. A webhook is an `https://` URL in n8n or on your server. WalletFeed sends each new or changed transaction to that URL as JSON.

## Before you start

For this procedure, you must have:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings in Wallet on that iPhone.
- WalletFeed with [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/). WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.
- An n8n workflow, or a server that can receive HTTPS requests. The URL must start with `https://`.
- A computer for the steps in n8n or on your server.

WalletFeed also sends transactions when your iPhone is away from your home network. Thus, your iPhone must connect to the URL from the internet.

## Step 1: Get a webhook URL

Do the steps for n8n, or the steps for your server.

### Get the URL in n8n

The Webhook node in n8n gives you the URL. With **Header auth**, the node also makes sure that each request has the correct `Authorization` value.

1. On your computer, open n8n.
2. Make a new workflow.
3. Click **Add first step...**.
4. Select the **Webhook** node.
5. In **HTTP Method**, select **POST**.
6. In **Authentication**, select **Header auth**.
7. Make a new Header auth credential.
8. In **Name**, type `Authorization`.
9. In **Value**, type `Bearer`, a space and a long password that you make.
10. Keep a copy of the full value.

    You use this value in WalletFeed in Step 2.
11. Save the credential.
12. In **Respond**, select **Immediately**.

    With **Immediately**, n8n sends the status code when the workflow starts. WalletFeed waits a maximum of 30 seconds for the status code. If the workflow then stops because of an error, WalletFeed does not send the data again.
13. Select **Production URL**.
14. Copy the URL that n8n shows.
15. Click **Publish**.

    Result: n8n shows a window with a name for the version.
16. In that window, click **Publish**.

    Result: n8n starts to receive requests at the **Production URL**.
17. Send the URL and the full header value to your iPhone, for example with AirDrop.

You must use the **Production URL** in WalletFeed. The **Test URL** operates only for 120 seconds after you click **Listen for test event**.

n8n uses only the version of the workflow that you published. If you change the workflow, you must publish it again.

> **Note:** If requests go to your n8n server through a reverse proxy, n8n gets the **Production URL** from the environment variable `N8N_WEBHOOK_URL`. Its value must be your `https://` address. Before n8n 2.35.0, the name of this variable was `WEBHOOK_URL`. From version 2.35.0, n8n also reads `WEBHOOK_URL`, but it writes a message about the previous name in its log.

### Use your server

Your server must do these tasks:

- Accept `POST` requests with a JSON body at an `https://` URL.
- Send a status code from 200 to 299 after the server saves the data. If WalletFeed gets a different code, it sends the same data again at the next sync.
- Use the `id` of each transaction to find a transaction that the server received previously. WalletFeed sends a transaction again when it changes.
- Remove the transactions that have their IDs in `data.deletedIDs`.

[Webhook format](/docs/webhooks/) gives the JSON format and the signature check. In Step 2, you get the secret for the signature check.

## Step 2: Add the webhook in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The empty Destinations screen with the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-webhook/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. Tap **Webhook**, below **Developers**.

   **Webhook** is at the bottom of the list. To find it with the search field, you can type `webhook` or `n8n`.

   Result: WalletFeed shows the **Webhook** screen. If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, it shows **WalletFeed Pro** first.
5. If WalletFeed shows **WalletFeed Pro**, get [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/).
6. To give the destination a different name, for example n8n, type the name in **Name**.

   ![The Webhook screen in WalletFeed with Name, the URL field, Authorization (Optional), Share Signing Secret, Send Test and the Webhook Format link.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-webhook/walletfeed-setup-webhook.webp)

7. Paste the URL into the field that shows `https://example.com/hook`.

   If the URL does not start with `https://`, you cannot tap **Send Test** or **Add**.
8. If you use n8n, paste the full header value into **Authorization (Optional)**.
9. If you do not use n8n, and your server examines the `Authorization` header, type the header value into **Authorization (Optional)**.
10. If your server does not examine the signature, go to step 14. For example, n8n with **Header auth** does not examine it.
11. Tap **Share Signing Secret**.

    Result: Your iPhone shows the share sheet. The secret starts with `whsec_`.
12. Tap **Copy**.
13. Add the secret to your server.
14. Tap **Send Test**.

    Result: WalletFeed sends one test transaction of $4.20 from the merchant WalletFeed. If the server accepts it, WalletFeed shows a green check mark.

    If the server does not accept it, WalletFeed shows the error below **Send Test**. In n8n, the **Executions** tab of the workflow shows the test.
15. Tap **Add**.

    Result: WalletFeed shows **Send Transactions to Your Server?** with a message. The message tells you the data that your server receives. It also gives the Wallet accounts and the start date.

    If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes the new destination and does not send data.
16. Tap **Send**.

    Result: WalletFeed starts to send transactions to the URL.

    ![The Destinations screen with the n8n webhook destination and three other destinations.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-webhook/walletfeed-destinations.webp)

## Data that the webhook receives

WalletFeed sends each change to the URL as an HTTP `POST` request with a JSON body. One request contains a maximum of 100 transactions. The body has these items:

- `type` is `transactions.changed`. For **Send Test**, the value is `walletfeed.test`.
- `timestamp` is the date and time when WalletFeed sent the request.
- `data.upserted` is a list of the new and changed transactions.
- `data.deletedIDs` is a list of the IDs of the transactions to remove.

WalletFeed does not send the IDs to remove in the same request as the new and changed transactions. Thus, in each request, one of the two lists is empty.

This table shows the fields of each transaction in `data.upserted`.

| WalletFeed sends | JSON field |
| --- | --- |
| Transaction ID, which stays the same when the transaction changes | `id` |
| ID and name of the Wallet account, for example Apple Card | `accountID`, `accountName` |
| `liability` for Apple Card, or `asset` for Apple Cash and Savings | `accountType` |
| Date and time of the transaction | `date` |
| Date and time when the charge posted, if Wallet gives it | `postedDate` |
| Amount, as a positive number | `amount` |
| `debit` for purchases and fees, or `credit` for refunds, payments and deposits | `direction` |
| Currency code, for example `USD` | `currencyCode` |
| Amount and currency of a purchase in a different currency | `foreignAmount`, `foreignCurrencyCode` |
| Description from Wallet | `description` |
| Description from the card network | `originalDescription` |
| Merchant name, if Wallet has it | `merchantName` |
| Merchant category code (MCC), if Wallet has it | `merchantCategoryCode` |
| WalletFeed category, for example `dining` or `groceries` | `category` |
| Wallet status: `authorized`, `pending`, `booked` or `memo` | `status` |
| Transaction type from Wallet, for example `pointOfSale`, `refund`, `billPayment` or `transfer` | `type` |

If Wallet has no value for a field, the transaction does not include that field. The dates use the ISO 8601 format and UTC, for example `2026-10-30T06:29:40Z`.

Each request also has the Standard Webhooks headers `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp` and `webhook-signature`. The `User-Agent` header is `WalletFeed-Webhooks/1`. If you typed a value in **Authorization**, the request has that value in the `Authorization` header.

WalletFeed sends the data from your iPhone directly to the URL. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. It keeps the URL, the **Authorization** value and the secret in the Keychain on your iPhone. The server or service that receives the data keeps it. The terms of that service are applicable to the data.

### Get one item for each transaction in n8n

The Webhook node puts the JSON in `body`. To get one n8n item for each transaction, do these steps:

1. After the Webhook node, add a **Split Out** node.
2. In **Field to Split Out**, type `body.data.upserted`.
3. Click **Publish**.
4. In the window, click **Publish**.

The IDs of the transactions to remove are in `body.data.deletedIDs`.

The request from **Send Test** also starts the workflow. In that request, `body.type` is `walletfeed.test`.

## New and changed transactions

While WalletFeed is open, the webhook receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. Then WalletFeed sends the change. For this, [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) must be on in **Settings** › **Sync**.

Wallet shows a new charge as pending until the charge posts. WalletFeed sends it with `pending` or `authorized` in `status`. When the charge posts, WalletFeed sends the same `id` again with `booked` in `status` and the posted amount. To keep one item for each transaction, you must change the item that has the same `id`. If Wallet gives the posted charge a new ID, WalletFeed sends the previous ID in `deletedIDs` and the new transaction in `upserted`.

If **Include Pending** is off in the filter, WalletFeed sends charges only after they post. [Send only some transactions](#send-only-some-transactions) tells you how to set the filter.

A refund is a different transaction. Its `direction` is `credit`. If Wallet shows a charge as declined or expired, or removes a transaction, WalletFeed sends the ID of that transaction in `deletedIDs`.

If the server does not send a status code from 200 to 299, WalletFeed sends the same changes again at the next sync. Thus, the server can receive the same data two times. Two requests with the same data have the same `webhook-id`. The `webhook-timestamp` header, the `timestamp` value and the signature are different in each request.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. To start from a different date, you must set **Initial History** before you add the webhook.

To send more previous transactions after you add the webhook, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. In **Destinations**, tap the webhook destination.
2. Tap **Send History**.
3. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

   Result: WalletFeed shows **Sending History** and a progress bar.

WalletFeed uses `transactions.changed` requests for previous transactions, and it sends the newest transactions first. It sends them in groups of approximately 500 and waits 1 second between groups. Each request contains a maximum of 100 transactions. n8n starts the workflow one time for each request.

To stop **Send History**:

1. In the destination, tap **Send History**.
2. Tap **Stop Sending**.

## Change or remove the destination

### Send only some transactions

1. In **Destinations**, tap the webhook destination.
2. Set **Filter** to on.
3. Set the filter controls. The table that follows gives each control and its result.

| Control | WalletFeed sends |
| --- | --- |
| **Include** | All transactions, only purchases or only credits. |
| **Minimum** | Only transactions of this amount or more. |
| **Include Pending** | If it is off, charges only after they post. |
| **Accounts** | Only transactions from the Wallet accounts that you select. |
| **Categories** | Only transactions in the categories that you select. |
| **Exclude** | No transactions from the merchants that you type. Put a comma between the merchants. |

If Apple Intelligence is on, you can also type a rule, for example "Travel over $50, not Uber". When you tap the Apple Intelligence symbol, WalletFeed makes the filter from the rule. For more data about the filter, refer to [Choose what to send](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).

WalletFeed uses the filter only for the transactions that it sends after you set the filter.

### Change the URL

1. In **Destinations**, tap the webhook destination.
2. Tap **URL**.

   Result: WalletFeed shows **Webhook URL** with the URL that the destination uses.
3. Delete the URL in the field.
4. Paste the new URL.

   If the URL does not start with `https://`, you cannot tap **Save**.
5. Tap **Save**.

   Result: WalletFeed starts a sync with the new URL.

The **URL** row shows only the server name from the URL. WalletFeed does not send the previous transactions to the new URL. You can send them with **Send History**.

### Change the Authorization value

1. In **Destinations**, tap the webhook destination.
2. Tap **Authorization**.
3. Delete the value in the field.
4. Type or paste the new value.
5. Tap **Save**.

If the field is empty when you tap **Save**, the destination has no value, and **Authorization** shows **None**.

You can get the secret again with **Share Signing Secret** in the destination. The destination always uses the same secret.

### Stop or delete the destination

To stop the destination for a period, set **Enabled** to off in the destination.

To delete the destination, do these steps:

1. In **Destinations**, tap the webhook destination.
2. Tap **Delete**.
3. Tap **Delete** again.

The transactions that WalletFeed sent stay on your server or in n8n.

If you do not use the n8n workflow again, do these steps in n8n:

1. Open the menu adjacent to **Publish**.
2. Select **Unpublish**.

## If there is a problem

### If you cannot tap Send Test or Add

**Send Test** and **Add** operate only with a full URL that starts with `https://`. For **Add**, a name is also necessary.

1. Make sure that the URL starts with `https://` and has a server name after it.
2. Make sure that **Name** is not empty.

### If WalletFeed shows "Rejected (HTTP 404)"

The server has no webhook at the URL. For example, the URL is the n8n **Test URL**, you did not publish the workflow, or **HTTP Method** is not **POST**. On the Webhook screen, **Send Test** shows "The server returned an error (HTTP 404)." for this problem.

1. In the n8n Webhook node, make sure that **HTTP Method** is **POST**.
2. Make sure that you published the workflow after your last change.
3. In the Webhook node, select **Production URL**.
4. Copy the URL again.
5. In WalletFeed, do the steps in [Change the URL](#change-the-url).
6. In the destination, tap **Send Test**.
7. If WalletFeed shows "Rejected (HTTP 404). Check the destination, then try again." below **Sending History**, tap **Try Again**.

If the HTTP code is not 404, the server did not accept the request because of a different problem. To find the problem, examine the log of your server, or the **Executions** tab in n8n.

### If the destination shows "Authentication failed"

The server did not accept the **Authorization** value (HTTP 401 or 403). In n8n, this problem occurs if the value is not the same as **Value** in the Header auth credential.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.

   ![The n8n destination in WalletFeed, which shows Authentication failed below Last Sync and None for Authorization.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-webhook/walletfeed-destination-failure.webp)

2. Tap **Authorization**.
3. Delete the value in the field.
4. Type the full header value from **Value** in n8n.
5. Tap **Save**.
6. If WalletFeed shows "Authentication failed. Check the connection." below **Sending History**, tap **Try Again**.

### If the destination shows "Can't connect"

Your iPhone cannot connect to the URL, or the server did not send a status code in 30 seconds. For example, the server is off, or the URL operates only on your home network.

1. Make sure that your server or n8n is on.
2. On your iPhone, set Wi-Fi to off.
3. In the destination, tap **Send Test**.

   If WalletFeed shows an error, the URL operates only on your home network. You must use a URL that operates from the internet.
4. Set Wi-Fi to on again.
5. In n8n, make sure that **Respond** is **Immediately**.

WalletFeed sends the changes again at the next sync.

### If the destination shows "Server error"

The server sent a status code of 500 or more. The destination shows the code, for example "Server error (500)". WalletFeed sends the same changes again at the next sync.

1. Examine the log of your server, or the **Executions** tab of the workflow in n8n.
2. Correct the error.
3. In the destination, tap **Send Test**.

### If the server receives a transaction two times

WalletFeed sends a transaction again when it changes, for example when a pending charge posts. It also sends a request again if it did not get a status code from 200 to 299.

1. Find the item that has the same `id` as the transaction.
2. Change that item. Do not add a new item.
3. To find a request that the server received two times, compare the `webhook-id` headers.

### If the webhook does not receive new transactions

WalletFeed does not send to the URL. For example, the destination is off, or **Background Sync** is off.

1. Open WalletFeed. While WalletFeed is open, it sends changes in seconds.
2. If **Destinations** shows **Sync Requires Pro**, tap **Upgrade**.
3. If the destination shows **Off**, set **Enabled** to on in the destination.
4. If **Filter** is on, make sure that the filter includes the transaction.
5. In n8n, make sure that you published the workflow.
6. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of **Destinations**.
7. Make sure that **Background Sync** is on.
8. Tap **Sync Now**.

After your iPhone starts again, WalletFeed cannot send to destinations until you type your passcode one time.

To make sure that the connection operates, tap **Send Test** in the destination. If the server accepts the test transaction, WalletFeed shows a green check mark.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-ynab/ -->
# Get Apple Card transactions into YNAB

The YNAB app for iPhone can import your Apple Card transactions into YNAB through a connection to Wallet. WalletFeed can also save your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions as OFX or CSV files, and YNAB can import these files on a computer.

## Import with the YNAB app

The YNAB Help Center gives these steps for an iPhone with iOS 17.4 or a newer version and an updated YNAB app:

1. On your iPhone, open YNAB.
2. In the **Accounts** tab, tap **Add Account**.
3. In **Popular Options**, tap the Apple icon.
4. Do the steps that YNAB shows to connect to Wallet.
5. Select the Wallet accounts that YNAB will import.

The YNAB Help Center says that the connection operates only with the iPhone that you used to add it. On that iPhone, **Background App Refresh** must stay on in **Settings** › **Apps** › **YNAB**. For all the steps and the error messages, refer to the [YNAB Help Center page for Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings](https://support.ynab.com/en_us/apple-connections-rkShEfrUh).

## Before you start

To import WalletFeed files into YNAB, you must have:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version, and WalletFeed. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- For files that WalletFeed updates, [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/). It is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase. **Export CSV** is free.
- YNAB in a web browser on a computer, or YNAB in Safari on an iPad. YNAB does not import files on an iPhone.
- iCloud Drive on your iPhone and on your computer. You can also use a different app that Files shows, for example Dropbox.

## Step 1: Add an OFX File destination in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+**.

   ![The Destinations screen has no destinations and shows the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-ynab/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In the search field, type `OFX`.
5. Tap **OFX File**.

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed shows the **WalletFeed Pro** screen first. After you start the free trial or get a plan, the **Files** screen opens.

6. Make sure that **Format** is **OFX**.

   ![The Files screen shows OFX in Format and WalletFeed in Name.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-ynab/walletfeed-setup-ofx-file.webp)

7. Tap **Folder**, then select a folder in iCloud Drive.

   **Add** is available after you select a folder.

8. Optional: In **Name**, type a different name for the files.

   WalletFeed makes one file for each month. With the name `WalletFeed`, the file for October 2026 is `WalletFeed 2026-10.ofx`.

9. Tap **Add**.

   The message **Save Transactions to Files?** opens. It tells you that the folder receives the date, the merchant, the amount and other data of posted transactions. It also gives the accounts and the start date.

10. Tap **Save**.

    WalletFeed writes your posted transactions to the files.

> **Note:** WalletFeed keeps no copy of the files. The files are in your iCloud Drive. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers.

## Step 2: Keep only Apple Card in the files

YNAB puts all the transactions in a file into one account. If WalletFeed reads only your Apple Card, go to step 3.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination, for example **WalletFeed**.
2. Set **Filter** to on.
3. Tap **Accounts**, then select your Apple Card account.
4. Go back to the destination.
5. Tap **Send History**.
6. Tap **All**.

   WalletFeed writes the file for each month again, with only your Apple Card transactions.

To import Apple Cash into a different YNAB account, add a second OFX File destination. In **Name**, type a different name, for example `Apple Cash`. Then set its filter to your Apple Cash account.

## Step 3: Import a file in YNAB

1. On your computer, open YNAB in a web browser.
2. Open the folder in iCloud Drive that has the files from WalletFeed.
3. Drag the file for a month, for example `WalletFeed 2026-10.ofx`, into YNAB.

   YNAB shows **Import Transactions**. You can drag more than one OFX file at the same time.

4. At the top, make sure that YNAB shows your Apple Card account.
5. Optional: Select **Import Memos**.

   The memo has the description from Wallet, the text from your card statement and the foreign amount.

6. Import the transactions.

If you import a file again, YNAB does not import the transactions that have the same date and amount as imported transactions.

> **Note:** On an iPad, you can drag the file from Files into YNAB in Safari. For the steps, refer to the [YNAB Help Center page for file import](https://support.ynab.com/en_us/file-based-import-a-guide-Bkj4Sszyo).

YNAB does not keep the file, but it keeps the transactions that you import. The terms of YNAB are applicable to these transactions.

## Use a CSV file

YNAB also imports CSV files. The OFX file has only posted transactions. A CSV file from WalletFeed has all transactions, with `pending` in the Status column for a pending transaction.

WalletFeed Pro is not necessary for **Export CSV**. To make a CSV file one time:

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. At the top of the screen, tap **Settings**.
3. In **Data**, tap **Export CSV**.

   ![The Settings screen shows Export CSV in the Data section.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-ynab/walletfeed-settings-3.webp)

4. Tap **Range**, then select a range, for example **Last Month**.

   ![The Export CSV screen shows the range This Month and 29 transactions.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-ynab/walletfeed-export-csv.webp)

5. Tap **Export**.
6. Tap **Save to Files**, then save the file in iCloud Drive.

The file has the transactions of all the Wallet accounts that WalletFeed reads. YNAB puts all of them in the account that you select. With WalletFeed Pro, a CSV File destination updates a file when your transactions change. It can have a filter for one account. For the steps, refer to the [guide for a CSV file](/guides/apple-card-to-csv/).

In YNAB, use these columns of the CSV file:

| YNAB field | Column in the CSV file |
| --- | --- |
| **Date** | Date |
| **Payee** | Merchant |
| **Memo** | Description |
| **Outflow** | Amount |
| **Inflow** | Amount |

To import the CSV file in YNAB:

1. On your computer, open YNAB in a web browser.
2. Drag the CSV file into YNAB.
3. At the top of **Import Transactions**, make sure that YNAB shows your Apple Card account.
4. Make sure that each YNAB field uses the column in the table.

   The CSV file has one Amount column. A purchase is a negative amount. The YNAB Help Center tells you to select **Amount** for **Outflow** and for **Inflow**.

5. Import the transactions.

## The data that YNAB receives

The OFX file has this information for each posted transaction:

| Wallet data | In the OFX file | In YNAB |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Merchant | The name of the merchant, with a maximum of 32 characters | **Payee** |
| Amount | A purchase is negative. A payment or a refund is more than zero. | **Outflow** or **Inflow** |
| Date and Posted Date | The date of the transaction and the date that it posted | **Date** |
| Description, Original Description and Foreign Amount | The memo of the transaction | **Memo**, if you select **Import Memos** |
| Account | One statement for each Wallet account | The YNAB account that you select |

The OFX file has no category. YNAB says that it changes the payee names from a file. It also gives each transaction the category that its payee usually has. You can change the payee and the category of each transaction in YNAB.

## Changes to the files

While WalletFeed is open, its files in iCloud Drive receive changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. For this, [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) must be on in **Settings** › **Sync**.

If WalletFeed cannot open the folder at that time, the files get the changes when one of these occurs:

- You open WalletFeed.
- A Shortcuts automation starts WalletFeed.
- iOS starts WalletFeed while your iPhone charges.

WalletFeed writes the file for a month again each time that a transaction in that month changes. YNAB gets the changes only when you import the file again.

- A pending transaction is not in the file. When it posts, WalletFeed adds it to the file for its month.
- A refund is a new transaction with an amount that is more than zero.
- If Wallet removes a transaction, WalletFeed removes it from the file. If you imported it before, delete it in YNAB.

## Send previous transactions

A new OFX File destination also receives previous posted transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it.

The YNAB Help Center tells you not to import transactions that are more than 1 year old. If a file has transactions from before the start date of your YNAB account, YNAB lets you include them or not.

To write the previous transactions to the files again:

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**, then tap the destination, for example **WalletFeed**.
3. Tap **Send History**.
4. Select **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

WalletFeed writes the file for each month in that period again. For more information, refer to [Send History](/docs/send-history/).

## Change or remove the destination

To change the destination, tap it in [**Destinations**](/docs/destinations/). These are the changes that you can make:

- Set **Filter** to on, and select the accounts, the categories or a minimum amount. For more information, refer to [Choose what to send](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).
- Tap **Change Folder** to use a different folder. WalletFeed writes all your transactions to new files in that folder.
- Set **Enabled** to off to stop the changes to the files for a time.
- Type a different name in **Name**. The names of the files stay the same.

To remove the destination:

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap **Delete**.
3. In the message, tap **Delete** again.

The files stay in iCloud Drive. The transactions that you imported stay in YNAB.

## If there is a problem

### If YNAB puts Apple Cash transactions in your Apple Card account

The file has the transactions of more than one Wallet account.

1. In WalletFeed, set a filter for your Apple Card account, as in step 2.
2. In YNAB, delete the transactions that are not from your Apple Card.

### If YNAB does not import some transactions

YNAB does not import a transaction that it imported before, or that you deleted in YNAB after an import.

1. In **Import Transactions**, look at the transactions above **Options**.

   YNAB shows why it did not import each transaction.

2. If you deleted the transactions in YNAB, type them in YNAB.

### If a pending transaction is not in the file

The OFX file has a transaction only after it posts.

1. After the transaction posts, import the file for its month again.

### If the destination shows "Can't open the folder. Choose it again."

WalletFeed cannot open the folder that you selected.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap **Change Folder**.
3. Select the folder again.

WalletFeed writes your transactions to the files again.

### If the files on your computer do not show new transactions

WalletFeed did not update the files after the last change in Wallet.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. At the top of the screen, tap **Settings**.
3. In **Sync**, tap **Sync Now**.

**Sync Now** shows the time of the last sync.

### If Destinations shows "Sync Requires Pro"

You do not have WalletFeed Pro at this time. WalletFeed keeps the destination, but it does not update the files.

1. In **Destinations**, tap **Upgrade**.
2. Start the free trial, or get a plan.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to Zapier

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to Zapier. Your Zap starts one time each month, or one time for each transaction. In Zapier, you make a Zap with the **Webhooks by Zapier** trigger **Catch Hook**. Then you paste the webhook URL of the trigger into WalletFeed.

## Before you start

You must have:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- WalletFeed, with access to your Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account.
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase. WalletFeed Pro is necessary for all destinations.
- A Zapier account on a plan that includes **Webhooks by Zapier**: Professional, Team or Enterprise. The Zapier Free plan does not include it.
- A computer, for the steps on the Zapier website.

> **Note:** A new Zapier account starts with a 14-day Professional trial, and Zapier does not ask for a payment card. During the trial, you can use **Webhooks by Zapier**. After the trial, the account changes to the Free plan, and the Zap cannot use **Webhooks by Zapier**.

## Step 1: Make a Zap with a Catch Hook trigger

The Catch Hook trigger has its own webhook URL. When WalletFeed sends data to this URL, the Zap starts.

1. On your computer, open [Zapier](https://zapier.com/app/home).
2. Sign in to your Zapier account. If you do not have an account, make one on [Zapier's sign-up page](https://zapier.com/sign-up).
3. Click **+** at the top of the left sidebar.

   ![The Zapier home page, with the + button at the top of the left sidebar highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/zapier-home-create.webp)

4. Click **Zaps**.

   ![The Create menu in Zapier, with Zaps highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/zapier-create-zaps.webp)

5. Click the **Trigger** box.

   ![A new Zap in the Zapier editor, with the empty Trigger step highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/zapier-zap-editor-trigger.webp)

6. In the search box, type `Webhooks`.
7. Click **Webhooks**. After you select it, Zapier shows its full name, **Webhooks by Zapier**.

   ![The Zapier app picker with Webhooks in the search box and the Webhooks result highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/zapier-search-webhooks.webp)

8. Under **Trigger event**, click **Choose an event**.

   ![The Setup tab of the trigger, with the empty Trigger event field highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/zapier-trigger-event.webp)

9. Click **Catch Hook**, not **Catch Raw Hook**.

   ![The list of Webhooks by Zapier trigger events, with Catch Hook highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/zapier-catch-hook.webp)

10. Click **Continue**.

    ![The Setup tab with Catch Hook in the Trigger event field and the Continue button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/zapier-setup-continue.webp)

    Zapier can also show a box about API by Zapier. WalletFeed does not use it.

11. On the **Configure** tab, make sure that **Pick off a Child Key** is empty. If this field has text, Zapier keeps only a part of each transaction.
12. Click **Continue**.

    ![The Configure tab with the Pick off a Child Key field empty and the Continue button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/zapier-configure-continue.webp)

13. On the **Test** tab, under **Your webhook URL**, click **Copy**.

    ![The Test tab with the webhook URL and the Copy button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/zapier-copy-webhook-url.webp)

    The field shows only the start of the URL, but **Copy** copies the full URL.

14. Keep this page open. You use it again in Step 3.

> **Note:** The URL stays on the **Test** tab of the trigger. You can open the Zap at a later time and copy the URL again, for example on your iPhone.

## Step 2: Add Zapier in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Optional: If you select **Each Transaction** in step 8, you can set **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History** to **Today**.

   Then Zapier receives only the transactions from today.

   ![WalletFeed Settings with the Sync section and Initial History set to All.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/walletfeed-settings.webp)

3. Tap **Destinations**.
4. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen in WalletFeed with the + button and no destinations.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

5. Under **Automations**, tap **Zapier**. You can also type `Zapier` in the search field.
6. If WalletFeed shows the **WalletFeed Pro** screen, get WalletFeed Pro there. The **Zapier** screen then opens.
7. Paste the URL into **Catch Hook URL**. WalletFeed keeps the URL in the Keychain on your iPhone, because a person with the URL can start your Zap.

   ![The Zapier screen in WalletFeed with the Catch Hook URL field, three steps and the Zapier Help link.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/walletfeed-setup-zapier.webp)

8. In **Send**, select **Monthly** or **Each Transaction**.

   With **Monthly**, Zapier receives one request 5 days after the end of each month. The request contains all the transactions of that month, and the Zap starts one time. **Monthly** is the default.

   With **Each Transaction**, the Zap starts one time for each new or changed transaction.

9. Tap **Add**. WalletFeed sends a sample to Zapier.

   With **Each Transaction**, the sample is one transaction. With **Monthly**, the sample is one month that contains the same transaction.

10. Read the message **Send Transactions to Zapier?** It tells you the data that Zapier receives, from which accounts and from which date.
11. Tap **Send**. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed does not add the destination.

**Destinations** then shows the new Zapier destination.

## Step 3: Find the sample in Zapier

1. On your computer, in the Zap editor, click **Test trigger**.

   ![The Test tab with the Test trigger button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/zapier-test-trigger.webp)

2. Click **request A**.

   ![The Test tab after a successful test, with the record request A highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/zapier-request-found.webp)

   Zapier shows the fields of the sample. With **Each Transaction**, **Merchant** is WalletFeed and **Amount** is -4.2. With **Monthly**, Zapier shows the fields of the month, and the transaction as a line item.

3. Click **Continue with selected record**. Zapier then shows the apps for the **Action** step.

## Step 4: Add the Action step in Zapier

The **Action** step tells Zapier what to do with the data, for example add a row to a Google Sheets spreadsheet.

1. Select the app that receives the data, for example **Google Sheets**.

   ![The Zapier app picker for the Action step, with apps such as Google Sheets, Gmail and Notion.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/zapier-choose-action-app.webp)

2. Do the steps that Zapier shows for this app.
3. Where the action must have a value from the transaction, use the fields from Step 3, such as **Merchant** and **Amount**.

   With **Monthly**, Zapier shows the transactions of the month as line items. Use an action that accepts line items, for example Create Multiple Spreadsheet Rows in Google Sheets. You can also use Looping by Zapier.
4. Click **Publish**. A Zap that is a draft does not do its action.
5. In **Automations** › **Zaps**, find your Zap. If its **Status** switch is off, set it to on.

   ![The Zaps list in Zapier, with a Zap named WalletFeed and its Status switch set to off.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/zapier-zap-list-off.webp)

Zapier counts one task for each action step that runs, and the trigger uses no task. With **Monthly**, the Zap runs one time each month. With **Each Transaction**, it runs one time for each change.

## Data that Zapier receives

Your transactions go from your iPhone directly to Zapier. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. After Zapier receives your transactions, Zapier's terms are applicable to them.

With **Monthly**, WalletFeed sends one request for each month. The request has these fields:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `event` | `month` |
| `month` | The month in your time zone, for example `2026-10` |
| `count` | The number of transactions in `transactions` |
| `total` | All the amounts of the month, added together, for example -16.95 |
| `currency` | The currency code of `total`, for example USD |
| `transactions` | The transactions of the month, newest first. Each transaction has the fields in the next table, but not **Event**. |

If the month has more than one currency, `total` and `currency` have no value.

With **Each Transaction**, the Zap starts one time for each change to a transaction. Zapier shows the data of each change as these fields:

| Field in Zapier | Value from Wallet |
| --- | --- |
| **Event** | `created` the first time that WalletFeed sends the transaction, `updated` for a later change, and `deleted` when Wallet removes it |
| **ID** | The transaction ID from Wallet. It stays the same when the transaction changes. |
| **Date** | The date of the purchase in your time zone, for example 2026-10-29 |
| **Merchant** | The merchant name, or the description if Wallet has no merchant name |
| **Amount** | Negative for a purchase, for example -84.12, and positive for a refund or a payment, for example 49 |
| **Currency** | The currency code, for example USD |
| **Category** | The WalletFeed category, for example Groceries |
| **Status** | The Wallet status: `pending`, `authorized` or `booked` |
| **Pending** | `true` while the purchase is pending or authorized, and `false` after it posts |
| **Account** | The Wallet account, for example Apple Card |
| **Description** | The description from Wallet |
| **Type** | The type of transaction, for example `pointOfSale` or `refund` |
| **Mcc** | The merchant category code, for example 5411 |
| **Foreign Amount** and **Foreign Currency** | The amount and the currency code of a purchase in a different currency |
| **querystring** | A field that Zapier adds. It is always empty. |

![A Whole Foods Market transaction from WalletFeed in the Zapier test results, with each field on its own line.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/zapier-result-transaction-fields.webp)

For a deleted transaction, the request has only **Event** and **ID**. A field is empty when Wallet does not give a value for it, for example **Foreign Amount** for a purchase in dollars. In Zapier, an amount has no zeros at the end, for example 49 for $49.00.

## Sync times and changes

To send to Zapier while WalletFeed is closed, [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) must be on in **Settings** › **Sync**. **Background Sync** is on until you set it to off.

### Monthly

WalletFeed sends each month at the first sync on or after the 6th day of the next month. For example, Zapier receives October on or after November 6. If the filter keeps no transactions of a month, Zapier receives nothing for that month.

If a charge is pending when WalletFeed sends the month, its `pending` value is `true`. WalletFeed does not send the charge again after it posts. After WalletFeed sends a month, it does not send changes to that month.

If a sync stops after WalletFeed sends a month, Zapier can receive the same month two times. A Zap can use Storage by Zapier, or a step that finds a row, to find a `month` value that it received before.

### Each Transaction

While WalletFeed is open, Zapier receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet.

One transaction can start the Zap more than one time:

- A new purchase comes with **Event** `created` and **Status** `pending`.
- When the purchase posts, the same **ID** comes again with **Event** `updated` and **Status** `booked`.
- If the bank declines a pending charge, or Wallet removes a transaction, Zapier receives **Event** `deleted` and the **ID**.

A refund is a different transaction, with a positive **Amount** and the **Type** `refund`.

If WalletFeed stops during a sync, it sends the same changes again at the next sync. Zapier does not look for duplicates. Thus, a Zap that adds a row for each change can add a transaction two times. A Zap that first finds the row by **ID**, and then updates it, keeps one row for each transaction. This Zap uses two tasks for each change.

## Send previous transactions

A new Zapier destination also receives previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it.

With **Each Transaction**, Zapier receives a maximum of 30 days of previous transactions. With **Monthly**, there is no limit of 30 days. The start date moves back to the first day of its month, and Zapier receives one request for each previous month. WalletFeed sends the newest month first.

To send more transactions, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Zapier destination.
2. Tap **Send History**.
3. Select a period: **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.
4. In the message **Send History to Zapier?**, tap **Send**.

   With **Monthly**, the message shows "Each month runs your Zap once." With **Each Transaction**, it shows "Each transaction runs your Zap."

WalletFeed sends the newest transactions first. With **Monthly**, the period starts on the first day of its month, and **Send History** also sends the months that Zapier received before. Each Zap run uses tasks in Zapier. To stop, tap **Send History**, then tap **Stop Sending**.

## Change or delete the destination

### Send only some transactions

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Zapier destination.
2. Set the **Filter** switch to on.

   ![A destination screen in WalletFeed, here for Lunch Money, with the Filter switch set to off.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/walletfeed-destination-detail.webp)

3. Change **Include**, **Minimum**, **Include Pending**, **Accounts** or **Categories** as necessary.

With **Each Transaction** and no filter, you can also tap **Turn On Filter** below **Send**. To stop for a time, set the **Enabled** switch to off.

### Change Send

1. In WalletFeed, open the Zapier destination.
2. In **Send**, select **Monthly** or **Each Transaction**.

   With **Monthly**, Zapier receives the month of the change 5 days after the end of that month. The request contains all the transactions of the month. These include the transactions that Zapier received before. With **Each Transaction**, Zapier receives the changes from that time. To send previous transactions, use **Send History**.

3. Tap **Send Test**.
4. On your computer, open the Zap in Zapier.
5. On the **Test** tab of the trigger, click **Test trigger**.
6. Make sure that the Action step uses the fields of your new selection in **Send**.

### Replace the URL

If you make a new Zap, give its URL to WalletFeed:

1. In Zapier, copy the webhook URL of the new Zap, as in Step 1.
2. In WalletFeed, open the Zapier destination.
3. Tap **Replace URL**.
4. Paste the new URL into **Catch Hook URL**.
5. Tap **Replace**. WalletFeed sends a sample transaction to the new URL before it keeps the URL.

The destination screen shows **Webhook** with `hooks.zapier.com`, not the full URL.

### Delete the destination

1. In WalletFeed, open the Zapier destination.
2. Tap **Delete**, then tap **Delete** again in the message.

The transactions that WalletFeed sent stay in Zapier, and in the apps that your Zap sent them to.

Zapier accepts requests at the URL until you set the Zap to off or delete it. To delete the Zap, open it in Zapier, then select **Delete** in the menu of the Zap name.

## If something goes wrong

### If you cannot tap Add

The text in **Catch Hook URL** is not a Zapier webhook URL. The URL must start with `https://hooks.zapier.com/hooks/`.

1. In Zapier, open the **Test** tab of the Catch Hook trigger.
2. Click **Copy**.
3. In WalletFeed, delete the text in **Catch Hook URL**.
4. Paste the URL again.

### If WalletFeed shows "The webhook refused the test"

Zapier did not accept the sample transaction, because the URL is not correct or Zapier stopped the URL.

1. In Zapier, open **Automations** › **Zaps**.
2. If you deleted the Zap, make a new Zap, as in Step 1.
3. Copy the URL again from the **Test** tab of the trigger.
4. In WalletFeed, paste the URL into **Catch Hook URL**, then tap **Add**.

### If the destination shows "Rejected (HTTP 404)"

Zapier did not accept the transactions, because the Zap is off or someone deleted it. Zapier can stop the URL up to several hours after the Zap goes off.

1. In Zapier, open **Automations** › **Zaps**.
2. If your Zap is in the list, set its **Status** switch to on.
3. If your Zap is not in the list, make a new Zap, as in Step 1.
4. Give the URL of the new Zap to WalletFeed, as in [Replace the URL](#replace-the-url).

### If Zapier finds no request

You clicked **Test trigger** before WalletFeed sent the sample transaction.

1. In WalletFeed, open the Zapier destination.
2. Tap **Send Test**. WalletFeed sends the sample transaction again.
3. In Zapier, click **Find new records**.

Zapier loads a maximum of 3 records at a time, and not always the newest ones. This is not a problem. When the Zap is on, it starts for each month or for each change.

### If the Zap does not do its action

The Zap is a draft, or it is off. A draft Zap receives the requests but does not do its action, and WalletFeed shows no error.

1. In the Zap editor, click **Publish**.
2. In **Automations** › **Zaps**, set the **Status** switch of the Zap to on.

### If the Zap stops after the Zapier trial

After the 14-day trial, the Zapier account is on the Free plan. The Free plan does not include **Webhooks by Zapier**.

1. In Zapier, click **Upgrade**.
2. Select a plan that includes webhooks, for example Professional.

### If the Zap starts only one time each month

**Send** is **Monthly**, which is the default. With **Monthly**, Zapier receives each month 5 days after the end of the month.

To start the Zap for each transaction, do these steps:

1. In WalletFeed, open the Zapier destination.
2. In **Send**, select **Each Transaction**.
3. Tap **Send Test**.
4. On your computer, open the Zap in Zapier.
5. On the **Test** tab of the trigger, click **Test trigger**.
6. Change the Action step to use the fields of one transaction.

### If one transaction makes two rows

With **Each Transaction**, the Zap starts for each change to a transaction, and WalletFeed can send the same change again.

1. In the Zap, add a step that finds the row by **ID**, before the step that adds a row.
2. If the step finds a row, update that row.

### If Zapier receives transactions only while WalletFeed is open

**Background Sync** is off.

1. In WalletFeed, open **Settings** › **Sync**.
2. Set the **Background Sync** switch to on.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/export-apple-card-transactions/ -->
# Export Apple Card transactions

You can export your Apple Card transactions as a file from Wallet on your iPhone, from card.apple.com or from WalletFeed. With WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed also updates a file or a service when your transactions change.

## Before you start

- Your Apple Card in Wallet on your iPhone.
- For card.apple.com, a computer with a web browser.
- For WalletFeed, an iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US. You must [share your Apple Card with WalletFeed](/docs/wallet-accounts/).
- For a file or a service that WalletFeed updates, [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/). It is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase. WalletFeed Pro is not necessary for **Export CSV**.

## Export a statement in Wallet

Wallet has a statement for each previous month. You can export the transactions of a statement as a CSV, OFX, QFX or QBO file.

1. On your iPhone, open Wallet.
2. Tap your Apple Card.
3. Tap **Card Balance**.
4. Scroll down to **Statements**.
5. Tap a statement.
6. Tap **Export Transactions**.
7. Select a file format.

   For a spreadsheet, for example Numbers or Excel, select CSV.

8. To keep the file on your iPhone, tap **Save to Files**.

   You can also send the file with Mail or AirDrop.

9. Select a folder.
10. Tap **Save**.

To download a statement as a PDF file:

1. In Wallet, open a statement.
2. Tap **Download PDF Statement**.
3. When the PDF file opens, tap the share button.

   You can then save, print or send the file.

## Export transactions between two dates in Wallet

Wallet can also export the transactions between two dates that you select.

1. On your iPhone, open Wallet.
2. Tap your Apple Card.
3. Tap **Card Balance**.
4. Below **Statements**, tap **Export Transactions**.
5. Select a start date.
6. Select an end date.
7. Select a file format.
8. Tap the done button.

## Export transactions at card.apple.com

1. On your computer, open [card.apple.com](https://card.apple.com).
2. Sign in with your Apple Account.
3. Click **Statements**.
4. Click **Export Transactions**.
5. Select a start date.
6. Select an end date.
7. Select a file format.
8. Click **Export**.

To download a statement as a PDF file:

1. Click **Statements**.
2. Click the download button for a statement.

Apple gives the steps for Wallet and card.apple.com in [Download your Apple Card statements or export your transactions](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102284).

## Export a CSV file with WalletFeed

[Export CSV](/docs/export-csv/) in WalletFeed makes one CSV file with your transactions from a period that you select. You can use it without WalletFeed Pro. The file includes pending transactions, and it does not change after you export it.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In the **Data** section, tap **Export CSV**.

   ![The Settings screen with Export CSV in the Data section.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/export-apple-card-transactions/walletfeed-settings-3.webp)

4. Tap **Range**.
5. Select a period: **This Month**, **Last Month**, **Last 90 Days**, **This Year** or **All**.

   ![The Export CSV screen with Range set to This Month, 29 transactions and the Export button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/export-apple-card-transactions/walletfeed-export-csv.webp)

   **Transactions** shows the number of transactions in the period.

6. Tap **Export**.
7. In the share sheet, tap **Save to Files**.
8. Select a folder.
9. Tap **Save**.

The name of the file includes the period, for example `Apple Card Last Month.csv`. The file has the transactions from all the Wallet accounts that you share with WalletFeed. The **Account** column shows the account of each transaction. WalletFeed makes the file on your iPhone and does not keep it.

## Columns in the CSV file

Each CSV file from WalletFeed has one row for each transaction and these columns:

| Column | Data |
| --- | --- |
| **Date** | The date of the transaction, for example 2026-10-28. |
| **Posted Date** | The date that the charge posted. It is empty while the charge is pending. |
| **Merchant** | The merchant name, or the description if Wallet has no merchant name. |
| **Description** | The description of the transaction in Wallet. |
| **Original Description** | The description of the transaction with no changes. |
| **Amount** | The value of the transaction, for example -23.40. Purchases and fees have a minus sign. Payments and refunds have no minus sign. |
| **Currency** | The currency code, for example USD. |
| **Direction** | `debit` for purchases and fees, or `credit` for refunds, payments and deposits. |
| **Status** | The status in Wallet, for example `pending` or `authorized` before the charge posts, `booked` after it posts, or `rejected` for a declined charge. |
| **Type** | The type of transaction in Wallet, for example `pointOfSale` for a purchase, `refund`, `transfer` or `fee`. |
| **Category** | The WalletFeed category, for example Groceries, Dining or Cash & Transfers. |
| **MCC** | The merchant category code (ISO 18245), for example 5411 for a grocery store. It is empty if Wallet has no code. |
| **Account** | The Wallet account, for example Apple Card. |
| **Foreign Amount** | For a purchase in a different currency, the value in that currency. |
| **Foreign Currency** | The code of that different currency. |
| **WalletFeed ID** | The ID of the transaction. You can use it to find the same transaction in a different file. |

## Update a file or a service with WalletFeed Pro

With WalletFeed Pro, it is not necessary to export again. WalletFeed sends your transactions from your iPhone to a [destination](/docs/destinations/), and updates the destination when your transactions change. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. Your transactions go from your iPhone directly to the folder or the service that you select.

A destination can be one of these:

- A [CSV file](/guides/apple-card-to-csv/) in a folder, for example in iCloud Drive. WalletFeed writes one file or one file for each month. You can open a CSV file in [Excel](/guides/apple-card-to-excel/) or [Numbers](/guides/apple-card-to-numbers/).
- An [OFX file](/guides/apple-card-to-ofx/) or a [QIF file](/guides/apple-card-to-qif/) for each month. You can import these files into an app that reads OFX or QIF. These files include a charge only after the charge posts.
- A spreadsheet in [Google Sheets](/guides/apple-card-to-google-sheets/).
- A budget app, for example [Lunch Money](/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/) or [PocketSmith](/guides/apple-card-to-pocketsmith/).

> **Note:** WalletFeed writes CSV, OFX and QIF files. It does not write QFX or QBO files. Quicken for Windows cannot import the OFX files from WalletFeed, but it can import the CSV files.

To add a CSV file that WalletFeed updates:

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with no destinations and the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/export-apple-card-transactions/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In the search field, type `CSV`.
5. Tap **CSV File**.

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, the **WalletFeed Pro** screen opens. After you get WalletFeed Pro, the **Files** screen opens.

   ![The Files screen with Format set to CSV, Save As set to One File and the name WalletFeed Transactions.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/export-apple-card-transactions/walletfeed-setup-csv-file.webp)

6. Tap **Folder**.
7. Select a folder in iCloud Drive.
8. Tap **Add**.
9. When WalletFeed shows **Save Transactions to Files?**, tap **Save**.

   The message tells you the data that the folder will receive. It also gives the accounts and the period of the transactions. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes the new destination.

WalletFeed then writes your transactions to `WalletFeed Transactions.csv` in the folder.

## Changes to the file

While WalletFeed is open, the file receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**, WalletFeed then updates the file. If WalletFeed cannot open the folder at that time, the file changes when you open WalletFeed, when an automation starts, or while your iPhone charges.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives your previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. To send a different period after you add the destination, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/) on the screen of the destination. You can select **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

## Delete a destination

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Delete**.
4. Tap **Delete** again.

The file and the transactions in it stay in the folder. A service keeps the transactions that it received. The terms of that service are applicable to these transactions.

## If there is a problem

### If this month has no statement in Wallet

Wallet makes a statement only after the end of the month. To export the transactions of this month, use **Export CSV** in WalletFeed.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In the **Data** section, tap **Export CSV**.
4. Set **Range** to **This Month**.
5. Tap **Export**.
6. In the share sheet, tap **Save to Files**.
7. Select a folder.
8. Tap **Save**.

### If you cannot tap Export in WalletFeed

**Export** is not available while WalletFeed reads your transactions, or when the period has no transactions.

1. Make sure that **Transactions** shows a number.
2. If the number is 0, select a different period in **Range**.

### If there is an apostrophe before a name or a description

If the text in a column has `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` as the first character, WalletFeed puts an apostrophe (`'`) before the text. Thus, a spreadsheet does not use the text as a formula.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/find-apple-card-subscriptions/ -->
# Find subscriptions on your Apple Card

WalletFeed finds the subscriptions and other [recurring charges](/docs/recurring-charges/) on your Apple Card and shows them on its [Spending](/docs/spending/) screen. It can also monitor these charges and send you a notification when a charge becomes a recurring charge or its price changes.

## Before you start

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- WalletFeed, with [access to your Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/). These accounts are Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings.
- Charges from two or more months in Wallet. WalletFeed shows a charge that occurs each month only after its second charge.
- For short names and for [Ask Spending](/docs/ask-spending/), an iPhone that can use Apple Intelligence, with Apple Intelligence on.

[WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/) is not necessary for Recurring Charges or for Recurring Charge Alerts.

## Step 1: Open Recurring Charges

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Spending**.
3. Scroll down to **Recurring Charges**.

   ![The Recurring Charges section on the Spending screen, with PG&E, Netflix and Spotify.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/find-apple-card-subscriptions/walletfeed-recurring.webp)

Each row shows a name, the price of the last charge, and **Monthly** or **Weekly**. With Apple Intelligence, the row also shows the type of service, for example **Streaming · Monthly**.

The list starts with the charge that has the largest total for one month. If WalletFeed finds no recurring charges, the **Recurring Charges** section does not show. For more information, refer to [Recurring Charges](/docs/recurring-charges/).

## Step 2: See the total for one month

Ask Spending calculates the total of your recurring charges for one month. For this step, Apple Intelligence must be on. Without it, the **Spending** screen does not show **Ask about your spending**. To set Apple Intelligence to on, refer to [Ask Spending](/docs/ask-spending/#if-spending-does-not-show-ask-about-your-spending).

1. On the **Spending** screen, tap **Ask about your spending**.

   ![The Spending screen with the Ask about your spending field at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/find-apple-card-subscriptions/walletfeed-spending.webp)

2. Type `Subscriptions I pay for`.
3. Tap **Go** on the keyboard.

   Ask Spending shows the number of recurring charges and their total for one month. Below the chart, **Recurring Charges** shows the price of each charge for one month.

4. To see the full **Spending** screen again, tap **Clear** (the x button) in the field.

To get the price for one month of a charge that occurs each week, WalletFeed multiplies the price by approximately 4.3. The total also includes charges that are not subscriptions, for example a charge for electricity each month.

If you also type a period of time, for example `last month`, Ask Spending shows the total of these charges in that period.

## Step 3: Get a notification when a charge starts or changes

1. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Notifications** section, set the **Recurring Charge Alerts** switch to on.

   ![The Settings screen with the Recurring Charge Alerts switch in the Notifications section.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/find-apple-card-subscriptions/walletfeed-settings.webp)

3. If iOS shows a message about notifications, let WalletFeed send them.
4. Tap **Done**.

When a charge becomes a recurring charge, the notification shows, for example, “Netflix repeats monthly” and “$15.49 each month”.

If the price of a recurring charge changes by more than 2%, the notification shows, for example, “Netflix costs more” and “$17.99, up from $15.49”.

WalletFeed sends only one notification for each charge, and only for charges from the last 7 days. It sends no notifications for the charges that were in Wallet before you set the **Recurring Charge Alerts** switch to on.

When you open WalletFeed, it examines your transactions and sends the new notifications. When WalletFeed is closed, iOS starts WalletFeed in approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet.

> **Note:** For these notifications, WalletFeed keeps only the IDs of the transactions that it sent a notification for. It keeps no prices and no merchant names.

## Conditions for a recurring charge

WalletFeed examines your transactions from this month and from the two months before it. It shows the charges from a merchant in **Recurring Charges** when they agree with these conditions:

- All the charges have the same merchant name. For example, “Netflix.com” and “NETFLIX.COM” are the same merchant name.
- The difference between the price of each charge and the price of the last charge is 15% or less.
- For **Monthly**, there are two or more charges, and each charge is 26 to 35 days after the charge before it.
- For **Weekly**, there are three or more charges, and each charge is 6 to 8 days after the charge before it.

These transactions do not show in **Recurring Charges**:

- Apple Card Monthly Installments. They show in **Monthly Installments** on the same screen.
- Refunds, transfers, bill payments and rejected transactions
- Charges that occur each year. WalletFeed finds only charges that occur each month or each week.

Some recurring charges are not subscriptions. **Recurring Charges** also shows these charges.

## Names from Apple Intelligence

With Apple Intelligence, WalletFeed shows a short name and a type of service. For example, for the merchant name “NETFLIX.COM 866-579” from Wallet, WalletFeed shows Netflix and **Streaming**. If the first word of the name from Apple Intelligence is not in the merchant name, WalletFeed does not use that name. WalletFeed gets names only for the first 12 charges in the list. Below the list, WalletFeed also shows **Apple Intelligence suggested these names.**

Apple Intelligence gets only the merchant names. It operates on your iPhone. WalletFeed does not send data to a server for these names.

Without Apple Intelligence, each row shows the merchant name from Wallet, and **Monthly** or **Weekly**.

## Stop the notifications

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Notifications** section, set the **Recurring Charge Alerts** switch to off.
3. Tap **Done**.

A notification shows the name of the charge and its prices. Notification Center keeps the notification until you remove it. When notification previews are off, iOS does not show the text on the Lock Screen.

## If something goes wrong

### If Spending shows “No Cards”

WalletFeed does not have access to your Wallet accounts.

1. Tap **Choose Accounts**.
2. Make sure that the **Apple Card** switch is on.

   ![The Share Wallet Data screen with the Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings switches on.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/find-apple-card-subscriptions/walletfeed-wallet-access.webp)

3. Tap **Share**.

If WalletFeed shows **Wallet Access Off**, refer to [Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/).

### If Spending shows “Couldn't Read Wallet”

WalletFeed did not get your transactions from Wallet.

To try again, pull down on the **Spending** screen.

### If a new subscription is not in Recurring Charges

WalletFeed shows a charge that occurs each month only after its second charge. It shows a charge that occurs each week only after its third charge.

1. Wait for the next charge from the merchant.
2. Open **Spending** again.

### If a subscription with a new price is not in Recurring Charges

If the price changes by more than 15%, WalletFeed does not show the charge. It shows the charge again when all its charges in this month and the two months before it have the new price.

Recurring Charge Alerts can send a notification for this type of change. To get these notifications:

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Notifications** section, set the **Recurring Charge Alerts** switch to on.

### If a subscription with a charge each year is not in Recurring Charges

WalletFeed finds only charges that occur each month or each week.

To find the charges from the merchant:

1. Tap **Search** at the bottom of the screen.
2. Type the name of the merchant.

### If a charge shows the merchant name from Wallet

The cause is one of these:

- Apple Intelligence is off.
- Apple Intelligence gave no name that agrees with the merchant name.
- The charge is not in the first 12 charges of the list.

If Apple Intelligence is off, do these steps:

1. Make sure that your iPhone can use Apple Intelligence.

   Apple gives the list of iPhone models in [How to get Apple Intelligence](https://support.apple.com/en-us/121115).

2. In the Settings app, tap **Apple Intelligence & Siri**.
3. Set **Apple Intelligence** to on.
4. In WalletFeed, open **Spending** again.

### If Recurring Charge Alerts does not stay on

iOS does not let WalletFeed send notifications.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Notifications** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Set **Allow Notifications** to on.
4. Open WalletFeed.
5. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
6. In the **Notifications** section, set the **Recurring Charge Alerts** switch to on.

### If you do not get a notification

WalletFeed sends a notification only for a new recurring charge or a price change of more than 2%. It sends notifications only for charges from the last 7 days.

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. Make sure that the **Recurring Charge Alerts** switch is on.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/ -->
# Guides

Each guide shows how to send Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to one app or file type with WalletFeed.

- [Send Apple Card transactions to Zapier](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/index.md): Send your Apple Card transactions from your iPhone to Zapier with WalletFeed. A Catch Hook trigger starts your Zap each month or for each transaction.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to Make](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-make/index.md): Send your Apple Card transactions from your iPhone to a scenario in Make, previously Integromat. A Custom webhook receives each month or each transaction.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to a webhook](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-webhook/index.md): Send Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a webhook in n8n or on your server with WalletFeed.
- [Run a shortcut after each Apple Card purchase](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-shortcuts/index.md): Make a Shortcuts automation that sends each Apple Card purchase from your iPhone to your WalletFeed destinations in seconds.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to Lunch Money](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/index.md): Send Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to Lunch Money with WalletFeed. You paste a Lunch Money access token into WalletFeed.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to PocketSmith](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-pocketsmith/index.md): Get your Apple Card transactions into PocketSmith from your iPhone, with no file to import. Make a PocketSmith developer key, then paste it in WalletFeed.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to Firefly III](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/index.md): Send Apple Card transactions from your iPhone to Firefly III with WalletFeed. Make a personal access token, then paste it and your server address.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to Sure](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/index.md): Send Apple Card transactions from your iPhone to Sure, the self-hosted budget app that is a fork of Maybe Finance. Make an API key in Sure, then paste it.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to Toshl Finance](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/index.md): Send your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to Toshl Finance. Make a personal token in Toshl, then paste it into WalletFeed.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to BankSync](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/index.md): Send Apple Card transactions from your iPhone to a BankSync table. Then your AI agents can read them through BankSync's MCP tools or REST API.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to AWS](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-aws/index.md): Send your Apple Card transactions from your iPhone to Amazon S3, SQS, Kinesis Data Streams, DynamoDB or EventBridge in your AWS account with WalletFeed.
- [Export Apple Card transactions](https://walletfeed.app/guides/export-apple-card-transactions/index.md): Export or download your Apple Card transactions from Wallet, card.apple.com or WalletFeed. With WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed can also update a file.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to your app or server](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-api/index.md): There is no web API for your Apple Card transactions. iPhone apps read them with FinanceKit. WalletFeed sends them to a webhook, AWS, Supabase or BankSync.
- [Export Apple Card transactions to a CSV file automatically](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-csv/index.md): Export your Apple Card transactions from your iPhone to a CSV file. WalletFeed writes the file in a folder that you select and updates it automatically.
- [Save Apple Card transactions as OFX files](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-ofx/index.md): WalletFeed saves your Apple Card transactions in one OFX file for each month. It updates the files automatically, and you import them into your app.
- [Save Apple Card transactions as QIF files](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-qif/index.md): Export your Apple Card transactions as QIF files. WalletFeed saves one QIF file for each month from your iPhone to a folder that you select.
- [Import Apple Card transactions into Quicken](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-quicken/index.md): You can import your Apple Card transactions into Quicken for Mac from OFX files that WalletFeed saves in iCloud Drive. Quicken for Windows uses a CSV file.
- [Import Apple Card transactions into Actual Budget](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/index.md): Import Apple Card transactions into Actual Budget. WalletFeed saves them from your iPhone to an OFX file each month, and you import the file on a computer.
- [Import Apple Card transactions into GnuCash](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-gnucash/index.md): You can import your Apple Card transactions into GnuCash. WalletFeed writes an OFX file for each month from your iPhone, and you import the files.
- [Get Apple Card transactions into YNAB](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-ynab/index.md): Import your Apple Card transactions into YNAB with the YNAB app for iPhone, or with an OFX or CSV file that WalletFeed saves on your iPhone.
- [See Apple Card spending by category](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-spending-by-category/index.md): See your Apple Card spending by category on your iPhone, with the total for the month and the merchants. You can use it without WalletFeed Pro.
- [Find subscriptions on your Apple Card](https://walletfeed.app/guides/find-apple-card-subscriptions/index.md): See the subscriptions and other recurring charges on your Apple Card in WalletFeed. Get a notification when a new one starts or a price changes.
- [Search Apple Card transactions](https://walletfeed.app/guides/search-apple-card-transactions/index.md): Find a purchase in your Apple Card transactions on your iPhone with Search in WalletFeed. Type a merchant, amount or category, or use Apple Intelligence.
- [Add an Apple Card spending widget](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-spending-widget/index.md): Add an Apple Card spending widget to the Home Screen or Lock Screen of your iPhone. It compares this month with the same day and time last month.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to Google Sheets](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-google-sheets/index.md): Send your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a Google Sheets spreadsheet automatically with WalletFeed.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to Airtable](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/index.md): Send your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to an Airtable base. WalletFeed adds each transaction as a record.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to Notion](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/index.md): Send your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a Notion database with WalletFeed, for a budget in Notion.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to Coda](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/index.md): Send your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a table in Coda (Superhuman Docs) with WalletFeed and an API token.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to Supabase](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/index.md): Send your Apple Card transactions from your iPhone to a Postgres database in Supabase with WalletFeed. Each transaction is a row in your project.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to Linear](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-linear/index.md): Send your Apple Card transactions from your iPhone to Linear with WalletFeed. Each month, or each transaction, becomes an issue in a Linear team.
- [Open Apple Card transactions in Excel](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-excel/index.md): WalletFeed exports your Apple Card transactions to a CSV file on your iPhone. Excel opens the file on a Mac or a PC.
- [Open Apple Card transactions in Numbers](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-numbers/index.md): Open your Apple Card transactions in a Numbers spreadsheet. WalletFeed saves them from your iPhone to a CSV file in iCloud Drive and updates the file.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/search-apple-card-transactions/ -->
# Search Apple Card transactions

On your iPhone, [Search](/docs/search/) in WalletFeed finds a purchase in your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions when you type its merchant, amount or category. With Apple Intelligence, a search can also include a category, an amount and a period together, for example `dining over $50 last month`.

## Before you start

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- WalletFeed with access to your Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account.
- For a search with Apple Intelligence, an iPhone that can use Apple Intelligence and has Apple Intelligence on.

You can use Search without [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/).

## Step 1: Open Search

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap the search button in the bottom right corner of the screen.

   ![The Transactions screen with the tab bar and the search button at the bottom of the screen.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/search-apple-card-transactions/walletfeed-transactions.webp)

   The search field opens, and the keyboard shows. While the field is empty, **Categories** shows the categories of your transactions.

## Step 2: Find a purchase

1. Type the name of a merchant, an amount or a category, for example `Uber`, `23.40` or `Dining`.

   While you type, WalletFeed shows the transactions that have your text in their merchant, description, category or amount.

   The results show in one section for each month. In each section, the newest transaction is at the top. Each row shows the merchant, the amount and the date. The rows are the same as in [Transactions](/docs/transactions/).
